raw_source.text: In a two-dimensional steady flow field, in a certain region of the x-y plane, the velocity component in the x-direction is given by [latex]v_{x}=x^{2}[/latex] and the density varies as [latex]\rho =\frac{1}{x}[/latex]. Which of the following is a valid expression for the velocity component in the y- direction, [latex]v_{y}[/latex] ?
raw_source.solution:
Continuity equation in steady flow.
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{\partial(\rho u)}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial(\rho v)}{\partial y} &=0 \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x}\left[\frac{1}{x} \cdot x^{2}\right]+\frac{\partial}{\partial y}\left(\frac{1}{x} \cdot v_{y}\right) &=0 \\ \frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x)+\frac{1}{x} \frac{\partial v_{y}}{x \partial y} &=0 \\ 1+\frac{1}{x} \frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial y} &=0 \\ -x &=\frac{\partial v_{y}}{\partial y} \end{aligned}[/latex]
On integrating both sides
[latex] v_{y}=-x y[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The smallest and largest Eigen values of the following matrix are :
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 3 &-2 &2 \\ 4 &-4 &6 \\ 2 &-3 &5 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
raw_source.solution:
For eigen values
[latex]\begin{aligned} \left | A-\lambda I \right |&=0 \\ \begin{vmatrix} 3-\lambda & -2 &2 \\ 4 & -4-\lambda &6 \\ 2 & -3 & 5-\lambda \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\ \left ( 3-\lambda \right )\left ( -20+4\lambda -5\lambda +\lambda ^{2}+18 \right ) &\\ +2 \left ( 20-4\lambda -12 \right )+2\left ( -12+8+2\lambda \right )&=0 \\ \lambda ^{3}-4\lambda ^{2}+5\lambda -2&=0\end{aligned}[/latex]
Only 1 and 2 satisfy this equation.
[latex]\lambda =1,\: 1,\: 2[/latex]
Hence, Smallest eigen value =1 and
Largest eigen value =2

raw_source.text: The quadratic equation [latex]x^{2}-4x+4=0[/latex] is to be solved numerically, starting with the initial guess [latex]x_0=3[/latex]. The Newton-Raphson method is applied once to get a new estimate and then the Secant method is applied once using the initial guess and this new estimate. The estimated value of the root after the application of the Secant method is __________.
raw_source.solution: [latex] \begin{aligned}  f\left ( x \right )&=x^{2}-4x+4 \\   {f}'\left ( x \right )&=2x-4 \\   x_{0}&=3 \\   f\left ( 3 \right )&=1, {f}'\left ( 3 \right )=2 \\ \text{By Newton } & \text{Rapshon method,}\\   x_{1}&=x_{0}-\frac{f\left ( x_{0} \right )}{{f}'_{x_{0}}} \\    &=3-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{5}{2} \\   f\left ( \frac{5}{2} \right )&=\frac{25}{4}-10+4=\frac{1}{4} \\ & \text{By Secant method,}\\   x_{2}&=x_{1}-\frac{\left ( x_{1}-x_{0} \right )f\left ( x_{1} \right )}{f\left ( x_{1} \right )-f\left ( x_{0} \right )} \\    &=\frac{f_{1}x_{0}-f_{0}x_{1}}{f_{1}-f_{0}} \\    &=\frac{\left ( \frac{1}{4}\times 3 \right )-\left ( 1\times \frac{5}{2} \right )}{\frac{1}{4}-1} \\    &=\frac{7}{3}=2.33 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Consider the following differential equation:
[latex]x(ydx+xdy)\cos \frac{y}{x}=y(xdy-ydx)\sin \frac{y}{x}[/latex]
Which of the following is the solution of the above equation (c is an arbitrary constant)?
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} x\left ( ydx+xdy \right )\cos \frac{y}{x}&=y\left ( xdy-ydx \right )\sin \frac{y}{x} \\ \frac{ydx+xdy}{xdy-ydx}&=\frac{y}{x}\tan \frac{y}{x}\\ \text{Let } y&=v \cdot x \\ dy&=vdx+xdv \\ \frac{vxdx+vxdx+x^{2}dv}{vxdx+x^{2}dv-vxdx}&=v\tan v \\ \frac{xdv+2vdx}{xdv}&=v\tan v \\ 1+\frac{2v}{x}\frac{dx}{dv}&=v\tan v \\ \frac{2v}{x}\frac{dx}{dv}&=v\tan v-1 \\ 2\frac{dx}{x}&=\left ( \tan v-\frac{1}{v} \right )dv \end{aligned}[/latex]
Integrating both sides.
[latex]\begin{aligned}2\log x&=\log \left | \sec v \right |-\log v+\log c \\ \Rightarrow \;\; x^{2}&=\frac{c\sec v}{v} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; x^{2}\frac{y}{x}&=c\sec \frac{y}{x} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; xy\cos \frac{y}{x}&=c \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Consider the following complex function:
[latex]f(z)=\frac{9}{(z-1)(z+2)^{2}}[/latex]
Which of the following is one of the residues of the above function?
raw_source.solution:
[latex]f(z)[/latex] has poles at [latex]z=1, -2[/latex]
Residue of [latex]f(z)[/latex] at [/latex](z=1)[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 1}\left ( z-1 \right )f\left ( z \right ) \\ &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 1}\frac{9}{\left ( z+2 \right )^{2}} \\&=1 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Residue of [latex]f(z)[/latex] at [latex](z=-2)[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\frac{d}{dz^{2-1}}\left [ \left ( z+2 \right )^{2}f\left ( z \right ) \right ] \\ &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\frac{d}{dz}\left ( \frac{9}{z-1} \right ) \\ &=\lim_{z\rightarrow 2}\left ( \frac{9}{\left ( z-1 \right )^{2}} \right ) \\ &=-1\end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The composition of an air-entrained concrete is given below:

Assume the specific gravity of OPC, sand and coarse aggregate top be 3.14, 2.67 and 2.74, respectively. The air content is ________ [latex]litres/m^{3}[/latex] .
raw_source.solution:
Let the total volume of air-entrained concrete is unity.
[latex] \begin{array}{c} \frac{M_{C}}{\rho_{C}}+\frac{M_{F A}}{\rho_{F A}}+\frac{M_{C A}}{\rho_{C A}}+V_{W}+V_{\mathrm{Air}}=1.0 \\ \frac{368}{3.14 \times 1000}+\frac{606}{2.67 \times 1000} \\ +\frac{1155}{2.74 \times 1000}+\frac{184}{1000}+V_{V}=1.0 \\ 0.11720+0.22697+0.42153 \\ \begin{aligned} +0.184+V_{v}&=1.0 \\ V_{V}&=0.0503 \\ V_{V}&=0.0503 \times 1000 \\ \quad&=50.3\; litres / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A bracket plate connected to a column flange transmits a load of 100 kN as shown in the following figure. The maximum force for which the bolts should be designed is ___________ kN.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} F_{1}&=\frac{100}{5}=20kN \\ F_{2}&=\frac{Per}{\sum r^{2}} \\ &=\frac{\left ( 100\times 0.6 \right )\times \left ( 75\sqrt{2}\times 10^{-3} \right )}{\left ( 75\sqrt{2} \right )^2\times 4\times 10^{-6}} \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{10}\times 1000=141.42kN \\ \theta &=45^{\circ} \\ \Rightarrow \; \; F_{R}&=\sqrt{\left ( 20 \right )^{2}+\left ( 141.42 \right )^{2}+2\times 20\times 141.42\cos 45^{\circ}} \\ &=156.2 kN\end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider the singly reinforced beam section given below (left figure). The stress block parameters for the cross-section from IS: 456 : 2000 are also given below (right figure). The moment of resistance for the given section by the limit state method is ________ kN-m
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} A_{s t} &=4 \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times 12^{2} \\ &=452.38 \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ x_{u, \lim } &=0.48 \times 300=144 \mathrm{mm} \\ \because \quad C &=T \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.36 f_{c k} b x_{u} &=0.87 \mathrm{f}_{y} A_{s t} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x_{u}&=\frac{0.87 f_{y} A_{s t}}{0.36 f_{c k} b}=90.73 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex] \because x_{u} \lt x_{u, l \mathrm{im}},[/latex] it is under reinforced section
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad M O R&=0.36 f_{c k} b x_{u}\left(d-0.42 x_{u}\right) \\ &=42.7708 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{mm} \\ &=42.7708 \mathrm{kN}-\mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: For formation of collapse mechanism in the following figure, the minimum value of [latex]P_{u}[/latex] is [latex]cM_{p}/L[/latex]. [latex]M_{p}[/latex] and [latex]3M_{p}[/latex] denote the plastic moment capacities of beam sections as shown in this figure. The value of c is _____.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} L\phi&=3L\theta \\ \phi&=3\theta \\4M_{P}\theta +2M_{P}\phi &=PL\phi \\ \frac{4M_{P}\phi }{3}+2M_{P}\phi &=PL\phi \\ \frac{10M_{P}\phi }{3}&=PL\phi \\ P=\frac{10M_{P}}{3L} \; \Rightarrow \; C&=\frac{10}{3}=3.33 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A tapered circular rod of diameter varying from 20 mm to 10 mm is connected to another uniform circular rod of diameter 10 mm as shown in the following figure. Both bars are made of same material with the modulus of elasticity, [latex]E=2\times 10^{5}[/latex] MPa. When subjected to a load [latex]P=30\pi kN[/latex] , the deflection at point A is ______ mm.
raw_source.solution:
Total elongation,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta &=\Delta_{A B}+\Delta_{B C} \\ &=\frac{P L}{A E}+\frac{4 P L}{\pi d_{1} d_{2} E} \\ &=\frac{30 \pi \times 1.5}{\frac{\pi \times(0.01)^{2}}{4} \times 2 \times 10^{5}} \\ &+\frac{30 \pi \times 2}{\frac{\pi \times(0.01) \times(0.02)}{4} \times 2 \times 10^{5}} \\ &=9+6=15 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Properties of Metals, Stress and Strain

raw_source.text: Two beams are connected by a linear spring as shown in the following figure. For a load P as shown in the figure, the percentage of the applied load P carried by the spring is __________.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\Delta_{\text {spring }}=\Delta_{B}-\Delta_{D}[/latex]
Compression of spring
[latex] \begin{aligned} =\frac{(P-R) L^{3}}{3 E I}-\frac{R L^{3}}{3 E I}&=\frac{R}{K_{S}} \\ \frac{(P-R) L^{3}}{3 E I}-\frac{R L^{3}}{3 E I}&=\frac{R \times\left(2 L^{3}\right)}{3 E I}\\ (P-A)-R &=2 R \\ P &=4 R \\ R &=\frac{P}{4} \end{aligned}[/latex]
% force carried by spring =25 %

raw_source.text: For the 2D truss with the applied loads shown below, the strain energy in the member XY is _______ kN-m. For member XY, assume AE = 30 kN, where A is cross-section area and E is the modulus of elasticity.
raw_source.solution:
First calculating reactions
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Sigma M_{A}&=0\\ \Rightarrow\quad R_{B} \times 3-10 \times 9-5 \times 3 &=0 \\ R_{B} &=35 \mathrm{kN} \\ H_{A} &=10 \mathrm{kN} \\ \Sigma M_{B} &=0 \\ \Rightarrow\quad R_{A} \times 3+10 \times 9 &=0 \\ R_{A} &=-30 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Let us cut a section 1-1 as shown in figure and consider the lower part.


Given AE = 30 kN and L = 3 m.
Calculation for force Pin XY member


[latex] \begin{aligned} \Sigma F_{\text {horizontal }} &=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad F_{X Y}&=10 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Strain energy,
[latex] \begin{aligned} U&=\frac{P^{2} L}{2 A E}\\ U &=\frac{10^{2} \times 3}{2 \times 30} \\ &=5 \mathrm{kNm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: An earth embankment is to be constructed with compacted cohesionless soil. The volume of the embankment is 5000 [latex]m^{3}[/latex] and the target dry unit weight is 16.2 [latex]kN/m^{3}[/latex]. Three nearby sites (see figure blwo) have been identified from where the required soil can be transported to the construction site. The void ratios (e) of different sites are shown in the figure. Assume the specific gravity of soil to be 2.7 for all three sites. If the cost of transportation per km is twice the cost of excavation per [latex]m^{3}[/latex] of borrow pits, which site would you choose as the most economic solution? (Use unit weight of water = 10[latex]kN/m^{3}[/latex])
raw_source.solution:
Volume of solids at embankment,
[latex] \begin{aligned} V_{s} &=\frac{W_{s}}{G_{s} \gamma_{w}} \\ V_{s} &=\frac{16.2 \times 5000}{27 \times 10} \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ &=3000 \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Volume of solids will remain constant.
also,
[latex] \begin{aligned} V &=V_{V}+V_{s} \\ &=e V_{s}+V_{s}=V_{s}(1+e) \\ V &=3000(1+e) \\ V_{X} &=3000 \times 1.6=4800 \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ V_{Y} &=3000 \times 1.7=5100 \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ v_{z} &=3000 \times 1.64=4920 \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Let cost of excavation be [latex]\alpha / \mathrm{m}^{3} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} P_{X} &=4800 \alpha+140 \times \alpha \times 2 \\ &=5080 \alpha \\ P_{Y} &=5100 \alpha+80 \times \alpha \times 2 \\ &=5260 \alpha \\ P_{Z} &=4920 \alpha+100 \times \alpha \times 2 \\ &=5120 \alpha \end{aligned}[/latex]
Hence [latex] P_{X}[/latex] is least.
Hence total cost for site X is least.

raw_source.text: A water tank is to be constructed on the soil deposit shown in the figure below. A circular footing of diameter 3 m and depth of embedment 1 m has been designed to support the tank. The total vertical load to be taken by the footing is 1500 kN. Assume the unit weight of water as 10 [latex]kN/m^{3}[/latex] and the load dispersion pattern as 2V:1H. The expected settlement of the tank due to primary consolidation of the clay layer is ________ mm.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \Delta H &=\frac{C_{C} H_{0}}{1+e_{0}} \log _{10}\left[\frac{\bar{\sigma}_{0}+\Delta \bar{\sigma}}{\bar{\sigma}_{0}}\right] \\ H_{0} &=\text { Thickness of clay layer } \\ &=10 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \bar{\sigma}_{0}=[/latex] Effective stress before application
of load at the centre of clay layer
[latex] \begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{0}&=(15 \times 2)+(18-10) \times 6+(18-10) \times 5 \\ &= 118 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \Delta \bar{\sigma}=[/latex] Increase in effective stress due
to the structural weight at the centre of clay layer
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta \bar{\sigma} &=\frac{1500}{\frac{\pi}{4} \times(3+12)^{2}}=8.488 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \Delta H &=\frac{0.3 \times 10}{1+0.7} \log _{10}\left(\frac{118+8.488}{118}\right) \\ &=0.053236 \mathrm{m}=53.236 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A 20 m thick clay layer is sandwiched between a silty sand layer and a gravelly sand layer. The layer experiences 30 mm settlement in 2 years.

Given:
[latex]T_{v}=\left\{\begin{matrix} \frac{\pi }{4}\left ( \frac{U}{100} \right )^{2}& forU\leq 60\%\\ 1.781-0.933\log_{10}(100-U)& for U>60\%\end{matrix}\right.[/latex]

Where [latex]T_v[/latex] is the time factor and U is the degree consolidation in [latex]\%[/latex].
If the coefficient of consolidation of the layer is 0.003 [latex]cm^{2}/s[/latex], the deposit will experience a total of 50 mm settlement in the next _______ years.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} T_{v}&=\frac{C_{v} t}{d^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad T_{v}&=\frac{0.003 \times 2 \times 86400 \times 365}{\left(\frac{20}{2} \times 100\right)^{2}}\\ T_{v}&=0.1892 \lt 0.02827 \\ T_{v}&=\frac{\pi}{4} U^{2}=0.1892 &(\therefore U \lt 60 \%)\\ \Rightarrow \quad U&=0.4908 \\ \Rightarrow \quad&\text{Total consolidation}\\ &=\frac{30}{0.4908}=61.12 \mathrm{mm}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Degree of consolidation for 50 mm settlement
[latex] \begin{aligned} U &=\frac{50}{61.12}=0.818=81.8 \% \\ \Rightarrow \quad T_{v} &=0.60835=\frac{C_{v} t}{H^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad t &=\frac{0.60835 \times(10)^{2}}{0.003 \times 10^{-4}} \\ &=6.43 \text { years } \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow [/latex]Additional number of years =4.43

raw_source.text: A non-homogenous soil deposit consists of a silt layer sandwiched between a fine-sand layer at top and a clay layer below. Permeability of the silt layer is 10 times the permeability of the clay layer and one-tenth of the permeability of the sand layer. Thickness of the silt layer is 2 times the thickness of the sand layer and two-third of the thickness of the clay layer. The ratio of equivalent horizontal and equivalent vertical permeability of the deposit is __________.

A square footing (2m x 2m) is subjected to an inclined point load P as shown in the figure below. The water table is located well below the base of the footing. Considering one-way eccentricity, the net safe load carrying capacity of the footing for a factor of safety of 3.0 is _________ kN.

The following factor may be used:

Bearing capacity factors: [latex]N_{q}[/latex] =33.3, [latex]N_{\gamma }[/latex]=37.16; Shape factor:[latex]F_{qs }=F_{\gamma s }[/latex]=1.314; Depth factors : [latex]F_{q d }=F_{\gamma d }[/latex]=1.133; Inclination factors: [latex]F_{q i }[/latex]=0.444, [latex]F_{\gamma i }[/latex]=0.02
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} B'&= B-2e_x\\ &= 2-2 \times 0.15\\ &= 1.7m \end{aligned}[/latex]
As per Meyerhof theory
[latex]\begin{aligned} q_u&=CN_cS_cd_ci_c+\gamma D_fN_qd_qi_q\\ &+0.5B'\gamma N_\gamma S_\gamma d_ri_r\\ q_u&=18 \times 1(1.314 \times 1.113 \times 0.444) \times 33.3\\ &+10.5 \times 1.7 \times 18 \times 37.16 \\ & \times (1.314 \times 1.113 \times 0.02)\\ &=405.84 \; kN/m^2\\ q_{ns}&=\frac{q_u-\sigma }{F}=\frac{q_u-\gamma D_f}{F}\\ &=\frac{405.84-18 \times 1}{3}\\ &=129.28 \; kN/m^2\\ &\text{Net safe load}\\ &=q_{ns} \times \text{Area}\\ &=q_{ns} \times (B' \times L)\\ &=129.28 \times 1.7 \times 2\\ &=439.55\; kN \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Two reservoirs are connected through a 930 m long, 0.3 m diameter pipe, which has a gate valve. The pipe entrance is sharp (loss coefficient = 0.5) and the valve is half-open (loss coefficient = 5.5). The head difference between the two reservoirs is 20 m. Assume the friction factor for the pipe as 0.03 and g = 10 [latex]m/s^{2}[/latex]. The discharge in the pipe accounting for all minor and major losses is _________ [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex] .
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} L&=930 \mathrm{m} \\ D&= 0.3 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Apply energy equation between A and B
[latex] \begin{aligned} 20&=\frac{0.5 V^{2}}{2 g}+\frac{(0.03)(930) V^{2}}{2 g(0.3)}+\frac{5.5 V^{2}}{2 g}+\frac{V^{2}}{20} \\\ 20&=\frac{(0.03)(930)}{(03)} \frac{v^{2}}{20}+\frac{70 v^{2}}{20} \\ 20&=\frac{100 v^{2}}{2 g} \\ V&=2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{se} \\ a&=\frac{\pi}{4}(0.3)^{2}(2) \\ Q&=0.1414 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A hydraulic jump is formed in a 2 m wide rectangular channel which is horizontal and frictionless. The post-jump depth and velocity are 0.8 m and 1 [latex]m/s[/latex], respectively. The pre-jump velocity is _______[latex]m/s[/latex] (use g=10 [latex]m/s^{2}[/latex]).
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} y_{2} &=0.8 \mathrm{m} \\ v_{2} &=1 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ F_{f_{2}} &=\frac{v_{2}}{\sqrt{g D}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{10 \times \frac{0.8 \times 2}{2}}} \\ F_{f_{2}} &=0.3535 \\ y_{1} &=\frac{y_{2}}{2}\left(-1+\sqrt{1+8 F_{12}^{2}}\right) \\ &=\frac{0.8}{2}\left(-1+\sqrt{1+8 \times 0.3535^{2}}\right) \\ &=0.165643 \\ \Rightarrow \quad v_{1} y_{1} &=v_{2} y_{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad v_{1} &=\frac{1 \times 0.8}{0.165643}=4.83 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A short reach of a 2 m wide rectangular open channel has its bed level rising in the direction of flow at a slope of 1 in 10000. It carries a discharge of 4 [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex] and its Manning's roughness coefficient is 0.01. The flow in this reach is gradually varying. At a certain section in this reach, the depth of flow was measured as 0.5 m. The rate of change of the water depth with distance, dy/dx, at this section is ____ (use g = 10 [latex]m/s^{2}[/latex]).
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Adverb slope }&= -\frac{1}{1000}\\\\ Q &=4 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} \\ n &=0.01 \\ y &=0.5 \mathrm{m} \\ \frac{d y}{d x} &=\frac{S_{0}-S_{f}}{1-F_{t}^{2}} \\ F_{r} &=\frac{V}{\sqrt{g y}}=\frac{Q}{2 y \sqrt{g y}} \\ &=\frac{4}{2 \times 0.5 \sqrt{10 \times 0.5}}=1.789 \\ R &=\frac{A}{P}=\frac{2 \times 0.5}{2+2 \times 0.5}=\frac{1}{3} \\ Q &=\frac{1}{n} A R^{2 / 3} S_{f}^{1 / 2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
On solving for [latex]S_{f} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} S_{f}^{1 / 2} &=6.923 \times 10^{-3} \\ \frac{d y}{d x} &=\frac{-\frac{1}{10000}-6.923 \times 10^{-3}}{1-(1.789)^{2}} \\ &=3.191 \times 10^{-3} \simeq 0.0032 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The drag force [latex]F_{D}[/latex], on a sphere kept in a uniform flow field depends on the diameter of the sphere, D; flow velocity, V; fluid density, [latex]\rho[/latex]; and dynamic viscosity, [latex]\mu[/latex]. Which of the following options represents the non-dimensional parameters which could be used to analyze this problem?
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{For sphere,}\quad A&=\frac{\pi}{4} D^{2} \\ F_{D} &=C_{D} \times \frac{1}{2} \times p \times A \times V^{2} \\ F_{D} &=C_{D} \times \frac{1}{2} \times \rho \times\left(\frac{\pi}{4} D^{2}\right) \times V^{2} \\ \frac{F_{D}}{\rho D^{2} V^{2}} &=\frac{1}{2} \times\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right) \times C_{D} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a catchment, there are four rain-gauge stations, P, Q, R, and S. Normal annual precipitation values at these stations are 780 mm, 850 mm, 920 mm, and 980 mm respectively. In the year 2013, stations Q, R, and S, were operative but P was not. Using the normal ratio method, the precipitation at station P for the year 2013 has been established as 860 mm. If the observed precipitation at station Q and R for the year 2013 were 930 mm and 1010 mm, respectively; what was the observed precipitation (in mm) at station S for that year?
raw_source.solution:
Let [latex]P_{p}=[/latex] Precipitation in 2013 at station P
[latex] N_{p}=[/latex] Noramal annual precipitation at station P
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{P_{p}}{N_{p}}&=\frac{1}{3}\left [ \frac{P_{Q}}{N_{q}}+\frac{P_{R}}{N_{R}}+\frac{P_{S}}{N_{S}} \right ]\\ \frac{860}{780}&=\frac{1}{3}\left [ \frac{930}{850}+\frac{1010}{920}+\frac{P_{S}}{980} \right ] \\ \Rightarrow \;\; P_{s}&=1093.43 mm \end{aligned}[/latex]

The concentration of Sulfur Dioxide ([latex]SO_{2}[/latex]) in ambient atmosphere was measured as 30 [latex]\mu g/m^{3}[/latex]. Under the same conditions, the above [latex]SO_{2}[/latex] concentration expressed in ppm is ___________.

Given: (P/(RT) = 41.6 [latex]mol/m^{3}[/latex]; where, P=Pressure; T=Temperature; R=universal gas constant; Molecular weight of [latex]SO_{2}[/latex]= 64.
raw_source.solution:
1 [latex]m^{3}[/latex] of air has 30[latex]\mu g\; \; SO_{2}[/latex]
[latex]10^{6}[/latex][latex]m^{3}[/latex] of air has 30g [latex]SO_{2}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} 30g\; SO_{2} &=\frac{30}{64}\text{mole}\; SO_{2} \\ \text{From}\; PV &=nRT \\ V &=\frac{nRT}{P}=\frac{n}{P/RT} \\ &=\frac{\left ( 30/64 \right )}{41.6\; mol/m^{3}} \\ \text{Volume of}SO_{2} &=\frac{30}{64\times 41.6} \\ &=0.01127\; m^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow[/latex] Concentration of [latex]SO_{2}[/latex] in PPM=0.0113 ppm

raw_source.text:
Consider a primary sedimentation tank (PST) in a water treatment plant with Surface Overflow Rate (SOR) of 40 [latex]m^{3}/m^2/d[/latex]. The diameter of the spherical particle which will have 90 percent theoretical removal efficiency in this tank is_________ [latex]\mu m[/latex]. Assume that settling velocity of the particle in water described by Stokes' Law.

Given: Density of water = 1000 [latex]kg/m^{3}[/latex]; Density of particle = 2650 [latex]kg/m^{3}[/latex]; g = 9.81[latex]m/s^{2}[/latex]; Kinematic viscosity of water [latex](v) = 1.10 \times 10^{-6} m^{2}/s[/latex]
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { \% removal } &=\frac{V_{s}^{\prime}}{V_{s}} \times 100 \\ V_{s}^{\prime} &=0.9 \times V_{s} \\ &=0.9 \times \text { Overfiow rate } \\ V_{s}^{\prime} &=\frac{0.9 \times 40}{86400} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \frac{(G-1) g d^{2}}{18 \mathrm{v}} &=\frac{0.9 \times 40}{86400} \\ d &=\sqrt{\frac{0.9 \times 40 \times 18 \mathrm{p}_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{V}}{86400 \times\left(G_{s}-1\right) \times \rho_{\mathrm{w}} \times g}} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{0.9 \times 40 \times 18 \times 1.1 \times 10^{-6}}{86400 \times 1.64 \times 9.81}} \\ &=2.2576 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{m}=22.576 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The acceleration time relationship for a vehicle subjected to non-uniform acceleration is,
[latex]\frac{\mathrm{d}v }{\mathrm{d} t}=(\alpha -\beta v_{0})e^{-\beta t}[/latex]
Where, v is the speed in m/s, t is the time in s, [latex]\alpha[/latex] and [latex]\beta[/latex] are parameters, and [latex]v_{0}[/latex] is the initial speed in m/s. If the accelerating behavior of a vehicle, whose drive intends to overtake a slow moving vehicle ahead, is described as,
[latex]\frac{\mathrm{d} v}{\mathrm{d} t}=(\alpha -\beta v)[/latex]
considering [latex]\alpha =2 m/s^{2}[/latex], [latex]\beta =0.05s^{-1}[/latex] and [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d}v }{\mathrm{d} t}=1.3 m/s^{2}[/latex] at t=3s, the distance(in m) travelled by the vehicle in 35s is _______.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} &\frac{d v}{d t}=\alpha-\beta v\\ &\Rightarrow \quad \int \frac{d v}{(\alpha-\beta v)}=\int d t\\ &\Rightarrow \quad \frac{\ln (\alpha-\beta v)}{-\beta}=t+C\\ &\text { at } t=3 \text { sec, } \frac{d v}{d t}=\alpha-\beta v=1.3 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\\ &\Rightarrow \frac{\ln (1.3)}{-0.05}=3+c \Rightarrow c=-8.247\\ &\therefore \quad \ln (2-0.05 \times v)=(t-8.247)(-0.05)\\ &\Rightarrow 2-0.05 \times v=1.51 \mathrm{e}^{-0.05 t}\\ &\Rightarrow v=\frac{d s}{d t}=40-30.21 e^{-0.05 t}\\ &\Rightarrow s=40 t+604.15 e^{-0.05 t}+c^{\prime}\\ &\therefore \quad \text { at } t=0, s=0 \Rightarrow c^{\prime}=-604.15\\ &\Rightarrow \quad s=40 t+604.15 e^{-0.05 t}-604.15\\ &\text { at } t=35 \mathrm{sec}\\ &\Rightarrow \quad s=40 \times 35+604.15 \mathrm{e}^{-0.05 \times 35}-604\\ &\Rightarrow \quad s=900.84 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

raw_source.text: In Newton-Raphson iterative method, the initial guess value ( [latex]x_{ini}[/latex]) is considered as zero while finding the roots of the euation:[latex]f(x)=-2+6x-4x^{2}+0.5x^{3}[/latex]. [latex] y=\: \lim_{x\rightarrow \infty }\left ( 1+\frac{1}{x} \right )^{2x} [/latex]
[latex] \log y = \lim_{x\rightarrow \infty }2x\log \left ( 1+\frac{1}{x} \right )[/latex]
Which is in the form of [latex]\infty \times 0[/latex].
To convert this into [latex]\frac{0}{0}[/latex] form, we rewrite as,
[latex]\Rightarrow \log y= \lim_{x\rightarrow \infty }\frac{2\log \left ( 1+\frac{1}{x} \right )}{1/x}[/latex]
Now is in [latex]\frac{0}{0}[/latex] form.
Using L'Hospital's Rule,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \log y&=\lim_{x\rightarrow \infty }\frac{\frac{2\times -\frac{1}{x^{2}}}{1+\frac{1}{x}}}{-\frac{1}{x^{2}}} \\ \log y&=\lim_{x\rightarrow \infty }\frac{2}{1+\frac{1}{x}}=2 \\ \therefore \;\; y&= e^{2}\end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A superspeedway in New Delhi has among the highest super-elevation rates of any track on the Indian Grand Prix circuit. Using Rise and Fall method
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Sigma F S, &>\Sigma B . S \\ \therefore \text { Fall }&=\Sigma F . S,-\Sigma B . S .=R . L, \text { of first }\\ &\text{station - R.L, of last station}\\ &=5.645-3.085=2.56 \mathrm{m}\\ R.L.\text{ (last station) }&= R.L.\text{ (firet station) - Fall}\\ &=100-2.56=97.44 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The combined correction due to curvature and refraction (in m) for distance of 1 km on the surface of Earth is
raw_source.solution:
Correction due to curvature,
[latex] C_{c}=-0.0785 d^{2}[/latex]
Correction due to refraction,
[latex] C_{f}=+0.0112 d^{2}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore [/latex] Composite correction
[latex] \begin{aligned} C &=-0.0785 d^{2}+0.0112 d^{2} \\ &=-0.0673 d^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
where d is in km, C is in m.
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad C=0.0673 \times 1^{2}=0.0673 \mathrm{m}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
For probability density function of a random variable,x is
[latex]\begin{matrix} f(x) &=\frac{x}{4}(4-x^2) &for \;\; 0\leq x\leq 2 \\ &=0 & ohterwise \end{matrix}[/latex]
The mean, [latex]\mu _{x}[/latex] of the random variable is _____.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} f\left ( x \right ) &=\begin{cases} \frac{x}{4}\left ( 4-x^{2} \right ), & \text{ if } \; \; 0\leq x\leq 2\\ 0, & \text{ if } \; \; Otherwise \end{cases} \\ \mu _{x} &=\int_{0}^{2}xf\left ( x \right )dx \\ \therefore \text{Mean}\: \left ( \mu _{x} \right ) &=\int_{0}^{2}x\frac{x}{4}\left ( 4-x^{2} \right )dx \\ &=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( x^{2}-\frac{x^{4}}{4} \right )dx \\ &=\left [ \frac{x^{3}}{3}-\frac{x^{5}}{20} \right ]_{0}^{2}=\frac{8}{3}-\frac{32}{20}=\frac{16}{15} \\ &=1.066 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Consider the following second order linear differential equation:
[latex]\frac{d^2 y}{ dx^2}=-12x^{2}+24x-20[/latex]
The boundary conditions are: at x = 0, y = 5 and at x = 2, y = 21.
The value of y at x = 1 is ____________.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\frac{\mathrm{d^{2}} y}{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}=-12x^{2}+24x-20[/latex]
Integrating both sides wrt. x,
[latex]\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}=-4x^{3}+12x^{2}-20x+c_{1}[/latex]
Integrating both sides wrt. x, [latex]y=-x^{4}+4x^{3}-10x^{2}+c_{1}x+c_{2} \;\;...(i)[/latex]
At [latex]x=0, \; y=5 [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\; 5=c_{2}[/latex]
At [latex]x=2, \; y=21[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \;\; 21&=-16+32-40+2c_{1}+c_{2} \\ 2c_{1}&=21+16-2+40-5 \\ 2c_{1}&=40 \\ c_{1}&=20 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; y&=-x^{4}+4x^{3}-10x^{2}+20x+5\\ &\text{Put } x=1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; y&=-1+4-10+20+5 \\ y&=18 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The two Eigen values of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1\\ 1 & p \end{bmatrix}[/latex]  have a ratio of 3:1 for p = 2. What is another value of p for which the Eigen values have the same ratio of 3:1?
raw_source.solution:
[latex] A=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1\\ 1 & p \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
Let [latex]\lambda _{1}[/latex] and [latex]\lambda _{2}[/latex] be the eigen value of matrix A
[latex]\therefore \;\; \frac{\lambda _{1}}{\lambda _[2]}=\frac{3}{1}[/latex] for [latex]p=2[/latex]
Sum of eigen value
[latex] =\lambda _{1}+\lambda _{2}=2+p \;\;...(i)[/latex]
Product of eigen value
[latex] =\lambda _{1}\lambda _{2}=2p-1 \;\;...(ii)[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{\lambda _{1}}{\lambda _{2}}&=\frac{3}{1} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \lambda _{1}&=3\lambda _{2}\\ &\text{From eq. (i)}\\ \Rightarrow \;\; 3\lambda _{2}+\lambda _{2}&=2+p \\ 4\lambda _{2}&=2+p \\ \lambda _{2}&=\frac{p+2}{4} \\ \text{From eq. (ii)}\\ \Rightarrow \;\; 3\lambda _{2}^{2}&=2p-1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; 3\left ( \frac{p+2}{4} \right )^{2}&=2p-1 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; p&=2,\frac{14}{3}\end{aligned}[/latex]
OR
[latex] \begin{aligned} A=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1\\ 1 & p \end{bmatrix} \\ A-I\lambda &=0 \\ \begin{bmatrix} 2-\lambda & 1\\ 1 & p-\lambda \end{bmatrix}&=0 \\ \left ( 2-\lambda \right )\left ( p-\lambda \right )-1&=0 \\ \lambda ^{2}-\left ( p+2 \right )\lambda +\left ( 2p-1 \right )=0\end{aligned} [/latex]
By putting values of p from options.
By putting option (D) [latex]\frac{14}{3}[/latex] in above equations gives value 5, [latex]\frac{5}{3}[/latex].
Hence ratio of two eigen values [latex]=\frac{5}{5/3}= 3:1[/latex].

raw_source.text:
For step-size, [latex]\Delta x=0.4[/latex], the value of following integral using Simpson's 1/3 rule is _________.
[latex]\int_{0}^{0.8}(0.2+25x-200x^{2}+675x^{3}-900x^{4}+400x^{5})dx[/latex]
raw_source.solution:
[latex]a=0, b=0.8, \Delta x=0.4 [/latex]
[latex]f\left ( x \right )=0.2+25x-200x^{2}+675x^{3}-900x^{4}+400x^{5}[/latex]



By Simpson's 1/3 Rule,
[latex] \begin{aligned} y\left ( x \right )&=\int_{0}^{0.8}\left ( 0.2+25x-200x^{2}+675x^{3}-900x^{4}+400x^{5} \right )dx \\ &=\frac{4}{3}\left [ y_{0}+4y_{1}+y_{2} \right ] \\ y_{0}&=y\left ( 0 \right )=0.2 \\ y_{1}&=y\left ( 0.4 \right )=2.456 \\ y_{2}&=y\left ( 0.8 \right )=0.232 \\ y\left ( n \right )&=\frac{0.4}{3}\left ( 0.2+4\times 2.456+0.232 \right ) \\ &=1.367 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a system,two connected rigid bars AC and BC are of identical length, L with pin supports at A and B. The bars are interconnected at C by a frictionless hinge. The rotation of the hinge is restrained by a rotational spring of stiffness, k. The system initially assumes a straight line configuration, ACB. Assuming both the bars as weightless, the rotation at supports, A and B, due to a transverse load, P applied at C is
raw_source.solution:
Deflection under load [latex]P=\theta L [/latex]
Work done by force [latex]P=\frac{1}{2} P(\theta L) [/latex]


Strain energy stored in spring
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{1}{2}[k(2 \theta)](2 \theta) \\ \frac{1}{2} P(\theta L) &=\frac{4 k \theta^{2}}{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \theta &=\frac{P L}{4 k} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Theory of Columns and Shear Centre

raw_source.text: A simply supported reinforced concrete beam of length 10 m sags while undergoing shrinkage. Assuming a uniform curvature of 0.004 [latex]m^{-1}[/latex]  along the span, the maximum deflection (in m) of the beam at mid-span is _______.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Radius. }R&=\frac{1}{C}=250 \mathrm{m} \\ O A &=\sqrt{250^{2}-5^{2}} \\ &=249.95 \mathrm{m} \\ \text { Deflection } &=A A^{\prime}=250-249.95 \\ &=0.05 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A steel strip of length, L = 200 mm is fixed at end A and rests at B on a vertical spring of stiffness, k = 2 N/mm. The steel strip is 5 mm wide and 10 mm thick. A vertical load, P = 50 N is applied at B, as shown in the figure. Considering E = 200 GPa, the force (in N) developed in the spring is _________.
raw_source.solution:
Deflection of point B= Deflection of spring
[latex] \Delta_{B}=\frac{(P-R) L^{3}}{3 E I}=\frac{R}{k}[/latex]
Where, R= Force in the spring
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \frac{(50-R) 200^{3}}{3 \times 200 \times 10^{3} \times \frac{5 \times 10^{3}}{12}}&=\frac{R}{2} \\ 0.064(50-R)&= R \\ 3.2&=R+0.064 R \\ R &=3.0075 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A simply supported beam AB of span, L=24 m is subjected to two wheel loads acting at a distance, d=5m apart as shown in the figure below. Each wheel transmits a load, P=3 kN and may occupy any position along the beam. If the beam is an I-section having section modulus, S=16.2 [latex]cm^{3}[/latex], the maximum bending stress (in GPa) due to the wheel loads is ___________.
raw_source.solution:
C.G. of system= 2.5 m from any load For maximum bending moment, system of load should be,

Ordinate of ILD at C

Ordinate of LLD at D
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{5.935 \times 8.25}{13.25}=3.695 \\ \text { Maximum } \mathrm{BM} &=5.935 \times 3+3.695 \times 3 \\ &=28.89 \mathrm{kN}-\mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Maximum bending stress,

raw_source.text: According to the concept of Limit State Design as per IS 456: 2000, the probability of failure of a structure is__________.
raw_source.solution:
The structure may fail when, the load exceeds the design load
(ii) the strength is less than the characteristic strength
(iii) both the load exceeds the design load and strength is less than the characteristic strength.
The probability of load exceeding design load = 5%
(iv) The probability of strength less than characteristic strength = 5%
The probability of failure is
[latex] =0.05 \times 0.95+0.05 \times 0.95+0.05 \times 0.05 [/latex]
[latex] =0.0975[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a pre-stressed concrete beam section shown in the figure, the net loss is 10% and the final pre-stressing force applied at X is 750 kN. The initial fiber stresses (in [latex]N/mm^{2}[/latex] ) at the top and bottom of the beam were:

Given, net loss =10 %
Final prestressing force after loss =750 kN
Hence, initial prestressing force
[latex] =\frac{750}{0.9}=833.33 \mathrm{kN}[/latex]
Initial stresses at top and bottom
[latex] \begin{array}{l} =\frac{P}{A} \pm \frac{P e}{Z}=\frac{833.33 \times 10^{3}}{250 \times 400} \pm \frac{833.33 \times 10^{3} \times 100 \times 6}{250 \times 400^{2}} \\ =8.33 \pm 12.50 \\ \end{array}[/latex]
Stress at top [latex]=8.33-12.50=-4.17[/latex] (tensile)

raw_source.text: A fixed end beam is subjected to a load, W at 1/3rd span from the left support as shown in the figure. The collapse load of the beam is:

A 588 [latex]cm^{3}[/latex] volume of moist sand weighs 1010 gm. Its dry weight is 918 gm and specific gravity of solids, G is 2.67. Assuming density of water as 1 gm/[latex]cm^{3}[/latex], the void ratio is __________.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \gamma_{\mathrm{d}} &=\frac{918}{588}=1.561 \mathrm{g} / \mathrm{cc} \\ \gamma_{\mathrm{d}} &=\frac{G \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}}{1+e} \\ 1.561 &=\frac{2.67 \times 1}{1+\mathrm{e}} \\ e &=0.71 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 4 m thick layer of normally consolidated clay has an average void ratio of 1.30. Its compression index is 0.6 and coefficient of consolidation is 1 [latex]m^{2}/yr[/latex]. If the increase in vertical pressure due to foundation load on the clay layer is equal to the existing effective overburden pressure, the change in the thickness of the clay layer is ______ mm.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} e &=1.3 \\ C_{C} &=0.6 \\ C_{V} &=1 \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{year} \\ \Delta H &=\frac{\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{H}_{0}}{1+\mathrm{e}_{0}} \log _{10}\left[\frac{\overline{\mathrm{\sigma}}_{0}+\Delta \bar{\sigma}}{\bar{\sigma}_{0}}\right] \end{aligned}[/latex]
As increase in vertical pressure [latex](\Delta \sigma)[/latex] is equal to existing effective over burden pressure [latex]\left(\bar{\sigma}_{0}\right), [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{0.6 \times 4}{1+1.3} \log _{10}\left(\frac{\bar{\sigma}_{0}+\bar{\sigma}_{0}}{\bar{\sigma}_{0}}\right) \\ &=\frac{0.6 \times 4}{2.3} \log _{10} 2 \\ &=0.314 \mathrm{m}=314 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A pile of diameter 0.4 m is fully embedded in a clay stratum having 5 layers, each 5 m thick as shown in the figure below. Assume a constant unit weight of soil as 18 kN/[latex]m^{3}[/latex] for all the layers. Using [latex]\lambda[/latex]-method ([latex]\lambda[/latex]=0.15 for 25 m embedment length) and neglecting the end bearing component, the ultimate pile capacity (in kN) is ________.
raw_source.solution:
Ultimate bearing capacity
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\lambda\left(\sigma_{\mathrm{v} a v}+2 C_{u}\right) A_{s} \\ &=0.15\left[18 \times 12.5+2 C_{u}\right] \times(\pi \times 0.4 \times 25) \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] C_{u}[/latex] is the average value of all layers i.e., 60 kPa.
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=0.15[18 \times 12.5+2 \times 60] \times(\pi \times 0.4 \times 25) \\ &=1625.77 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Stress path equation for tri-axial test upon application of deviatoric stress is, [latex]q=10\sqrt{3}+0.5p[/latex]. The respective values of cohesion, c (in kPa) and angle of internal friction, [latex]\phi[/latex] are:
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{\alpha_{2}-\alpha_{2t}}{2}&= c \cos \phi+\frac{\alpha_{2}-\alpha_{2t}}{2}\sin\phi\\ \text{as}\quad q&=10\sqrt{3}+0.5p\\ \Rightarrow \quad c \cos\phi&=10\sqrt{3}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \tan \beta&=\sin^{-1}(0.5)=30^{\circ}\\ \Rightarrow \quad c&=\frac{10\sqrt{3}}{\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}}=20\\ \Rightarrow \quad c&=20\\ \phi&=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 6 m high retaining wall having a smooth vertical back face retains a layered horizontal backfill. Top 3 m thick layer of the backfill is sand having an angle of internal friction, [latex]\phi=30^{\circ}[/latex] while the bottom layer is 3 m thick clay with cohesion, c = 20 kPa. Assume unit weight for both sand and clay as 18 kN/[latex]m^{3}[/latex]. The totalactive earth pressure per unit length of the wall (in kN/m) is:
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \phi_{\text {clay }}&=0 \\ K_{a_{1}}&=\frac{1-\sin \phi}{1+\sin \phi}=\frac{1}{3} \\ K_{a_{2}}&=1 \\ p_{B}&=K_{a_{1}} \gamma z=\frac{1}{3} \times 18 \times 3=18 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ p_{B^{\prime}}&=K_{a_{2}} \gamma z-2 c \sqrt{K_{a_{2}}} \\ &=1 \times 18 \times 3-2 \times 20 \sqrt{1}=14 \\ p_{C}&=K_{a_{2}} \gamma Z-2 c \sqrt{K_{a_{2}}} \\ &=18 \times 6-2 \times 20 \sqrt{1}=68 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Total active earth pressure per unit length of wall
[latex] P_{a}=\frac{1}{2} \times 18 \times 3+\frac{1}{2}(68+54) \times 3=150 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A field channel has cultivable commanded area of 2000 hectares. The intensities of irrigation for gram and wheat are 30% and 50% respectively. Gram has a kor period of 18 days, kor depth of 12 cm, while wheat has a kor period of 18 days and a kor depth of 15 cm. The discharge (in [latex]m^{3}[/latex]/s) required in the field channel to supply water to the commanded area during the kor period is_____.
raw_source.solution:
Gram and wheat are Rabi crops.
So both are grown in the same period.
Discharge required for gram,
[latex] Q_{g}=\frac{A_{g}}{D_{g}}=\frac{2000 \times 0.3}{8.64 \times \frac{18}{0.12}}=0.4630 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
Discharge required for wheat,
[latex] Q_{w}=\frac{A_{w}}{D_{w}}=\frac{2000 \times 0.5}{8.64 \times \frac{18}{0.15}}=0.9645 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
[latex] Total discharge =Q_{g}+Q_{w}=1.4275 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A triangular gate with a base width of 2 m and a height of 1.5 m lies in a vertical plane. The top vertex of the gate is 1.5 m below the surface of a tank which contains oil of specific gravity 0.8. Considering the density of water and acceleration due to gravity to be 1000 kg/[latex]m^{3}[/latex] and 9.81 m/[latex]s^{2}[/latex], respectively, the hydrostatic force (in kN) exerted by the oil on the gate is__________.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \bar{h} &=1.5+1.5\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)=2.5 \mathrm{m} \\ F_{R} &=\rho g \bar{h} A \\ &=(800)(9.81)(2.5)\left(\frac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 1.5\right) \\ &=29430 \mathrm{N}=29.43 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The velocity components of a two dimensional plane motion of a fluid are: [latex]u=\frac{y^{3}}{3}+2x-x^{2}y[/latex] and [latex]v=xy^{2}-2y-\frac{x^{3}}{3}[/latex].
The correct statement is:
raw_source.solution:
Continuity equation
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} &=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad(2-2 x y)+(2 x y-2) &=0 \\ 0 &=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Hence, incompressible fluid.
[latex] \begin{aligned} \omega_{z} &=\frac{1}{2}\left[\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\right] \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left[y^{2}-\frac{3 x^{2}}{3}-\left(\frac{3 y^{2}}{3}-x^{2}\right)\right] \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left[y^{2}-x^{2}-y^{2}+x^{2}\right] \\ &=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Hence, flow is irrotational.
options: Fluid is incompressible and flow is irrotational
Fluid is incompressible and flow is rotational
Fluid is compressible and flow is irrotational
Fluid is compressible and flow is rotational

raw_answer.option_text: Fluid is incompressible and flow is irrotational

raw_source.text: The average surface area of a reservoir in the month of June is 20 [latex]km^{2}[/latex]. In the same month, the average rate of inflow is 10 [latex]m^{3}[/latex]/s, outflow rate is 15 [latex]m^{3}[/latex]/s, monthly rainfall is 10 cm, monthly seepage loss is 1.8 cm and the storage change is 16 million [latex]m^{3}[/latex]. The evaporation (in cm) in that month is
raw_source.solution:
Let 'x' cm evaporation takes place in month of June.
Total inflow
[latex] \begin{array}{l} =\left(\frac{10 \times 30 \times 24 \times 60 \times 60}{20 \times 10^{6}} \times 100\right)+10 \\ =139.6 \mathrm{cm} \end{array}[/latex]
Total outflow
[latex] \begin{array}{l} =\left(\frac{15 \times 30 \times 24 \times 60 \times 60}{20 \times 10^{6}} \times 100\right)+1.8+x\\ =196.2+x \mathrm{cm} \end{array}[/latex]
As total outflow is more than total inflow, therefore depression in storage takes place.
Depression in storage
[latex] \begin{aligned} =-\frac{16 \times 10^{6}}{20 \times 10^{6}} \times 100&=-80 \mathrm{cm} \\ \Rightarrow 139.6-(196.2+x)&=-80 \\ -x &=-80+56.6\\ \therefore \quad x&=23.4 \mathrm{cm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Evaporation, Transpiration and Stream Flow Measurement

raw_source.text: A pipe of 0.7 m diameter has a length of 6 km and connects two reservoirs A and B. The water level in reservoir A is at an elevation 30 m above the water level in reservoir B. Halfway along the pipe line, there is a branch through which water can be supplied to a third reservoir C. The friction factor of the pipe is 0.024. The quantity of water discharged into reservoir C is 0.15 [latex]m^{3}[/latex]/s. Considering the acceleration due to gravity as 9.81 [latex]m/s^{2}[/latex] and neglecting minor losses, the discharge (in [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex]) into the reservoir B is __________.

A landfill is to be designed to serve a population of 200000 for a period of 25 years. The solid waste (SW) generation is 2 kg/person/day. The density of the un-compacted SW is 100 kg/[latex]m^{3}[/latex] and a compaction ratio of 4 is suggested. The ratio of compacted fill (i.e. SW + cover) to compacted SW is 1.5. The landfill volume (in million [latex]m^{3}[/latex] ) required is _______.
raw_source.solution:
Solid waste generated per day
[latex]=2\times 200000=400000\: kg[/latex]
Total solid waste generated in 25 years
[latex]=400000\times 365\times 25=3.65\times 10^{9}\: kg[/latex]
Compaction ratio,
[latex] 4=\frac{Volume\; before\; compaction}{Volume\; after\; compaction}[/latex]
Volume of waste before compaction,
[latex]V=\frac{3.65\times 10^{9}}{100}=3.65\times 10^{7}\: m^{3}[/latex]
Volume of waste after compaction,
[latex]V'=\frac{3.65\times 10^{7}}{4}=9.125\times 10^{6}\: m^{3}[/latex]
[latex]\frac{SW+cover}{SW}=\frac{SW}{SW}+\frac{cover}{SW}=1.5[/latex]
[latex]\frac{Cover}{SW}=0.5[/latex]
[latex]Cover=0.5\times 9.125\times 10^{6}[/latex]
[latex]\; \; \; =4.5625\times 10^{6}\: m^{3}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Total volume} &=SW+Cover \\ &=\left ( 9.125+4.5625 \right )\times 10^{6}\: m^{3} \\ &=13.6875\: million\: m^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A water treatment plant of capacity,[latex]1\: m^{3}/s[/latex] has filter boxes of dimensions 6m x 10m. Loading rate to the filters is [latex]120 m^{3}/day/m^{2}[/latex]. When two of the filters are out of service for back washing, the loading rate (in [latex]m^{3}/day/m^{2}[/latex])is_______.
raw_source.solution:
Total water filtered in a day
[latex] =60 \times 60 \times 24=86400 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{day} [/latex]
Total surface area of filter required
[latex] =\frac{86400 m^{3} / d a y}{120 m^{3} / d a y / m^{2}}=720 m^{2} [/latex]
Area of one filter [latex] =6 \times 10=60 \mathrm{m}^{2} [/latex]
Total no. of filter [latex]=\frac{720}{60}=12\text{ filtres }[/latex]
As two filters are out of service, number of filters working =12-2=10
Total surface area of filter
[latex] =60 \times 10=600 \mathrm{m}^{2} [/latex]
The new loading rate
[latex] =\frac{86400 m^{3} / d a y}{600 m^{2}}=144 m^{3} / d a y / m^{2}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Ultimate BOD of a river water sample is 20 mg/L. BOD rate constant (natural log) is 0.15 [latex]day^{-1}[/latex]. The respective values of BOD (in %) exerted and remaining after 7 days are:
raw_source.solution:
BOD remaining FTER 7 DAYS
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=BOD_{u}e^{-kt} \\ &=20\times e^{-0.15\times 7} \\ &=20\times 0.35=7 \\ \%: remaining &=\frac{7\times 100}{20}=35\% \end{aligned}[/latex]
BOD exerted in 7 days
[latex] =\left ( 100-35 \right )\%=65\%[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

raw_source.text: In a wastewater treatment plant, primary sedimentation tank (PST) designed at an overflow rate of 32.5 [latex]m^{3}/day/m^{2}[/latex] is 32.5 m long, 8.0 m wide and liquid depth of 2.25 m. If the length of the weir is 75 m, the weir loading rate (in [latex]m^{3}/day/m[/latex]) is ___________.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} V_{0} &=\frac{Q}{B L} \\ Q &=\left(32.5 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{d} / \mathrm{m}^{2}\right) \times 32.5 \times 8 \\ &=8450 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{d}\\ \text{Weir length }&=75 \mathrm{m} \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.solution:
Mean of f(x) is E(x)
[latex]=\int_{-a}^{0}x\left ( \frac{x}{a}+1 \right )dx+\int_{0}^{a}x\left ( \frac{-x}{a}+1 \right )dx[/latex]
[latex]=\left ( \frac{x^{3}}{3a}+\frac{x^{2}}{2} \right )_{-a}^{0}+\left ( \frac{-x^{3}}{3a}+\frac{x^{2}}{2} \right )_{0}^{a}=0[/latex]
Variance of f(x) is [latex]E\left ( x \right )^{2}-\left \{ E\left ( x \right )^{2} \right \}[/latex] where,
[latex]E\left ( x \right )^{2}=\int_{-a}^{0}x^{2}\left ( \frac{x}{a}+1 \right )dx+\int_{0}^{a}x^{2}\left ( \frac{-x}{a}+1 \right )dx[/latex]

[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; [/latex]Variance is [latex]\frac{a^{3}}{6}[/latex]
Next, mean of g(x) is E(x)
[latex]=\int_{a}^{0}s\left ( \frac{-x}{a} \right )dx+\int_{0}^{a}x\left ( \frac{x}{a} \right )dx=0[/latex]
Variance of g(x) is [latex]E\left ( x^{2} \right )-\left \{ E\left ( x \right )^{2} \right \}[/latex], where,

[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; [/latex]Variance is [latex]\frac{a^{3}}{2}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Newton-Raphson method is to be used to find root of equation [latex]3x-e^{x}+\sin x=0[/latex]. If the initial trial value for the root is taken as 0.333, the next approximation for the root would be _________
raw_source.solution:
According to Newton-Raphson Method:
[latex] \begin{aligned} x_{N+1}&=X_{N}-\frac{f\left ( X_{N} \right )}{{F}'\left ( X_{N} \right )} \\ f\left ( x \right )&=3x-e^{x}+\sin x \\ {f}'\left ( x \right )&=3-e^{x}+\cos x \\ \Rightarrow \;\; X_{1}&=X_{0}-\frac{f\left ( 0.333 \right )}{{f}'\left ( 0.333 \right )} \\ &=0.333-\frac{3\times 0.333-e^{0.333}+\sin 0.333}{3-e^{0.333}+\cos 0.333} \\ \therefore \;\; X_{1}&=0.36 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.solution:
The PDE [latex]\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=\alpha \frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2} \;\;...(i)[/latex]
Solution of (i) is,
[latex] u\left ( x,t \right )=\left ( A\cos px+B\sin px \right )Ce^{-p^{2}\alpha t}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned}u\left ( x,t \right )&=\left ( A\cos \sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x+b\sin h\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x \right )Ce^{kt} \\ &=Ce^{kt}\left [ A\left \{ \frac{e^{\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}+e^{-\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}}{2} \right \}+B\left \{ \frac{e^{\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}-e^{-\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}}{2} \right \} \right ] \\ &=Ce^{kt}\left [ e^{\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}\left \{ \frac{A+B}{2} \right \}+e^{-\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}\left \{ \frac{A-B}{2} \right \} \right ] \\ &=Ce^{kt}\left [ c_{1}e^{\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x}+c_{2}e^{-\sqrt{\frac{k}{\alpha }}x} \right ] \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The semi-compact section of a laterally unsupported steel beam has an elastic section modulus, plastic section modulus and design bending compressive stress of [latex]500 \; cm^3, 650 \; cm^3[/latex] and 200MPa, respectively. raw_source.solution:
Design flexural capacity,
[latex]M_{d}= \beta _{b}Z_{p}\frac{f_{y}}{\gamma _{m0}}[/latex]
[latex]\beta _{b}= 1.0[/latex] (for plastic and compact sections)
[latex]\; \; \; \; = \frac{Z_{e}}{Z_{p}}[/latex] (for semi-compact sections)
[latex]Z_{p}=\,[/latex] Plastic section modulus
[latex]Z_{e}=\,[/latex] elastic section modulus
[latex]f_{y}=\,[/latex] yeild stress of steel provided
[latex]\gamma_{m0}=\,[/latex] material factor of safety of steel against yeilding
As, design bending stress is directly given,
[latex]\begin{aligned} M_{d}&= \beta _{b}Z_{p}f_{d} \\ &= \frac{Z_{e}}{Z_{p}}\times Z_{p}\times f_{d} \\ &= Z_{e}\times f_{d} \\ &= 500\times 10^{3}\times 200\times 10^{-6} \\ &= 100 kN-m \end{aligned}[/latex]

and

raw_source.text:
A 3 m long simply supported beam of uniform cross section is subjected to a uniformly distributed load of w=20kN/m in the central 1 m as shown in the figure

If the flexural rigidity (EI) of the Beam is [latex]30\times 10^{6}N-m^{2}[/latex], the Maximum slope (expressed in Radians ) of the deformed beam is:
raw_source.solution:
Due to symmetrical loading,
[latex] R_{p}=R_{Q}=\frac{w \times 1}{2}=\frac{w}{2}[/latex]


[latex] M_{x}=R_{\rho} x /-\frac{w}{2}(x-1)^{2} /+\frac{W}{2}(x-2)^{2}[/latex]
According to Macaulay method
[latex] E I \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}=R_{\rho} x /-\frac{w}{2}(x-1)^{2} /+\frac{w}{2}(x-2)^{2}[/latex]
After integrating once
[latex] E I \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{R_{p} x^{2}}{2}+c_{1} /-\frac{w}{6}(x-1)^{3} /+\frac{w}{6}(x-2)^{3} [/latex]
Due to symmetrical loading slope will be zero at
mid section (x=1.5 m)
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \text{at }x&=15 \mathrm{m}, \frac{d y}{d x}=0 \\ 0 &=\frac{R_{p}(1.5)^{2}}{2}+c_{1}-\frac{w}{6}(1.5-1)^{3} \\ &=\frac{9 R_{p}}{8}+c_{1}-\frac{w}{48}=\frac{9 w}{16}+c_{1}-\frac{w}{48} \\ \therefore \quad c_{1} &=\frac{w}{48}-\frac{9 w}{16}=-\frac{26 w}{48}=-\frac{13 w}{24} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\therefore \quad[/latex] Equation of slope
[latex] E I \cdot \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{R_{p} x^{2}}{2}-\frac{13 w}{24} /-\frac{w}{6}(x-1)^{3} /+\frac{w(x-2)^{3}}{6} [/latex]
The slope will be maximum at the support
[latex] \therefore \theta_{\max }(x=0)[/latex]
[latex] =\frac{-13 w}{24 E I}=\frac{-13 \times 20 \times 10^{3}}{24 \times 30 \times 10^{6}}=-0.361 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{radiar} [/latex]
Alternatively.
Moment Area Method


[latex] \begin{aligned} M_{A} & =P \times x \\ & =10 \times 1=10 \mathrm{kNm} \\ M_{B} & =P_{x}-\frac{W}{2}(x-1)^{2} \\ & =10 \times 1.5-\frac{20 \times 0.5^{2}}{2}=12.5 \mathrm{kNm} \end{aligned} [/latex]


[latex] \theta_{A}-\theta_{C}=[/latex] Area of M/EI diagram between points
P and B
[latex]\begin{aligned} &\theta_{B}-\theta_{A}=A_{l}+A_{II}+A_{III}\\ &=\left(\frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times \frac{10}{E I}\right)+\left(0.5 \times \frac{10}{E I}\right)+\left(\frac{2}{3} \times 0.5 \times \frac{2.5}{E I}\right) \\ &=\frac{5}{E I}+\frac{5}{E I}+\frac{0.833}{E I} \\ \theta_{A} &=-\frac{10.833}{E I}=-\frac{10.833 \times 10^{3}}{30 \times 10^{6}} \\ &=-0.3611 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{radians} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 4 m wide rectangular channel, having bed slope of 0.001 carries a discharge of [latex]16\:\, m^{3}/s[/latex].  Considering Manning's roughness coefficient = 0.012 and [latex]g =10\: \: m/s^{2}[/latex], the category of the channel slope is

raw_source.text: An electrostatic precipitator (ESP) with 5600 [latex]m^{2}[/latex] of collector plate area is 96 percent efficient in treating 185[latex]m^{3}/s[/latex] of flue gas from a 200 MW thermal power plant. It was found that in order to achieve 97 percent efficiency, the collector plate area should be 6100 [latex]m^{2}[/latex]. In order to increase the efficiency to 99 percent, the ESP collector plate area (expressed in [latex]m^{2}[/latex] ) would be ______
raw_source.solution:
As per Deutsch-Anderson equation, to determine the collection efficiency of the precipitator under ideal conditions,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \eta &=1-e^{-w\left ( A/Q \right )} \\ \eta &=\text{Collection efficiency of the precipitator} \\ w &=\text{Migration velocity,}\: cm/s \\ A &=\text{The effective collecting plate area of the precipitator,}\: m^{2} \\ Q &=\text{Gas flow through the precipitator,}\: m^{3}/s \\ 0.96&=1-e^{-\left ( \frac{w}{Q} \right )\times 5600}\; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; ...\left ( i \right ) \\ 0.97 &=1-e^{-\left ( \frac{w}{Q} \right )\times 6100}\; \; \; \; \; \; \; ...\left ( ii \right ) \end{aligned}[/latex]
From both equations,
[latex]\; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \; \frac{w}{Q}=5.748\times 10^{-4}[/latex]
Now for 99% efficiency plate area required,
[latex]0.99=1-e^{-5.748\times 10^{-4}\times A}[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; \; \; \; A=8011.78\: m^{2}[/latex]

The Fourier series of the function,
[latex]\begin{matrix} f(x) & =0 & -\pi \lt x \leq 0 \\ f(x) &=\pi-x & 0 \lt x \lt \pi \end{matrix} [/latex]

in the interval [latex][-\pi ,\pi ][/latex] is

[latex]f(x)=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{2}{\pi }\left [ \frac{\cos x}{1^{2}}+\frac{\cos 3x}{3^{2}}+\cdots\: \cdots \ \cdots \right ][/latex] [latex]+ \left [ \frac{\sin x}{1}+\frac{\sin 2x}{2}+\frac{\sin 3x}{3}+\cdots \: \cdots\: \cdot \right ][/latex]

The convergence of the above Fourier series at x = 0 gives
raw_source.solution:
The function is [latex]f(x)=0[/latex]
[latex] -p\lt x\leq 0 [/latex]
[latex] =p-x,\, 0 \lt x \lt \pi [/latex]
And Fourier series is,
[latex]f\left ( x \right )=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{2}{\pi }\left [ \frac{\cos x}{1^{2}}+\frac{\cos 3x}{3^{2}}+\frac{\cos 5x}{5^{2}}+... \right ]+\left [ \frac{\sin x}{1}+\frac{\sin 2x}{2}+\frac{\sin 3x}{3}+... \right ] ...\left ( i \right )[/latex]
At x=0, (a point of discontinuity), the fourier series converges to [latex]\frac{1}{2}\left [ f\left ( 0^{-1} \right )+f\left ( 0^{+} \right ) \right ][/latex]
where [latex]f\left ( 0^{-} \right )=\lim_{x\rightarrow 0}\left ( \pi -x \right )=\pi [/latex]
Hence, eq. (i), we get,
[latex] \frac{\pi }{2}=\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{2}{\pi }\left [ \frac{1}{1^{2}}+\frac{1}{3^{2}}+... \right ] [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \;\; \frac{1}{1}+\frac{1}{3^{2}}+\frac{1}{5^{2}}+...\frac{\pi ^{2}}{8}[/latex]

X and Y are two random independent events. It is known that [latex]P(X)=0.40[/latex] and 
[latex]P(X\cup Y^{C})=0.7[/latex]. Which one of the following is the value of [latex]P(X\cup Y)[/latex] ?
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\; \; \; \; P\left ( X\: \cup \: Y^{c} \right )=0.7[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; P\left ( X \right )+P\left ( Y^{c} \right )-P\left ( X \right )P\left ( Y^{c} \right )=0.7[/latex]
(Since X, Y are independent events)
[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; P\left ( X \right )+1-P\left ( Y \right )-P\left ( X \right )\left \{ 1-P\left ( Y \right ) \right \}=0[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; P\left ( X \right )-P\left ( X\: \cap \: Y \right )=0.3\; \; \; \; \; \; ...\left ( i \right )[/latex]
[latex]\; \; \; \; P\left ( X\: \cup \: Y \right )=P\left ( X \right )+P\left ( Y \right )-P\left ( X\: \cap \: Y \right )[/latex]
[latex]\; \; \; \; =0.4+0.3=0.7[/latex]

(ii) [latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow 0 y\rightarrow 0}\frac{xy}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\lim_{x\rightarrow 0}\left ( \frac{0}{x^{2}+0} \right )=0[/latex]
( i.e., put [latex]y=0[/latex] and then [latex]x=0[/latex])
(iii)[latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow 0 y\rightarrow 0}\frac{xy}{x^{2}+y^{2}}\lim_{x\rightarrow 0}\frac{x\left ( mx \right )}{x^{2}+m^{2}x^{2}}[/latex]
(i.e., put [latex]y=mx[/latex])
[latex] \lim_{x\rightarrow \infty }\left ( \frac{m}{1+m^{2}} \right )=\frac{m}{1+m^{2}}[/latex]
which depends on m.

If f(x) and g(x) are two probability density functions,
[latex]f(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix} \frac{x}{a}+1 & :-a\leq x \lt 0\\ -\frac{x}{a}+1 & :0\leq x\leq a\\ 0& : otherwise \end{matrix}\right.[/latex]

[latex]g(x)=\left\{\begin{matrix} -\frac{x}{a} & :-a\leq x \lt 0\\ \frac{x}{a} & :0\leq x\leq a\\ 0& : otherwise \end{matrix}\right.[/latex]
Which one of the following statements is true?
raw_source.solution:
Mean of f(x) is E(x)
[latex]=\int_{-a}^{0}x\left ( \frac{x}{a}+1 \right )dx+\int_{0}^{a}x\left ( \frac{-x}{a}+1 \right )dx[/latex]
[latex]=\left ( \frac{x^{3}}{3a}+\frac{x^{2}}{2} \right )_{-a}^{0}+\left ( \frac{-x^{3}}{3a}+\frac{x^{2}}{2} \right )_{0}^{a}=0[/latex]
Variance of f(x) is [latex]E\left ( x \right )^{2}-\left \{ E\left ( x \right )^{2} \right \}[/latex] where,
[latex]E\left ( x \right )^{2}=\int_{-a}^{0}x^{2}\left ( \frac{x}{a}+1 \right )dx+\int_{0}^{a}x^{2}\left ( \frac{-x}{a}+1 \right )dx[/latex]
[latex]=\left ( \frac{x^{4}}{4a}+\frac{x^{3}}{3} \right )_{-a}^{0}+\left ( \frac{-x^{4}}{4a}+\frac{x^{3}}{3} \right )_{0}^{a}=\frac{a^{3}}{6}[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; [/latex]Variance is [latex]\frac{a^{3}}{6}[/latex]
Next, mean of g(x) is E(x)
[latex]=\int_{a}^{0}s\left ( \frac{-x}{a} \right )dx+\int_{0}^{a}x\left ( \frac{x}{a} \right )dx=0[/latex]
Variance of g(x) is [latex]E\left ( x^{2} \right )-\left \{ E\left ( x \right )^{2} \right \}[/latex], where,
[latex]E\left ( x^{2} \right )=\int_{-a}^{0}x^{2}\left ( \frac{-x}{a} \right )dx+\int_{0}^{a}x^{2}\left ( \frac{x}{a} \right )dx=\frac{a^{3}}{2}[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; \; [/latex]Variance is [latex]\frac{a^{3}}{2}[/latex]
[latex]\therefore [/latex] Mean of f(x) and g(x) are same but variance of f(x) and g(x) are different.
options: Mean of f(x) and g(x) are same; Variance of f(x) and g(x) are same.
Mean of f(x) and g(x) are same; Variance of f(x) and g(x) are different.
Mean of f(x) and g(x) are different; Variance of f(x) and g(x) are same.
Mean of f(x) and g(x) are different; Variance of f(x) and g(x) are different.

raw_answer.option_text: Mean of f(x) and g(x) are same; Variance of f(x) and g(x) are different.

raw_source.text: The angle of intersection of the curves [latex]x^{2}=4y[/latex] and [latex]y^{2}=4x[/latex] at point (0, 0) is
raw_source.solution:
Given curve,
[latex] \begin{aligned} x^{2}&=4y \;\; ...(i)\\ y^{2}&=4y \;\;...(ii)\\ 2x&=4\frac{dy}{dx} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \left ( \frac{dy}{dx} \right )_{\left ( 0\,, 0 \right )}&=0=m_{1}\\ 2y\frac{dy}{dx}&=4 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \left ( \frac{dy}{dx} \right )_{\left ( 0\, ,0 \right )}&=\infty =m_{2}\\ \text{Let }m_{2}&=\frac{1}{{m}'} , \text{ where }{m}'=0 \\ \tan \theta &=\left | \frac{m_{1}-m_{2}}{1+m_{1}m_{2}} \right | \\&=\left | \frac{m_{1}{m}'-1}{{m}'+m_{1}}\right | \\&=\left | \frac{0-1}{0+0} \right |=\infty \\ \Rightarrow \;\; \theta &=\frac{\pi }{2}=90^{\circ}\end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The area between the parabola [latex]x^{2}=8y[/latex] and the straight line y=8 is ______.
raw_source.solution:
Parabola is [latex]x^{2}=8y[/latex]
[latex] y=\frac{x^{2}}{8}[/latex] and straight is [latex]y=0[/latex]
At the point of intersection, we have,
[latex] \frac{x^{2}}{8}=8 [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow x=-8,\, 8 \text{ and } y=8\geq y=\frac{x^{2}}{8} [/latex]
[latex] \therefore[/latex] Required area is [latex]\int_{x=-8}^{8}\left ( 8-\frac{x^{2}}{8} \right )dx [/latex]
[latex] =2\int_{0}^{8}\left ( 8-\frac{x^{2}}{8} \right )dx[/latex] ([latex]\because \;\; 8-\frac{x^{2}}{8}[/latex] is even function)
[latex]=2\left [ 8x-\frac{x^{3}}{24} \right ]_{0}^{8}=\frac{256}{3}=85.33[/latex] sq. units

raw_source.solution:

raw_source.text: An elastic isotropic body is in a hydrostatic state of stress as shown in the figure. For no change in the volume to occur, what should be its Poisson's ratio?
raw_source.solution:
Volumetric strain,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \epsilon_{\mathrm{v}}&=\left(\frac{\sigma_{x}+\sigma_{y}+\sigma_{z}}{3}\right)(1-2 \mu)\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\delta V}{V}&=\left(\frac{\sigma_{x}+\sigma_{y}+\sigma_{z}}{3}\right)(1-2 \mu) \\ \text{As }\quad \Delta V&=0 \\ \Rightarrow\text{ Either }\sigma_{x}&+\sigma_{y}+\sigma_{z}=0 or 1-2 \mu=0 \\ \Rightarrow \quad 1-2 \mu&=0 \\ \mu&=0.5 \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Properties of Metals, Stress and Strain

For the stress state (in MPa) shown in the figure, the major principal stress is 10 MPa.

The shear stress [latex]\tau[/latex] is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma_{x}+\sigma_{y}&=\sigma_{1}+\sigma_{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 5+5&=10+\sigma_{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \sigma_{2}&=0\\ \text { Now, } \quad \sigma_{1 / 2}&=\frac{\sigma_{x}+\sigma_{y}}{2} \pm \sqrt{\left(\frac{\sigma_{x}-\sigma_{y}}{2}\right)^{2}+\tau_{x y}^{2}} \\ \therefore \quad \sigma_{1}&=\frac{5+5}{2}+\sqrt{\left(\frac{5-5}{2}\right)^{2}+\tau_{x y}^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 10&=5+\tau_{x y} \\ \therefore \quad \tau_{x y}&=5 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Given data:

Consider joint 'S.


[latex] \begin{aligned} & F_{\mathrm{SO}}=F_{\mathrm{SR}} \\ 2 F_{\mathrm{SQ}} \cos 45^{\circ}=& \mathrm{W} \\ \Rightarrow \quad F_{\mathrm{SQ}}=& \frac{W}{2} \times \sqrt{2}=\frac{W}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \therefore \quad & F_{\mathrm{SO}}=\frac{W}{\sqrt{2}} \end{aligned} [/latex]
As the truss is symmetrical,
[latex] \therefore \quad F_{\mathrm{OP}}=F_{\mathrm{PR}}=\frac{W}{\sqrt{2}} \qquad \text{(Tensile)}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 450 mm long plain concrete prism is subjected to the concentrated vertical loads as shown in the figure. Cross section of the prism is given as 150 mm x 150 mm. Considering linear stress distribution across the cross-section, the modulus of rupture (expressed in MPa) is _______ .

[latex]\begin{aligned} -2M_{P}\theta -2M_{P}\theta -2M_{P}\theta -M_{P}\theta +P\left ( \frac{2L}{3}\theta \right )&=0 \\ 4M_{P}\theta +3M_{P}\phi &=\frac{2PL}{3}\theta \\ 8M_{P}\phi +3M_{P}\phi &=\frac{4PL}{3}\phi \\ 11M_{P}&=\frac{4P_{u}L}{3}\phi \\ P_{u}&=\frac{33}{4}\frac{M_{P}}{L} \\ \therefore \;\; P_{u}&=8.25\frac{M_{P}}{L} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Mechanism 2:



[latex]\begin{aligned} 2M_{P}\theta +M_{P}\theta +M_{P}\theta +M_{P}\theta &=P\left ( \frac{2L}{3} \right ) \\ 5M_{P}&=\frac{2PL}{3} \\ P_{u}&=\frac{15M_{P}}{2L} \\ \therefore \;\; P_{u}&=7.5\frac{M_{P}}{L} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The seepage occurring through an earthen dam is represented by a flow net comprising of 10 equipotential drops and 20 flow channels. The coefficient of permeability of the soil is 3 mm/min and the head loss is 5 m. The rate of seepage (expressed in [latex]cm^{3}/s[/latex] per m length of the dam) through the earthen dam is ___.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} q&=\frac{KH.N_{f}}{N_{d}}\\ K&=\frac{3 \mathrm{mm}}{\mathrm{min}}=\frac{3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}}{60} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}\\ H&=5 \mathrm{m}, N_{\mathrm{f}}=20, \quad N_{\mathrm{d}}=10\\ q&=\frac{3 \times 10^{-3}}{60} \times 5 \times \frac{20}{10} \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{sec} \text { per } \mathrm{m} \text { length of dam }\\ q&=\frac{3 \times 10^{-3} \times 5 \times 20}{60 \times 10} \times 10^{6} \mathrm{cm}^{3} / \mathrm{sec} \text { per } \mathrm{m} \text { length of dam }\\ q&=500 \mathrm{cm}^{3} / \mathrm{sec} \text { per } \mathrm{m} \text { length of } \mathrm{dam} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The soil profile at a site consists of a 5 m thick sand layer underlain by a [latex]c-\phi[/latex] soil as shown in figure. The water table is found 1 m below the ground level. The entire soil mass is retained by a concrete retaining wall and is in the active state. The back of the wall is smooth and vertical. The total active earth pressure (expressed in [latex]kN/m^{2}[/latex] ) at point A as per Rankine's theory is _________.
raw_source.solution:
In [latex]\mathrm{c}-\phi[/latex] soil
Earth pressure
[latex] \begin{array}{l} p_{\mathrm{a}}=k_{\mathrm{a}} \sigma_{\mathrm{v}}-2 \mathrm{c} \sqrt{\mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{a}}} \\ k_{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{1-\sin \phi}{1+\sin \phi}=\frac{1-\sin 24}{1+\sin 24}=0.4217 \end{array}[/latex]
Note: Below water table, water pressure will not be multiplied by [latex] k_{\mathrm{a}} [/latex]
at point A
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \sigma_{v}=1 \times \gamma_{b}+4 \gamma_{\text {sat }}+3 \gamma_{\text {sat }} \\ \sigma_{v}=1 \times \gamma_{b}+\left(4 \times \gamma^{\prime}+4 \times \gamma_{w}\right)+\left(3 \gamma^{\prime}+3 \gamma_{w}\right) \\ \sigma_{v}=\left(1 \times \gamma_{b}+4 \gamma^{\prime}+3 \gamma^{\prime}\right)+\left(4 \gamma_{w}+3 \gamma_{w}\right) \end{array}[/latex]
Earth Pressure at 'A'
[latex] \begin{array}{l} p_{\mathrm{a}}=k_{\mathrm{a}} \sigma_{v}-2 c \sqrt{k_{\mathrm{a}}} \\ =k_{a}\left[\gamma_{b}+4 \gamma^{\prime}+3 \gamma^{\prime}\right]+4 \gamma_{w}+3 \gamma_{w}-2 \times c^{\prime} \sqrt{k_{a}} \\ =0.4217[16.5+4(19-9.81)+3(18.5-9.81)] \\ +7 \times 9.81-2 \times 25 \times \sqrt{0.4217} \\ p_{\mathrm{a}}=69.65 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{array}[/latex]

OMC-MP and MDD-MP denote the optimum moisture content and maximum dry density obtained from the modified Proctor compaction test, respectively. Which one of the following is correct?

raw_source.text: Water flows from P to Q through two soil samples, Soil 1 and Soil 2, having cross sectional area of 80[latex]cm^2[/latex] as shown in the figure. Over a period of 15 minutes, 200 ml of water was observed to pass through any cross section. The flow conditions can be assumed to be steady state. If the coefficient of permeability of Soil 1 is 0.02 mm/s, the coefficient of permeability of Soil 2 (expressed in mm/s) would be ____
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Discharge } &=\frac{200 \mathrm{ml}}{15 \mathrm{min}} \\ &=\frac{200 \mathrm{cm}^{3}}{15 \times 60 \mathrm{sec}}=\frac{200 \times 10^{3}}{900} \frac{\mathrm{mm}^{3}}{\mathrm{sec}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
As per Darcy's Law,
[latex] \begin{aligned} q &=k_{a v g} i A \\ k_{a v g} &=\frac{\Sigma z_{i}}{\Sigma \frac{z_{i}}{k_{i}}}\\ &(\because\text{ flow is normal to bedding plane})\\ k_{\text {avg }}&=\frac{150+150}{\frac{150}{0.02}+\frac{150}{k}}\\ i&=\frac{\text { Head difference }}{\text { length }}=\frac{600-300}{300}=1 \\ A&=80 \mathrm{cm}^{2}=80 \times 10^{2} \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ q&=\left[\frac{150+150}{\frac{150}{0.02}+\frac{150}{k}}+\right] \times 1 \times 80 \times 10^{2} \\ &=\frac{200 \times 10^{3}}{900} \\ k&=0.045 \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A 4 m wide strip footing is founded at a depth of 1.5 m below the ground surface in a [latex]c-\phi[/latex] soil as shown in the figure. The water table is at a depth of 5.5 m below ground surface. The soil properties are: [latex]{c}'=35\: kN/m^{2},{\phi }'=28.63^{\circ}, [/latex] [latex]\gamma _{sat}=19\: kN/m^{3}, \; \gamma _{bulk}=17\:kN/m^{3}[/latex] and [latex] \gamma _{w}=9.81kN/m^{3}[/latex]. The values of bearing capacity factors for different [latex]{\phi }'[/latex] are given below.

Using Terzaghi's bearing capacity equation and a factor of safety [latex]F_{s}=2.5[/latex], the net safe bearing capacity (expressed in [latex]kN/m^{2}[/latex] ) for local shear failure of the soil is ________.
raw_source.solution:
Local shear failure is occuring hence modified c
and [latex]\phi[/latex] should be used
[latex] \begin{aligned} c_{m} &=\frac{2}{3} c=\frac{2}{3} \times 35=23.33 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \tan \phi_{m} &=\frac{2}{3} \tan \phi=\frac{2}{3} \tan 28.63 \\ \phi_{m} &=20^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
for [latex]\quad \phi_{m}=20^{\circ}, N_{c}=17.7, N_{\mathrm{q}}=7.4, N_{\gamma}=5.0 [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow[/latex] Water table is at
[latex] D_{t}+B=1.5+4=5.5 \mathrm{m} [/latex] hence no effect on
bearing capacity
[latex] \Rightarrow [/latex] As per Terzaghi for strip footing
[latex] \begin{aligned} a_{u} &=c N_{c}+8 D_{f} N_{q}+0.5 B \gamma N_{\gamma} \\ q_{u} &=\frac{2}{3} \times 35 \times 17.7+17+1.5 \times 7.4+0.5 \\ & \times 4 \times 17 \times 5 \\ q_{u} &=771.7 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ q_{\mathrm{nu}} &=q_{u}-\bar{\sigma}=q_{u}-\gamma D_{f}=771.7-17 \times 1.5 \\ q_{n} &=746.2 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Net safe bearing capacity
[latex] q_{n s}=\frac{q_{n u}}{F}=\frac{746.2}{2.5}=298.48 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}[/latex]

A water jet of 20 mm diameter having a velocity of 10 m/s strikes the plate at its mid-point, at an angle of [latex]30^{\circ}[/latex] with the vertical. Consider g as [latex]9.81\: m/s^{2}[/latex] and neglect the self-weight of the plate. The force F (expressed in N) required to keep the plate in its vertical position is _______________

Taking mornent about hinge
[latex] \begin{array}{r} F_{x} \times \frac{0.2}{2}=F \times 02 \\ F=7.85 \mathrm{N} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 3m wide rectangular channel carries a flow of [latex]6\: m^{3}/s[/latex] . The depth of flow at a section P is 0.5 m. A flat-topped hump is to be placed at the downstream of the section P. Assume negligible energy loss between section P and hump, and consider g as [latex]9.81\: m/s^{2}[/latex] . The maximum height of the hump (expressed in m) which will not change the depth of flow at section P is ____________
raw_source.solution:
The maximum hump [latex](\Delta Z)[/latex] that can be provided
is given by
[latex] \begin{aligned} y+\frac{Q^{2}}{2 g A^{2}} =&\Delta Z_{\text {hump }}+\frac{3}{2} y_{c} \\ \text{Here}\quad A =&3 \times 0.5=1.5 \mathrm{m}^{2}\\ y_{c}=&\left(\frac{Q^{2}}{g B^{2}}\right)^{1 / 3}=\left(\frac{6^{2}}{9.81 \times 3^{2}}\right)^{1 / 3} \\ =& 0.7415 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 0.5+\frac{6^{2}}{2 \times 9.81 \times 1.5^{2}}=\Delta Z_{\text {hump }}+\frac{3}{2} \times 0.7415 \\ \Rightarrow \quad \Delta Z_{\text {hump }}=0.20 \mathrm{m} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A penstock of 1 m diameter and 5 km length is used to supply water from a reservoir to an impulse turbine. A nozzle of 15 cm diameter is fixed at the end of the penstock. The elevation difference between the turbine and water level in the reservoir is 500 m. Consider the head loss due to friction as 5% of the velocity head available at the jet. Assume unit weight of water = [latex]10\: kN/m^{3}[/latex] and acceleration due to gravity (g)=[latex]10\: m/s^{2}[/latex]. If the overall efficiency 80%, power generated (expressed in kW and rounded to nearest integer) is ___________
raw_source.solution:
Apply energy equaiton at the free surlace of
reservior and exit of nozzle
[latex] \begin{aligned} 500&=\text{Head loss } \frac{v_{1}^{2}}{2 g}\\ 500&=0.05 \frac{v_{1}^{2}}{2 g}+\frac{v_{1}^{2}}{2 g}\\ \sqrt{\frac{2 \times 10 \times 500}{1.05}}&=v_{1} \\ V_{1}&=97.59 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{sec}\\ \text{Water Power WP }\\ &=\frac{1}{2} m v_{1}^{2} \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left(10^{2}\right) \times \frac{\pi}{4}(0.15)^{2}(9759) \\ &=8212178 \mathrm{kW} \\ \text{Now,}\quad \eta_{0}&=\frac{\text { Shaft power }(\$ P)}{W P} \\ 08&=\frac{S P}{8212178} \\ S P&=6569.74 \mathrm{kW} \\ &\simeq 6570 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A tracer takes 100 days to travel from Well-1 to Well-2 which are 100 m apart. The elevation of water surface in Well-2 is 3m below that in Well-1. Assuming porosity equal to 15%, the coefficient of permeability (expressed in m/day) is
raw_source.solution:
Seepage velocity,
[latex] \begin{aligned} V_{s}&=\frac{v}{n}=\frac{\text { distance }}{\text { time }}\\ \text{as per Darcy},\\ v &=k i \\ \frac{k i}{n} &=\frac{100 \mathrm{m}}{100 \mathrm{days}} \\ i &=\frac{\text { head difference }}{\text { length }}=\frac{3}{100} \\ \frac{k \times 3}{0.15 \times 100} &=\frac{100}{100} \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{day} \\ k &=5 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{day} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Source of Water Supply, Distribution System and Well Hydraulics

raw_source.text:
A sample of water has been analyzed for common ions and results are presented in the form of a bar diagram as shown.

The non-carbonate hardness (expressed in mg/L as [latex]CaCO_{3}[/latex] ) of the sample is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} &=2.65 \mathrm{meq} / \mathrm{l} \\ \mathrm{Mg}^{2+} &=1.45 \mathrm{meq} / 1 \\ \mathrm{Na}^{+} &=2.25 \mathrm{meq} / l \\ \mathrm{K}^{+} &=0.5 \mathrm{meq} / \mathrm{l} \\ \mathrm{HCO}_{3} &=3.3 \mathrm{meq} / \mathrm{l} \\ \mathrm{SO}_{4}^{2-} &=0.6 \mathrm{meq} / \mathrm{l} \\ \mathrm{Cl}^{-} &=2.85 \mathrm{meq} / \mathrm{l} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Hardness is due to multivalent metallic cations,
[latex] \mathrm{Ca}^{2+} and \mathrm{Mg}^{2+} [/latex]
Total hardness [latex]\left(\mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{l}\text{ as }\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}\right)[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=(\text{Total }meq/l) \times (\text{eq. weight of }\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}\text{ in }\mathrm{mg} )\\ &=(2.65+1.45) \times 50 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{l} \text { as } \mathrm{CaCO}_{3} \\ &=205 \mathrm{mg} / l \text { as } \mathrm{CaCO}_{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Alkalinity is due to the presence of [latex]\mathrm{HCO}_{3}^{-}[/latex] in this case,
Alkalinity [latex]\left(\mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{l}\right. as \left.\mathrm{CaCO}_{3}\right) [/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} =3.3 \times 50 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{l} \text { as } \mathrm{CaCO}_{3} \\ =165 \mathrm{mg} / \mathrm{l} \text { as } \mathrm{CaCO}_{3} \end{array}[/latex]
Now, Carbonate Hardness
= Min { Total Hardness, Alkalinity }
[latex] =165 \mathrm{mg} / l[/latex]
[latex] \therefore [/latex] Non-carbonate hardness
= Total Hardness - Carbonate Hardness
[latex] =205-165=40 \mathrm{mg} / l as \mathrm{CaCO}_{3}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A noise meter located at a distance of 30 m from a point source recorded 74 dB . The reading at a distance of 60 m from the point source would be _________
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} L_{2} &=L_{1}-\left | 20\log \left ( \frac{R_{2}}{R_{1}} \right ) \right | \\ &=74-\left | 20\log 0.5 \right | \\ &=74-6.02 \\ &=74-20\log 0.5 \\ &= 67.98\: dB \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: For a wastewater sample, the three-day biochemical oxygen demand at incubation temperature of [latex]20\: ^{\circ}C \; (BOD_{3days,20{\circ}C})[/latex], is estimated as 200 mg/L. Taking the value of the first order BOD reaction rate constant as [latex]0.22\: day^{-1}[/latex], the five-day BOD (expressed in mg/L) of the wastewater at incubation temperature of  [latex]20\: ^{\circ}C[/latex] [latex](BOD_{5days,20{\circ}C})[/latex] would be ___________
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} BOD_{5} &=L_{0}\left ( 1-e^{-0.22\times 5} \right ) \\ BOD_{3}&=L_{0}\left ( 1-e^{-0.22\times 3} \right ) \end{aligned}[/latex]
From equation (i) and (ii), we get,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{BOD_{5}}{BOD_{3}} &=\frac{\left ( 1-e^{-0.22\times 5} \right )}{\left ( 1-e^{-0.22\times 3} \right )} \\ BOD_{5} &=200\times \frac{0.667}{0.483} \\ &=200\times 1.38 \\ &=276.19\: mg/l \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The critical flow ratios for a three-phase signal are found to be 0.30, 0.25, and 0.25. The total time lost in the cycle is 10 s. Pedestrian crossings at this junction are not significant. The respective Green times (expressed in seconds and rounded off to the nearest integer) for the three phases are
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} Y &=y_{1}+y_{2}+y_{3} \\ &=0.30+0.25+0.25 \\ &=0.80 \end{aligned}[/latex]
NowTotal lost time,
L=10 sec (given)
[latex] \therefore \quad[/latex] Optimum cycle time.
[latex] \begin{aligned} C_{0} &=\frac{1.5 L+5}{1-Y} \\ C_{0} &=\frac{(1.5 \times 10)+5}{1-0.80}=\frac{15+5}{0.20}=\frac{20}{0.2} \\ &=100 \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Now green times are calculated by,
[latex] \begin{aligned} G_{1} &=\frac{y_{1}}{y}\left(C_{0}-L\right)=\frac{0.30}{0.80}(100-10) \\ &=33.75 \simeq 34 \mathrm{sec} \\ G_{2} &=\frac{y_{2}}{y}\left(C_{0}-L\right)=\frac{0.25}{0.80}(100-10) \\ &=28.11 \simeq 28 \mathrm{sec} \\ G_{3} &=\frac{y_{3}}{y}\left(C_{0}-L\right)=\frac{0.25}{0.80}(100-10) \\ &=28.11 \simeq 28 \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A motorist travelling at 100 km/h on a highway needs to take the next exit, which has a speed limit of 50 km/h. The section of the roadway before the ramp entry has a downgrade of 3% and coefficient of friction (f) is 0.35. In order to enter the ramp at the maximum allowable speed limit, the braking distance (expressed in m) from the exit ramp is________
raw_source.solution:
Total energy lost between point (1) and (2)
= Work done by frictional force
[latex] \frac{1}{2} m v_{1}^{2}-\frac{1}{2} m v_{2}^{2}+m g \times 0.03 s=f \times(m g) \times s [/latex]
[latex] \frac{(0.278 \times 100)^{2}}{2}-\frac{(0.278 \times 50)^{2}}{2}+9.81 \times 0.03 \times s [/latex]
[latex] =0.35 \times 9.81 \times s [/latex]
[latex] 289.815=3.1392 \mathrm{s} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad s=92.32 \mathrm{m}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A tall tower was photographed from an elevation of 700 m above the datum. raw_source.text: Consider the equation [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}=3t^{2}+1[/latex] with u=0 at t=0. This is numerically solved by using the forward Euler method with a step size [latex]\Delta t= 2[/latex]. The absolute error in the solution at the end of the first time step is_________
raw_source.solution:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}&=3t^{2}+1 \\ f\left ( u,\: t \right )&=3t^{2}+1 \\ u_{0}&=0 \\ t_{0}&=0 \\ \Delta t&=2\\ &\text{By Euler's method} \\ u_{1}&=u_{0}+hf\left ( u_{0}t_{0} \right ) & t_{1}&=t_{0}+h \\ &=u_{0}+h\left ( 3t^{2}_{0}+1 \right ) & &=0+2 \\ &=0+2\left ( 3\left ( 0 \right )^{2}+1 \right ) & &=2 \\ &=2 \end{aligned}[/latex]
After first iteration u=0 when t=2,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}&=3t^{2}+1 \\ du&=\left ( 3t^{2}+1 \right )dt \\ \int du&=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( 3t^{2}+1 \right )dt \\ u&=\left.\begin{matrix} \left ( 3\frac{t^{3}}{3}+t \right ) \end{matrix}\right|_{0}^{2} \\ &=8+2=10 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Absolute error = Exact value - approx value
[latex]=10-2 =8[/latex]
