raw_source.text:
Consider the following second-order differential equation:
[latex]{y}''-4y'+3y=2t-3t^{2}[/latex]
The particular solution of the differential equations is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} {y}''-4{y}'+3y&=2t-3t^{2} \\ \left ( D^{2}-4D+3 \right )y&=2t-3t^{2} \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} P.I.&=\frac{1}{D^{2}-4D+3}\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \\ &=\frac{1}{\left ( 1-D \right )\left ( 3-D \right )}\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \\ &=\left ( \frac{1/2}{1-d}-\frac{1/2}{3-D} \right )\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left ( 1-D \right )^{-1}\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \\ &-\frac{1}{6}\left ( 1-\frac{D}{3} \right )^{-1}\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left ( 1+D+D^{2} \right )\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \\ &\times \frac{1}{6}\left ( 1+\frac{D}{3}+\frac{D^{2}}{9} \right )\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left ( 2t-3t^{2}+D\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) +D^{2}\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \right ) \\ &-\frac{1}{6}\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right ) \\ & +\frac{D\left ( 2t-3t^{2} \right )}{3}+\frac{D^{2}}{9}\left (2t-3t^{2} \right) \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left [ 2t-3t^{2}+2-6t-6 \right ]- \\ &\frac{1}{6}\left [ 2t-3t^{2}+\frac{2-6t}{3}+\frac{-6}{9} \right ] \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\left ( -4-4t-3t^{2} \right )-\frac{1}{6}\left ( -3t^{2} \right ) \\ &=-2-2t-t^{2}\end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Group I contains three broad classes of irrigation supply canal outlets. Group II presents hydraulic performance attributes.

The correct match of the items in Group I with the items in Group II is
raw_source.solution:
Non-modular outlet :These are the outlets whose discharge depends on the difference in water levels in the distributing channel and the water < course. The discharge of such outlets, therefore, varies with the variation of the water levels in the distributing channel and the water course.
Semi-modular outlet : These are the outlets whose discharge varies with the variation of the water level in the distribution channel but it is independent of the water level in the water course, so long as the minimum working head required for their working is available.
Modular outlet : These are the outlets whose discharge is independent of the water levels in the distributing channel and the water course, within reasonable working limits. In other words modular outlets maintain a constant discharge irrespective of variation of the water levels in the distributing channel and the water course.

raw_source.text: Consider the equation [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}=3t^{2}+1[/latex] with u=0 at t=0. This is numerically solved by using the forward Euler method with a step size [latex]\Delta t= 2[/latex]. The absolute error in the solution at the end of the first time step is_________
raw_source.solution:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}&=3t^{2}+1 \\ f\left ( u,\: t \right )&=3t^{2}+1 \\ u_{0}&=0 \\ t_{0}&=0 \\ \Delta t&=2\\ &\text{By Euler's method} \\ u_{1}&=u_{0}+hf\left ( u_{0}t_{0} \right ) & t_{1}&=t_{0}+h \\ &=u_{0}+h\left ( 3t^{2}_{0}+1 \right ) & &=0+2 \\ &=0+2\left ( 3\left ( 0 \right )^{2}+1 \right ) & &=2 \\ &=2 \end{aligned}[/latex]
After first iteration u=0 when t=2,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{\mathrm{d} u}{\mathrm{d} t}&=3t^{2}+1 \\ du&=\left ( 3t^{2}+1 \right )dt \\ \int du&=\int_{0}^{2}\left ( 3t^{2}+1 \right )dt \\ u&=\left.\begin{matrix} \left ( 3\frac{t^{3}}{3}+t \right ) \end{matrix}\right|_{0}^{2} \\ &=8+2=10 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Absolute error = Exact value - approx value
[latex]=10-2 =8[/latex]

raw_source.text: A pre-tensioned rectangular concrete beam 150 mm wide and 300 mm depth is prestressed with three straight tendons, each having a cross-sectional area of 50 [latex]mm^{2}[/latex], to an initial stress of 1200 [latex]N / mm^{2}[/latex]. The tendons are located at 100 mm from the soffit of the beam. If the modular ratio is 6, the loss of prestressing force (in kN, up to one decimal place) due to the elastic deformation of concrete only is ______
raw_source.solution:
Prestressing force,
[latex] \begin{aligned} P&=3 \times 50 \times 1200=180000 \mathrm{N} \\ e&=\left(\frac{D}{2}-100\right)=\left(\frac{300}{2}-100\right)=50 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Stress in concrete at the location of steel
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{P}{A}+\frac{P \cdot e}{I} e\\ &=\frac{180000}{150 \times 300}+\frac{180000 \times 50^{2}}{\left(\frac{150 \times 300^{3}}{12}\right)} \\ &=4.0+1.33=5.333 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Loss of stress
[latex] =m \times f_{c}=6 \times 5.3333=32 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2}[/latex]
Loss of prestressing force
[latex] =\frac{3 \times 50 \times 32}{1000} \mathrm{kN}=4.8 \mathrm{kN}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider two axially loaded columns, namely, 1 and 2, made of a linear elastic material with Young's modulus [latex]2 \times 10^{5}[/latex]  MPa, square cross- section with side 10 mm, and length 1 m. For Column 1, one end is fixed and the other end is free. For Column 2, one end is fixed and the other end is pinned. Based on the Euler's theory, the ratio (up to one decimal place) of the buckling load of Column 2 to the buckling load of Column 1 is ________
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} P_{c r 1}&=\frac{\pi^{2} E \cdot I}{(2 l)^{2}}=\frac{\pi^{2} E I}{4 l^{2}} \\ P_{c r 2}&=\frac{\pi^{2} E \cdot I}{\left(\frac{l}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2}}=\frac{2 \pi^{2} E I}{l^{2}}\\ \therefore \text{Required ratio }&=\frac{P_{C r 2}}{P_{c r 1}}=\frac{\frac{2 \pi^{2} E I}{l^{2}}}{\frac{\pi^{2} E I}{4 l^{2}}}=8 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A sluice gate used to control the flow in a horizontal channel of unit width is shown in the figure.

It is observed that the depth of flow is 1.0 m upstream of the gate, while the depth is 0.2 m downstream of the gate. Assuming a smooth flow transition across the sluice gate, i.e., without any energy loss, and the acceleration due to gravity as 10 [latex] m/s^{2}[/latex] the discharge (in [latex] m^{3}/ s [/latex], up to two decimal places) passing under the sluice gate is_____
raw_source.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's energy balance equation
[latex] \begin{aligned} y_{1}+\frac{Q^{2}}{2 g A_{1}^{2}}&=y_{2}+\frac{Q^{2}}{2 g A_{2}^{2}}\\ \text{Given }\quad y_{1}=1 \mathrm{m}, b&=1 \mathrm{m}, \quad y_{2}=0.2 \\ \Rightarrow 1+\frac{q^{2} \times 1^{2}}{2 g(1 \times 1)^{2}}&=0.2+\frac{q^{2} \times 1^{2}}{2 g \times(0.2 \times 1)^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.8 &=\frac{q^{2}}{2 g}\left(\frac{1}{(0.2)^{2}}-1\right) \\ 0.8 &=\frac{q^{2}}{20} \times 24 \\ q &=0.816 \mathrm{m}^{2} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Water flows through a 90[latex]^{\circ}[/latex] bend in a horizontal plane as depicted in the figure.

A pressure of 140 kPa is measured at section 1-1. The inlet diameter marked at section 1-1 is [latex]\frac{27}{\sqrt{\pi }}cm[/latex], while the nozzle diameter marked at section 2-2 is [latex]\frac{14}{\sqrt{\pi }}cm[/latex]. Assume the following:

(i) Acceleration due to gravity = 10 [latex] m/s^{2} [/latex]
(ii) Weights of both the bent pipe segment as well as water are negligible.
(iii) Friction across the bend is negligible.

The magnitude of the force (in kN, up to two decimal places) that would be required to hold the pipe section is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} P_{1} A_{1} &=F_{x} \\ F_{x} &=\left(140 \times 10^{3}\right)\left[\frac{\pi}{4}\left(\frac{0.27}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^{2}\right] \\ &=2551.5 \mathrm{N}\\ F_{y} &=P_{2} A_{2} \\ &=\left(1.013 \times 10^{5}\right)\left[\frac{\pi}{4}\left(\frac{0.14}{\sqrt{\pi}}\right)^{2}\right] \\ &=49637 \mathrm{N} \\ \text { Resultant force } &=\sqrt{F_{x}^{2}+F_{y}^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{(2551.5)^{2}+(49637)^{2}} \\ &=259933 \mathrm{N} \\ &=2.60 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A consolidated undrained [latex]\bar{CU}[/latex] triaxial compression test is conducted on a normally consolidated clay at a confining pressure of 100 kPa. The deviator stress at failure is 80 kPa, and the pore-water pressure measured at failure is 50 kPa. The effective angle of internalfriction (in degrees, up to one decimal place) of the soil is _________
raw_source.solution:
CU test is conducted.
[latex] \begin{aligned} \sigma_{3}= 100 &\mathrm{kPa}, \sigma_{a}=80 \mathrm{kPa}, u=50 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \sigma_{1}&=\sigma_{3}+\sigma_{d} =100+80=180 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \bar{\sigma}_{1}&=\sigma_{1}-u= 180-50=130 \mathrm{kPa}\\ \bar{\sigma}_{3}&=\sigma_{3}-u=100-50=50 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \bar{\sigma}_{1}&=\bar{\sigma}_{3} \tan ^{2}\left(45+\frac{\phi^{\prime}}{2}\right)+2 C^{\prime} \tan \left(45+\frac{\phi^{\prime}}{2}\right) \\ \text{Assume }\quad C^{\prime}&=0 \\ \bar{\sigma}_{1}&=\bar{\sigma}_{3} \tan ^{2}\left(45+\frac{\phi^{\prime}}{2}\right) \\ 130&=50 \tan ^{2}\left(45+\frac{\phi^{\prime}}{2}\right) \\ \phi^{\prime}&=26.4^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Two identical concrete piles having the plan dimensions 50 cm x 50 cm are driven into a homogeneous sandy layer as shown in the figures. Consider the bearing capacity factor [latex]N_{q}[/latex], for [latex]\phi =30^{\circ}[/latex] as 24

If [latex]Q_{P1}[/latex] and [latex]Q_{P2}[/latex] represent the ultimate point bearing resistance of the piles under dry and submerged conditions, respectively, which one of the following statements is correct?
raw_source.solution:
The point bearing resistance of piles in sandy soils
[latex]Q_P=A_b\ \cdot \sigma '_v \cdot N_q[/latex]
As the area at base [latex](A_b)[/latex] and [latex]N_q[/latex] are same for both the piles given, [latex]Q_P \propto \sigma '_v[/latex]
For dry sand condition, [latex]\sigma '_v=\sigma _v=20 \times \gamma[/latex]
For submerged condition, [latex]\sigma '_v=20 \times \gamma '[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Since, } \gamma '&= \frac{1}{2} \gamma \\ \therefore \;\; QP_2&\approx \frac{1}{2} QP_1\\ QP_1& \approx QP_2 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Therefore, [latex]QP_1 \gt QP_2[/latex] by about 100%.

raw_source.text:
Following are the statements related to the stress paths in a triaxial testing of soils:
P. If [latex]\sigma _{1}=\sigma _{3}[/latex] , the stress point lies at the origin of the p-q plot.
Q. If, [latex]\sigma _{1}=\sigma _{3}[/latex] the stress point lies on the p-axis of the p-q plot.
R. If [latex]\sigma _{1} \gt \sigma _{3}[/latex] , both the stress points p and q are positive.
For the above statements, the correct combination is
raw_source.solution:
On stress path in terms of p-q plot
[latex] \begin{aligned} p=\frac{\sigma_{1}+\sigma_{3}}{2} \\ q=\frac{\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{3}}{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
If [latex]\sigma_{1}=\sigma_{3}[/latex] then [latex]q=0[/latex] and [latex]p \neq 0[/latex] hence point does not lie at origin, point will lies on the p-axis.
If [latex]\sigma_{1}>\sigma_{3}[/latex], both the stress point will be positive.
options: P - False; Q - True; R - True
P - False; Q - True; R - True
P - False; Q - True; R - False
P - True; Q - False; R - False

raw_answer.option_text: P - False; Q - True; R - True

raw_source.text:
Two cars P and Q are moving in a racing track continuously for two hour. Assume that no other vehicles are using the track during this time. The expressions relating the distance travelled d (in km) and time t (in hour) for both the vehicles are given as

P: [latex]d=60t[/latex]
Q: [latex]d=60t^{2}[/latex]

Within the first one hour, the maximum space headway would be
raw_source.solution:
Space headway,
[latex] \begin{aligned} S &=60 t-60 t^{2} \\ \frac{d S}{d t} &=60-120 t=0 \\ t &=0.5 \mathrm{hr}=30 \text { minutes } \\ \frac{d^{2} S}{d t^{2}} &=-120 \times 0 \text { (Maxima) } \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore
[/latex] Maximum space head,
[latex] \begin{aligned} S_{\max } &=60 \times 0.5-60 \times(0.5)^{2} \\ &=15 \mathrm{km} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
For the construction of a highway. A cut is to be made as shown in the figure.

The soil exhibits [latex]c'=20kPa,\; \; \phi '=18^{\circ}[/latex] and the undrained shear strength = 80 kPa. The unit weight of water is 9.81[latex]kN/m^{3}[/latex]. The unit weights of the soil above and below the ground water table are 18 and 20 [latex]kN/m^{3}[/latex], respectively. If the shear stress at Point A is 50 kPa, the factors of safety against the shear failure at this point, considering the undrained and drained conditions, respectively, would be
raw_source.solution:
Drained parameters:
[latex] c^{\prime}=20 \mathrm{kPa}, \phi^{\prime}=18^{\circ}[/latex]
Undrained shear strength.
[latex] S=80 \mathrm{kPa}[/latex]
Normal stress at point A.
[latex] \begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{n} &=\sigma_{n}-u=2 \times \gamma_{b}+4 \gamma \\ \bar{\sigma}_{n} &=2 \times 18+4(20-981) \\ &=76.76 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Shear stress at point A=50kPa
FOS under undrained condition
[latex] =\frac{\text { Shear strength }}{\text { Sthear stress }}=\frac{80}{50}=1.6[/latex]
FOS in drained condition
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{c+\bar{\sigma}_{n} \tan \phi^{\prime}}{\tau} \\ &=\frac{20+76.76 \tan 18^{\circ}}{50}=0.9788 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Two towers A and B, standing vertically on a horizontal ground, appear in a vertical aerial photograph as shown in the figure.

The length of the image of the tower A on the photograph is1.5 cm and of the tower B is 2.0 cm. The distance of the top the tower A (as shown by the arrowhead) is 4.0 cm and the distance of the top of the tower B is 6.0 cm, as measured form the principal point p of the photograph. If the height of the tower B is 80 m, the height (in meters) of the tower A is_____
raw_source.solution:
For Tower A:
Reliet displacement,
[latex] \begin{array}{l} d_{A}=1.5 \mathrm{cm} \\ r_{A}=4 \mathrm{cm} \\ h_{A}=? \end{array}[/latex]
For Tower B:
Relier displacement.
[latex] \begin{array}{l} d_{B}=2.0 \mathrm{cm} \\ r_{B}=6 \mathrm{cm} \\ h_{B}=80\mathrm{m} \end{array}[/latex]
Reliet displacement.
[latex] \begin{aligned} D&=\frac{h.r}{\left(H-h_{\text{avg}} \right )}\\ \text{For A:}d_{A}&=\frac{h_{A}.r_{A}}{\left(H-h_{\text{avg}} \right )}\\ 1.5&=\frac{h_{A}\times 4}{240}\\ h_{A}&=90m\\ \text{For B: }d_{B}&=\frac{h_{B}.r_{B}}{\left(H-h_{\text{avg}} \right )}\\ \Rightarrow \quad 2&=\frac{80\times 6}{\left(H-h_{\text{avg}} \right )}\\ \Rightarrow \left(H-h_{\text{avg}} \right )&=240m \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Remote Sensing, GIS, GPS and Photogrammetry

raw_source.text: A hollow circular shaft has an outer diameter of 100 mm and inner diameter of 50 mm. If the allowable shear stress is 125 MPa, the maximum torque (in kN-m) that the shaft can resist is____
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \frac{T}{I_{p}}&=\frac{\tau}{r} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \tau&=\frac{T}{Z_{p}}=\frac{T}{\frac{\pi\left(D^{4}-d^{4}\right)}{16 \times D}}=\frac{16 T}{\frac{\pi}{D}\left(D^{4}-d^{4}\right)} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \tau&=\frac{16 T}{\pi D^{3}\left[1-\left(\frac{d}{D}\right)^{4}\right]} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 125&=\frac{16 T}{\pi(100)^{3}\left[1-\left(\frac{50}{100}\right)^{4}\right]} \\ \Rightarrow \quad T&=23 \mathrm{kNm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Torsion of Shafts and Pressure Vessels

Two plates of 8 mm thickness each are connected by a fillet weld of 6 mm thickness as shown in the figure.

The permissible stresses in the plate and the weld are 150 MPa and 110 MPa, respectively. Assuming the length of the weld shown in the figure to be the effective length, the permissible load P (in KN) is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned}P_{W}&=f_{b}\times l_{eff}\times t_{t} \\ &=110\left ( 100+100+50 \right )\times 0.7\times 6 \\ &=115.5\, kN \\ P_{plate}&=\sigma _{at}\times A_{net} \\ &=150\times \left ( 50\times 8 \right ) \\ &=60\, kN\end{aligned}[/latex]
So permissible load = 60 kN

Consider the portal frame shown in the figure and assume the modulus of elasticity [latex]E=2.5\times 10^{4}[/latex] MPa and the moment of inertial, [latex]I=8\times 10^{8}\; mm^{4}[/latex] for all the members of the frame.

The rotations (in degrees, up to decimal place) at the rigid joint Q would be ___

A 2 m long, axially loaded mild steel rod of 8 mm diameter exhibits the load-displacement [latex](P-\delta )[/latex] behavior as shown in the figure.

Assume the yield stress of steel as 250 Mpa. The complementary energy (in N-mm) stored in the bar up to its linear elastic behavior will be____
raw_source.solution:

Elastic strain energy [latex]=\frac{1}{2} \sigma_{y} \in_{E} A L [/latex]
[latex] =\frac{1}{2} \times 250 \times 1.25 \times 10^{-3} \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times 8^{2} \times 2000 [/latex]
[latex] =15707.96 \mathrm{Nmm} [/latex]

raw_source.text:
Consider a square-shaped area ABCD on the ground with its Centre at M as shown in the figure. Four concentrated vertical load of P=5000 kN are applied on this area, at each corner.

The vertical stress increment (in kPa, up to one decimal place) due to these loads according to the Boussinesq's equation, at a point 5 m right below M, is_____
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} P=5000 \mathrm{kN} \\ r=\sqrt{2^{2}+2^{2}}=2 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{m} \end{array}[/latex]
According to Boussinesq's
[latex] \sigma_{z}=k \frac{Q}{z^{2}}=\frac{3}{2 \pi}\left(\frac{1}{1+\frac{r^{2}}{z^{2}}}\right)^{5 / 2} \frac{Q}{z^{2}}[/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow [/latex] Vertical stress at 5m below point M
[latex] \begin{aligned} \sigma_{z} &=4 \times \frac{3}{2 \pi} \times\left\{\frac{1}{1+\left(\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{5}\right)^{2}}\right\}^{5/2} \quad \times \frac{5000}{5^{2}} \\ &=190.8 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

So, the new height (in cm to two decimal place of
mercury in the left limb will be

raw_source.text: A 1 m wide rectangular channel carries a discharge of 2 [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex]. The specific energy-depth diagram is prepared for the channel. It is observed in this diagram that corresponding to a particular specific energy; the subcritical depth is twice the supercritical depth. The subcritical depth (in meters, up to two decimal places) is equal to _____
raw_source.solution:
Let Supercritical depth =Y
Subcritical depth =2 Y
As the specific energy E remains constant for alternate depths
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad E_{1}&=E_{2} \\ \Rightarrow Y_{1}+\frac{Q^{2}}{2 g B^{2} Y_{1}^{2}}&=Y_{2}+\frac{Q^{2}}{2 g B^{2} Y_{2}^{2}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad Y+\frac{2^{2}}{2 \times 9.81 \times 1^{2} \times( Y)^{2}}&=2 Y+\frac{2^{2}}{2 \times 9.81 \times 1 \times(2 Y)^{2}} \\ Y+\frac{0.204}{Y^{2}}&=2Y+\frac{0.051}{Y^{2}}\\ \Rightarrow \quad Y=\frac{0.204-0.051}{Y^{2}}&=Y \\ \Rightarrow \quad Y^{3}&=0.1530 \\ \Rightarrow \quad Y&=0.534 \\ \therefore \quad \text{Subcritical depth} \\ &=0.534 \times 2 \\ &=1.0697 \\ &\simeq 1.07 \mathrm{m} \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A catchment is idealized as a 25 km x 25 km square. It has five rain gauges, one at each corner and one at the center, as shown in the figure.

During a month, the precipitation at these gauges is measured as [latex]G_{1}[/latex] = 300 mm, [latex]G_{2}[/latex] = 285 mm, [latex]G_{3}[/latex] = 272mm, [latex]G_{4}[/latex] = 290mm and [latex]G_{5}[/latex] = 288mm. The average precipitation (in mm, up to one decimal place) over the catchment during this month by using the Thiessen polygon method is ______
raw_source.solution:
Let sides of square as,
a=25 km
Now area of the polygon is calculated as,
[latex] \begin{aligned} A_{1}&=A_{2}=A_{3}=A_{4} \\ &=\frac{1}{2}\times \frac{a}{2}\times \frac{a}{2} \\ &=\frac{a^{2}}{8}=\frac{25^{2}}{8}=78.125 \\ A_{5}&=\text{Area of square of sides } \frac{\sqrt{2}a}{2} \\ &=\frac{a}{\sqrt{2}} =\frac{a^{2}}{2}=\frac{25^{2}}{2}=312.5\, km^{2} \\ \therefore & \text{Mean precipitation,}\\ \bar{P}&=\frac{G_{1}A_{1}+G_{2}A_{2}+G_{3}A_{3}+G_{4}A_{4}+G_{5}A_{5}}{A_{1}+A_{2}+A_{3}+A_{4}+A_{5}} \\ \therefore \;\;\bar{P}&=\frac{\left ( 300+255+272+290 \right )\times 78.125+288\times 312.5}{\left ( 4\times 78.125 \right )+312.5} \\ &= 287.375 mm\end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Precipitation and General Aspects of Hydrology

raw_source.text: The culturable command area of a canal is 10,000 ha. The area grows only two crops-rice in the Kharif season and wheat in the Rabi season. The design discharge of the canal is based on the rice requirements, which has an irrigated area of 2500 ha, base period of 150 days and delta of 130 cm. The maximum permissible irrigated area (in ha) for wheat, with a base period of 120 days and delta of 50 cm, is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{CCA} &=10000 \mathrm{ha} \\ \text { For rice, } \Delta_{r}&=130 \mathrm{cm}=1.3 \mathrm{m} \\ A_{r} & =2500 \mathrm{ha} \\ B_{r} & =150 \text { days } \\ \text{Duty,}\quad D_{r} & =\frac{8.64 B_{r}}{\Delta_{r}}=\frac{8.64 \times 150}{1.30} \\ D_{r} & =996.923 \mathrm{ha} / \mathrm{cumecs} \\ D_{r} & =\frac{A}{Q} \\ Q & =\frac{2500}{996.923} \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s}=2.5077 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s}\\ \text{For wheat also,} &\text{discharge is }2.5077 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s}\\ B_{w} &=120 \text { days } \\ \Delta &=50 \mathrm{cm} \\ A_{w} &=Q \times D_{w} \\ D_{w} &=\frac{8.64 \times B_{w}}{\Delta_{w}} \\ &=\frac{8.64 \times 120}{0.5}=2073.6 \\ \therefore \quad A_{w} &=2.5077 \times 2073.6 \\ &=5199.966 \mathrm{ha} \simeq 5200 \mathrm{ha} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Water is pumped at a steady uniform flow rate of 0.01 [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex] through a horizontal smooth circular pipe of 100 mm diameter. Given that the Reynolds number is 800 and g is 9.81[latex] m/s^{2}[/latex], the head loss (in meters, up to one decimal place) per km length due to friction would be_____
raw_source.solution:
Head loss due to frictions,
[latex] \begin{aligned} h_{L}&=\frac{n O^{2}}{12.1 d^{5}}\\ \text{Here. }f&= \text{ friction factor}\\ &=\frac{64}{\text { Re }}=\frac{64}{800}=0.08\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Head loss per metre length
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{h_{L}}{L}&=\frac{fQ^{2}}{12.1d^{5}}=\frac{0.08\times(0.01)^{3}}{12.1\times(1.0)^{5}}\\ \frac{h_{L}}{L}&=\frac{0.8}{12.1} = 0.06611 \text{meter/meter}\\ &=66.11\text{meter/km} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: For a given water sample, the ratio between [latex]BOD_{5-day,20^{\circ}C}[/latex] and the ultimate BOD is 0.68. The value of the reaction rate constant k (on base e) (in [latex]day^{-1}[/latex] up to two decimal places) is_____
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} BOD/20^{\circ}C &=C_{0}\left ( 1-e^{-k\: 20^{\circ}C\times 5} \right ) \\ \frac{BOD/20^{\circ}C}{C_{0}} &=0.68=\left ( 1-e^{-k\: 20^{\circ}C\times 5} \right ) \\ K,20^{\circ}C &=0.227\; day^{-1}\simeq 0.23\; day^{-1} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

raw_source.text: A municipal corporation is required to treat 1000 [latex]m^{3}/day[/latex] of water. It is found that an overflow rate of 20 m/day will produce a satisfactory removal of the discrete suspended particles at a depth of 3 m. The diameter (in meters, rounded to the nearest integer) of a circular settling tank designed for the removal of these particles would be______

raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned}\left ( D^{2}+2D+1 \right )y&=0 \;\;  \left ( \therefore \; \text{Roots are }-1,-1\right ) \\    CF&=\left ( C_{1}+C_{2}x \right )e^{-x} \\    y&=C_{1}e^{-x}+C_{2}xe^{-x} \;\;...(i) \\ y\left ( 0 \right )&=1  \;\;\;1=C_{1}        \;\;\;...(ii) \\    {y}'&=C_{1}e^{-x}+C_{2}\left ( e^{-x}-xe^{-x} \right ) \\ {y}'\left ( 0 \right )&=-1,  \;\;\;-1=-C_{1}+C_{2}     \;\;...(iii)\\ \text{From eq. } & \text{ (ii) and (iii),}\\    C_{1}&=1,\, C_{2}=0 \\ \therefore \;\;   y&=e^{x}\\ \text{At } x=1, y&=e^{-1}=\frac{1}{e}=0.368\end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The solution of the equation [latex]x\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+y=0[/latex] passing through the point (1,1) is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned}x\frac{dy}{dx}+y&=0 \\ x\frac{dy}{dx}&=-y \\ \frac{dy}{y}&=-\frac{dx}{x} \\ \int \frac{1}{y}dy&=\int \frac{-1}{x}dx \\ \ln y&=-\ln x+c\\ \text{when } y&=1, x=1\\  c&=0\\ \Rightarrow  \;\; y&=\frac{1}{x}=x^{-1} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The quadratic equation [latex]2x^{2}-3x+3=0[/latex] is to be solved numerically starting with an initial guess as [latex]x_{0}=2[/latex] . The new estimate of x after the first iteration using Newton-Raphson method is ______
raw_source.solution:
Given [latex]\begin{aligned} f\left ( x \right )&=2x^{2}-3x+3, x_{0}&=2 \\ {f}'\left ( x \right )&=4x-3 \end{aligned}[/latex]
By Newton-Rapshon
[latex] \begin{aligned} x_{1}&=x_{0}-\frac{f\left ( x_{0} \right )}{{f}'\left ( x_{0} \right )} \\ &=2-\frac{2\left ( 2 \right )^{2}-3\left ( 2 \right )+3}{4\left ( 2 \right )-3} \\ &=2-\frac{5}{5}=1 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The matrix [latex]\begin{pmatrix} 2 &-4 \\ 4 &-2 \end{pmatrix}[/latex] has
raw_source.solution:
[latex] \begin{aligned} A&=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -4\\ 4 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \\ \left | A-\lambda I \right |&=0 \\ \begin{vmatrix} 2-\lambda & -4\\ 4 & -2-\lambda \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\ -4-2\lambda +2\lambda +\lambda ^{2}+16&=0 \\ \lambda ^{2}+12&=0 \\ \lambda &=\pm 2\sqrt{3}i\text{ (Complex eigen values)} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex](1) \;\; \lambda =2\sqrt{3}i[/latex]
Consider [latex]\left ( A-\lambda I \right )X=0 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{bmatrix} 2-2\sqrt{3}i &-4 \\ 4 & -2-2\sqrt{3}i \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} 2-2\sqrt{3}ix_{1}&=4x_{2} \\ \frac{x_{1}}{4}&=\frac{x_{2}}{2-2\sqrt{3}i} \\ \begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix} 4\\ 2-2\sqrt{3}i \end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex](2)\;\; \lambda =-2\sqrt{3}i[/latex]
Consider [latex]\left ( A-\lambda I \right )X=0 [/latex]
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2+2\sqrt{3}i & -4\\ 4 & -2+2\sqrt{3}i \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} 2+2\sqrt{3}ix_{1}&=4x_{2} \\ \frac{x_{1}}{4}&=\frac{x_{2}}{2+2\sqrt{3}i} \\ \begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x-{2} \end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix} 4\\ 2+2\sqrt{3}i \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Complex eigen values and complex eigen vectors.

raw_source.text: The laplace transform F(s) of the exponential function ,[latex]f(t)=e^{at}\; when \; t\geq 0[/latex], where a is a constant and (s-a)[latex]\gt [/latex]0, is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} L(e^{at}) &=\frac{1}{s-a} \\ L(e^{at}) &=\int_{0}^{\infty }e^{-st}e^{at}dt \\ &= \int_{0}^{\infty }e^{-(s-a)t}dt\\ &= \left.\begin{matrix} \frac{e^{-(s-a)t}}{-(s-a)} \end{matrix}\right|_{0}^{\infty }\\ &=-\frac{1}{s-a}(0-1)\\ &=\frac{1}{s-a} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The percent reduction in the bearing capacity of a strip footing resting on sand under flooding condition (water level at the base of the footing) when compared to the situation where the water level is at a depth much greater than the width of footing, is approximately
raw_source.solution:
For strip footing on sand (c=0)
[latex] q_{u}=\gamma D_{f} N_{q}+0.5 \mathrm{B} \gamma N_{\gamma}[/latex]
In flooding condition water level rises to base of footing hence IIIrd term unit weight of soil will change and IInd term unit weight will be unaffected.
[latex] \begin{array}{ll} \therefore & q_{u}=\gamma D_{f} N_{q}+0.5 B \gamma N_{\gamma} \\ \because & \gamma \simeq \frac{1}{2} \gamma_{s a t} \end{array}[/latex]
Hence third term reduced and second term will be same thereby percentage reduction will not be 50%.
According to option approach answer should be 25%
Note: If water table rises to ground level then both [latex]\gamma[/latex] will reduce to [latex]\gamma[/latex]. Hence, percentage reduction would be approximately 50%.

raw_source.text:
The frequency distribution of the compressive strength of 20 concrete cube specimens is given in the table.

If [latex]\mu [/latex] is the mean strength of the specimens and [latex]\sigma[/latex] is the standard deviation, the number of specimens (out of 20) with compressive strength less than [latex]\mu -3\sigma[/latex] is ______
raw_source.solution:
Average strength,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \mu &=\frac{(4 \times 23)+(2 \times 28)+(5 \times 22.5)+(5 \times 31)+(4 \times 29)}{20} \\ &=26.575 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \sigma &=\sqrt{\frac{\Sigma(\mu-f)^{2}}{n-1}} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{\begin{array}{c} (26.575-23)^{2} \times 4+(26.575-28)^{2} \times 2\\ +(26.575-22.5)^{2} \times 5+(26.575-31)^{2} \\ \times 5+(26.575-29)^{2} \times 4 \end{array}}{(20-1)}} \\&=3.7 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Now, [latex]\mu-3 \sigma=26.575-3 \times 3.7=15.48 [/latex]
Thus, no specimen is having compressive strength less than [latex]\mu-3 \sigma.[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a fillet weld, the direct shear stress and bending tensile stress are 50 MPa and 150 MPa, respectively. As per IS 800: 2007, the equivalent stress (in MPa, up to two decimal places) will be ______
raw_source.solution:
Direct bending tensile stress,
[latex] f_{a}=150 Mpa[/latex]
Direct shear stress,
[latex] q=50 Mpa[/latex]
According to IS 800:2007, clause 10.5.10.1.1
The equivalent stress,
[latex]\begin{aligned} f_{e}&=\sqrt{f^{2}_{a}+3q^{2}}\leq \frac{f_{u}}{\sqrt{3}\gamma _{mW}} \\ f_{e}&=\sqrt{150^{2}+3\times 50^{2}} \\&=173.21 MPa\\ \Rightarrow \;\; f_{e} & \leq \frac{f_{u}}{\sqrt{3}\gamma _{mW}} \\&=\frac{400}{\sqrt{3}\times 1.25} \\ &=184.75 MPa \end{aligned}[/latex]
(Hence OK)
Note: The above check for combination of stressed need not be done for fillet welds where the sum of normal and shear stresses does not exceed [latex]f_{wd}[/latex] [Clause 10.5.10.1.2(b)].
Thus, [latex]f_{a}+q=150+50=200[/latex] MPa
[latex] f_{a}+q \gt f_{wd}[/latex] (= 184.75 MPa)
[latex]\Rightarrow \;\;f_{e}= 173.21[/latex] MPa
Thus, the weld is designed for an equivelent stress of 173.21 MPa

raw_source.text: In a shrinkage limit test, the volume and mass of a dry soil pat are found to be 50 [latex]cm^{3}[/latex] and 88 g, respectively. The specific gravity of the soil solids is 2.71 and the density of water is 1 g/cc. The shrinkage limit (in %, up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution:
Dry soil mass =88 gm
Volume of dry soil = 50 cc
Dry density of soil mass,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \rho_{d}&=\frac{M_{d}}{V_{d}}=\frac{88}{50} \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{cc}\\ \therefore \text{ Shrinkage limit, } w_{s}&=\frac{1}{R}-\frac{1}{G}=\frac{1}{\left(\rho_{d} / \rho_{w}\right)}-\frac{1}{G} \\ w_{s} &=\frac{\rho_{w}}{\rho_{d}}-\frac{1}{G} \\ &=\frac{1}{1.76}-\frac{1}{2.71}=0.1990 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A core cutter of 130 mm height has inner and outer diameters of 100 mm and 106 mm, respectively. The area ratio of the core cutter (in %, up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Area ratio } &=\frac{A_{\text {outer }}-A_{\text {inne }} r}{A_{\text {inner }}} \times 100 \\ &=\frac{\frac{\pi}{4} D_{0}^{2}-\frac{\pi}{4} D_{i}^{2}}{\frac{\pi}{4} D_{i}^{2}} \times 100 \\ &=\frac{\frac{\pi}{4}(106)^{2}-\frac{\pi}{4}(100)^{2}}{\frac{\pi}{4}(100)^{2}} \times 100 \\ &=12.36 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 1:50 model of a spillway is to be tested in the laboratory. The discharge in the prototype spillway is 1000 [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex]. The corresponding discharge (in [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex], up to two decimal places) to be maintained in the model, neglecting variation in acceleration due to gravity, is ______
raw_source.solution:
Froude law is valid
[latex] \begin{aligned} Q_{r} &=L_{r}^{25} \\ \frac{Q_{m}}{Q_{p}} &=\left(\frac{1}{50}\right)^{25} \\ \frac{Q_{m}}{1000} &=\left(\frac{1}{50}\right)^{25} \\ Q_{m} &=0.0566 \mathrm{m}^{3 / \mathrm{s}} \\ \text{So},\quad Q_{m} & \simeq 0.06 \mathrm{m}^{3 / \mathrm{s}} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 10 m wide rectangular channel carries a discharge of 20 [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex] under critical condition. Using g = 9.81 [latex]m/s^{2}[/latex], the specific energy (in m, up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} E_{c}&=\frac{3}{2} y_{c} \\ y_{c}&=\left(\frac{q^{2}}{g}\right)^{1 / 3} \\ \text{Hear},\quad q&=\frac{20}{10}=2 \\ \Rightarrow\quad E_{c}&=\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{2^{2}}{9.81}\right)^{1 / 3}=1.11 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A city generates [latex]40 \times 10^{6}[/latex] kg of municipal solid waste (MSW) per year, out of which only 10% is recovered/recycled and the rest goes to landfill. The landfill has a single lift of 3 m height and is compacted to a density of [latex]550 kg/m^{3}[/latex]. If 80% of the landfill is assumed to be MSW, the landfill area (in [latex]m^{2}[/latex], up to one decimal place) required would be ______
raw_source.solution:
Total weight generated by city
[latex]=40\times 10^{6}\: kg/year[/latex]
Weight of MSW going into landfill
[latex]=0.9\times 40\times 10^{6}\: kg/year[/latex]
[latex]=36\times 10^{6}\: kg/year[/latex]
Compacted density
[latex]=550\: kg/m^{3}[/latex]
Compacted volume of MSW
[latex]=\frac{36\times 10^{6}\: kg/year}{550\: kg/m^{3}}[/latex]
[latex]=65454.5454\: m^{3}/year[/latex]
Total landfill volume = Vol. of MSD + Vol. of cover
Given, Volume of MSW [latex]=0.8\times[/latex] Total landfill volume
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Vol. of cover [latex] =0.2\times [/latex] Total landfill volume
[latex] \therefore [/latex]Total landfill volume [latex] =\frac{65454.5454}{0.8}m^{3}/year =81818.18175m^{3}/year[/latex]
Height of landfill [latex]=3\: m[/latex]
[latex]\therefore [/latex] Area of lanfill[latex]=\frac{81818.18175}{3} =27272.7\: m^{2}/year[/latex]

raw_source.text: The value of the integral [latex]\int_{0}^{\pi}x\cos ^{2}x\: dx[/latex] is
raw_source.solution:
The value of
[latex]\begin{aligned}&\int_{0}^{\pi }x\cos ^{2}x\, dx \\ &=\int_{0}^{\pi } \left ( \frac{x}{2}+\frac{x\cos 2x}{2} \right )dx \\ &=\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{x^{2}}{4} \end{matrix}\right|_{0}^{\pi }+\frac{1}{2}\left ( \frac{x\sin 2x}{2}+\frac{\cos 2x}{4} \right ) \\ &=\frac{\pi ^{2}}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\left \{ \left ( 0+\frac{1}{4} \right )-\left ( 0+\frac{1}{4} \right ) \right \} \\ &=\frac{\pi ^{2}}{4}+\frac{1}{2}\left ( \frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{4} \right ) \\ &=\frac{\pi ^{2}}{4} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A cantilever beam of length 2 m with a square section of side length 0.1 m is loaded vertically at the free end. The vertical displacement at the free end is 5 mm. The beam is made of steel with Young's modulus of [latex]2.0 \times 10^{11} N/m^{2}[/latex]. The maximum bending stress at the fixed end of the cantilever is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} I&=\frac{(0.1)^4}{12} \\ \text{Deflection }\delta &=\frac{Pl^2}{3eI} \\ 5 \times 10^{-3}&=\frac{P(2)^3}{3 \times 2 \times 10^11 \times \frac{(0.1)^4}{12}} \\ P&=3125N \\ \text{Now, } M&= Pl=3125 \times 2\\ &= 6250Nm\\ \text{As, }\frac{M}{I} &=\frac{\sigma }{y}=\frac{E}{R} \\ \sigma _{max}&=\frac{M}{Z}=\frac{6250}{\frac{(0.1)^3}{6}}\\ &=37.5 \times 10^6 N/m^2=37.5MPa \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A cylinder of radius 250 mm and weight, W = 10 kN is rolled up an obstacle of height 50 mm by applying a horizontal force P at its centre as shown in the figure.

All interfaces are assumed frictionless. The minimum value of P is
raw_source.solution:
Given: r=250 mm, W=10 kN
Note:
1. When the cylinder will be about to move out of the cylinder, it will loose its contact at point A, only contact will be at point B.
2. Considering equation of cylinder of that instant under P, W and [latex]R_{B}[/latex] (contact force at B).
[latex]\begin{aligned} \sum \vec{M}_{B} &=0 \\ P\times OC-W\times BC &=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
In [latex]\Delta OCB[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} OC^{2}+CB^{2} &=OB^{2} \\ CB &=\sqrt{250^{2}-200^{2}}=150 \\ P &=\frac{10\times 10^{3}\times 150}{200} \\ &=2.5\times 3\: \text{kN}=7.5\: \text{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A plate in equilibrium is subjected to uniform stresses along its edges with magnitude [latex]\sigma_{xx}[/latex] = 30 MPa and [latex]\sigma_{yy}[/latex] = 50 MPa as shown in the figure.

The Young's modulus of the material is [latex]2 \times 10^{11} N/m^{2}[/latex] and the Poisson's ratio is 0.3. If [latex]\sigma_{zz}[/latex] is negligibly small and assumed to be zero, then the strain [latex]\varepsilon _{zz}[/latex] is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma _{xx} &=30MPa \\ \sigma _{yy} &=50MPa \\ \sigma _{zz} &=0 \\ \varepsilon _{zz} &=\frac{\sigma _{zz}}{E}-\mu \frac{\sigma _{xx}}{E}-\mu \frac{\sigma _{yy}}{E} \\ &= -\frac{\mu }{E} (\sigma _{xx}+\sigma _{yy})\\ &= -\frac{0.3}{2 \times 10^5}(30+50)\\ &=-120 \times 10^{-6} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Properties of Metals, Stress and Strain

The figure shows a simply supported beam PQ of uniform flexural rigidity EI carrying two moments M and 2M.

The slope at P will be

raw_source.text: A 0.5 m x 0.5 m square concrete pile is to be driven in a homogeneous clayey soil having undrained shear strength, [latex]c_{u}[/latex]= 50 kPa and unit weight, [latex]\gamma = 18.0 kN/m^{3}[/latex]. The design capacity of the pile is 500 kN. The adhesion factor [latex]\alpha[/latex] is given as 0.75. The length of the pile required for the above design load with a factor of safety of 2.0 is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} C_{u}=& 50 \mathrm{kPa}, \gamma=18 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3}, \mathrm{FOS}=2 \\ Q_{\text {up}}=& 9 \mathrm{C} \times B^{2}+\alpha \bar{C}(4 \mathrm{BL})=1000 \mathrm{kN} \\ 1000=& 9 \times 50 \times 0.5 \times 0.5+0.75 \\ & \times 50(4 \times 0.5 \mathrm{L}) \\ L=& 11.83 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

A priority intersection has a single-lane one-way traffic road crossing an undivided two-lane two-way traffic road. The traffic stream speed on the single-lane road is 20 kmph and the speed on the two-lane road is 50 kmph. The perception-reaction time is 2.5s, coefficient of longitudinal friction is 0.38 and acceleration due to gravity is 9.81 m/[latex]s^{2}[/latex]. A clear sight triangle has to be ensured at this intersection. The minimum lengths of the sides of the sight triangle along the two-lane road and the single-lane road, respectively will be
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{SSD}_{2} &=0.278 \times V t_{R}+\frac{V^{2}}{254 f} \\ &=0.278 \times 50 \times 2.5+\frac{50^{2}}{254 \times 0.38} \simeq 61 \mathrm{m} \\ \mathrm{SSD}_{1} &=0.278 \times 20 \times 2.5+\frac{20^{2}}{254 \times 0.38} \simeq 18 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
As per data given and based on calculation of SSD the answer would be 61 m and 18 m.
But, as per the code IRC : 66 of sight distance calculation at priority intersection, the sight triangle at priority intersection should be formed by measuring a distance of 15 m along minor road and a distance equal to 8 seconds travel at the design speed [latex](50 \times 0.278 \times 8 \simeq 111 m) [/latex] along major road. Hence answer will be 111 m and 15 m.
raw_source.tag2: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

raw_source.text: A square area (on the surface of the earth) with side 100 m and uniform height, appears as 1 [latex]cm^{2}[/latex] on a vertical aerial photograph. The topographic map shows that a contour of 650 m passes through the area. If focal length of the camera lens is 150 mm, the height from which the aerial photograph was taken, is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} A&=100 \times 100 \mathrm{m}^{2}\\ \text { Area on photo, }\\ a &=1 \mathrm{cm}^{2} \\ \text { Scale } \quad 1 \mathrm{cm} &=100 \mathrm{m} \\ f &=150 \mathrm{mm} \\ h &=650 \mathrm{m} \\ \text { Scale } \quad &=\frac{1}{100}=\frac{1}{100 \times 10^{2}}\\ &=\frac{1}{10000}=\frac{f}{H-h}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{10000}&=\frac{150 \times 10^{-3}}{H-650} \\ \Rightarrow \quad H&=2150 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Remote Sensing, GIS, GPS and Photogrammetry

raw_source.text: The solution at x=1,t=1 of the partial differential equation [latex]\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial x^2}=25 \frac{\partial^2u}{\partial t^2}[/latex] subject to boundary conditions u(0)=3x and [latex]\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}(0)=3[/latex] is

The solution at ( up to three decimal places) at x=1 of th euation [latex]\frac{d^{2}y}{dx^2}+2\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}+y=0[/latex] subject to boundary condition y(0)=1 and [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}(0)=-1[/latex] is______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned}\left ( D^{2}+2D+1 \right )y&=0 \;\;  \left ( \therefore \; \text{Roots are }-1,-1\right ) \\    CF&=\left ( C_{1}+C_{2}x \right )e^{-x} \\    y&=C_{1}e^{-x}+C_{2}xe^{-x} \;\;...(i) \\ y\left ( 0 \right )&=1  \;\;\;1=C_{1}        \;\;\;...(ii) \\    {y}'&=C_{1}e^{-x}+C_{2}\left ( e^{-x}-xe^{-x} \right ) \\ {y}'\left ( 0 \right )&=-1,  \;\;\;-1=-C_{1}+C_{2}     \;\;...(iii)\\ \text{From eq. } & \text{ (ii) and (iii),}\\    C_{1}&=1,\, C_{2}=0 \\ \therefore \;\;   y&=e^{x}\\ \text{At } x=1, y&=e^{-1}=\frac{1}{e}=0.368\end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Variation of water depth(y) in a gradually varied open channel flow is given by the first order differential equation
[latex]\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}=\frac{1-e^{-\frac{10}{3}\ln(y)} }{250-45e^{-3\ln(y)}}[/latex]
Given initial condition: y(x=0)=0.8 m. The depth (in m, up to three decimal places) of flow at a downstream section at x = 1 m from one calculation step of Single Step Euler Method is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{d y}{d x}&=\frac{1-e^{-\frac{10}{3} \ln y}}{250-45 e^{-3 \ln y}}\\ y_{1} &=y_{0}+h f\left(x_{0}, y_{0}\right) \\ y_{1} &=0.8+1\left(\frac{1-e^{-\frac{10}{3} \ln 0.8}}{250-45 e^{-3 \ln 0.8}}\right] \\ &=0.8+1\left(\frac{-1.1039}{162.109}\right) \\ &=0.793 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: An RCC short column (with lateral ties) of rectangular cross section of 250 mm x 300 mm is reinforced with four numbers of 16 mm diameter longitudinal bars. The grades of steel and concrete are Fe415 and M20, respectively. Neglect eccentricity effect. Considering limit state of collapse in compression (IS 456 : 2000), the axial load carrying capacity of the column (in kN, up to one decimal place), is ______
raw_source.solution:
since eccentricity effect is being neglected so column can be considered as concentrically loaded.
Ultimate axial load carrying capacity of column.
[latex] \begin{aligned} P_{u} &=0.45 \mathrm{f}_{c k} A_{g}+\left(0.75 \mathrm{f}_{y}-0.45 \mathrm{f}_{c k}\right) A_{\mathrm{sc}} \\ &=0.45 \times 20 \times 250 \times 300 \\ &+(0.75 \times 415-0.45 \times 20) 4 \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times 16^{2} \\ &=918.1 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: An RCC beam of rectangular cross section has factored shear of 200 kN at its critical section. Its width b is 250 mm and effective depth d is 350 mm. Assume design shear strength [latex]\tau _{c}[/latex] of concrete as 0.62 [latex]N/mm^{2}[/latex] and maximum allowable shear stress [latex]\tau _{c,max}[/latex]    in concrete as 2.8 [latex]N/mm^{2}[/latex] . If two legged 10 mm diameter vertical stirrups of Fe250 grade steel are used, then the required spacing (in cm, up to one decimal place) as per limit state method will be ______
raw_source.solution:
Nominal shear stress,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \tau_{v}&=\frac{V_{u}}{b d}=\frac{200 \times 10^{3}}{250 \times 350}=2.286 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{mm}^{2} \lt \tau_{c m a x} \\ &\text{(OK)}\\ SF&\text{ taken by stirrups}\\ &=\left(\tau_{v}-\tau_{c}\right) b d \\ &=(2.286-0.62) \times 250 \times 350 \\ &=145.75 \mathrm{kN} \\ \text{Now, }V_{u s}&=\frac{0.87 f_{y} A_{s v} d}{S_{v}} \\ \Rightarrow \quad S_{v}&=\frac{0.87 \times 250 \times 350 \times 2 \times \frac{\pi}{4} \times 10^{2}}{145.75 \times 10^{3}} \\ &=82 \mathrm{mm}=8.2 \mathrm{cm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Shear, Torsion, Bond, Anchorage and Development Length

raw_source.text: A conventional drained triaxial compression test was conducted on a normally consolidated clay sample under an effective confining pressure of 200 kPa. The deviator stress at failure was found to be 400 kPa. An identical specimen of the same clay sample is isotropically consolidated to a confining pressure of 200 kPa and subjected to standard undrained triaxial compression test. If the deviator stress at failure is 150 kPa, the pore pressure developed (in kPa, up to one decimal place) is ______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]I^{st}[/latex] Specimen : Drained condition
[latex] \bar{\sigma}_{3}=200 \mathrm{kPa}: \sigma_{\mathrm{d}}=400 \mathrm{kPa}: \bar{\sigma}_{1}=600 \mathrm{kPa}[/latex]
[latex] II^{nd} [/latex]Specimen : Undrained condition
[latex] \begin{aligned} \sigma_{3} &=200 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \sigma_{\mathrm{d}} &=150 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \sigma_{1} &=\sigma_{3}+\sigma_{\mathrm{d}}=350 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Let pore pressure developed is u
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \bar{\sigma}_{3}&=(200-u)\\ \bar{\sigma}_{1}&=(350-u)\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
From stress relationship
[latex] \bar{\sigma}_{1}=\bar{\sigma}_{3} \tan ^{2}\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)+2 c\tan\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)[/latex]
For clay under drained condition c=0
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad \bar{\sigma}_{1} &=\bar{\sigma}_{3} \tan ^{2}\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right) \\ 600 &=200 \tan ^{2}\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right) \\ \phi &=30^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For second specimen,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \bar{\sigma}_{1}&=\bar{\sigma}_{3} \tan ^{2}\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{\phi}{2}\right)\\ (350-u) &=(200-u) \tan ^{2}\left(45^{\circ}+\frac{30^{\circ}}{2}\right) \\ u &=125 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The void ratio of a soil is 0.55 at an effective normal stress of 140 kPa. The compression index of the soil is 0.25. In order to reduce the void ratio to 0.4, an increase in the magnitude of effective normal stress (in kPa, up to one decimal place) should be ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \Delta H &=\frac{H_{0} \Delta e}{1+e_{0}}=\frac{H_{0} C_{c}}{1+e_{0}} \log \left(\frac{\sigma_{0}+\Delta \sigma}{\sigma_{0}}\right) \\ \Delta H &=H_{0}\left(\frac{0.55-0.40}{1+0.50}\right)=\frac{H_{0} \times 0.25}{1+0.50} \log \left(\frac{140+\Delta \sigma}{140}\right) \\ \frac{0.15}{0.25} &=\frac{3}{5}=\log \left(\frac{140+\Delta \sigma}{140}\right) \\ \Delta \sigma &=417.35 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a laboratory, a flow experiment is performed over a hydraulic structure. The measured values of discharge and velocity are 0.05 [latex]m^{3}[/latex]/s and 0.25 m/s, respectively. If the full scale structure (30 times bigger) is subjected to a discharge of 270 [latex]m^{3}[/latex]/s, then the time scale (model to full scale) value (up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Froude Law }(F r)_{m}&=(F r)_{p} \\ \left(\frac{V}{\sqrt{L \mathrm{g}}}\right)_{m} &=\left(\frac{v}{\sqrt{L g}}\right)_{p} \quad\left(g_{m}=g_{p}\right) \\ v_{r} &=\sqrt{L_{r}} \\ \text{or}\quad \frac{L_{r}}{T_{r}} &=\sqrt{L} \\ T_{r} &=\sqrt{L_{r}} \\ T_{r} &=\sqrt{\frac{1}{30}}=0.1826 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A fillet weld is simultaneously subjected to factored normal and shear stresses of 120 MPa and 50 MPa, respectively. As per IS 800 : 2007, the equivalent stress (in MPa, up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution:
Factrored normal stress, [latex]f_{a}= 120 Mpa[/latex]
factrored shear stress, [latex]q= 50 Mpa[/latex]
According to IS-800:2007, clause 10.5.10.1.1
The equivalent stress,
[latex]\begin{aligned} f_{e}&=\sqrt{f_{a}^{2}+3q^{2}}\leq \frac{F_{u}}{\sqrt{3}y_{mW}} \\ f_{e}&=\sqrt{120^{2}+3\times 50^{2}} \\ &=147.99 \\ \Rightarrow \;\; f_{e}& \leq \frac{f_{u}}{\sqrt{3}y_{mW}}=\frac{400}{\sqrt{3}\times 1.25} \\ &=\left ( 184.75 MPa \right )\end{aligned}[/latex]
Note: The above check for combination of stresses need not be done for fillet welds where the sum of normal and shear stresses does not exceed [latex]f_{wd}[/latex] [clause 10.5.10.1.2(b)]. Hence, sum of normal and shear stresses [latex]=120+50=170 MPa \leq f_{wd} (= 184.75 MPa)[/latex]
So, the above check need not be done.
So, weld is designed for a resultant shear stress of [latex]\left ( f_{r} \right )[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} f_{r}&=\sqrt{f_{a}^{2}+q^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{120^{2}=50^{2}} \\ &=130 N/mm^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
So, the design stress is [latex]130 N/mm^{2}[/latex]; however equivalent stress 147.99 MPa.

raw_source.text: The matrix [latex]\begin{pmatrix} 2 &-4 \\ 4 &-2 \end{pmatrix}[/latex] has
raw_source.solution:
[latex] \begin{aligned} A&=\begin{bmatrix} 2 & -4\\ 4 & -2 \end{bmatrix} \\ \left | A-\lambda I \right |&=0 \\ \begin{vmatrix} 2-\lambda & -4\\ 4 & -2-\lambda \end{vmatrix}&=0 \\ -4-2\lambda +2\lambda +\lambda ^{2}+16&=0 \\ \lambda ^{2}+12&=0 \\ \lambda &=\pm 2\sqrt{3}i\text{ (Complex eigen values)} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex](1) \;\; \lambda =2\sqrt{3}i[/latex]
Consider [latex]\left ( A-\lambda I \right )X=0 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{bmatrix} 2-2\sqrt{3}i &-4 \\ 4 & -2-2\sqrt{3}i \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} 2-2\sqrt{3}ix_{1}&=4x_{2} \\ \frac{x_{1}}{4}&=\frac{x_{2}}{2-2\sqrt{3}i} \\ \begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix} 4\\ 2-2\sqrt{3}i \end{bmatrix}\end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex](2)\;\; \lambda =-2\sqrt{3}i[/latex]
Consider [latex]\left ( A-\lambda I \right )X=0 [/latex]
[latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2+2\sqrt{3}i & -4\\ 4 & -2+2\sqrt{3}i \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x_{2} \end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix} 0\\ 0 \end{bmatrix} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} 2+2\sqrt{3}ix_{1}&=4x_{2} \\ \frac{x_{1}}{4}&=\frac{x_{2}}{2+2\sqrt{3}i} \\ \begin{bmatrix} x_{1}\\ x-{2} \end{bmatrix}&=\begin{bmatrix} 4\\ 2+2\sqrt{3}i \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Complex eigen values and complex eigen vectors.

raw_source.text: The laplace transform F(s) of the exponential function ,[latex]f(t)=e^{at}\; when \; t\geq 0[/latex], where a is a constant and (s-a)[latex]\gt [/latex]0, is

[latex]a=\frac{36}{9}=4\; m/s^{2}[/latex]



[latex]\begin{aligned} N &=ma\; \; \; \; \; \text{(Newton's 2nd law)} \\ N&=4\times 4=16\; \text{N} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Four bolts P, Q, R and S of equal diameter are used for a bracket subjected to a load of 130 kN as shown in the figure.

The force in bolt P is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} F_{1} &= \frac{P}{n}=\frac{130}{4}=32.5 kN \\ F_{2} &= \frac{Pe}{\sum r^{2}_{i}}\times r_{p} \\ r_{P} &= r_{Q} = r_{R} = r_{S} \\ &= \sqrt{50^{2}+120^{2}} \\&=130 mm \\ F_{2} &=\frac{\left ( 130\times 200 \right )\times 130}{4\times 130^{2}} \\ &= \frac{200}{4} =50 kN \\ \cos \theta &= \frac{50}{130} \\ \Rightarrow \; \; F_{R} &= \sqrt{\left [ \left ( 32.5^{2} \right )+\left ( 50^{2} \right )+\left ( 2\times 32.5\times 50 \right )\times \left ( \frac{50}{130} \right ) \right ]} \\ &= 69.33 kN \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A singly-reinforced rectangular concrete beam of width 300 mm and effective depth 400 mm is to be designed using M25 grade concrete and Fe500 grade reinforcing steel. For the beam to be under-reinforced, the maximum number of 16 mm diameter reinforcing bars that can be provided is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} B&=300 \mathrm{mm}\\ d&=400 \mathrm{mm} \text{ (effective depth)} \\ &\mathrm{M} 25\text{ and }\mathrm{Fe} 500 \\ A_{s t,} \lim &=0.414\left(\frac{f_{c k}}{f_{y}}\right) x_{u, l \operatorname{irn}} b \\ &=0.414\left(\frac{25}{500}\right) 0.46 \times 400 \times 300 \\ &=1142.64 \mathrm{mm}^{2}\\ \text{Number of }&16 \mathrm{mm} \phi \\ &=\frac{1142.64}{\frac{\pi}{4}(16)^{2}}=5.68\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
For [latex] A_{s t} \lt A_{s t \text { lim' }},[/latex] maximum number of bars to be provided is 5.

raw_source.text: A 3 m high vertical earth retaining wall retains a dry granular backfill with angle of internal friction of [latex]30^{\circ}[/latex] and unit weight of 20 [latex]kN/m^{3}[/latex]. If the wall is prevented from yielding (no movement), the total horizontal thrust (in kN per unit length) on the wall is
raw_source.solution:
Soil is dry sand
[latex] \therefore K_{0}=1-\sin \phi=1-\sin 30^{\circ}=0.5 [/latex]
Total horizontal thrust
[latex] \begin{aligned} P_{0} &=\frac{1}{2} K_{0} \gamma H \cdot H=\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{1}{2} \times 20 \times 3^{2} \\ &=45 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Three soil specimens (Soil 1, Soil 2 and Soil 3), each 150 mm long and 100 mm diameter, are placed in series in a constant head flow set-up as shown in the figure. Suitable screens are provided at the boundaries of the specimens to keep them intact. The values of coefficient of permeability of Soil 1, Soil 2 and Soil 3 are 0.01, 0.003 and 0.03 cm/s, respectively.

The value of h in the set-up is
raw_source.solution:
In normal to bedding plane flow (series arrangement), Discharge will be same and Head loss and Hydraulic gradient will be different
[latex] \begin{aligned} q &=K_{1} i_{1} A=K_{2} i_{2} A \\ &=K_{3} i_{3} A=K_{\mathrm{avg}} \cdot\left(\frac{H_{L}}{L}\right) A \\ K_{\mathrm{avg}_{1}} &=\frac{\Sigma Z_{i}}{\Sigma \frac{Z_{i}}{K_{i}}}=\frac{150+150+150}{\frac{150}{0.01}+\frac{150}{0.003}+\frac{150}{0.03}} \\ &=0.0064\\ \text{Total head loss}\\ &=H_{L}=560 \mathrm{mm} \\ \therefore K_{3} \cdot \frac{h}{150} \times A &=K_{a v g} \cdot \frac{560}{(150+150+150)} A \\ 0.03 \cdot\left(\frac{h}{150}\right) &=0.0064\left(\frac{560}{450}\right) \\ h &=40 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 5 m wide rectangular channel, the velocity u distribution in the vertical direction y is given by [latex]u=1.25y^{\frac{1}{6}}[/latex]. The distance y is measured from the channel bed. If the flow depth is 2 m, the discharge per unit width of the channel is
raw_source.solution:
Discharge through elementary strip,
[latex] d Q=5 d y \times u[/latex]
[latex] \therefore [/latex] Total discharge,
[latex] \begin{aligned} Q&=\int_{0}^{2}(5 d y)\left(1.25 y^{\sqrt{6}}\right) \\ \Rightarrow Q&=6.25 \int_{0}^{2} y^{1 / 6} d y=6.25 \times\left[\frac{y^{1 / 6+1}}{\frac{1}{6}+1}\right]_{0}^{2}\\ \because \quad Q&=12.026 \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore [/latex] Discharge per unit width,
[latex] q=\frac{12.026}{5}=2.405 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} / \mathrm{m}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A car follows a slow moving truck (travelling at a speed of 10 m/s) on a two-lane two-way highway. The car reduces its speed to 10 m/s and follows the truck maintaining a distance of 16 m from the truck. On finding a clear gap in the opposing traffic stream, the car accelerates at an average rate of 4 m/[latex]s^2[/latex], overtakes the truck and returns to its original lane. When it returns to its original lane, the distance between the car and the truck is 16 m. The total distance covered by the car during this period (from the time it leaves its lane and subsequently returns to its lane after overtaking) is
raw_source.solution:
Overtaking time,
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \quad T=\sqrt{\frac{4 S}{a}}=\sqrt{\frac{4 \times 16}{4}}=4 \mathrm{sec} \\ S=\text { Space heady way }=16 \mathrm{m} \\ a=\text { Acceleration }=4 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{array}[/latex]
Distance travelled by vehicle [latex]=S_{2} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} S_{2} &=u T+\frac{1}{2} a T^{2} \\ &=10 \times 4+\frac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 4^{2}=72 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning

raw_source.text: A level instrument at a height of 1.320 m has been placed at a station having a Reduced Level (RL) of 112.565 m. The instrument reads -2.835 m on a levelling staff held at the bottom of a bridge deck. The RL (in m) of the bottom of the bridge deck is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} &\text { RL of bottom of bridge deck }\\ &=112.565+1.320+(2.835)\\ &=116.720 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The value (up to two decimal places) of a line integral [latex]\int_{c}\vec{F}(\vec{r}).\vec{dr},\: \: for\: \vec{F}(\vec{r})=x^{2}\hat{i}+y^{2}\hat{j}[/latex] along C which is a straight line joining (0,0) to (1,1) is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \bar{F}&=x^{2}\bar{i}+y^{2}\bar{j} \\ \int \bar{F}.d\bar{r}&=\int \left ( x^{2}\bar{i}+y^{2}\bar{j} \right ).\left ( dx\bar{i}+dy\bar{j} \right ) \\   &=\int x^{2}dx+y^{2}dy\\ (0, 0)\text{ to }&(1, 1) \text{ line is }y=x\\  &=\int x^{2}dx+x^{2}dx=\int_{0}^{1}2x^{2}dx \\   &=2\left.\begin{matrix} \left ( \frac{x^{3}}{3} \right ) \end{matrix}\right|_{0}^{1}=\frac{2}{3}=0.666 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: An 8 m long simply-supported elastic beam of rectangular cross-section (100 mm x 200mm) is subjected to a uniformly distributed load of 10 kN/m over its entire span. The maximum principal stress (in MPa, up to two decimal places) at a point located at the extreme compression edge of a cross-section and at 2 m from the support is ______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} V_A+V_B&=80\\ V_A&=V_B=40\\ &\text{[Due to symmetry]}\\ M_A&=(-10\times 2 \times 1)+40 \times 2\\ &=60 kNm \end{aligned}[/latex]

At extreme compression edge,
Bending stress,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma &=\frac{My}{I}\\ &=\frac{(60 \times 10^6) \times \frac{200}{2}}{100 \times \frac{200^3}{12}}\\ &=90MPa \end{aligned}[/latex]
Direct share stress = 0
Principal stress,
[latex]\sigma_{p1}/\sigma_{p2}=\frac{90+0}{2}\pm \frac{1}{2}\sqrt{(0-90)^2+y(0)^2}[/latex]
[latex]\sigma_{p1}=90 MPa[/latex]
So, pricipal stress [latex]=90 N/mm^2=90MPa[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A prismatic beam P-Q-R of flexural rigidity [latex]EI=1\times 10^{4}kNm^{2}[/latex] is subjected to a moment of 180 kNm at Q as shown in the figure.

The rotation at Q (in rad, up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} K_{Q} &=K_{Q P}+K_{Q R} \\ &=\frac{4 E I}{5}+\frac{4 E I}{4}=1.8 \mathrm{EI} \\ \theta_{Q} &=\frac{M_{Q}}{K_{Q}}=\frac{180}{1.8 \times 10^{4}}=0.01 \mathrm{rad} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Alternate solution
[latex] \begin{aligned} &\begin{aligned} M_{Q P} &=M_{f Q P}+\frac{2 E I}{l}\left[2 \theta_{Q}+\theta_{P}\right] \\ &=\frac{4 \times 10^{4}}{5} \times \theta_{Q}=8000 \theta_{Q} \\ M_{Q R}=& M_{f Q R}+\frac{2 E I}{l}\left[2 \theta_{Q}+\theta_{R}\right] \\ & \quad\left\{M_{f Q R}=0, \theta_{R}=0\right\} \\ &=\frac{2 \times 10^{4}}{4}\left[2 \theta_{Q}\right]=10000 Q \\ \Sigma M_{Q} &=0 \end{aligned} \\ &\Rightarrow \quad M_{Q P}+M_{Q R}+180=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad 18000 \cdot \theta_{Q}=-180 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \theta_{Q}=0.01 \;\text{radian (anticlockwise)} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A prismatic propped cantilever beam of span L and plastic moment capacity [latex]M_{p}[/latex] is subjected to a concentrated load at its mid-span. If the collapse load of the beam is [latex]\alpha \frac{M_{p}}{L}[/latex], the value of [latex]\alpha[/latex] is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]P_{u}=\frac{6M_{P}}{l}[/latex] So, [latex]\alpha =6[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A 6 m long simply-supported beam is prestressed as shown in the figure.

The beam carries a uniformly distributed load of 6 kN/m over its entire span. If the effective flexural rigidity [latex]EI=2\times 10^{4}kN/m^{2}[/latex] and the effective prestressing force is 200 kN, the net increase in length of the prestressing cable (in mm, up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Span of PSC beam }&=6 \mathrm{m} \\ E I&=2 \times 10^{4} \mathrm{kNm}^{2} \\ &=2 \times 10^{13} \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ P&=200 \mathrm{kN} \\ \text { Total UDL }&=6 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m} \\ \text { eccentricity }&=e=50 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
(a) Slope of beam due to P-force
[latex]\theta_{1}=\frac{P \cdot e \cdot L}{2 E I}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{array}{l} =\frac{200 \times 10^{3} \times 50 \times 6000}{2 \times 2 \times 10^{13}} \\ =1.5 \times 10^{-3} \text {(upward) } \end{array}[/latex]
(b) Slope of beam due to UDL
[latex] \theta_{2}=\frac{w^{3}}{24 E I}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{array}{l} =\frac{6 \times(6000)^{3}}{24 \times 2 \times 10^{13}} \\ =(+) 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \text {(downward) } \end{array}[/latex]
(c) Net slope of beam
[latex] \begin{aligned} \theta &=\theta_{1}+\theta_{2} \\ &=(-) 1.5 \times 10^{-3}+(+) 2.7 \times 10^{-3} \\ &=1.2 \times 10^{-3} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Total net increase in length
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=2 e \theta \\ &=2 \times 50 \times 1.2 \times 10^{-3} \\ &=0.12 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A cable PQ of length 25 m is supported at two ends at the same level as shown in the figure. The horizontal distance between the supports is 20 m. A point load of 150 kN is applied at point R which divides it into two equal parts.

Neglecting the self-weight of the cable, the tension (in kN, in integer value) in the cable due to the applied load will be _____
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} 12.5^{2} &=x^{2}+10^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \; \; x &=7.5\; \text{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Bending moment at S=0 {consider the left part}
[latex]\begin{aligned} H_{P}\times 7.5 &=75\times 10 \\ H_{P} &=100\; \text{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Tension in cable
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=\sqrt{H_{P}^{2}+V_{P}^{2}}=\sqrt{75^{2}+100^{2}} \\ &=125\; \text{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The compression curve (void ratio, e vs. effective stress, [latex]{\sigma_{v}}'[/latex] ) for a certain clayey soil is a straight line in a semi-logarithmic plot and it passes through the points [latex](e = 1.2; {\sigma_{v}}' = 50 kPa)[/latex] and [latex](e = 0.6; {\sigma_{v}}' = 800 kPa).[/latex] The compression index (up to two decimal places) of the soil is ______
raw_source.solution:
Compression Index
[latex] C_{c}=\frac{\Delta e}{\log \left(\frac{\bar{\sigma}_{1}}{\bar{\sigma}_{0}}\right)}=\frac{1.2-0.6}{\log \left(\frac{800}{50}\right)}[/latex]
[latex] C_{c}=\frac{0.6}{\log (16)}=\frac{0.6}{1.204}=0.4982[/latex]

raw_source.text: The total horizontal and vertical stresses at a point X in a saturated sandy medium are 170 kPa and 300 kPa, respectively. The static pore-water pressure is 30 kPa. At failure, the excess pore-water pressure is measured to be 94.50 kPa, and the shear stresses on the vertical and horizontal planes passing through the point X are zero. Effective cohesion is 0 kPa and effective angle of internal friction is [latex]36^{\circ}[/latex]. The shear strength (in kPa, up to two decimal places) at point X is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \because\quad \sigma_{n} &=\frac{300+170}{2}+\frac{300-170}{2} \cos 2 \alpha \\ \alpha &=45^{\circ}+\frac{36^{\circ}}{2}=63^{\circ} \\ \Rightarrow\quad \sigma_{n} &=196.79 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \sigma_{n}^{\prime} &=\sigma_{\mathrm{n}}-u=196.79-(30+94.5) \\ \sigma_{n}^{\prime} &=72.29 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \Rightarrow\quad \tau &=c+\sigma_{\mathrm{n}}^{\prime} \tan \phi \\ &=72.29 \text { tan } 36=52.52 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A group of nine piles in a 3 x 3 square pattern is embedded in a soil strata comprising dense sand underlying recently filled clay layer, as shown in the figure. The perimeter of an individual pile is 126 cm. The size of pile group is 240 cm x 240 cm. The recently filled clay has undrained shear strength of 15 kPa and unit weight of [latex]16 kN/m^{3}[/latex]

The negative frictional load (in kN, up to two decimal places) acting on the pile group is______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]3 \times 3 [/latex] pile group
Negative skin friction for group.
[latex] =\alpha \bar{c}(4 B L)+ [/latex] weight of soil in
negative zone.
[latex] \begin{aligned} =& \alpha \bar{c}(4 B L)+\gamma(\text { Area } \times \text { length }] \\ =& 1 \times 15[4 \times 2.4 \times 2]+16\left[2.4^{2} \times 2\right] \\ &=472.32 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Negative skin friction in individual action.
[latex] \begin{array}{l} =n[\alpha \bar{c} \text { (perimeter } \times l] \\ =9[0.5 \times 15 \times 1.26 \times 2] \\ \text { [Assume } \alpha=0.5] \\ =170.1 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{array}[/latex]
Negative skin friction is maximum of above
(two)
[latex] Q_{n t}=472.32 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A three-fluid system (immiscible) is connected to a vacuum pump. The specific gravity values of the fluids (S1, S2) are given in the figure.

The gauge pressure value (in [latex]kN/m^{2}[/latex], up to two decimal places) of [latex]p_{1}[/latex] is ______
raw_source.solution:
Taking [latex]P_{1}[/latex] is in gauge pressure.
[latex] \begin{aligned} P_{A}=& P_{1}+\left(0.88 \times 10^{3}\right) \cdot(9.81)(0.5) \\ &+\left(0.95 \times 10^{3}\right)(9.81)(1) \\ \left(10^{3}\right)(9.81)(0.5)=& P_{1}+\left(0.88 \times 10^{3}\right) \cdot(9.81)(0.5) \\ &+\left(0.95 \times 10^{3}\right)(9.81)(1) \\ P_{1}=&-8.73 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The total rainfall in a catchment of area [latex]1000\: km^{2}[/latex], during a 6 h storm, is 19 cm. The surface runoff due to this storm computed from triangular direct runoff hydrograph is [latex]1 \times 10^8 m^{3}[/latex]. The [latex]\phi _{index}[/latex] for this storm (in cm/h, up to one decimal place) is ______
raw_source.solution:
Surface runoff [latex]=\frac{1\times 10^{8}m^{3}}{1000\times 10^{6}m^{2}} =0.1 m=10 cm [/latex]
Total rainfall = 19cm
Rainfall intensity [latex]=\frac{19}{6}=3.167 cm/hr[/latex]
w-Index [latex]= \frac{P-Q}{t} =\frac{\text{Total Infiltration}}{\text{Total duration of storm}} [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \;\; w-Index=\frac{19-10}{6}=1.5 cm/hr[/latex]
As intensity of rainfall [latex] \gt [/latex]w-Index
And rainfall intensity is uniform therefore [latex]\phi[/latex]-index = w-Index= 1.5 cm/hr.

raw_source.text: A rough pipe of 0.5 m diameter, 300 m length and roughness height of 0.25 mm, carries water (kinematic viscosity [latex]0.9\times 10^{-6}\: \: m^{2}/s[/latex]) with velocity of 3 m/s. Friction factor (f) for laminar flow is given by [latex]f=64/R_{e}[/latex], and for turbulent flow it is given by [latex]\frac{1}{\sqrt{f}}=2\log_{10}\left ( \frac{r}{k} \right )+1.74[/latex] where, [latex]R_e[/latex] = Reynolds number, r = radius of pipe, k = roughness height and [latex]g=9.81\: \: m/s^{2}[/latex]. The head loss (in m, up to three decimal places) in the pipe due to friction is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} R e &=\frac{\rho \cdot V \cdot D}{\mu}=\frac{V \cdot D}{v}=\frac{3 \times(0.5)}{0.9 \times 10^{-6}} \\ &=1.67 \times 10^{6}\\ \text{Means }R e&>2000 \text{ turbulent flow.}\\ \text{So, }\quad \frac{1}{\sqrt{f}}&=2 \log _{10} \frac{D}{2 k_{s}}+1.74 \\ \frac{1}{\sqrt{f}} &=2 \log _{10} \frac{0.5}{2 \times 0.25 \times 10^{-3}}+1.74 \\ f &=0.01669 \\ h_{f} &=\frac{f \cdot L \cdot V^{2}}{2 g D}=\frac{(0.01669)(300)(3)^{2}}{2 \times 9.81 \times 0.5} \\ &=4.594 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A flocculation tank contains [latex]1800\: m^{3}[/latex] of water, which is mixed using paddles at an average velocity gradient G of 100/s. The water temperature and the corresponding dynamic viscosity are [latex]30^{\circ}C\: \: and \: \: 0.798\times 10^{-3}\: \: Ns/m^{2}[/latex] respectively. The theoretical power required to achieve the stated value of G (in kW, up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution:
Power required
[latex] \begin{aligned} P &=\mu \mathrm{VG}^{2} \\ &=0.798 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{Ns} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \times 1800 \mathrm{m}^{3} \times(1005)^{2} \\ &=14364 \mathrm{Nm} / \mathrm{s} \text { or } \mathrm{Watt} \\ &=14.364 \mathrm{kW} \\ &=14.36 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A coal containing 2% sulfur is burned completely to ash in a brick kiln at a rate of 30 kg/min. The sulfur content in the ash was found to be 6% of the initial amount of sulfur present in the coal fed to the brick kiln. The molecular weights of S, H and O are 32, 1 and 16 g/mole, respectively. The annual rate of sulfur dioxide ([latex]SO_{2}[/latex]) emission from the kiln (in tonnes/year, up to two decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution:
Coal burned in one year
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=30\times 24\times 60\times 365 \\ &=1.5768\times 10^{7}\: \text{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Sulfur content=[latex]\frac{2}{100}\times 1.5768\times 10^{7}\times 10^{-6}[/latex]
[latex] =315.36\; tonnes/year[/latex]
Sulphur content in ash
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=\frac{6}{100}\times 315.36 \\ &= 18.92\; tonnes/year \end{aligned}[/latex]
Sulphur converted to [latex]SO_{2}=315.36-18.92[/latex]
[latex] =296.44\; tonnes/year[/latex]
[latex]\; \; \; S\, +\, O_{2}\rightarrow SO_{2}[/latex]
1 mole of S is present in 1 mole of [latex]SO_{2}[/latex]
32 gm of S is present in 64 gm of [latex]SO_{2}[/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Rate of [latex]SO_{2}[/latex] emission
[latex]=\frac{64}{32}\times 296.44=592.88\: tonnes/year[/latex]

raw_source.text: At a small water treatment plant which has 4 filters, the rates of filtration and backwashing are 200 [latex]m^{3}/d/m^{2}[/latex] and 1000 [latex]m^{3}/d/m^{2}[/latex], respectively. Backwashing is done for 15 min per day. The maturation, which occurs initially as the filter is put back into service after cleaning, takes 30 min. It is proposed to recover the water being wasted during backwashing and maturation. The percentage increase in the filtered water produced (up to two decimal places) would be ______
raw_source.solution:
Let total area of filters be [latex]1 \mathrm{m}^{2} [/latex]
Water used for backwashing
[latex] =1000 \times \frac{15}{24 \times 60}=10.4166 \mathrm{m}^{3}[/latex]
Water used for maturation
[latex] =200 \times \frac{30}{24 \times 60}=4.166 \mathrm{m}^{3}[/latex]
Total water wasted for backwashing and
maturation
[latex] =10.4166+4.166=14.58 \mathrm{m}^{3}[/latex]
Water to be treated by filtered
[latex] =200 \times \frac{23.25}{24}=193.75 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{day}[/latex]
% increase in filtered water produced
[latex] =\frac{14.58}{193.75} \times 100=7.525 \%[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A schematic flow diagram of a completely mixed biological reactor with provision for recycling of solids is shown in the figure.

The mean cell residence time (in days, up to one decimal place) is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \theta_{C} &=\frac{V X}{\left(Q_{0}-Q_{w}\right) X e+Q_{w} X_{u}} \\ &=\frac{Q_{0} H R T X}{\left(Q_{0}-Q_{w}\right) X_{e}+Q_{w} X_{u}}\left(X_{e}=0\right)\\ &=\frac{15000 \times \frac{2}{24} \times 3000}{50 \times 10000}=7.5 \text{ days} \end{aligned}\\[/latex]

raw_source.text: The space mean speed (kmph) and density (vehicles/km) of a traffic stream are linearly related. The free flow speed and jam density are 80 kmph and 100 vehicles/km respectively. The traffic flow (in vehicles/h, up to one decimal place) corresponding to a speed of 40 kmph is ______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} V_{t}=\text { Free mean speed }=50 \mathrm{kmph} \\ k_{j}=\text { Jam density }=100 \mathrm{veh} / \mathrm{km} \end{array}[/latex]
As per linear model (green-shield)
[latex] V=V_{f}\left(1-\frac{k}{k_{j}}\right)[/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow [/latex] Density @ speed =40 kmph
[latex] 40 =80\left(1-\frac{k}{100}\right)=50 \mathrm{veh} / \mathrm{km}[/latex]
Traffic flow @ density 50 veh/km @ speed
[latex] 40 \mathrm{kmph} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} q=V k \\ q=V_{f}\left(k-\frac{k^{2}}{k_{j}}\right)\\ \Rightarrow \quad 80\left(50-\frac{50^{2}}{100}\right)=2000 \mathrm{veh} / \mathrm{hr} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 7.5 m wide two-lane road on a plain terrain is to be laid along a horizontal curve of radius 510 m. For a design speed of 100 kmph, super-elevation is provided as per IRC: 73-1980. Consider acceleration due to gravity as 9.81 [latex]m/s^{2}[/latex]. The level difference between the inner and outer edges of the road (in m, up to three decimal places) is _____
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} e &=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{225 R}=\frac{100^{2}}{225 \times 510} \\ &=0.0871 \times 0.07=\tan \theta \\ \sin \theta & \simeq 0.07 \\ x &=7.5 \times \sin \theta=0.525 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Which one of the following is NOT a correct statement?
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Let}\;y &=\sqrt[x]{x}\;\;x \gt 0 \\ y&=x^{\frac{1}{x}} \\ \ln y&=\ln x^{\frac{1}{x}} \\ \ln y &=\frac{1}{x} \ln x \\ \frac{1}{y} \frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{1}{x^2}-\frac{\ln x}{x^2} \\ \frac{1}{y} \frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{1}{x^2}(1-\ln x) \\ \frac{dy}{dx}&= \frac{y}{x^2}(1-\ln x)\\ \text{put}\;\; \frac{dy}{dx}&=0\Rightarrow \frac{y}{x^2}(1-\ln x)=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; x&=e \\ \text{Now,}\;\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} &=\frac{-y}{x^3}-\frac{2y}{x^3}(1- \ln x)+\frac{1}{x^2}(1-\ln x)\frac{dy}{dx} \\ \text{At}\; x &=e, \\ \frac{d^2y}{dx^2}&=\left ( \frac{-y}{x^3} \right )_{x=e}-\frac{2y}{x^3}(1-\ln e)+\frac{1}{x^2}(1- \ln e)\frac{dy}{dx} \\ &= \left ( \frac{-x^{\frac{1}{x}}}{x} \right )_{at\; x=e}\\ &=\frac{-e^{\frac{1}{e}}}{e}=0\\ \frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\; & \text{has maximum at }\; x=e \end{aligned}[/latex]
options: The function [latex]\sqrt[x]{x},(x \gt 0)[/latex], has the global maxima at [latex]x=e[/latex]
The function [latex]\sqrt[x]{x},(x \gt 0)[/latex], has the global minima at [latex]x=e[/latex]
The function [latex]x^3[/latex] has neither global minima nor global maxima
The function |x| has the global minima at x=0

raw_source.text: Consider two functions: [latex]x=\psi ln\phi[/latex] and [latex]y=\phi ln\psi[/latex]. Which one of the following is the correct expression for [latex]\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial x}[/latex]?
raw_source.solution:
Taking the partial derivative with respect to x for the two equations, we get
[latex]\begin{aligned} 1&=\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial x}\ln \phi +\frac{\psi }{\phi }\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial x}\\ 0&=\frac{\phi }{\psi }\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial x}+ \ln \psi \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial x} \end{aligned}[/latex]
From above two equations, we get
[latex]\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial x}=\frac{\ln \psi }{\ln \phi \ln \psi -1}[/latex]

peak 5 min rate = 160 veh/5min

raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} Q&=\frac{A_1A_2}{\sqrt{A_1^2-A_2^2}}\sqrt{2gh} \\ h&=x\left [ \frac{\rho H_g}{\rho _w}-1 \right ] \\ &=0.08(13.6-1)=1.008m \;\;(A_1=4A_2) \\ Q&=\frac{4A_2 \times A_2}{\sqrt{16A_2^2-A_2^2}}\times \sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times 1.008} \\ &= \frac{4}{\sqrt{15}} \times A_2 \times \sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times 1.008}\\ &= \frac{4}{\sqrt{15}} \times \frac{\pi}{4}(0.15)^2 \times \sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times 1.008} \\ Q&=0.081m^3/s \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A concentrated load of 500 kN is applied on an elastic half space. The ratio of the increase in vertical normal stress at depths of 2m and 4m along the point of the loading, as per Boussinesq's theory, would be ___
raw_source.solution:
As per Boussinesq's equation,
The vertical stress below the ground level at a depth, Z, vertically below the load,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma _Z&=\frac{3}{2\pi}\frac{Q}{Z^2}\\ \sigma _Z &\propto \frac{1}{Z^2}\\ \therefore \;\; \frac{\sigma _{Z_1}}{\sigma _{Z_2}}&=\left [ \frac{Z_2}{Z_1} \right ]^2\\ &=\left [ \frac{4}{2} \right ]^2=4 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Which one of the following is NOT a correct statement?
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Let}\;y &=\sqrt[x]{x}\;\;x \gt 0 \\ y&=x^{\frac{1}{x}} \\ \ln y&=\ln x^{\frac{1}{x}} \\ \ln y &=\frac{1}{x} \ln x \\ \frac{1}{y} \frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{1}{x^2}-\frac{\ln x}{x^2} \\ \frac{1}{y} \frac{dy}{dx}&=\frac{1}{x^2}(1-\ln x) \\ \frac{dy}{dx}&= \frac{y}{x^2}(1-\ln x)\\ \text{put}\;\; \frac{dy}{dx}&=0\Rightarrow \frac{y}{x^2}(1-\ln x)=0 \\ \Rightarrow \; x&=e \\ \text{Now,}\;\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} &=\frac{-y}{x^3}-\frac{2y}{x^3}(1- \ln x)+\frac{1}{x^2}(1-\ln x)\frac{dy}{dx} \\ \text{At}\; x &=e, \\ \frac{d^2y}{dx^2}&=\left ( \frac{-y}{x^3} \right )_{x=e}-\frac{2y}{x^3}(1-\ln e)+\frac{1}{x^2}(1- \ln e)\frac{dy}{dx} \\ &= \left ( \frac{-x^{\frac{1}{x}}}{x} \right )_{at\; x=e}\\ &=\frac{-e^{\frac{1}{e}}}{e}=0\\ \frac{d^2y}{dx^2}\; & \text{has maximum at }\; x=e \end{aligned}[/latex]
options: The function [latex]\sqrt[x]{x},(x \gt 0)[/latex], has the global maxima at [latex]x=e[/latex]
The function [latex]\sqrt[x]{x},(x \gt 0)[/latex], has the global minima at [latex]x=e[/latex]
The function [latex]x^3[/latex] has neither global minima nor global maxima
The function |x| has the global minima at x=0

raw_answer.option_text: The function [latex]\sqrt[x]{x},(x \gt 0)[/latex], has the global minima at [latex]x=e[/latex]

raw_source.text: A one-dimensional domain is discretized into N sub-domains of width [latex]\Delta x[/latex] with node numbers i=0,1, 2, 3,...,N. If the time scale is discretized in steps of [latex]\Delta t[/latex], the forward-time and centered-space finite difference approximation at [latex]i^{th}[/latex] node and [latex]n^{th}[/latex] time step, for the partial differential equation [latex]\frac{\partial v}{\partial t}=\beta \frac{\partial^2 v}{\partial x^2}[/latex] is
raw_source.solution:

The centred space finite difference approximation at [latex]i^{th}[/latex] node [latex]n^{th}[/latex] time step is

raw_source.text: A rectangular open channel has a width of 5 m and a bed slope of 0.001. For a uniform flow of depth 2 m, the velocity is 2 m/s. The Manning's roughness coefficient for the channel is
raw_source.solution:
Given,
[latex]\begin{aligned} V&= 2 m/sec, \; S=0.001\\ A&=5 \times 2=10m^2\\ P&=5+2+2=9m\\ & \text{Hydraulic mean radius}\\ (R)&=\frac{A}{P}=\frac{10}{9}\\ V&=\frac{1}{n}R^{2/3}S^{1/2}\\ 2&=\frac{1}{n}\left ( \frac{10}{9} \right )^{2/3}(0.001)^{1/2}\\ n&=0.0169\simeq 0.017 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
For the following statements:

P: The lateral stress in the soil while being tested in an oedometer is always at-rest.
Q: For a perfectly rigid strip footing at deeper depths in a sand deposit, the vertical normal contact stress at the footing edge is greater than that at its centre.
R: The corrections for overburden pressure and dilatancy are not applied to measured SPT-N values in case of clay deposits.

The correct combination of the statements is
raw_source.solution:
P: True
In the Oedometer test, stress is applied to the soil specimen along the vertical axis, while strain in the horizontal direction is prevented by the confining ring (a condition of zero lateral strain). Thus it simulates at-rest condition.

Q: True
For a perfectly rigid footing resting on surface of sand deposit, the contact pressure distribution is zero at the edges and maximum at centre. However, for a very deep rigid footing on sand, the contact pressure distribution may tend to become like that of rigid footing on clayey soil, with edge contact stress greater than at its centre.

R: True
For cohesive soil, there is no need for overburden pressure correction (Peck et al 1974). For cohesionless soil at first overburden pressure correction is made, then if it is fine sand or silt under water table with N-value [latex]\gt[/latex] 15, dilatancy correction is made.

raw_source.text: Consider two functions: [latex]x=\psi ln\phi[/latex] and [latex]y=\phi ln\psi[/latex]. Which one of the following is the correct expression for [latex]\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial x}[/latex]?
raw_source.solution:
Taking the partial derivative with respect to x for the two equations, we get
[latex]\begin{aligned} 1&=\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial x}\ln \phi +\frac{\psi }{\phi }\frac{\partial \phi }{\partial x}\\ 0&=\frac{\phi }{\psi }\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial x}+ \ln \psi \frac{\partial \phi }{\partial x} \end{aligned}[/latex]
From above two equations, we get
[latex]\frac{\partial \psi }{\partial x}=\frac{\ln \psi }{\ln \phi \ln \psi -1}[/latex]

The shear force acting on nail at 'P'.
