raw_source.text:
Sedimentation basin in a water treatment plant is designed for a flow rate of 0.2 [latex]m^3/s[/latex]. The basin is rectangular with a length of 32m, width of 8m, and depth of 4m. Assume that the settling velocity of these particles is governed by the Stokes' law. Given:
density of the particles = 2.5 [latex]g/cm^3[/latex];
density of water = 1 [latex]g/cm^3[/latex];
dynamic viscosity of water = 0.01 g/(cm.s);
gravitational acceleration = 980 [latex]cm/s^2[/latex].

If the incoming water contains particles of diameter 25 [latex]\mu m[/latex](spherical and uniform), the removal efficiency of these particles is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} Q&=0.2m^3/sec,\; L=32m\\ B&=8m,\; H=4m\\ \rho _p&=2.5gm/cc=2500kg/m^3\\ \rho _w&=1gm/cc=1000kg/m^3\\ \mu &=0.01gm/cm-sec=1 \times 10^{-3}kg/m-sec\\ d&=25\mu m=25 \times 10^{-6}m\\ g&=980cm/sec^2=9.8m/sec^2\\ v_0&=\frac{Q}{A_s}=\frac{Q}{L \times B}\\ &=\frac{0.2}{32 \times 8}=7.8125 \times 10^{-4}m/sec\\ v_s&=\frac{g(\rho _p-\rho _w)d^2}{18\mu }\\ &=\frac{9.8(2500-1000)\times (25 \times 10^{-6})^2}{18 \times (1 \times 10^{-3})}\\ &=5.1041 \times 10^{-4}m/sec\\ \eta &=\frac{v_s}{v_0}\times 100\\ &=\frac{5.1041 \times 10^{-4}}{7.8125 \times 10^{-4}}\times 100\\ &=65.33\%\simeq 65\% \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A survey line was measured to be 285.5 m with a tape having a nominal length of 30 m. On checking, the true length of the tape was found to be 0.05 m too short. If the line lay on a slope of 1 in 10, the reduced length (horizontal length) of the line for plotting of survey work would be
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} L&=30m, \; L'=30-0.05=29.95m\\ \therefore \;\;& \; \text{Correct Length}\\ l&=l' \times \frac{l'}{L}\\ &=285.5 \times \frac{29.95}{30}=285.024m\\ D&=l \cos \theta \\ \cos \theta &=\frac{10}{\sqrt{10^2+1^2}}=0.995\\ \therefore \;D \;&\; =\text{ correct Horizontal length }\\ &=l\cos \theta \\ &=285.024 \times 0.9950\\ &=283.6m \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A 16 mm thick gusset plate is connected to the 12 mm thick flange plate of an I-section using fillet welds on both sides as shown in the figure. The gusset plate is subjected to a point load of 350 kN acting at a distance of 100 mm from the flange plate. Size of fillet weld is 10 mm.

The maximum resultant stress (in MPa, round off to 1 decimalplace) on the fillet weld along the vertical plane would be ____
raw_source.solution:
Direct concentrated load (P) = 350 kN
Eccentricity (e) = 100 mm
Depth of weld ([latex]d_w[/latex]) at each face = 500 mm
Size of weld (S) = 10 mm
Throat thickness of weld ([latex]t_t[/latex]) = 0.7S = 7 mm
It is a case of combined shear (P) and Bending moment (M = P.e)
Shear stress acting on weld due to direct shear force P,
[latex]\begin{aligned} (q)&=\frac{P}{A_w} \\ &= \frac{P}{2d_wt_t}\\ &=\frac{350 \times 10^3}{2 \times 500 \times 7}=50MPa \end{aligned}[/latex]
Bending normal stress acting at [latex]i^{th}[/latex] point from Neutral axis [latex][f_i]=\frac{M}{I}y_i[/latex]
Maximum bending stress at extreme point in weld
[latex]\begin{aligned} [f]&=\frac{M}{I}y_{max} \\ &= \frac{Pe}{2t_t \frac{d_w^3}{12}} \times y_{max}\\ &= \frac{350 \times 10^3 \times 100}{2 \times 7 \times \frac{(500)^3}{12}} \times 250\\ &= 60MPa \end{aligned}[/latex]

As per IS800:2007. Maximum resultant stress an equivalent stress in fllet weld due to combined shear and bending stress
[latex]\begin{aligned} (f_{eq})&=\sqrt{f^2+3q^2} \\ &= \sqrt{60^2+3 \times 50^2}\\ &=105.3MPa \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A box measuring 50 cmx50cmx50cm is filled to the top with dry coarse aggregate of mass 187.5 kg. raw_source.text: A portal frame shown in figure has a hinge support at joint P and a roller support at joint R. A point load of 50 kN is acting at joint R in the horizontal direction. The flexural rigidity, EI, of each member is 10 [latex]kNm^2[/latex]. Under the applied load, the horizontal displacement (in mm, round off to 1 decimal place) of joint R would be _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \Sigma M_p&=0\;\;[\text{Take clockwise as positive}]\\ R_R \times 5-50 \times 10&=0\\ R_R&=-100kN(\downarrow )\\ R_P&=100kN(\uparrow )\\ EI&=10^6kN-m^2\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Using unit load method:
The horizontal displacement at 'R'
[latex]\delta _{HR}=\int_{0}^{L}\frac{M_xm_x}{EI}dx[/latex]
where
[latex]M_x=[/latex] BM at X-X due to real loads
[latex]m_x=[/latex] BM at X-X due to vertical unit load applied where we want to find the deflection.

[latex]\begin{aligned} \Sigma M_R &=0\;\;[\text{Take clockwise as positive}]\\ R_P \times 5-1 \times 10&=0\\ R_P&=2kN(\uparrow )\end{aligned}[/latex]
Sign conventions:
Sagging +ve
Hogging -ve

[latex]\delta _{HR}=\int_{0}^{5}\frac{200x^2}{10^6}dx+\int_{0}^{10}\frac{50x^2}{10^6}dx=\frac{1}{40}=0.025m=25mm[/latex]

raw_source.text: A sample of air analysed at 0[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and 1 atm pressure is reported to contain 0.02 ppm(parts per million) of [latex]NO_2[/latex]. Assume the gram molecular mass of [latex]NO_2[/latex] as 46 and its volume at 0[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and 1 atm pressure as 22.4 litres per mole. The equivalent [latex]NO_2[/latex] concentration (in microgram per cubic meter, round off to 2 decimalplaces) would be ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} k&=22.4\\ M&=46\\ 0.02\; \text{ppm of}\; NO_2&=0.02 \times \frac{M}{k}\times 10^3 \mu g/m^3\\ &=0.02 \times \frac{46}{22.4}\times 10^{3}\\ &=41.0714\mu g/m^3 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 0.80 m deep bed of sand filter (length 4 m and width 3 m) is made of uniform particles (diameter = 0.40 mm, specific gravity = 2.65, shape factor = 0.85) with bed porosity of 0.4. The bed has to be backwashed at a flow rate of 3.60 [latex]m^3/min[/latex]. During backwashing, if the terminal settling velocity of sand particles is 0.05 m/s, the expanded bed depth (in m, round off to 2 decimal places) is ________
raw_source.solution:
Given,
[latex]\begin{aligned} z &=0.8m \\ n &=0.4m \\ Q_B &=3.6m^3/min \\ &= \frac{3.6}{60}m^3/sec=0.06m^3/sec\\ L&=4m \\ B&= 3m\\ V_B&= \frac{Q_B}{A_s}=\frac{Q_B}{LB}\\ &= \frac{0.06}{4 \times 3}=5 \times 10^{-3}m/sec\\ V_s&= 0.05m/sec\\ V_B&=V_s(n_e)^{4.5} \\ (n_e)^{4.5}&= \frac{V_B}{V_s}=\frac{5 \times 10^{-3}}{0.05}\\ n_e&=\left ( \frac{5 \times 10^{-3}}{0.05} \right )^{\frac{1}{4.5}} \\ &= 0.599\simeq 0.6\\ \frac{z_e}{z}&=\frac{1-n}{1-n_e} \\ z_e &=z\left ( \frac{1-n}{1-n_e} \right ) \\ z_e&=0.8 \times \left ( \frac{1-0.4}{1-0.6} \right )=1.2m \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A wastewater is to be disinfected with 35 mg/Lof chlorine to obtain 99% kill of micro-organisms. The number of micro-organisms remaining alive ([latex]N_t[/latex]) at time t, is modelled by [latex]N_t=N_oe^{-kt}[/latex], where [latex]N_o[/latex] is number of micro-organisms at t= 0, and k is the rate of kill. The wastewater flow rate is 36 [latex]m^3/hr[/latex], and k= 0.23 [latex]min^{-1}[/latex]. If the depth and width of the chlorination tank are 1.5 m and 1.0 m, respectively, the length of the tank (in m, round off to 2 decimal places) is ________
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} N_t&=N_0e^{-kt}\\ \therefore \; \eta &=[1-e^{-kt}]100\\ 99&=[1-e^{-0.23\times t}]100\\ \therefore \;t&=20.22min\\ Q&=36m^3/hr\\ V&=Q \times t\\ &=\frac{36}{60}\times 20.22=12.0132\\ \text{Length}&=\frac{V}{B \times H}=\frac{12.0132}{1 \times 1.5}\\ &=8.008\cong 8m \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A staff is placed on a benchmark (BM) of reduced level (RL) 100.000 m and a theodolite is placed at a horizontal distance of 50 m from the BM to measure the vertical angles. The measured vertical angles from the horizontal at the staff readings of 0.400 m and 2.400 m are found to be the same. Taking the height of the instrument as 1.400m, the RL (in m) of the theodolite station is _____

raw_source.text: Consider the ordinary differential equation [latex]x^2\frac{d^2y}{dx^2}-2x\frac{dy}{dx}+2y=0[/latex]. Given the values of y(1)=0 and y(2)=2, the value of y(3) (round off to 1 decimal place), is ____

Average free flow speed and the jam density observed on a roadstretch are 60 km/h and 120 vehicles/km, respectively. For a linear speed-density relationship, the maximum flow on the road stretch (in vehicles/h) is _________

Maximum Speed / Free ?ow speed, [latex]V_m[/latex] = 60 kmph
Jam density, [latex]K_m[/latex] = 120 kmph
for linear speed - density (Green shield's model) relationship,
max. ?ow, is [latex]q_{max}=\frac{k_j}{2}\times \frac{V_f}{2}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Traffic on a highway is moving at a rate of 360 vehicles per hour at a location. If the number of vehicles arriving on this highway follows Poisson distribution, the probability (round off to 2 decimal places) that the headway between successive vehicles lies between 6 and 10 seconds is ______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]h_1=[/latex] 6 seconds, [latex]h_1=[/latex] 10 seconds
given, avg. rate, [latex]\lambda =360\;veh/hr=360\times \frac{1}{3600}=\frac{1}{10}\; veh/sec[/latex]
Probability that the headway is between [latex]h_1 \; and \; h_2[/latex] is given by,
[latex]\begin{aligned} P(h_1\leq h\leq h_2)&=e^{\lambda h_1}-e^{-\lambda h_2} \\ &= e^{-\frac{1}{10}\times 6}-e^{-\frac{1}{10}\times 10}\\ &= 0.1808\approx 0.18 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A parabolic vertical curve is being designed to join a road of grade +5% with a road of grade -3%. The length of the vertical curve is 400m measured along the horizontal. The hyetograph of a storm event of duration 140 minutesis shown in the figure.

The infiltration capacity at the start of this event (t=0) is 17 mm/hour, which linearly decreases to 10 mm/hour after 40 minutes duration. As the event progresses, the infiltration rate further drops down linearly to attain a value of 4 mm/hour at t=100 minutes and remains constant thereafter till the end of the storm event. The value of the infiltration index, [latex]\phi[/latex] (in mm/hour, round off to 2 decimal places), is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} P&=(4+8+15+10+8+3+1) \times \frac{20}{60} \\ &=16.33\; minute \\ Q&=(15-10) \times \frac{20}{60} +(10-8) \times \frac{20}{60} \\ &+(8-6) \times \frac{20}{60} +\frac{1}{2}\times 2 \times \frac{20}{60}+\frac{1}{2} \\ &+\frac{1}{2}\times 2 \times \frac{20}{60}+frac{1}{2}\times 2 \times \frac{20}{60}\\ &=4mm\\ W-index&=\frac{P-Q}{t}=\frac{16.33-4}{\frac{140}{60}}=5.28 mm/hr\\ \text{Since,} \; \phi & \geq W\\ \text{Assume, }\; \phi &=5.28 mm/hr\\ \Rightarrow \; \text{Corrected, }\phi &=\frac{16.33-4-4 \times \frac{20}{60}-3 \times \frac{20}{60}-1 \times \frac{20}{60}}{\left ( \frac{140-30-20-20}{60} \right )} \\ &=7.2475 mm/hr \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Two water reservoirs are connected by a siphon (running full) of total length 5000 m and diameter of 0.10m, as shown below

The inlet leg length of the siphon to its summit is 2000m. The difference in the water surface levels of the two reservoirs is 5 m. Assume the permissible minimum absolute pressure at the summit of siphon to be 2.5 m of water when running full. Given:
friction factor f=0.02 throughout,
atmospheric pressure= 10.3 m of water, and
acceleration due to gravity g= 9.81 [latex]m/s^2[/latex].

Considering only major loss using Darcy-Weisbach equation, the maximum height of the summit of siphon from the water level of upper reservoir,h (in m, round off to 1 decimal place)is _____
raw_source.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's equation between 1 & 3
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{P_1}{\rho g}+\frac{v_1^2}{2g}+z_1&= \frac{P_3}{\rho g}+\frac{v_3^2}{2g}+z_3+h_{f13}\\ z_1-z_3&=h_{f13}\;\;\;(\because \; P_1=P_3=P_{atm}\; and \; v_1=v_3=0) \\ 5&=\frac{fLv^2}{2gd} \\ v^2&=\frac{5 \times 2\times 9.81\times 0.1}{0.02\times 5000} \\ v&=0.313m/s \end{aligned}[/latex]
Applying Bernoulli's equation between 1 & 2
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{P_1}{\rho g}+\frac{v_1^2}{2g}+z_1&= \frac{P_2}{\rho g}+\frac{v_2^2}{2g}+z_2+h_{f12}\\ 10.3+0+0&=2.5+\frac{0.313^2}{2 \times 9.81}+h+\frac{0.02 \times 2000 \times 0.313^2}{2 \times 9.81 \times 0.1}\\ h&=5.798m \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider a laminar flow in the x-direction between two infinite parallel plates (Couette flow). The lower plate is stationary and the upper plate is moving with a velocity of 1 cm/s in the x-direction. The distance between the plates is 5 mm and the dynamic viscosity of the fluid is 0.01 [latex]N-s/m^2[/latex]. If the shear stress on the lower plate is zero, the pressure gradient, [latex]\frac{\partial p}{\partial x}[/latex], (in [latex]N/m^2[/latex] per m,round off to 1 decimal place)is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given fl\ow is a couette flow with pressure gradient
[latex]\mu =0.01N-s/m^2[/latex]
h=5mm
if [latex]\tau _{y=0}=0, \; \text{find}\; \frac{dp}{dx}[/latex]
The velocity distribution, for the couette flow with pressure gradient is given by
[latex]u=\frac{wy}{h}-\frac{1}{2\mu }\frac{dp}{dx}[hy-y^2][/latex]
where w is the velocity of the top plate and h is the gap between the plates
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{du}{dy}&=\frac{w}{h}-\frac{1}{2\mu }\frac{dp}{dx}[h-2y] \\ \left.\begin{matrix} \frac{du}{dy} \end{matrix}\right|_{y=0} &=\frac{w}{h}-\frac{1}{2\mu }\frac{dp}{dx}h \\ \tau _{y=0}&=\mu \left [ \frac{w}{h}-\frac{1}{2\mu }\frac{dp}{dx}h \right ] \\ \tau _{y=0}&=\frac{w\mu }{h}-\frac{1}{2}\frac{dp}{dx}h \\ \text{when}\; \tau _{y=0}&=0, \; \text{we will have}\\ \frac{1}{2}\frac{dp}{dx}h&=\frac{w\mu }{h}\\ \frac{dp}{dx}&=\frac{2w\mu }{h^2} \\ &=\frac{2 \times 1 \times 10^{-2}\times 0.01}{(5 \times 10^{-3})^2} \\ &=8 N/m^2 \; \text{per} \; m \end{aligned}[/latex]

The adhesion factor is 0.5. The Net Ultimate Pullout (uplift) Load for the pile (in kN, round off to 1 decimal place) is _______

raw_source.text: A granular soil has a saturated unit weight of 20[latex]kN/m^3[/latex] and an effective angle of shearing resistance of 30[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]. The unit weight of water is 9.81 [latex]kN/m^3[/latex]. A slope is to be made on this soil deposit in which the seepage occurs parallel to the slope up to the free surface. Under this seepage condition for a factor of safety of 1.5, the safe slope angle (in degree, round off to 1 decimal place) would be _____
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \gamma _{sat}&=20kN/m^3\\ \gamma _w&=9.81kN/m^3\\ \therefore \; \gamma '&=\gamma _{sat}-\gamma _w=10.19kN/m^3\\ \therefore \; \phi '&=30^{\circ},\; F=1.5 \end{aligned}[/latex]
For infnite slope, the F.O. safety for seepage parallel to the slope in a granular soil (C = 0) is given below
[latex]\begin{aligned} F&=\frac{\gamma '}{\gamma _{sat}}\frac{\tan \phi '}{\tan i}\\ 1.5&=\frac{10.19}{20}\frac{\tan 30}{\tan i}\\ i&=11.095 \; \text{say}\; 11.1^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A 3mx3m square precast reinforced concrete segments to be installed by pushing them through an existing railway embankment for making an underpass as shown in the figure. A reaction arrangement using precast PCC blocks placed on the ground is to be made for the jacks.

At each stage, the jacks are required to apply a force of 1875 kN to push the segment. The jacks will react against the rigid steel plate placed against the reaction arrangement. The footprint area of reaction arrangement on natural ground is 37.5 [latex]m^2[/latex]. The unit weight of PCC block is 24 [latex]kN/m^3[/latex]. The properties of the natural ground are: c = 17 kPa; [latex]\phi =25^{\circ}[/latex] and [latex]\gamma =18 kN/m^3[/latex]. Assuming that the reaction arrangement has rough interface and has the same properties that of soil, the factor of safety (round off to 1 decimal place) against shear failure is _____
raw_source.solution:
Weight of Precast PCC block,
[latex]W=volume \times \gamma _c=37.5 \times 7.5 \times 24=6750kN[/latex]
Shear resistance below the Precast PCC block is,
[latex]S = C.A + W\tan \phi[/latex]
F.O safety against shear failure,
[latex]\begin{aligned} F&=\frac{S}{T} \\ F&=\frac{C.A.+W \tan \phi }{T} \\ &= \frac{C.A.+N \tan \phi }{T}\;\;\; (Since, \; N=W)\\ &= \frac{17 \times 37.5+6750 \times \tan 25^{\circ}}{1875}\\ &= 2.0187\approx 2.0 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A square footing of 4 m side is placed at 1 m depth in a sand deposit. The dry unit weight ([latex]\gamma[/latex]) of sand is 15 [latex]kN/m^3[/latex]. This footing has an ultimate bearing capacity of 600 kPa. Consider the depth factors: [latex]d_q=d_\gamma =1.0[/latex] and the bearing capacity factor: [latex]N_\gamma =18.75[/latex]. This footing is placed at a depth of 2m in the same soil deposit. For a factor of safety of 3.0 as per Terzaghi's theory, the safe bearing capacity (in kPa) of this footing would be _______
raw_source.solution:
As per Terzaghi's theory, the ultimate bearing capacity for a square footing considering depth factors: [latex]d_q=d_\gamma =1[/latex] is as follows:
[latex]\begin{aligned} q_u&=1.3CN_C+\gamma D_fN_q+0.4\gamma BN_\gamma \\ &\text{For sand,} \\ C&=0 \\ q_u&=\gamma D_fN_q+0.4\gamma BN_\gamma \\ \text{Given:} \\ \gamma &=15kN/m^3 \\ B&=4m \\ N_\gamma &= 18.75\\ &\text{Initial condition: } \\ D_f&= 1m\\ q_u&=600kPa\\ q_u&=\gamma D_fN_q+0.4\gamma BN_\gamma \\ 600&=15 \times 1 \times N_q +0.4 \times 15 \times 4 \times 18.75\\ N_q&=10\\ \text{If}\;\; D_f&=2m, \;\; \text{then,}\\ q_u&=\gamma D_fN_q+0.4\gamma BN_\gamma \\ &=15 \times 2 \times 10 +0.4 \times 15 \times 4 \times 18.75\\ &=750kN/m^2\\ &\text{Net ultimate BC of soil, }\\ q_{nu}&=q_u-\gamma D_f\\ &=750-15 \times 2=720kN/m^2\\ &\text{The gross safe BC or safe BC, }\\ q_s&=\frac{q_{nu}}{F}+\gamma D_f\\ &=\frac{720}{3}+15 \times 2\\ &=270kPa \end{aligned}[/latex]

\vec{v} &=2\hat{i}(x+y)\hat{j}+xyz\hat{k} \\ 
 u&=2 \\

 &= 2(yz)+(x+y)(xz)+xyz(xy)\\

&At\;(1,1,2) \\ 
a_y&=11+2=4\\

&=4+2+2+2=10\\

raw_source.text: A vehicle is moving on a road of grade +4% at a speed of 20 m/s. Consider the coefficient of rolling friction as 0.46 and acceleration due to gravity as 10 [latex]m/s^2[/latex]. raw_source.text: Construction of a new building founded on a clayey soil was completed in January 2010. Jan. 2010 - Jan. 2014 (4 years)
Settlement is 10 mm
[latex]\Delta H = 40 mm[/latex]
2 - way drainage
Settlement in Jan. 2019 (in 9 years) = ?
In 4 years,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \%U &=\frac{\Delta h}{\Delta H}\times 100 \\ &= \frac{10}{40}\times 100=25\%\\ T_v&=C_v\frac{t}{d^2}\;\;\;\because \%U \lt 60\% \\ T_v&=\frac{\pi}{4}U^2 \\ \frac{\pi}{4}\left ( \frac{25}{100} \right )^2&=\frac{C_v}{d^2} \times 4 \; years...(1) \end{aligned}[/latex]
In 9 years
[latex]\begin{aligned} T_v&=C_v\frac{t}{d^2}\\ &=\frac{\pi }{4} \times\frac{(0.25)^2}{4}\times 9 \; \text{years}\\ &=0.11044\\ \because \; (T_v)_{60}&=0.283 \\ \therefore \;\%U &\lt 60\%\\ \therefore \;T_v&=0.11044=\frac{\pi}{4}U^2\\ \%U&=0.3749=37.499\%\\ \%U&=\frac{\Delta h}{\Delta H} \times 100\\ &=\frac{\Delta h}{40mm}\times 100=37.499\\ \Delta h&=14.99mm=15mm \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider the hemi-spherical tank of radius 13 m as shown in the figure. What is the volume of water (in [latex]m^3[/latex]) when the depth of water at the centre of the tank is 6 m?
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Volume of water}&=\frac{1}{3}\pi h^2(3r-h)\\ &=\frac{1}{3}\pi \times 6^2 \times (3 \times 13 -6)\\ &=396\pi \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
An ordinary differential equation is given below.
[latex]\left ( \frac{dy}{dx} \right )(x lnx)=y[/latex]
The solution for the above equation is
(Note: K denotes a constant in the options)
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{dy}{dx}(x \ln x) &=y \\ \frac{dy}{y}&=\frac{dx}{x \ln x} \\ \int \frac{dy}{y}&=\int \frac{1}{x \ln x}dx+ \ln K \\ \ln x&=t \\ \frac{1}{x}dx&=dt \\ \ln y&= \int \frac{dy}{t}+ \ln K\\ \ln y&=\ln t+ \ln K \\ \ln y&=Kt \\ y&=K \ln x \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
For a plane stress problem, the state of stress at a point P is represented by the stress element as shown in figure.
By how much angle ([latex]\theta[/latex]) in degrees the stress element should be rotated in order to get the planes of maximum shear stress?
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma _x&=80\\ \sigma _y&=-20\\ \sigma _z&=-25 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Angle of plane of max shear
[latex]\begin{aligned} \theta &=\theta _p+45^{\circ}\\ \tan 2\theta _p&=\frac{2\tau _{xy}}{\sigma _x-\sigma _y}\\ &=\frac{-50}{100}\\ \theta _p&=-13.28^{\circ}\\ \therefore \;\;\theta &=31.71^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The critical bending compressive stress in the extreme fibre of a structural steel section is 1000 MPa. It is given that the yield strength of the steel is 250 MPa, width of flange is 250 mm and thickness of flange is 15 mm. As per the provisions of IS:8002007, the non-dimensional slenderness ratio of the steel cross-section is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\lambda =\sqrt{\frac{f_y}{f_{cr}}}=\sqrt{\frac{250}{1000}}=0.5[/latex]

raw_source.text:
In the context of provisions relating to durability of concrete, consider the following assertions:

Assertion (1): As per IS 456-2000, air entrainment to the extent of 3% to 6% is required for concrete exposed to marine environment.

Assertion (2): The equivalent alkali content (in terms of [latex]Na_2O[/latex] equivalent) for a cement containing 1% and 0.6% of [latex]Na_2O[/latex] and [latex]K_2O[/latex], respectively, is approximately 1.4% (rounded to 1 decimal place).

Which one of the following statements is CORRECT?
raw_source.solution:
(1) As per clause 8.2.2.3 of IS 456-2000, entrained air percentage of 3 to 6% is required to resist freezing and thawing,
i.e. not for marine environment.
Hence, Assertion (1) is wrong
Equivalent alkali content is terms of [latex]Na_2O[/latex]
[latex] = [Na_2 O] + 0.685 [K_2 O][/latex]
[latex] = 1 + 0.685 \times 0.6 = 1.41 \%[/latex]
Hence, Assertion (2) is correct
raw_source.tag2: Working Stress and Limit State Method
options: Assertion (1) is FALSE and Assertion (2) is TRUE
Assertion (1) is TRUE and Assertion (2) is FALSE
Both Assertion (1) and Assertion (2) are FALSE
Both Assertion (1) and Assertion (2) are TRUE

raw_answer.option_text: Assertion (1) is FALSE and Assertion (2) is TRUE

It achieves 50 percent of disinfection efficiency measured in terms of killing the indicator microorganisms (E-Coli) in 3 minutes. The minimum time required to achieve 99 percent disinfection efficiency would be

A camera with a focal length of 20 cm fitted in an aircraft is used for taking vertical aerial photographs of a terrain. The average elevation of the terrain is 1200 m above mean sea level (MSL). What is the height above MSL at which an aircraft must fly in order to get the aerial photographs at a scale of 1:8000?
raw_source.solution:
Given focal length = 20 cm
as we know scale of vertical photograph [latex]=\frac{f}{H-h_{avg}}[/latex]
its given as 1 : 8000
Hence,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{f}{H-h_{avg}} &=\frac{1}{8000} \\ \frac{20 cm}{(H-1200) \times 100cm}&=\frac{1}{8000} \\ \Rightarrow \;\;H &=2800m \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Remote Sensing, GIS, GPS and Photogrammetry

raw_source.text:
A flexible pavement has the following class of loads during a particular hour of the day.

i. 80 buses with 2-axles (each axle load of 40 kN);
ii. 160 trucks with 2-axles (front and rear axle loads of 40 kN and 80 kN, respectively)

The equivalent standard axle load repetitions for this vehicle combination as per IRC:37-2012 would be
raw_source.solution:
(i) 80 buses with 2 axle with 40 kN each.
[latex]N_1=80 \times 2=160[/latex]
[latex]L_1=40kN[/latex]
[latex]160 \text{ truks} \left\{\begin{matrix} \text{Front axle}\rightarrow 40kN\\ \text{Rear axle}\rightarrow 80kN \end{matrix}\right.[/latex]
[latex]N_1=160,\;L_1=40kN[/latex]
[latex]N_2=160,\;L_2=80kN[/latex]
[latex]\text{Total no. of repetitions}\left\{\begin{matrix} &\text{For}\; 40kN=160+160=320\\ &\text{For}\; 80kN=160 \end{matrix}\right.[/latex]
[latex]N_1=320,\;L_1=40kN[/latex]
[latex]N_2=160,\;L_2=80kN[/latex]
As per 4th power law
[latex]\begin{aligned} N_s&=N_1\left ( \frac{L_1}{L_5} \right )^4 +N_2 \left ( \frac{L_2}{L_5} \right )^4 \\ &= 320\left ( \frac{40}{80} \right )^4+160\left ( \frac{80}{80} \right )^4\\ &= 20+160=180 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The inverse of the matrix [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 3 & 4\\ 4& 3 & 1\\ 1 & 2 & 4 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] is
raw_source.solution:
det (A) = 2(12 - 2) - 3 (16 - 1) + 4 (8 -3)
= 2(10) - 3 (15) + 4(5)
det (A) = - 5
Minor of 2 = 12 - 2 = 10
Minor of 3 = 16 - 1 = 15
Minor of 4 = 8- 3 = 5
Minor of 4 = 12 - 8 = 4
Minor of 3 = 8 - 4 = 4
Minor of 1 = 4 - 3 = 1
Minor of 1 = 3 - 12 = -9
Minor of 2 = 2 - 16 = -14
Minor of 4 = 6 - 12 = -6
Cofactors of [latex]A=\begin{bmatrix} 10 &-15 &5 \\ -4& 4 & -1\\ -9& 14 &-6 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{adj} \;A &= (\text{cofactors of A})^T \\ \text{adj} \;A &=\begin{bmatrix} 10 &-4 &-9 \\ -15& 4 &14 \\ 5& -1 &-6 \end{bmatrix} \\ \therefore \;A^{-1}=\frac{\text{adj} \;A}{|A|} &=\frac{-1}{5}\begin{bmatrix} 10 &-4 &-9 \\ -15& 4 &14 \\ 5& -1 &-6 \end{bmatrix}\\ A^{-1}&=\begin{bmatrix} -2 &\frac{4}{5} &\frac{9}{5} \\ 3& \frac{-4}{5} & \frac{-14}{5}\\ -1& \frac{1}{5} &\frac{6}{5} \end{bmatrix} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A plane frame shown in the figure has linear elastic springs at node H. The spring constants are [latex]k_x=k_y=5 \times 10^5kN/m[/latex] and [latex]k_\theta =3 \times 10^5kNm/rad[/latex].

For the externally applied moment of 30 kNm at node F, the rotation (in degrees, round off to 3 decimals) observed in the rotational spring at node H is_____
raw_source.solution:
No moment can be taken by segment FE.
[latex]\therefore \;\;M_{FE}=0[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} M_\theta &=k_\theta \times \theta \\ 30kNm&=3 \times 10^5 \times \theta \\ \theta &=1 \times 10^{-4} \; \text{radians} \\ &=0.0057^{\circ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Torsion of Shafts and Pressure Vessels

raw_source.text:
A rolled I-section beam is supported on a 75 mm wide bearing plate as shown in the figure. Thicknesses of flange and web of the I-section are 20 mm and 8 mm, respectively. Root radius of the I-section is 10 mm. Assume: material yield stress, [latex]f_y=250 MPa[/latex] and partial safety factor for material, [latex]\gamma _{mo}=1.10[/latex].

As per IS: 800-2007, the web bearing strength (in kN, round off to 2 decimal places) of the beam is ________
raw_source.solution:
Web bearing strength
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=[b+2.5(t_f+R)]\times t_w \times \frac{f_y}{\gamma _{mo}} \\ &= [75+2.5(20+10)] \times 8 \times \frac{250}{1.1}\\ &= 272.73kN \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: When aspecimen of M25 concrete is loaded to a stress level of 12.5 MPa, a strain of [latex]500 \times 10^{-6}[/latex] is recorded. If this load is allowed to stand for a long time, the strain increasesto [latex]1000 \times 10^{-6}[/latex]. In accordance with the provisions of IS:456-2000, considering the long-term effects, the effective modulus of elasticity of the concrete (in MPa) is________
raw_source.solution:
Effective modulus of elastic
[latex]\begin{aligned} E_{ce}&=\frac{E_c}{1+\theta } \\ E_c&= 5000\sqrt{f_{ck}}\\ &= 5000\sqrt{25}\\ &=25000MPa \end{aligned}[/latex]
Creep coefcient
[latex]\begin{aligned} \theta &=\frac{\text{creep strain}}{\text{elastic strain}} \\ &= \frac{\text{longterm strain - elastic strain}}{\text{elastic strain}}\\ &=\frac{(1000 \times 10^{-6})-(500 \times 10^{-6})}{(500 \times 10^{-6})}=1\\ \therefore \;\;E_{ce}&=\frac{25000}{1+1}=12500MPa \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Working Stress and Limit State Method

raw_source.text: A water treatment plant treats 6000 [latex]m^3[/latex] of water per day. As a part of the treatment process, discrete particles are required to be settled in a clarifier. A column test indicates that an overflow rate of 1.5 m per hour would produce the desired removal of particles through settling in the clarifier having a depth of 3.0 m. The volume of the required clarifier, (in [latex]m^3[/latex], round off to 1 decimal place) would be _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Design discharge, }\\ Q_0&=6000m^3/d\\ \text{Overflow rate}\\ OFR(v_s)&=1.5m/hr\\ SA&=\frac{Q_0}{OFR}\\ \text{Volume,}\; V&=SA \times \text{Depth}(H)\\ &=\frac{Q_0}{OFR} \times H\\ &=\frac{6000 \times 3}{1.5 \times 24}=500m^3 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Raw municipal solid waste (MSW) collected from a city contains 70% decomposable material that can be converted to methane. The water content of the decomposable material is 35%. An elemental analysis of the decomposable material yields the following mass percent.

C : H : O : N : other = 44 : 6 : 43 : 0.8 : 6.2

The methane production of the decomposable material is governed by the following stoichiometric relation

[latex]C_aH_bO_cN_d+nH_2O\rightarrow mCH_4+sCO_2+dNH_3[/latex]

Given atomic weights: C=12, H=1, O=16, N=14. The mass of methane produced (in grams, round off to 1 decimal place) per kg of raw MSW will be ______
raw_source.solution:
Let 1 kg of row municipal solid waste (MSW)
Decomposable material = 70% of 1 kg = 0.7 kg
Water content = 35%
Weight of solids in MSW [latex]=\left(\frac{100-35}{100}\right)\times0.7=0.455\;\mathrm{kg}=455\;\mathrm{gms}[/latex]
Given: C:H:O:N: other = 44 : 6: 43: 0.8:6.2[latex]\begin{array}{l}\mathrm{Weight}\;\mathrm{of}\;\mathrm C=\frac{(44)}{\left(44+6+43+0.8+6.2\right)}\times455=200.2\;\mathrm{gms}\\\mathrm{Weight}\;\mathrm{of}\;\mathrm H=\frac{\left(6\right)}{\left(44+6+43+0.8+6.2\right)}\times455=27.3\;\mathrm{gms}\\\mathrm{Weight}\;\mathrm{of}\;\mathrm O=\frac{(43)}{\left(44+6+43+0.8+6.2\right)}\times455=195.6\;\mathrm{gms}\\\mathrm{Weight}\;\mathrm{of}\;\mathrm N=\frac{\left(0.8\right)}{\left(44+6+43+0.8+6.2\right)}\times455=3.64\;\mathrm{gms}\\\Rightarrow12\mathrm a=200.2\Rightarrow\mathrm a=16.68\\1\times\mathrm b=27.3\Rightarrow\mathrm b=27.3\\16\times\mathrm c=195.6\Rightarrow\mathrm c=12.225\\14\times\mathrm d=3.64\Rightarrow\mathrm d=0.26\\\mathrm{Now},\;\mathrm{balancing}\;\mathrm{the}\;\mathrm{given}\;\mathrm{stoichiometic}\;\mathrm r\times\mathrm n\\{\mathrm C}_{\mathrm a}{\mathrm H}_{\mathrm b}{\mathrm O}_{\mathrm C}{\mathrm N}_{\mathrm d}+{\mathrm{nH}}_2\mathrm O\rightarrow{\mathrm{mCH}}_4+{\mathrm{SCO}}_2+{\mathrm{dNn}}_3\\12\mathrm a=12\mathrm m+12\mathrm s\Rightarrow12\mathrm m+12\mathrm s=200.2\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\left(12\mathrm a=200.2\right)\\\mathrm b+2\mathrm n=4\mathrm m+3\mathrm d\Rightarrow4\mathrm m-2\mathrm n=26.52\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\left(6=27.3\right)\\16\mathrm c+16\mathrm n=325\Rightarrow\mathrm n=25-12.225\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\;\left(16\mathrm c=195.6\right)\\\therefore\;\;\;\;\;4\mathrm m-2\left(2\mathrm s-12.225\right)=26.52\\\Rightarrow4\mathrm m-4\mathrm s=2.07\\\Rightarrow12\mathrm m-12\mathrm s=6.21\\\mathrm{Also},\;12\mathrm m+12\mathrm s=200.2\\\Rightarrow\mathrm m=8.6\\\therefore\;\;\mathrm{Mass}\;\mathrm{of}\;\mathrm{methane}\;\mathrm{produced} \\ =16\times\mathrm m=16\times8.6=137.6\;\mathrm{gms}\end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider the reactor shown in the figure. The flow rate through the reactor is [latex]Q \; m^3/h[/latex]. The concentrations (in mg/L) of a compound in the influent and effluent are [latex]C_0[/latex] and C, respectively. The compound is degraded in the reactor following the first order reaction. The mixing condition of the reactor can be varied such that the reactor becomes either a completely mixed flow reactor (CMFR) or a plug-flow reactor (PFR). The length of the reactor can be adjusted in these two mixing conditions to [latex]L_{CMFR}[/latex] and [latex]L_{PFR}[/latex] while keeping the cross-section of the reactor constant. Assuming steady stateand for [latex]C/C_0 =0.8[/latex], the value of [latex]L_{CMFR}/L_{PFR}[/latex] (round off to 2 decimal places) is _______
raw_source.solution:
Hydrocarbons and nitrogen oxides are considered primary air pollutants.
[latex]c=\frac{c_0}{1+kt}[/latex]
For (PFR) plug flow reactor
[latex]\begin{aligned} c&=c_0e^{-kt} \\ \text{As}\;\; c/c_0 &=0.8 \\ \text{For CMFR} \;\; 0.8&=\frac{1}{1+kt_{CMFR}} \\ \Rightarrow \;\;t_{CMFR} &=\frac{0.25}{k} \\ \text{For PFR} \;\; 0.8&=e^{-kt_{PFR}} \\ \Rightarrow \;\; t_{PFR}&=\frac{0.22314}{k} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Now for steady state
[latex]\begin{aligned} v&=\text{constant}\\ L&=vt\\ So, \;\;\frac{L_{CMFR}}{L_{PFR}}&=\frac{vt_{CMFR}}{vt_{PFR}}\\ &=\frac{0.25}{0.22314}=1.12 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A series of perpendicular offsets taken from a curved boundary wall to a straight survey line at an interval of 6m are 1.22, 1.67, 2.04, 2.34, 2.14, 1.87, and 1.15 m. The area (in [latex]m^2[/latex], round off to 2 decimal places) bounded by the survey line, curved boundary wall, the first and the last offsets, determined using Simpson's rule, is _______
raw_source.solution:
Area by Simpson's rule
[latex]\begin{aligned} A&=\frac{d}{3}[h_0+h_n+4(h_1+h_3+...)+\\ & 2(h_2+h_4+...)] \\ &= \frac{6}{3}[1.22+1.15+4 \times(1.67+2.34+1.87)+\\ & 2(2.04+2.14)]\\ &= 68.50m^2 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The uniform arrival and uniform service rates observed on an approach road to a signalized intersection are 20 and 50 vehicles/minute, respectively. For this signal, the red time is 30 s, the effective green time is 30 s, and the cycle length is 60 s. Assuming that initially there are no vehicles in the queue, the average delay per vehicle using the approach road during a cycle length(in s, round off to 2 decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution:
Arrival rate = 20 veh/min
Service rate = 50 veh/min
R = 30 sec, [latex]G_i[/latex] = 30 sec, Cycle length = 60sec

Time corresponding to which no. of arrival becomes same as no. of departure.
[latex]\begin{aligned} 20 \times (R+t) &=50t \\ 20 \times (30+t)&=50t \\ t &=\frac{600}{30}=20sec \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Avg. Delay}&=\left ( \frac{\text{Area under arrival line}-\text{Area under departure line}}{\text{Cumulative number of vehicle arrival}} \right ) \\ &=\left ( \frac{\frac{1}{2} \times 16.67 \times 50 -\frac{1}{2} \times 16.67 \times 25}{20} \right )\\ &=12.50sec \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A broad gauge railway line passes through a horizontal curved section (radius = 875 m) of length 200 m. The allowable speed on this portion is 100 km/h. For calculating the cant, consider the gauge as centre-to-centre distance between the rail heads, equal to 1750 mm. The maximum permissible cant (in mm, round off to 1 decimal place) with respect to the centre-to-centre distance between the rail heads is_____
raw_source.solution:
For a railway track
[latex]\begin{array}{l}\mathrm{Allowable}\;\mathrm{cant}=\frac{\mathrm G.\mathrm V^2}{127\mathrm R}\;\;\mathrm{where}\;\mathrm V\;\mathrm{is}\;\mathrm{in}\;\mathrm{km}/\mathrm{hr}=100\\\mathrm{Allowable}\;\mathrm{cant}=\frac{1750\times100^2}{127\times895}=157.5\;\mathrm{mm}\end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The speed-density relationship of a highway is given as

u=100-0.5k

where, u = speed in km per hour, k = density in vehicles per km. The maximum flow (in vehicles per hour, round off to the nearest integer) is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} u&=100-0.5k\\ u&=100\left [ 1-\frac{k}{(100/0.5)} \right ]\\ \text{Green shield model}\;\;u&=V_f\left ( 1-\frac{k}{k_j} \right )\\ V_f&=\text{free mean speed}\\ &=100kmph\\ k_j&=\text{Jam density }\\ &=\frac{100}{0.5}=200 veh./km\\ \text{Max flow.}\;\;q_{max}&=\frac{1}{4}V_fk_j\\ &=\frac{1}{4} \times 100 \times 200=5000veh./hr \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A confined aquifer of 15 m constant thickness is sandwiched between two aquicludes as shown in the figure.

The heads indicated by two piezometers P and Q are 55.2 m and 34.1 m, respectively. The aquifer has a hydraulic conductivity of 80 m/day and its effective porosity is 0.25. If the distance between the piezometers is 2500 m, the time taken by the water to travel through the aquifer from piezometer location P to Q (in days,round off to 1 decimal place) is______
raw_source.solution:
Discharge velocity,
[latex]\begin{aligned} V&=ki\\ V&=k\frac{h_1-h_2}{L}\\ &=80 \left ( \frac{55.2-34.1}{2500} \right )\\ &=0.6752 m/day\\ &\text{Porosity}, n =0.25\\ &\therefore \;\;\text{Seepage velocity,}\\ V_s&=\frac{V}{n}=\frac{0.6752}{0.25}\\ &=2.7008 m/day\\ \text{Time taken}&=\frac{L}{V_s}\\ &=\frac{2500}{2.7008}=925.65 days \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Theories of Seepage, Spillways and Miscellaneous

raw_source.text:
At the foot of a spillway, water flows at a depth of 23 cm with a velocity of 8.1 m/s, as shown in the figure.

The flow enters as an M-3 profile in the long wide rectangular channel with bed slope = [latex]\frac{1}{1800}[/latex] and Manning's n= 0.015. A hydraulic jump is formed at a certain distance from the foot of the spillway. Assume the acceleration due to gravity, g = 9.81 [latex]m/s^2[/latex]. Just before the hydraulic jump, the depth of flow [latex]y_1[/latex] (in m, round off to 2 decimal places) is _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} y &=0.23m \\ V&=8.1m/s \\ q&=Vy=0.23 \times 8.1 \\ &= 1.863 m^3/s-m\\ S_0&=\frac{1}{800} \\ D&=0.015 \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]y_n=[/latex] Normal depth of flow
R = y for wide rectangular channel
By Manning's equation
[latex]\begin{aligned} q&=\frac{y_n}{n}R^{2/3}S_0^{1/2} \\ 1.863&=\frac{y_n^{5/3}}{0.015} \times \left ( \frac{1}{1800} \right )^{1/2} \\ y_n&= 1.108m \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]y_1[/latex] is conjugate depth of [latex]y_0[/latex],
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{y_1}{y_n}&=\frac{-1+\sqrt{1+8Fr_n^2}}{2} \\ \because &\;\;\left ( Fr_n^2=\frac{q^2}{gy_n^3} \right ) \\ y_1&=\frac{-1+\sqrt{1+8 \times \frac{1.863^2}{9.81 \times 1.108^3}}}{2} \times 1.108\\ &=0.418m\simeq 0.42m \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Theories of Seepage, Spillways and Miscellaneous

raw_source.text: Two identical pipes (i.e., having the same length, same diameter, and same roughness) are used to withdraw water from a reservoir. In the first case, they are attached in series and discharge freely into the atmosphere. In the second case, they are attached in parallel and also discharge freely into the atmosphere. Neglecting all minor losses, and assuming that the friction factor is same in both the cases, the ratio of the discharge in the parallel arrangement to that in the series arrangement (round off to 2 decimal places) is ______
raw_source.solution:
Given: Two identical pipes of same length (L), diameter (D) and roughness ([latex]k_s[/latex]).
First case (series)
Assume height of reservoir = H

[latex]\begin{aligned} H &=h_{f1} +h_{f2}\;\;\;...(i)\\ H&=2h_{f1} \;\;\;(\because h_{f1}=h_{f2})\\ H&=2\left ( \frac{8Q_1^2}{\pi^2 g} \times \frac{fL}{D^5} \right ) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Second case (Parallel)

[latex]H =\frac{8}{\pi^2 g}\left ( \frac{Q_2}{2} \right )^2 \times \frac{fL}{D^5}\;\;\;...(ii)[/latex]
By eq. (i) and (ii)
[latex]\begin{aligned} 2\left ( \frac{8Q_1^2}{\pi^2 g} \times \frac{fL}{D^5} \right )&=\frac{8}{\pi^2 g}\left ( \frac{Q_2}{2} \right )^2 \times \frac{fL}{D^5}\\ \frac{Q_2}{Q_1}&=\sqrt{8}=2.83 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The ordinates, u, of a 2-hour unit hydrograph (i.e., for 1 cm of effective rain), for a catchment are shown in the table.
A 6-hour storm occurs over the catchment such that the effective rainfall intensity is 1 cm/hour for the first two hours, zero for the next two hours, and 0.5 cm/hour for the last two hours. If the base flow is constant at 5 [latex]m^3/s[/latex], the peak flow due to this storm (in [latex]m^3/s[/latex],round off to 1 decimal place) will be _____

[latex]R_1=1cm/hr \times 2 hr=2cm[/latex]
Rainfall excess in 2nd two hours
[latex]R_2=0[/latex]
Rainfall excess in 3rd two hours,
[latex]R_3=0.5cm/hr \times 2 hr=1cm[/latex]

The dimensions of a soil sampler are given in the table.
For this sampler, the outside clearance ratio (in percent, round off to 2 decimal places) is ______

raw_source.text: A 2mx 4m rectangular footing has to carry a uniformly distributed load of 120 kPa. As per the 2:1 dispersion method of stress distribution, the increment in vertical stress (in kPa) at a depth of 2m below the footing is ________
raw_source.solution:
The area of rectangular footing = 2 m x 4 m
q = 120 kPa
as 2:1 dispersion method of stress distribution

raw_source.text: Constant head permeability tests were performed on two soil specimens, S1 and S2. raw_source.text:
The soil profile at a site up to a depth of 10 m is shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). The soil is preloaded with a uniform surcharge (q) of 70 [latex]kN/m^2[/latex] at the ground level. The water table is at a depth of 3 m below ground level. The soil unit weight of the respective layers is shown in the figure. Consider unit weight of water as 9.81 [latex]kN/m^3[/latex] and assume that the surcharge (q) is applied instantaneously.

Immediately after preloading, the effective stresses (in kPa) at points P and Q respectively, are
raw_source.solution:
Surcharge ([latex]q=70kN/m^2[/latex]) is applied instantaneously hence excess pore pressure ([latex]u_i=70kPa[/latex]) is developed at point P and Q [GWT level is at level P]
At point P: Total stress
[latex]\sigma =q+3\gamma =70+3\times 18[/latex]
Pore water pressure = Hydrostatics pore pressure + Excess pore pressure
[latex]=0+u_i=0+70=70kN/m^2[/latex]
Effective stress, [latex]\bar{\sigma }=\sigma -u=54kPa[/latex]
At point Q: Total stress, [latex]\sigma= q+3\gamma +4\gamma _{sat}=70+3\times 18 +4 \times 20[/latex]
Pore pressure, u = Hydrostatics pore pressure + Excess pore pressure
[latex]= 4\gamma _{w}+u_i=4 \times 9.81 +70[/latex]
Effective stress, [latex]\bar{\sigma }=\sigma -u=94.76kPa[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Water flows at the rate of 12 [latex]m^3/s[/latex] in a 6 m wide rectangular channel. A hydraulic jump
is formed in the channel at a point where the upstream depth is 30 cm (just before the
jump). Considering acceleration due to gravity as 9.81 [latex]m/s^2[/latex] and density of water as 1000
[latex]kg/m^3[/latex], the energy loss in the jump is
raw_source.solution:
Assuming channle bed to be horizontal and frictionless.
[latex]q=\frac{12}{6}=2 m^3/s/m[/latex]

Initial Froude No.
[latex]\begin{aligned} (F_r) &=\left ( \frac{q^2}{gY_1^3} \right )^{1/2} \\ &= \left ( \frac{2^2}{9.81 \times 0.3^3} \right )^{1/2}\\ &=3.88 \end{aligned} [/latex]
From Belenger's Momentum equation for a rectangular channel
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{Y_2}{Y_1}&=\frac{1}{2}(-1+\sqrt{1+8F_1^2}) \\ &=\frac{1}{2}(-1+\sqrt{1+8\times 3.88^2}) \\ &= 5.018\\ Y_2&=5.018 \times 0.3=1.505m \end{aligned}[/latex]
Heal loss in the jump
[latex]\begin{aligned} (h_L) &=\frac{(Y_2-Y_1)^3}{4Y_1Y_2} \\ &= \frac{(1.505-0.3)^3}{4 \times 1.505 \times 0.3}\\ &= 0.968m \end{aligned}[/latex]
Power lost in the jump
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=\gamma _wQh_L \\ &= (9.81 \times 12 \times 0.968)kW\\ &=114.04 kW \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A water supply scheme transports 10 MLD (Million Litres per Day) water through a 450
mm diameter pipeline for a distance of 2.5 km. A chlorine dose of 3.50 mg/litre is applied
at the starting point of the pipeline to attain a certain level of disinfection at the downward
end. It is decided to increase the flow rate from 10 MLD to 13 MLD in the pipeline. Assume
exponent for concentration, n = 0.86. With this increased flow, in order to attain the same
level of disinfection, the chlorine does (in mg/litre) to be applied at the starting point
should be
raw_source.solution:
Waterson law,
[latex]\begin{aligned} tc^h &=\text{Constant} \\ t_1c_1^n&= t_2c_2^n\\ \frac{d_1}{v_1}c_1^n&=\frac{d_2}{v_2}c_2^n \\ \frac{d_1}{Q_1}A_1c_1^n&=\frac{d_2A_2c_2^n}{Q_2} \\ d_1=d_2, \;& A_1=A_2 \\ \frac{(3.5)^{0.86}}{10} &=\frac{(c_2)^{0.86}}{13} \\ c_2 &=\left ( \frac{13}{10} \right )^{1/0.86} \times 3.5 \\ &= 4.747 mg/l \end{aligned}[/latex]

A rigid, uniform, weightless, horizontal bar is connected to three vertical members P, Q and R as shown in the figure. All three members have identical axial stiffness of 10 kN/mm. The flange and web plates of the doubly symmetric built-up section are connected by continuous 10 mm thick fillet welds as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). The moment of inertia of the section about its principal axis X-X is [latex]7.73 \times 10^{6} mm^4[/latex]. The permissible shear stress in the fillet welds is 100 [latex]N/ mm^2[/latex]. The design shear strength of the section is governed by the capacity of the fillet welds.

The maximum shear force (in kN, round off to one decimal place) that can be carried by the section, is _______.
raw_source.solution:
q = Shear stress at the level mn in the weld = 100 MPa [latex]=\frac{SA\bar{y}}{Ib}[/latex]
Shear force at the given section

[latex]\bar{y}=[/latex]C.G. of shaded area above the level mn = 60-5 = 55 m
[latex]I=7.73 \times 10^6 mm^4[/latex]
b = Width of weld at mn (4 welds) = 4 x t = 4 x 7 = 28 mm
t = Throat thickness
[latex]\begin{aligned} &=0.7 \times s=0.7 \times 10 \times 4=28 mm \\ 100&= \frac{F \times (100 \times 10) \times 55}{7.73 \times 10^6 \times 28}\\ F&=\frac{100 \times 7.73 \times 10^6 \times 28}{1000\times 55} \\ &=393.527kN \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The singly reinforced concrete beam section shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale) is made of M25 grade concrete and Fe500 grade reinforcing steel. The total crosssectional area of the tension steel is 942 [latex]mm^2[/latex].

As per Limit State Design of IS 456 : 2000, the design moment capacity (in kNm round off to two decimal places) of the beam section, is __________
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} B&=300mm\\ d&=450mm\\ A_{st}&=942 mm^2\\ M_u&=?\\ (i)\; x_{ulim}&=0.46 \times d\\ &=0.46 \times 450=207mm\\ (ii)\;\; x_u&=\frac{0.87f_yA_{st}}{0.36 f_{ck}B}\\ &=\frac{0.87 \times 500 \times 942}{0.36 \times 25 \times 300}\\ &=151.77mm\\ (iii)\;\; x_y &\lt x_{ulim}\; \text{It is under reinforcement section}\\ (iv)\;\; M_u&=0.36f_{ck}B x_u(d-0.42x_u)\\ &=0.36 \times 25 \times 300 \times 151.77 \\ &\times (450-0.42 \times 151.77)/10^6\\ &=158.28kN-m \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A simply supported prismatic concrete beam of rectangular cross-section, having a span
of 8 m, is prestressed with an effective prestressing force of 600 kN. The eccentricity
of the prestressing tendon is zero at supports and varies linearly to a value of e at
the mid-span. In order to balance an external concentrated load of 12 kN applied at
the mid-span, the required value of e (in mm, round off to the nearest integer) of the
tendon, is _______.
raw_source.solution:
P = 600 kN
Simply supported span = L = 8 m
To support a point load applied at mid span (W) = 12 kN
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Balancing load} &= \text{Point load}\\ 2P \sin \theta &=Q\\ 2P\left ( \frac{e}{L/2} \right )&=2\\ \frac{2Pe \times 2}{L}&=W\\ \frac{4Pe}{L}&=W\\ e&=\frac{WL}{4P}\\ &=\frac{12000 N \times 8000mm}{4 \times 600 \times 1000N}\\ &=40mm \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Traffic volume count has been collected on a 2 lane road section which needs upgradation
due to severe traffic flow condition. Maximum service flow rate per lane is observed as
1280 veh/h at level of service 'C'. The Peak Hour Factor is reported as 0.78125. Historical
traffic volume count provides Annual Average Daily Traffic as 122270 veh/day. Directional
split of the traffic flow is observed to be 60 : 40. Assuming that traffic stream consists
of 'All Cars' and all drivers are 'Regular Commuters', the number of extra lane(s) (round
off to the next higher integer) to be provide, is ________.
raw_source.solution:
Number of the needed given LOS [latex]=\frac{DDHV}{PHF \times MSF \times F_{HV} \times f_p}[/latex]
where,
DDHV = Directional distribution hour volume
PHF = Peak hour factor
MSF = Maximum service flow rate of Los
[latex]F_{HV}[/latex] = Heavy vehicle familiarity adjustment factor
[latex]f_{p}[/latex] = Road under familiarity adjustment factor
DDHV = 122270 x 0.6 = 7362 vah/day (0.6 - max. directional distributed)
[latex]F_{HV}=f_p=1[/latex] as per given condition
[latex]N=\frac{7362}{0.78125 \times 1280 \times 1 \times 1} =7.362 = 8 \text{ lanes}[/latex]
Number of extra lanes [latex]= 8-2 = 6 \text{ lanes}[/latex]

Water flows in the upward direction in a tank through 2.5 m thick sand layer as shown in the figure. The void ratio and specific gravity of sand are 0.58 and 2.7, respectively. The sand is fully saturated. Unit weight of water is 10 [latex]kN/m^3[/latex].

The effective stress (in kPa, round off to two decimal places) at point A, located 1 m above the base of tank, is __________.

raw_source.text:
A 10 m thick clay layer is resting over a 3 m thick sand layer and is submerged. A fill of 2 m thick sand with unit weight of 20 [latex]kN/m^3[/latex] is placed above the clay layer to accelerate the rate of consolidation of the clay layer. Coefficient of consolidation of clay is [latex]9 \times 10^{-2} m^2/year[/latex] and coefficient of volume compressibility of clay is [latex]2.2 \times 10^{-4} m^2/kN[/latex]. Assume Taylor?s relation between time factor and average degree of consolidation.

The settlement (in mm, round off to two decimal places) of the clay layer, 10 years after the construction of the fill, is _________.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \Delta \bar{\sigma }&=2 \times 20=40 kN/m^2\\ \Delta H&=m_v\Delta \bar{\sigma }H \\ &= 2.2 \times 10^{-4} \times 40 \times 10 \times 10^3 mm\\ &= 88 mm\\ T_v&=\frac{C \times t}{H^2} \\ &= \frac{9 \times 10^{-2}\times 10}{5^2}=0.036\\ T_v&=\frac{\pi}{4}U^2 \\ U&=\sqrt{\frac{0.036 \times 4}{\pi}}=0.214 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The relationship between oxygen consumption and equivalent biodegradable organic removal (i.e. BOD) in a closed container with respect to time is shown in the figure.

Assume that the rate of oxygen consumption is directly proportional to the amount of degradable organic matter and is expressed as [latex]\frac{dL_t}{dt}=-kL_t[/latex], where, [latex]L_t[/latex] (in mg/litre) is the oxygen equivalent of the organics remaining at time t and [latex]k[/latex] (in [latex]d^{-1}[/latex]) is the degradation rate constant. [latex]L_0[/latex] is the oxygen of organic matter at time, t = 0.

In the above context, the correct expression is
raw_source.solution:
Given,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{dL_t}{dt}&=-kL_t \\ \Rightarrow \; \frac{dL_t}{L_t} &=-kdt \\ \Rightarrow \; \int_{L_o}^{L_t} \frac{dL_t}{L_t} &=-k\int_{0}^{t}dt \\ \Rightarrow \; \ln \left ( \frac{L_t}{L_o} \right ) &=-kt \\ \Rightarrow \; L_t&=L_o e^{-kt} \end{aligned}[/latex]
The term [latex]L_o[/latex] in the above equation represents the total oxygen equivalent of the organics at time [latex]t=0[/latex], while [latex]L_t[/latex] represents the amount remaining at time [latex]t[/latex], and decays exponentially with time.
The amount of oxygen used in the consumption of the organics, the [latex]{BOD}_t[/latex] can be found from the [latex]L_t[/latex] value.
The difference between the value [latex]L_o[/latex] and [latex]L_t[/latex] is the oxygen equivalent consumed, or the BOD exerted. Mathematically
[latex]{BOD}_t=(L_o-L_t)=L_o-L_oe^{-kt}=L_o(1-e^{-kt})[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} y_I&=\sqrt{2} \sin \theta \\ y_J&=\sqrt{2} \sin \theta \\ y_K&=\sqrt{2} \sin \theta \\ x_L&=\sqrt{2} \cos \theta \\ x_M&=5\sqrt{2} \cos \theta \\ x_S&=6\sqrt{2} \cos \theta \end{aligned}[/latex]
Step Two: Find virtual displacements of all the points
[latex]\begin{aligned} \delta y_I&=\sqrt{2} \cos \theta d\theta \\ \delta y_J&=\sqrt{2} \cos \theta d\theta \\ \delta y_K&=\sqrt{2} \cos \theta d\theta \\ \delta x_L&=-\sqrt{2} \sin \theta d\theta \\ \delta x_M&=-5\sqrt{2} \sin \theta d\theta \\ \delta x_S&=-6\sqrt{2} \sin \theta d\theta \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Step Three : Use principle of virtual work to find unknown horizontal force [latex]H_s[/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; \delta U=0[/latex]
[latex]=[-10 \times \sqrt{2} \cos \theta d\theta ] \times 3 + [-10 \times -\sqrt{2} \cos \theta d\theta ] +[-10 \times -5\sqrt{2} \sin \theta d\theta ] - [-H_S \times -6\sqrt{2} \sin \theta d\theta ][/latex]
[latex]H_S=\frac{30\sqrt{2} \cos \theta +10\sqrt{2} \sin \theta +50\sqrt{2} \sin \theta}{6\sqrt{2} \sin \theta}[/latex]
Substituting, [latex]\theta =45^{\circ},\; H_S=\frac{90}{6}=15kN[/latex]
Note : Sign conventions
If a force acts along positive x or positive y-axis, take it as positive.
If a force acts along negative x or negative y-axis, take it as negative.

raw_source.text:
The Fourier series to represent [latex]x-x^2[/latex] for [latex]- \pi \leq x\leq \pi[/latex] is given by

[latex]x-x^2=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty }a_n \cos nx +\sum_{n=1}^{\infty }b_n \sin nx[/latex]

The value of [latex]a_0[/latex] (round off to two decimal places), is _______.
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} a_0&=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi}f(x)dx\\ &=\frac{1}{\pi}\int_{-\pi}^{\pi} (x-x^2)dx\\ &=\frac{-1}{\pi}\int_{0}^{\pi}2x^2 dx\\ &=\frac{-1}{\pi}\left ( \frac{2x^3}{3} \right )_0^{\pi}\\ &=-\frac{2}{3 \pi}[\pi^3]=\frac{-2 \pi^2}{3}\\ &=-6.58 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The diameter and height of a right circular cylinder are 3 cm and 4 cm, respectively.
The absolute error in each of these two measurements is 0.2 cm. The absolute error in
the computed volume (in [latex]cm^3[/latex], round off to three decimal places), is _______.
raw_source.solution:
Let diameter, x = 3 and height = y = 4 and error= [latex]\pm 0.2[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} V&= \pi\left ( \frac{x}{2} \right )^2y=\frac{\pi x^2 y}{4}\\ V&=f(x,y) \\ dV&= \left ( \frac{\partial V}{\partial x} \right )dx +\left ( \frac{\partial V}{\partial y} \right )dy\\ dV&= \left ( \frac{1}{2}\pi xy \right )dx +\left ( \frac{\pi x^2}{4} \right )dy\\ &= \frac{1}{2} \pi \times 3 \times 4 \times (0.2)+\frac{\pi}{4} \times (3)^2 \times (0.2)\\ &= 1.65 \pi\\ &=1.65 \times 3.14=5.18 \end{aligned}[/latex]
i.e., absolute error = |5.18| = 5.18

A footing of size 2m x 2m transferring a pressure of 200 [latex]kN/m^2[/latex], is placed at a depth of 1.5 m below the ground as shown in the figure (not drawn to the scale). The clay stratum is normally consolidated. The clay has specific gravity of 2.65 and compression index of 0.3.

Considering 2:1 (vertical to horizontal) method of load distribution and [latex]\gamma _w = 10 kN/m^3[/latex], the primary consolidation settlement (in mm, round off to two decimal places) of the clay stratum is _________.
raw_source.solution:
For clay layer,
[latex]\begin{aligned} \gamma _{sat}&=\left ( \frac{G+e}{1+e} \right )\gamma _w \\ &= \left ( \frac{2.65+1}{1+e} \right )10=17kNm^3\\ e_0&=1.357 \\ H_0&=1.5m \\ (\bar{\sigma _0})_{c-c}&=[2\gamma _d+0.5\gamma _{sat}+0.75\gamma _{sat}]-1.25\gamma _w \\ &= (2 \times 15+0.5 \times 15+0.75 \times 17)-1.25 \times 10\\ &= 39.25kN/m^2\\ \Delta \bar{\sigma }&=\frac{Force}{Area} \\ &= \frac{qB^2}{(B+2nZ)^2}\\ &=\frac{200 \times 2 \times 2}{(2 \times 2 \times \frac{1}{2} \times 1.75)^2}\\ &=56.88kN/m^2\\ \Delta H&=\frac{H_0C_c}{1+e_0} \log \left ( \frac{\bar{\sigma _0}+\Delta \bar{\sigma }}{\bar{\sigma_0 }} \right )\\ &=\frac{1.5 \times 0.3}{1+1.357} \log \left ( \frac{39.25+56.88}{39.25} \right )\\ &=74.27mm \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A cast iron pipe of diameter 600 mm and length 400 m carries water from a tank and
discharges freely into air at a point 4.5 m below the water surface in the tank. The friction
factor of the pipe is 0.018. Consider acceleration due to gravity as 9.81 [latex]m/s^2[/latex]. The velocity
of the flow in pipe (in m/s, round off to two decimal places) is __________.
raw_source.solution:
Apply energy equation between (1) and (2)
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{P_1}{\rho g} +\frac{V_1^2}{2g}+z_1&= \frac{P_2}{\rho g} +\frac{V_2^2}{2g}+z_2+h_f\\ 4.5&=\frac{flV^2}{2gD}+0.5\frac{V^2}{2g}+\frac{V^2}{2g} \\ 4.5&=\frac{(0.018)(400)V^2}{2(9.81)(0.6)}+\frac{1.5V^2}{2g} \\ 4.5&=\frac{12V^2}{2g}+\frac{1.5V^2}{2g} \\ V^2&=6.54 \\ V&=2.557 m/s\simeq 2.56m/s \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A hydraulic jump occurs, in a triangular (V-shaped) channel with side slopes 1:1 (vertical
to horizontal). The sequent depths are 0.5 m and 1.5 m. The flow rate (in [latex]m^3/s[/latex], round
off to two decimal places) in the channel is _________.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} A &=\frac{1}{2} \times 2Y \times Y =Y^2 \\ \bar{Y} &=\frac{Y}{3} \end{aligned} [/latex]
For a horizontal and frictionless channel
Specific Force (F) [latex] =A\bar{Y}+\frac{Q^2}{Ag}=constant [/latex]
[latex]\Rightarrow \; Y^2\left ( \frac{Y}{3} \right )+\frac{Q^2}{(Y^2)g}=constant[/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \; \frac{Y^3}{3}+\frac{Q^2}{gY^2}=constant [/latex]
If [latex]Y_1[/latex] and [latex]Y_2[/latex] are conjugate depth
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{Y_1^3}{3}+\frac{Q^2}{gY_1^2} &= \frac{Y_2^3}{3}+\frac{Q^2}{gY_2}\\ \frac{0.5^3}{3}+\frac{Q^2}{g \times 0.5^2}&=\frac{1.5^3}{3}+\frac{Q^2}{g \times 1.5^2} \\ \frac{1.5^3}{3}-\frac{0.5^3}{3}&=\frac{Q^2}{g}\left ( \frac{1}{0.5^2}-\frac{1}{1.5^2} \right ) \\ Q&=1.728 m^3/sec \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A waste to energy plant burns dry solid waste of composition :

Carbon = 35%,
Oxygen = 26%,
Hydrogen = 10%,
Sulphur = 6%,
Nitrogen = 3% and
Inerts = 20%.

Burning rate is 1000 tonnes/d. Oxygen in air by weight is 23%. Assume complete conversion of Carbon to [latex]CO_2[/latex], Hydrogen to [latex]H_2O[/latex], Sulphur to [latex]SO_2[/latex] and Nitrogen to [latex]NO_2[/latex].

Given Atomic weighs : H=1, C=12, N=14, O=16, S=32.

The stoichiometric (theoretical) amount of air (in tonnes/d, round off to the nearest integer) required for complete burning of this waste, is __________.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\underbrace{C}_{12}\underbrace{O}_{2}\rightarrow CO_2[/latex]
Oxygen required for 350 tonne/day
[latex]\frac{32}{12}\times 350=933.33[/latex]
[latex]\underbrace{4H}_{4}+\underbrace{O_2}_{32}\rightarrow 2H_2O[/latex]
Oxygen required for 100 tonne/day
[latex]\frac{32}{4}\times 100=800[/latex]
[latex]\underbrace{S}_{32}+\underbrace{O_2}_{32}\rightarrow SO_2[/latex]
Oxygen required for 60 tonne/day
[latex]\frac{32}{32}\times 60=60[/latex]
[latex]\underbrace{N}_{14}+\underbrace{O}_{32}\rightarrow NO_2[/latex]
Oxygen required for 30 tonne/day
[latex]\frac{32}{14}\times 30=68.57[/latex]
Total [latex]O_2[/latex] = 1861.9 tonne/day
Available [latex]O_2[/latex] in waste = 260 tonne/day
Required =1861.9-260=1601.9 tinne/day
Amount of air required [latex]=\frac{1601.9}{0.23}=6964.78 \; \text{tonne/day} \simeq 6965 \; \text{tonne/day}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A sample of water contain an organic compound [latex]C_8H_{16}O_8[/latex] at a concentration of [latex]10^{-3}[/latex] mol/litre.
Given that the atomic weight of C = 12 g/mol, H = 1 g/mol, and O = 16 g/mol, the
theoretical oxygen demand of water (in g of [latex]O_2[/latex] per litre, round off to two decimal places),

raw_source.solution:
[latex]C_8H_{16}O_8[/latex] of conc [latex]10^{-3}[/latex] moles/lt required [latex]O_2[/latex] (in gm/lt)
[latex]C_8H_{16}O_8 +8O_2\rightarrow 8CO_2+8H_2O[/latex]
1 mole of [latex]C_8H_{16}O_8[/latex] requires 8 moles of [latex]O_2[/latex] for its decomposition
[latex]\begin{aligned} 240 gm &= 128 gm\\ 10^{-3} moles&=8 \times 10^{-3}moles \\ &= 8 \times 10^{-3} \times 32\\ &= 0.256 gm/lt \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Consider the limit:
[latex]\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left(\frac{1}{\ln x}-\frac{1}{x-1}\right)[/latex]
The limit (correct up to one decimal place) is _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left[\frac{1}{\ln x}-\frac{1}{x-1}\right]=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left[\frac{(x-1)-\ln x}{\ln x(x-1)}\right]\left(\frac{0}{0} \text { form }\right)[/latex]
So using L-Hospital's rule twices
[latex]=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left[\frac{1-\frac{1}{x}}{\log x+(x-1)\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)}\right]=\lim _{x \rightarrow 1}\left(\frac{1}{2+\log x}\right)=0.5[/latex]

raw_source.text: The volume determined from [latex]\iiint_{V} 8 x y z d V \text { for } V=[2,3] \times[1,2] \times[0,1][/latex] will be (in integer) _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \text{Given,}\qquad \qquad \qquad V&=[2,3,] \times[1,2] \times[0,1] \text { i.e. } \\ 2& \lt x  \lt  3,1  \lt  y  \lt  2,0  \lt  z  \lt  1 \\ I&=\iiint_{V} 8 x y z d V=8 \iiint_{V} x y z d x d y d z\\ So,\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad &=8 \int_{x=2}^{3} x d x \times \int_{y=1}^{2} y d y \times \int_{z=0}^{1} z d z \\ &=8\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{2}^{3}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{2}\left[\frac{z^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1} \\ &=(9-4)(4-1)(1-0) \\ &=5 \times 3 \times 1 \\ &=15 \end{aligned} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The solution of the second-order differential equation [latex]\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}+2 \frac{d y}{d x}+y=0[/latex] with boundary conditions y(0)=1 and y(1)=3 is
raw_source.solution:
Given [latex]\begin{aligned} \left(D^{2}+2 D+1\right) & y=0 \\ & y(0)=1 \\ & y(1)=3 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Auxiliary equation in [latex]m^{2}+2 m+1=0[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \quad &m=-1,-1\\ \mathrm{CF}&=\left(C_{1}+C_{2} x\right) e^{-x}\\ \text { And } \qquad \qquad \qquad \quad \mathrm{PI}&=0\\ C_{1} \text { solution is } \qquad \quad u y &=C F+P I \\ y &=\left(C_{1}+C_{2} x\right) e^{-x} \\ \text { Using } y(0)=1, \qquad C_{1} &=1 \\ \text { Using } y(1)=3, \qquad C_{2} &=3 e-1 \\ \text { Hence by eq. (i), } \qquad y &=[1+(3 e-1) x] e^{-x} \\ y &=e^{-x}+(3 e-1) x e^{-x} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The value of [latex]\int_{0}^{1} e^{x} d x[/latex] using the trapezoidal rule with four equal subintervals is
raw_source.solution:
Let [latex]\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx=\int_{0}^{1}e^x \; dx \text{ and }n=4[/latex]
Then [latex]a=0,b=1,f(x)=e^x \text{ and }h=\frac{b-a}{n}=\frac{1-0}{4}=0.25[/latex]
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline x&0&0.25&0.50&0.75&1\\ \hline y=f(x=e^x)&1&1.284&1.649&2.117&2.718\\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
The formula of trapezoidal rule to the given data is given by
[latex]\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx\simeq \int_{a}^{b}p(x)dx=\frac{h}{2}\left \{ (y_0+y_n)+2(y_1+y_2+y_3) \right \}[/latex]
[latex]\int_{0}^{1}e^x \; dx\simeq \int_{0}^{1}p(x)dx=\frac{0.25}{2}\left \{ (1+2.718)+2(1.284+1.640+2.117) \right \}[/latex]
[latex]\int_{0}^{1}e^x \; dx\simeq \int_{0}^{1}p(x)dx=\frac{0.25}{2}\left \{ (3.718)+2(5.03) \right \}=1.727[/latex]

raw_source.text: The value of [latex]\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty} \frac{x \ln (x)}{1+x^{2}}[/latex] is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} &\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{x \ln x}{x^{2}+1}\right) \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \left(\frac{\infty}{\infty} \text { form }\right)\\ &=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{x\left(\frac{1}{x}\right)+\ln x}{2 x}\right) \qquad \qquad \qquad \left(\frac{\infty}{\infty} \text { form }\right)\\ \lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{0+\frac{1}{x}}{2}\right)&=\lim _{x \rightarrow \infty}\left(\frac{1}{2 x}\right)=\frac{1}{2 \times \infty}=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The unit normal vector to the surface [latex]X^{2}+Y^{2}+Z^{2}-48=0[/latex] at the point (4,4,4) is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \phi &=x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}-48, P(4,4,4) \\ \operatorname{grad} \phi &=\vec{\nabla} \phi=\hat{i} \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial x}+\hat{j} \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial y}+\hat{k} \frac{\partial \phi}{\partial z} \\ &=(2 x) \hat{i}+(2 y) \hat{j}+(2 z) \hat{k} \\ \vec{n} &=(\operatorname{grad} \phi)_{P}=8 \hat{i}+8 \hat{j}+8 \hat{k} \\ \hat{n} &=\frac{\vec{n}}{|\vec{n}|}=\frac{8 \hat{i}+8 \hat{j}+8 \hat{k}}{\sqrt{64+64+64}}=\frac{\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}}{\sqrt{3}} \\ & \simeq\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}, \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}},\right) \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: If k is a constant, the general solution of [latex]\frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{y}{x}=1[/latex] will be in the form of
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{d y}{d x}-\frac{y}{x} &=1 \\ \frac{d y}{d x}+P y &=Q \\ P &=-\frac{1}{x}, Q=1 \\ I F &=e^{\int P d x}=e^{\int \frac{-1}{x} d x}=\frac{1}{x} \\ y(I F) &=\int Q(I F) d x+c \\ y\left(\frac{1}{x}\right) &=\int 1 \cdot \frac{1}{x} d x+\ln k \\ y &=x \ln (x k) \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The smallest eigenvalue and the corresponding eigenvector of the matrix [latex]\left[\begin{array}{cc} 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 6 \end{array}\right][/latex], respectively, are
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} A&=\left[\begin{array}{cc} 2 & -2 \\ -1 & 6 \end{array}\right] \Rightarrow|A-\lambda I|=0 \\ \Rightarrow \qquad \lambda&=(4+\sqrt{6}) \text { and }(4-\sqrt{6})\\ A X&=\lambda X\\ (A-\lambda I) X&=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] {\left[\begin{array}{cc} 2-(4-\sqrt{6}) & -2 \\ -1 & 6-(4-\sqrt{6}) \end{array}\right] \left[\begin{array}{l} x_{1} \\ x_{2} \end{array}\right] =\left[\begin{array}{l} 0 \\ 0 \end{array}\right]} [/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} x_{1}&=\left(\frac{2}{-2+\sqrt{6}}\right) x_{2}\\ \text { Let, } \qquad x_{2}&=K \text { then } x_{1}=\left(\frac{2}{-2+\sqrt{6}}\right) \text { K }\\ \Rightarrow \qquad\left[\begin{array}{l} x_{1} \\ x_{2} \end{array}\right]&=\left[\begin{array}{c} \frac{2}{-2+\sqrt{6}} k \\ k \end{array}\right] \approx\left[\begin{array}{c} 2 \\ -2+\sqrt{6} \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{l} 2.00 \\ 0.45 \end{array}\right] \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A function is defined in Cartesian coordinate system as [latex]f(x, y)=x e^{y}[/latex]. The value of the directional derivative of the function (in integer) at the point (2,0) along the direction of the straight line segment from point (2,0) to point [latex]\left(\frac{1}{2}, 2\right)[/latex] is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} f(x, y)&=x e^{y}\\ \mathrm{P}(2,0) \text{ and } Q\left(\frac{1}{2}, 2\right)\\ \operatorname{grad} f &=\hat{i}\left(e^{y}\right)+\hat{j}\left(x e^{y}\right)+\hat{k}(0) \\ \Rightarrow  \qquad \qquad \qquad (\operatorname{grad} f)_{p} &=\hat{i}+2 \hat{j} ]\\ \overline{P Q}&=\left(\frac{1}{2}-2\right) \hat{i}+(2-0) \hat{j}=-\frac{3}{2} \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}\\ \text{Required directional derivative} &=(\text { grad } f)_{P} \widehat{P Q}\\ &=(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}) \times \frac{\left(-\frac{3}{2} \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}\right)}{\sqrt{\frac{9}{4}+4}}=\frac{\frac{-3}{2}+4}{\sqrt{\frac{25}{4}}} \\ &=\frac{\frac{-3+8}{2}}{\left(\frac{5}{2}\right)}=1 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A partially-saturated soil sample has natural moisture content of 25% and bulk unit weight of [latex]18.5 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3}[/latex]. The specific gravity of soil solids is 2.65 and unit weight of water is [latex]9.81 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3}[/latex]. The unit weight of the soil sample on full saturation is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{w} &=0.25, \gamma_{\mathrm{t}}=18.5 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \mathrm{G}_{\mathrm{s}} &=2.65, \gamma_{\mathrm{w}}=9.81 \\ \gamma_{\mathrm{t}} &=\frac{G_{\mathrm{S}} \gamma_{W}(1+w)}{1+e} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \mathrm{e} &=\frac{2.65 \times 9.81 \times 1.25}{18.5}-1\\ \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad e&=0.756\\ \text{At full saturation}, \quad \mathrm{S}&=1\\ \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \quad \gamma_{\mathrm{sat}}&=\frac{\left(G_{\mathrm{S}}+e\right) \gamma_{\mathrm{W}}}{1+e}\\ \gamma_{\text {sat }} &=\frac{(2.65+0.756) \times 9.81}{1.756} \\ &=19.03 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \text{Given,}\qquad \qquad \qquad V&=[2,3,] \times[1,2] \times[0,1] \text { i.e. } \\ 2& \lt x  \lt  3,1  \lt  y  \lt  2,0  \lt  z  \lt  1 \\ I&=\iiint_{V} 8 x y z d V=8 \iiint_{V} x y z d x d y d z\\ So,\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad &=8 \int_{x=2}^{3} x d x \times \int_{y=1}^{2} y d y \times \int_{z=0}^{1} z d z \\ &=8\left[\frac{x^{2}}{2}\right]_{2}^{3}\left[\frac{y^{2}}{2}\right]_{1}^{2}\left[\frac{z^{2}}{2}\right]_{0}^{1} \\ &=(9-4)(4-1)(1-0) \\ &=5 \times 3 \times 1 \\ &=15 \end{aligned} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The state of stress in a deformable body is shown in the figure. Consider transformation of the stress from the x-y coordinate system to the X-Y coordinate system. The angle [latex]\theta[/latex], locating the X-axis, is assumed to be positive when measured from the x-axis in counter-clockwise direction.


The absolute magnitude of the shear stress component [latex]\sigma_{\mathrm{xy}}[/latex] (in MPa,round off to one decimal place) in x-y coordinate system is ________________
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma_{x}^{\prime}&=\frac{\sigma_{x}+\sigma_{y}}{2}+\left(\frac{\sigma_{x}-\sigma_{y}}{2}\right) \cos 2 \theta+\tau_{x y} \sin 2 \theta \\ \text { Here } \theta=60^{\circ} \\ \sigma_{x}&=40 \mathrm{MPa}, \sigma_{y}=35.6, \sigma_{x}^{\prime}=120, \tau_{x^{\prime} y^{\prime}}=-50 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Substituting the values in above equation, we get
[latex]\tau_{x y}=96.186 \mathrm{MPa}[/latex]

The equation of deformation is derived to be [latex]y=x^{2}-x L[/latex] for a beam shown in the figure.

The curvature of the beam at the mid-span (in units, in integer) will be ______________
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\text { Given, } \qquad \qquad y=x^{2}-x l[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A truss EFGH is shown in the figure, in which all the members have the same axial rigidity R. In the figure, P is the magnitude of external horizontal forces acting at joints F and G.

If [latex]R=500 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{kN}[/latex],[latex]P=150 \mathrm{kN}[/latex] and L=3 m, the magnitude of the horizontal displacement of joint G (in mm,round off to one decimal place) is ________
raw_source.solution:
Note: No need to calculate 'I< force in all members because 'P force is zero fore all members except FG
By unit load method
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text { 1. } \Delta_{\mathrm{HG}}=& \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{P_{i} k_{i} L_{i}}{A_{i} E_{i}} \\ \Delta_{\mathrm{HG}}=& \text { Horizontal deflection at joint } \mathrm{G} \\ \therefore \qquad & \qquad \qquad\Delta_{\mathrm{HG}} =\underbrace{\frac{P \times 1 \times L}{A E}}_{\text {FG-member }} \times \underbrace{Q^{\prime}}_{\text {(For all other members) }} \\ & \qquad \qquad\Delta_{\mathrm{HG}} =\frac{P L}{A E}=\left(\frac{150 \times 3}{500 \times 10^{3}} \times 10^{3}\right) \mathrm{mm} \\ & \qquad \qquad \qquad=0.90 \mathrm{~mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The cohesion (c), angle of internal friction [latex](\phi)[/latex] and unit weight [latex](\gamma)[/latex] of a soil are [latex]15 \mathrm{kPa}, 20^{\circ}[/latex]
 and [latex]17.5 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}^{3}[/latex], respectively. The maximum depth of unsupported excavation in the soil (in m, round off to two decimal places) is __________
raw_source.solution:
Maximum depth of unsupported excavation,
[latex]\begin{aligned} H&=\frac{4 C}{\gamma_{t} \sqrt{k_{a}}} \\ k_{a}&=\frac{1-\sin \phi}{1+\sin \phi}=\frac{1-\sin 20^{\circ}}{1+\sin 20^{\circ}}=0.49 \\ \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad H&=\frac{4 \times 15}{17.5 \sqrt{0.49}}=4.9 \mathrm{~m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Two reservoirs are connected through a homogeneous and isotropic aquifer having hydraulic conductivity (K) of 25 m/day and effective porosity [latex](\eta)[/latex] of 0.3 as shown in the figure (not to scale). Ground water is flowing in the aquifer at the steady state.

If water in Reservoir 1 is contaminated then the time (in days, round off to one decimal place) taken by the contaminated water to reach to Reservoir 2 will be _____________
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} k&=25 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{d} \\ n&=0.3 \\ i&=\frac{20 \mathrm{~m}}{2000 \mathrm{~m}}=0.01 \\ V&=k i \\ V_{s}&=\frac{V}{n} \\ t&=\frac{l}{V_{s}} \\ t&=2400 \mathrm{days} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Precipitation and General Aspects of Hydrology

raw_source.text: A signalized intersection operates in two phases. The lost time is 3 seconds per phase. The maximum ratios of approach flow to saturation flow for the two phases are 0.37 and 0.40. The optimum cycle length using the Webster's method (in seconds, round off to one decimal place) is ______________
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{n} &=2, \mathrm{~L}=3 \times 2=6 \mathrm{sec} \\ \mathrm{y}_{1} &=0.37, \mathrm{y}_{2}=0.40 \\ \mathrm{Y} &=\mathrm{y}_{1}+\mathrm{y}_{2} \\ &=0.37+0.40 \\ &=0.77 \\ \mathrm{C}_{0} &=\left(\frac{1.5 \mathrm{~L}+5}{1-\mathrm{Y}}\right)=\frac{1.5 \times 6+5}{1-0.77} \\ &=60.87 \mathrm{sec} \simeq 60.9 \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The solution of the second-order differential equation [latex]\frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}}+2 \frac{d y}{d x}+y=0[/latex] with boundary conditions y(0)=1 and y(1)=3 is
raw_source.solution:
Given [latex]\begin{aligned} \left(D^{2}+2 D+1\right) & y=0 \\ & y(0)=1 \\ & y(1)=3 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Auxiliary equation in [latex]m^{2}+2 m+1=0[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \quad &m=-1,-1\\ \mathrm{CF}&=\left(C_{1}+C_{2} x\right) e^{-x}\\ \text { And } \qquad \qquad \qquad \quad \mathrm{PI}&=0\\ C_{1} \text { solution is } \qquad \quad u y &=C F+P I \\ y &=\left(C_{1}+C_{2} x\right) e^{-x} \\ \text { Using } y(0)=1, \qquad C_{1} &=1 \\ \text { Using } y(1)=3, \qquad C_{2} &=3 e-1 \\ \text { Hence by eq. (i), } \qquad y &=[1+(3 e-1) x] e^{-x} \\ y &=e^{-x}+(3 e-1) x e^{-x} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The value of [latex]\int_{0}^{1} e^{x} d x[/latex] using the trapezoidal rule with four equal subintervals is
raw_source.solution:
Let [latex]\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx=\int_{0}^{1}e^x \; dx \text{ and }n=4[/latex]
Then [latex]a=0,b=1,f(x)=e^x \text{ and }h=\frac{b-a}{n}=\frac{1-0}{4}=0.25[/latex]
[latex]\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|c|} \hline x&0&0.25&0.50&0.75&1\\ \hline y=f(x=e^x)&1&1.284&1.649&2.117&2.718\\ \hline \end{array}[/latex]
The formula of trapezoidal rule to the given data is given by
[latex]\int_{a}^{b}f(x)dx\simeq \int_{a}^{b}p(x)dx=\frac{h}{2}\left \{ (y_0+y_n)+2(y_1+y_2+y_3) \right \}[/latex]
[latex]\int_{0}^{1}e^x \; dx\simeq \int_{0}^{1}p(x)dx=\frac{0.25}{2}\left \{ (1+2.718)+2(1.284+1.640+2.117) \right \}[/latex]
[latex]\int_{0}^{1}e^x \; dx\simeq \int_{0}^{1}p(x)dx=\frac{0.25}{2}\left \{ (3.718)+2(5.03) \right \}=1.727[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 50 mL sample of industrial wastewater is taken into a silica crucible. The empty weight of the crucible is 54.352 g. The crucible with the sample is dried in a hot air oven at 104 [latex]^{\circ}C[/latex] till a constant weight of 55.129 g. Thereafter, the crucible with the dried sample is fired at 600 [latex]^{\circ}C[/latex] for 1 h in a muffle furnace, and the weight of the crucible along with residue is determined as 54.783 g. The concentration of total volatile solids is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} V&= 50 \; ml\\ W_1&=54.352\; gm \\ W_2&=55.129 \; gm \\ W_3&=54.783 \; gm \\ &\text{Total volatile solids,} \\ &=\frac{W_2-W_3}{V} \\ &= \frac{(55.129-54.783)}{50} \times 10^6 \; mg/lit\\ &=6920\; mg/l \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Quality and Characteristics of Waste Water

raw_source.text:
A wedge M and a block N are subjected to forces P and Q as shown in the figure. If force P is sufficiently large, then the block N can be raised. The weights of the wedge and the block are negligible compared to the forces P and Q. The coefficient of friction [latex](\mu)[/latex] along the inclined surface between the wedge and the block is 0.2. All other surfaces are frictionless. The wedge angle is [latex]30^{\circ}[/latex].

The limiting force P, in terms of Q, required for impending motion of block N to just move it in the upward direction is given as [latex]P=\alpha Q[/latex]. The value of the coefficient '?' (rounded off to one decimal place) is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \Sigma Y&=0 \Rightarrow \\ N_{2} \sin 60^{\circ}-0.2 N_{2} \sin &30^{\circ}-Q=0 \\ Q&=0.766 \mathrm{~N}_{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} \Sigma X &=0 \\ \Rightarrow \qquad 0.2 N_{2} \cos 30^{\circ}+N_{2} \cos 60^{\circ}-P &=0\\ P &=0.67 N_{2} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad P &=0.67 \times \frac{Q}{0.766}\\ \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad P&=0.875 \mathrm{Q} \simeq 0.9 Q \\ P&=\alpha Q \\ \Rightarrow \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \alpha&=0.9 \end{aligned}[/latex]

Based on the bidding behaviour of the Contractor Y, the probability of winning against Contractor Y at a mark up of 8% for the next project is

raw_source.text:
A fluid flowing steadily in a circular pipe of radius R has a velocity that is everywhere parallel to the axis (centerline) of the pipe. The velocity distribution  along the radial direction is [latex]V_r=U\left ( 1-\frac{r^2}{R^2} \right )[/latex], where [latex]r[/latex] is the radial distance as 
measured from the pipe axis and [latex]U[/latex] is the maximum velocity at [latex]r=0[/latex]. The average velocity of the fluid in the pipe is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} u&=U\left ( 1-\frac{r^2}{R^2} \right ) \\ \dot{m}&=\int_{0}^{R} \rho (2 \pi r\; dr)u\\ &= 2 \pi \rho U\int_{0}^{R} \left ( 1-\frac{r^2}{R^2} \right ) r\; dr\\ \rho (\pi R^2)\bar{u} &= 2 \pi \rho U \left ( \frac{R^2}{2}-\frac{R^4}{R^2 \times 4} \right )\\ \bar{u}&= \frac{U}{2}\\ \bar{u} &= \text{Mean velocity} \\ U&=\text{Max velocity} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: On a road, the speed - density relationship of a traffic stream is given by u=70 - 0.7k (where speed, u, is in km/h and density, k is in veh/km). At the capacity condition, the average time headway will be
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{u}&=70-0.07 \mathrm{k} \\ \mathrm{u}&=70\left[1-\frac{\mathrm{k}}{\frac{70}{0.7}}\right]\\ V_{f} &=70 \mathrm{kmph} \\ \mathrm{k}_{\mathrm{j}} &=\frac{70}{0.7}=100 \mathrm{veh} / \mathrm{km} \\ \mathrm{q}_{\max } &=\frac{1}{4} V_{f} k_{j}=\left(\frac{1}{4} \times 70 \times 100\right)=1750 \mathrm{veh} / \mathrm{hr} \\ \mathrm{q}_{\max } &=\frac{3600}{h_{i}} \\ 1750 &=\frac{300}{h_{i}}\\ & \text{Average time headway}\\ h_{i}&=\frac{3600}{1750}=2.057=2.1 \mathrm{sec} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Geometric Design of Highway and Planning
