raw_source.text: A material P of thickness 1 mm is sandwiched between two steel slabs, as shown in the figure below. A heat flux 10 [latex]kW/m^{2}[/latex] is supplied to one of the steel slabs as shown. The boundary temperatures of the slabs are indicated in the figure. Assume thermal conductivity of this steel is 10 W/m.K. Considering one-dimensional steady state heat conduction for the configuration, the thermal conductivity (k, in W/m.K) of material P is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} x &=1 \mathrm{mm}=0.001 \mathrm{m} \\ \mathrm{q}^{\prime \prime} &=10 \mathrm{kW} / \mathrm{m}^{2}=10000 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \\ k_{s} &=10 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \\ \delta &=20 \mathrm{mm}=0.02 \mathrm{m} \\ T_{1} &=500 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{2} &=360 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { Heat flow: } Q&=\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{\frac{\delta}{k_{\mathrm{s}} A}+\frac{x}{k A}+\frac{\delta}{k_{\mathrm{s}} A}} \\ Q &=\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{\frac{2 \delta}{k_{s} A}+\frac{x}{k A}} \\ \frac{Q}{A}&= \frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{\frac{2 \delta}{k_{s}}+\frac{x}{k}} \\ q^{\prime \prime}&=\frac{\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{2 \delta}+\frac{x}{k}}{k_{s}} \\ or q^{\prime \prime}\left(\frac{2 \delta}{k_{s}}+\frac{x}{k}\right)&=T_{1}-T_{2} \\ 10000\left(\frac{2 \times 0.02}{10}+\frac{0.001}{k}\right)&=500-360 \\ 40+\frac{10}{k}&=140 \\ or \quad \frac{10}{k}&=140-40=100 \\ or \quad k=\frac{10}{100}&=0.1 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider laminar flow of water over a flat plate of length 1 m. If the  boundary layer thickness at a distance of 0.25 m from the leading edge of the plate is 8 mm, the boundary layer thickness  (in mm), at a distance of 0.75 m, is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \delta &\propto \sqrt{x} \\ \frac{\delta_{2}}{\delta_{1}}&=\sqrt{\frac{x_{2}}{x_{1}}}=\sqrt{\frac{0.75}{0.25}}=\sqrt{3} \\ \therefore \qquad \delta_{2}&=\delta_{1} \sqrt{3}=1.732 \times 8=13.8564 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In an ideal Brayton cycle, atmospheric air (ratio of specific heats, [latex]c_{p}/c_{v} = 1.4[/latex] , specific heat at constant pressure = 1.005 kJ/kg.K) at 1 bar and 300 K is compressed to 8 bar. The maximum temperature in the cycle is limited to 1280 K. If the heat is supplied at the rate of 80 MW, the mass flow rate (in kg/s) of air required in the cycle is _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Given, } \frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}&=\gamma=1.4 \\ c_{p} &=1.005 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ p_{1} &=1 \mathrm{bar} \\ T_{1} &=300 \mathrm{K} \\ p_{2} &=8 \mathrm{bar} \\ T_{3} &=T_{\max }=1280 \mathrm{K} \\ Q_{s} &=80 \mathrm{MW}=80 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For process 1-2
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&=\left(\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}\right)^{\frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma}}=8^{\frac{0.4}{1.4}}=1.8114\\ \text{or}\quad T_{2} &=300 \times 1.8114=543.43 \mathrm{K} \\ Q_{s} &=m c_{p}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right) \\ 80 \times 10^{3} &=m \times 1.005(1280-543.43)\\ \text{or}\quad m&=108.07 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a concentric counter flow heat exchanger, water flows through the inner tube at 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and leaves at 42[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. The engine oil enters at 100[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and flows in the annular flow passage. The exit temperature of the engine oil is 50[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. Mass flow rate of water and the engine oil are 1.5 kg/s and 1 kg/s, respectively. The specific heat of water and oil are 4178 J/kg.K and 2130 J/kg.K, respectively. The effectiveness of this heat exchanger is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} c_{c}=4178 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} ; c_{h}&=2130 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ m_{c}=1.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; m_{h}&=1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ C_{\min }=& c_{h} m_{h}=2130 \times 1=2130 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{k} \\ C_{\max }=& c_{c} m_{c}=4178 \times 1.5 \\ =& 6267 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{K} \\ \Delta T_{1}=& 100-42=58^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{2}=& 50-25=25^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{l m} =&\frac{\Delta T_{1}-\Delta T_{2}}{\ln \left(\frac{\Delta T_{1}}{\Delta T_{2}}\right)} \\ =& \ln \left(\frac{58}{25}\right)=39.21^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ Q=& \mathrm{UA} \Delta T_{\mathrm{Im}} \\ \text{ also}\quad Q=& m_{c} c_{\mathrm{c}}\left(T_{\mathrm{c} 2}-T_{\mathrm{c} 1}\right) \\ \therefore \quad UA \Delta T_{l m}=&m_{c} c_{c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right) \\ U A =&\frac{4178 \times 1.5(42-25)}{39.21} \\ =&2717.138 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{NTU} &=\frac{\mathrm{UA}}{\mathrm{C}_{\min }}=\frac{2717}{2130}=1.2756 \\ C &=\frac{C_{\min }}{C_{\max }}=\frac{2130}{6267}=0.34 \\ &=\frac{1-\exp [-N T U(1-C)]}{1-C \exp [-N T U(1-C)]} \\ &=\frac{1-\exp [-1.2756 \times 0.66]}{1-0.34 \exp [1-2756 \times 0.66]} \\ &=\frac{1-0.43}{1-0.34 \times 0.43}=0.6676\\ Alternatively:\\ \epsilon &=\frac{T_{h_{1}}-T_{h_{2}}}{T_{h_{1}}-T_{c_{1}}} \\ &=\frac{100-50}{100-25} \\ &=\frac{50}{75}=\frac{2}{3}=0.6667 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A heat pump with refrigerant R22 is used for space heating between temperature limits of -20[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. The heat required is 200 MJ/h. Assume specific heat of vapour at the time of discharge as 0.98 kJ/kg.K. Other relevant properties are given below. The enthalpy (in kJ/kg) of the refrigerant at isentropic compressor discharge is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} s_{2}-s_{2^{\prime}}&=c_{p} \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{2^{\prime}}} \\ s_{1}&=s_{2} \quad(\text { for isentropic process }) \\ s_{2} &=1.7841 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ s_{2} &=1.7183 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ c_{p} &=0.98 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{K} \\ \therefore \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{2^{\prime}}} &=\frac{s_{2}-s_{2^{\prime}}}{c_{p}} \\ &=\frac{1.7841-1.7183}{0.98}=0.0671\\ \text { or } \quad T_{2} &=1.0694 \times T_{2^{\prime}}=\sqrt{.0694 \times 298} \\ &=318.695 \mathrm{K} \\ h_{2}-h_{2^{\prime}} &=c_{p}\left(T_{2}-T_{2}\right) \\ h_{2} &=413.02+0.98(318.695-298) \\ h_{2} &=433.3 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A project has four activities P, Q, R and S as shown below.

The normal cost of the project is Rs. 10,000 and the overhead cost is Rs. 200 per day. If the project duration has to be crashed down to 9 days, the total cost (in Rupees) of the project is _______
raw_source.solution:
Path
P-Q = 10 days
P-R-S = 3+4+5 = 12 days
So P-R-S is critical path
Now we will crash the activity 'S' by 2 day
So now P-R = 10 day
P-R-S = 10 day
both are critical paths
So Total cost of project will be
= Normal cost + overhead cost + crashing cost
= 10000+200*(10 day) +200*2
= 10000+2000+400
= 12400 Rs

raw_source.text: An analytic function of a complex variable [latex]z=x+iy[/latex]  is expressed as [latex]f(z)=u(x,y)+iv(x,y)[/latex]  , where [latex]i=\sqrt{-1}[/latex]. If [latex]u(x,y)=x^{2}-y^{2}[/latex], then expression for [latex]v(x,y)[/latex]  in terms of x, y and a general constant c would be
raw_source.solution:
As per Cauchy-Riemann equations:
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=\frac{\partial v}{\partial y} and \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-\frac{\partial v}{\partial x} [/latex]
[latex] u=x^{2}-y^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}=2 x, \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=-2 y [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 x [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad v=2 x y+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}=2 y+f(x) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=2 y+f^{\prime}(x) [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad f^{\prime}(x)=0 \quad \text { i.e. } f(x)=c [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad v=2 x y+c [/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider two solutions [latex]x(t)=x_{1}(t)[/latex] and  [latex]x(t)=x_{2}(t)[/latex]  of the differential equation [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d}^2x(t)}{\mathrm{d} t^{2}}+x(t)=0,\; t\gt 0[/latex]  , such that [latex]x_{1}(0)=1,\; \frac{\mathrm{d}x_{1}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t}|_{t=0} =0,x_{2}(0)=0,\frac{\mathrm{d}x_{2}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t}|_{t=0} =1[/latex]  . The wronskian [latex]W(t)=\begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t)\\ \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t} & \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{2}(t)}{\mathrm{d} t} \end{vmatrix}[/latex]  at [latex]t=\pi /2[/latex]  is.
raw_source.solution:
Given differential equation in symbolic form is
[latex] \left(D^{2}+1\right) x(t)=0 [/latex]
Its A.E. is [latex] D^{2}+1=0 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad D=\pm i [/latex]
So, C.F. is
[latex] x_{1}(t)=C_{1} \cos t [/latex]
[latex] x_{2}(t)=C_{2} \sin t[/latex]
[latex] \therefore x_{1}(0)=C_{1}=1 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad x_{1}(t) &=\operatorname{cost} \\ \text { it satisfies }\left.\begin{matrix} \frac{\mathrm{d} x_{1}(t)}{d t}\end{matrix} \right|_{t=0} &=0 \end{aligned} \\ \qquad \begin{aligned} x_{2}(0) &=0=C_{2} \sin (0)\left(\because C_{2} \neq 0\right) \\ \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t} &=C_{2} \cos t \end{aligned} \\ \left.\Rightarrow \quad \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\right|_{t=0}=C_{2}=1 \end{array}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \therefore \;\; x_{2}(t)=\sin t \\ W(t)= \begin{vmatrix} x_{1}(t) & x_{2}(t) \\ \frac{d x_{1}(t)}{d t} & \frac{d x_{2}(t)}{d t}\end{vmatrix}= \begin{vmatrix} \cos t & \sin t \\ -\sin t & \cos t \end{vmatrix} \\ M(t)=\cos ^{2} t+\sin ^{2} t=1 \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A machine produces 0, 1 or 2 defective pieces in a day with associated probability of 1/6, 2/3 and 1/6, respectively. The mean value and the variance of the number of defective pieces produced by the machine in a day,  respectively, are
raw_source.solution: [latex] \begin{aligned} \operatorname{mean} &=\Sigma x \cdot p(x)=0\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+2\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{6}=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{3}{3}=1 \\ E\left(x^{2}\right) &=0\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)+1\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)+4\left(\frac{1}{6}\right) \\ &=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{4}{6}=\frac{2}{3}+\frac{2}{3}=\frac{4}{3} \\ \text { Variance } &=E\left(x^{2}\right)-\left(E(x)^{2}\right)=\frac{4}{3}-1=\frac{1}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider a simply supported beam of length, 50h, with a rectangular cross-section of depth, h, and width, 2h. The beam carries a vertical point load, P, at its mid-point. The ratio of the maximum shear stress to the maximum bending stress in the beam is

mass in area [latex]2 \pi r d r=d m [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} d m &=\frac{2 m r d r}{3 R^{2}} \\ I &=\int_{R}^{2 R} d m r^{2}=\frac{2 m}{3 R^{2}} \int_{R}^{2 R} r^{3} d r \\ &=\frac{2 m}{3 R^{2}}\left[\frac{r^{4}}{4}\right]_{R}^{2 R} \\ &=\frac{m}{6 R^{2}}\left[15 R^{4}\right]=\frac{5 m R^{2}}{2}\\ K \cdot E&=(K \cdot E)_{\text {translation }}+(K \cdot E)_{rotation} \\ \text{where }\quad V&=\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}+\frac{1}{2} I \omega^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \omega&=\frac{v}{2 R} \\ \therefore \quad K . E&=\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}+\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{5 m R^{2}}{2} \times \frac{v^{2}}{4 R^{2}} \\ & =\frac{1}{2} m v^{2}+\frac{5 m v^{2}}{16} \\ \mathrm{K.E}&=\frac{8 \mathrm{mv}^{2}+5 \mathrm{mv}^{2}}{16}=\frac{13 \mathrm{mv}^{2}}{16} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A force P is applied at a distance x from the end of the beam as shown in the figure. What would be the value of x so that the displacement at 'A' is equal to zero?
raw_source.solution:
Deflection due to load [latex]=\frac{P L^{3}}{3 E I}(-v e) [/latex]
Deflection due to moment
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{M L^{2}}{2 E I}=\frac{P(L-x) L^{2}}{2 E I}(+v e) \\ \delta_{P}+\delta_{M} &=0 \\ \therefore \frac{P(L-x) L^{2}}{2 E I} &=\frac{P L^{3}}{3 E I}\\ \text{or}\quad \frac{L-x}{2}&=\frac{L}{3} \\ \text{or}\quad 3 L-3 x &= 2 L \\ \text{or}\quad x &= \frac{L}{3}=0.33 L \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider a rotating disk cam and a translating roller follower with zero offset. Which one of the following pitch curves, parameterized by t, lying in the interval 0 to [latex]2\pi[/latex] , is associated with the maximum translation of the follower during one full rotation of the cam rotating about the center  at [latex](x,y)=(0,0)[/latex] ?
raw_source.solution:
Maximum translation of the follower during one full rotation about center will be
[latex]d=\sqrt{x^2+y^2}\text{ where }d: \text{translation of follower}[/latex]
and [latex]d_{max} \text{ at } \frac{d\;d(t)}{dt}=0[/latex]
[latex]d_{max}:[/latex] Maximum translation of follower
[latex]\begin{aligned} x(t)&=\frac{1}{2} + \cos t\\ y(t)&=2 \sin t \\ d &=\sqrt{\left (\frac{1}{2} + \cos t \right )^2 +(2 \sin t)^2} \\ &= \sqrt{\frac{1}{4}+ \cos t+ \cos ^2 t +4 \sin ^2 t}\\ &= \sqrt{\frac{5}{4}+\cos t +3 \sin ^2 t} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{For }d_{max}:\\ \frac{d(\cos t + 3 \sin ^2 t)}{dt}&=0\\ - \sin t +6 \sin t \cos t&=0\\ \cos t&=0\\ t=\frac{\pi}{2},\frac{3 \pi}{2}&\\ d_{max}=\sqrt{\frac{5}{4}+0+3}\\ =\sqrt{\frac{5+12}{4}}\\ =\sqrt{\frac{17}{4}}=2.06\\ d_{max}=2.06 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A four-wheel vehicle of mass 1000 kg moves uniformly in a straight line with the wheels revolving at 10 rad/s. The wheels are identical, each with a radius of 0.2 m. Then a constant braking torque is applied to all the wheels and the vehicle experiences a uniform deceleration. For the vehicle to stop in 10 s, the braking torque (in N.m) on each wheel is _______
raw_source.solution:
Initial velocity,
[latex] u=\omega r=10 \times 0.2=2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}[/latex]
For vehicle to stop,
[latex] \begin{aligned} v &=u-\mathrm{at} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0 &=u-\mathrm{at}\\ \therefore \quad a&=\frac{u}{t}=\frac{2}{10}=0.2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Braking force = Total mass x deceleration
[latex] \begin{aligned} F &=1000 \times 0.2 \\ &=200 \mathrm{N} \\ F_{\text {each wheel }} &=\frac{200}{4}=50 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Braking torque on each wheel
[latex] =50 \times 0.2=10 \mathrm{Nm}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A slider-crank mechanism with crank radius 60 mm and connecting rod length 240 mm is shown in figure. The crank is rotating with a uniform angular speed of 10 rad/s, counter clockwise. For the given configuration, the speed (in m/s) of the slider is _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} L=240\mathrm{mm}\\ r=60 \mathrm{mm} \\ n=\frac{L}{r}=\frac{240}{60}=4 \\ \omega=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \end{array}[/latex]
From the given configuration,
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \cos \theta=\frac{\sin \theta}{n} \text { or } \tan \theta=n\\ \text{or }\theta=\tan ^{-1} \\ \quad=75.96^{\circ} \\ \therefore \quad V_{s}=\omega r\left[\sin \theta+\frac{\sin 2 \theta}{2 n}\right] \\ =10 \times 0.06\left[\sin 75.96^{\circ}+\frac{\sin 151.92^{\circ}}{2 \times 4}\right] \\ =0.6[0.97+0.0588] \\ =0.6 \times 1.0288\\ \text{or }V_{0}=\omega \end{array}[/latex]
since slider is [latex] \perp [/latex] ar to the crank
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{so,} &=\omega r=10 \times 0.06 \\ &=0.6 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Consider an objective function [latex]Z(x_{1},x_{2})=3x_{1}+9x_{2}[/latex] and the constraints
[latex]x_{1}+x_{2}\leq 8,[/latex]

The maximum value of the objective function is __________

raw_source.text: A mass-spring-dashpot system with mass m = 10 kg, spring constant k = 6250 N/m is excited by a harmonic excitation of [latex]10 cos(25t)[/latex] N. At the steady state, the vibration amplitude of the mass is 40 mm. The damping coefficient (c, in N.s/m) of the dashpot is _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} \text { Given, } m=10 \mathrm{kg}, F_{0}=10 \mathrm{N} \\ \omega=25 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}, k=6250 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m} \\ X =\frac{F_{0}}{\sqrt{\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}+(c \omega)^{2}}}\\ \text{or}\quad \sqrt{\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}+(c \omega)^{2}}=\frac{F_{0}}{X} \\ \end{array}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} (c \omega) &=\sqrt{\left(\frac{F_{0}}{X}\right)^{2}-\left(k-m \omega^{2}\right)^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{\left(\frac{10}{0.04}\right)^{2}-(6250-10 \times 625)^{2}}\\c \omega &=\frac{10}{0.04}=250 \\ \therefore \quad c &=\frac{250}{\omega}=\frac{250}{25}=10 \mathrm{Ns} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned} [/latex]

raw_source.text: A certain amount of an ideal gas is initially at a pressure [latex]p_{1}[/latex]  and temperature [latex]T_{1}[/latex] . First, it undergoes a constant pressure process 1-2 such that [latex]T_{2}[/latex]=[latex]3T_{1}/4[/latex]. Then, it undergoes a constant volume process  2-3 such that [latex]T_{3}[/latex]=[latex]T_{1}/2[/latex]. The ratio of the final volume to the initial volume of the ideal gas is
raw_source.solution:
Process 1-2: Cooling at p=C
[latex] T=\frac{3 T_{1}}{4} \text { given condition }[/latex]
[latex] \text{Or} \quad \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\frac{3}{4}[/latex]
According to Charle's law
[latex] \frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}}=\frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}=\frac{3}{4}[/latex]
Process 2-3: Cooling at V=C
[latex] \begin{aligned} T_{3} &=\frac{T_{2}}{2} \text { given condition } \\ \frac{\text { Final volume }}{\text { Initial volume }} &=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{1}}=\frac{V_{2}}{V_{1}} \quad \because V_{3}=V_{2} \\ &=\frac{3}{4}=0.75 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: An amount of 100 kW of heat is transferred through a wall in steady state. One side of the wall is maintained at 127[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and the other side at 27[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. The entropy generated (in W/K) due to the heat transfer through the wall is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} s_{2}-s_{1} &=\int_{1}^{2} \frac{d Q}{T}+S_{\text {gen }} \\ \therefore \qquad 0 &=\frac{100}{400}-\frac{100}{300}+S_{\text {gen }} \\ \text{or} \qquad S_{\text {gen }} &=\frac{1}{3}-\frac{1}{4}=\frac{1}{12} \mathrm{kW} / \mathrm{K} \\ \therefore \qquad S_{\text {gen }} &=\frac{1000}{12} \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{K}=83.33 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

raw_source.text: Heat transfer through a composite wall is shown in figure. Both the sections of the wall have equal thickness ([latex]l[/latex]). The conductivity of one section is k and that of the other is 2k. The left face of the wall is at 600 K and the right face is at 300 K. The interface temperature [latex]T_{i}[/latex] (in K) of the composite wall is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} T_{1}&=600 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{2}&=300 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]


For steady state heat transfer,
Heat flow through layer-1
= Heat flow through layer-2
[latex] \begin{aligned} Q&=Q \\ \frac{T_{1}-T_{i}}{l / k A}&=\frac{T_{i}-T_{2}}{l / 2 k A} \\ \frac{k A\left(T_{1}-T_{i}\right)}{l}&=\frac{2 k A\left(T_{i}-T_{2}\right)}{l}\\ \text{or }\quad T_{1}-T_{i}&=2 T_{i}-2 T_{2} \\ \text{or }\quad T_{1}+2 T_{2}&=3 T_{i} \\ \text{or }\quad T_{i} &=\frac{T_{1}+2 T_{2}}{3} \\ &=\frac{600+2 \times 300}{3}=400^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A fluid of dynamic viscosity [latex]2\times 10^{-5}[/latex] kg/m.s and density 1 [latex]kg/m^{3}[/latex] flows with an average velocity of 1 m/s through a long duct of rectangular (25 mm x 15 mm) cross-section. Assuming laminar flow, the pressure drop (in Pa) in the fully developed region per meter length of the duct is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \mu&=2 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{ms} \\ \rho&=1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \bar{u}&=1 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex] a=25 \mathrm{mm}=0.025 \mathrm{m} [/latex]
[latex] b=15 \mathrm{mm}=0.015 \mathrm{m} [/latex]
Characteristic diameter,
[latex] D_{c}=\frac{4 A}{P}[/latex]
where [latex] \qquad A=a \times b,[/latex] cross-section area
[latex] =0.025 \times 0.015 [/latex]
[latex] =3.75 \times 10^{-4} \mathrm{m}^{2}[/latex]
and [latex] \qquad \mathrm{P}=2(\mathrm{a}+\mathrm{b}),[/latex] wetted perimeter
[latex] =2(0.025+0.015)=0.08 \mathrm{m}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore \qquad D_{c}=\frac{4 \times 3.74 \times 10^{-4}}{0.08}=0.0187 \mathrm{m}[/latex]
Pressure drop,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta p &=\frac{32 \mu \bar{u} L}{D_{c}^{2}} \\ \frac{\Delta p}{L} &=\frac{32 \mu \bar{u}}{D_{c}^{2}} \\ &=\frac{32 \times 2 \times 10^{-5} \times 1}{(0.0187)^{2}} \\ &=1.83 \mathrm{Pa} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: At the inlet of an axial impulse turbine rotor, the blade linear speed is 25 m/s, the magnitude of absolute velocity is 100 m/s and the angle between them is 25[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]. The relative velocity and the axial component of velocity remain the same between the inlet and outlet of the blades. The blade inlet and outlet velocity triangles are shown in the figure. Assuming no losses, the specific work (in J/kg) is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} u &=25 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{i} &=100 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \alpha_{i} &=25^{\circ} \\ V_{r_{i}}=V_{r_{0}} &=78 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{0} &=58.6 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{t_{i}} &=V_{r_{U}} \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex] \begin{aligned} \cos \alpha_{i} &=\frac{V_{w i}}{V_{i}} \\ \cos 25^{\circ} &=\frac{V_{w i}}{100} \\ or \quad V_{w_{i}}&=100 \times \cos 25^{\circ}=90.36 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}\\ \sin \alpha_{i} &=\frac{V_{f_{i}}}{V_{i}} \\ \sin 25^{\circ} &=\frac{V_{f_{i}}}{100} \\ or \quad V_{f_{i}}&=100 \times \sin 25^{\circ}=42.26 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{w_{0}} &=\sqrt{V_{0}^{2}-V_{f_{0}}^{2}} \\ &=\sqrt{(58.6)^{2}-(42.26)^{2}}=40.59 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \text{Specific work,}\\ w&=\left(V_{w_{i}}+V_{w_{0}}\right) u \\ &=(90.63+40.59) \times 25 \\ &=3280.5 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

A solid sphere of radius [latex]r_{1}=20[/latex] mm is placed concentrically inside a hollow sphere of radius [latex]r_{2}=30[/latex] mm as shown in the figure

raw_source.text: A double -price counter-flow heat exchanger transfers heat between two water streams. Tube side water at 19 liters/s is heated from 10[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C to 38[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. Shell side, water at 25 liters/s is entering at 46[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. Assume constant properties of water, destiny is 1000kg/[latex]m^{3}[/latex] and specific heat is 4186 J/kg.K. The LMTD (in [latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C) is ________
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] T_{h 1}=46^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ; \quad T_{n 2}=? ; \quad T_{c 1}=10^{\circ} \mathrm{C} ; \quad T_{c 2}=38^{\circ} \mathrm{C} [/latex]
[latex] \rho_{\text {water }}=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} [/latex]
[latex] m_{c}=19 \mathrm{L} / \mathrm{s}, m_{n}=25 \mathrm{L} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
From energy balance,
[latex] \begin{aligned} m_{c} c_{c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right)&=m_{h} c_{h}\left(T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}\right) \\ 19 \times(38-10) &=25\left(46-T_{h_{2}}\right) \\ \text { or } \quad T_{h_{2}} &=46-\frac{19 \times 28}{25}=24.72^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{1} &=T_{h_{1}}-T_{c_{2}}=46-38=8^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{2} &=T_{h_{2}}-T_{G}=24.72-10 \\ &=14.72^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \mathrm{LMTD} &=\frac{\Delta T_{1}-\Delta T_{2}}{\ln \left(\frac{\Delta T_{1}}{\Delta T_{2}}\right)} \\ &=\frac{8-14.72}{\ln \left(\frac{8}{14.72}\right)}=\frac{6.72}{0.60976} \\ &=11.02^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A diesel engine has a compression ratio of 17 and cut-off takes place at 10% of the stroke. Assuming ratio of specific heats ([latex]\gamma[/latex]) as 1.4, the air-standard effeciency is _________
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}&=17 \\ \frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}&=\gamma=1.4 \\ \text { or } \quad V_{3}-V_{2}&=0.1\left(V_{1}-V_{2}\right) \\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}-1&=0.1\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}-1\right)\\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}&=0.1 \times 16+1=2.6\\ r_{c}&=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}=2.6\\ &\begin{array}{l} \eta_{\text {Disel }}=1-\frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}}\left[\frac{r_{c}^{\gamma}-1}{\gamma\left(r_{c}-1\right)}\right] \\ \begin{array}{l} =1-\frac{1}{17^{0.4}}\left[\frac{2.6^{1.4}-1}{1.4(2.6-1)}\right] \\ =1-\frac{1}{17^{0.4}}\left(\frac{3.81-1}{1.4 \times 1.6}\right)\\=0.596=59.6 \% \end{array} \end{array} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A manufacturer can produce 12000 bearingsper day. The manufacturer received an order of 8000 bearings per day from a customer. The cost of holding a bearing in stock is Rs. 0.20 per month. Setup cost peer production run is Rs. 500 assuming 300 working days in a year, the frequency of production run should be

Given
[latex] \begin{aligned} D &=8000 \text { per day } \\ P &=12000 \text { per day } \\ C_{h} &=0.2 \text { Rs. per month } \\ C_{0} &=500 \text { per production run } \\ E O Q &=\sqrt{\frac{2 C_{0} D}{C_{h}\left(1-\frac{D}{P}\right)}} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{2 \times 500 \times 8000 \times 300}{0.2 \times 12\left(1-\frac{8000}{12000}\right)}} \\ &=54772.25 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A cylindrical blind riser with diameter d and height h, is placed on the top of the mold cavity of a closed type sand mold as shown in the figure. If the riser is of constant volume, then the rate of solidification in the riser is the least when the ratio h:d is
raw_source.solution:
For least solidification time, surface area should
be minimum
[latex] \begin{aligned} A&=\pi d h+\frac{\pi d^{2}}{4} \quad(\text { for top rises }) \\ V &=\frac{\pi}{4} d^{2} h \\ \Rightarrow \quad h &=\frac{4 V}{\pi d^{2}} \\ A &=\frac{4 V}{d}+\frac{\pi d^{2}}{4} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For area to be minimum,
[latex] \begin{aligned} & \frac{\partial A}{\partial d}=0 \\ \Rightarrow \qquad&-\frac{4 V}{d^{2}}+\frac{\pi d}{2}=0 \\ \Rightarrow \qquad d^{3}&=\frac{8 V}{\pi}=\frac{8}{\pi} \times \frac{\pi}{4} d^{2} \times h \\ \Rightarrow \qquad & \frac{h}{d}=\frac{1}{2}=1: 2 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The diameter of a recessed ring was measured by using two spherical balls of diameter [latex]d_{2}=60[/latex] mm and [latex]d_{1}=40[/latex] mm as shown in the figure.

The distance [latex]H_{2}=35.55[/latex] mm and [latex]H_{1}=20.55[/latex] mm. The diameter (D, in mm) of the ring gauge is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} d_1 &=60mm \\ d_2&= 40mm\\ \frac{d_1}{2}&=30mm \\ \frac{d_2}{2}&=20mm \\ H_1&= 35.55mm\\ H_2&=20.55mm \\ D&= \frac{d_1}{2}+AB+\frac{d_2}{2}\\ BC&=\left ( H_1+\frac{d_1}{2} \right )-\left ( H_2+\frac{d_2}{2} \right ) \\ &=(35.55+30)-(20.55+20) \\ &=65.55-40.55=25mm \\ &\text{In right angle } \; \Delta ABC \\ AC&= \frac{d_1}{2}+\frac{d_2}{2}\\ &= 30+20=50mm\\ AB&=\sqrt{AC^2-BC^2} \\ &= \sqrt{50^2-25^2}=25\sqrt{3}mm\\ D&=30+25\sqrt{3}+20=93.30mm \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Which pair of following statements is correct for orthogonal cutting using a single-point cutting tool?
P. Reduction in friction angle increases cutting force
Q. Reduction in friction angle decreases cutting force
R. Reduction in friction angle increases chip thickness
S. Reduction in friction angle decreases chip thickness
raw_source.solution:
For orthogonal cutting using a single-point cutting tool reduction in friction angle will increase the shear angle
From Merchant theory
[latex]\phi =\frac{\pi}{4}+\frac{\alpha }{2}-\frac{\beta }{2}[/latex]
[latex]\alpha \rightarrow[/latex] rate angle (constant)
[latex]\beta \rightarrow[/latex] friction angle
[latex]\phi \rightarrow[/latex] shear angle
[latex]\beta \downarrow \phi \uparrow[/latex]

we can see that as shear angle will increase shear plane area will get decrease which results decrease in cutting force subsequently reduction in chip thickness.

raw_source.text: For spot welding of two steel sheets (base metal) each of 3 mm thickness, welding current of  10000 A is applied for 0.2 s. The heat dissipated to the base metal is 1000 J. Assuming that the heat required for melting 1[latex]mm^{3}[/latex]  volume of steel is 20 J and interfacial contact resistance between sheets is 0.0002[latex]\Omega[/latex], the volume (in [latex]mm^{3}[/latex] ) of weld nugget is _______

Total heat generation
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=I^{2} R t \\ &=(10000)^{2} \times 0.0002 \times 0.2 \\ &=4000 \mathrm{J} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Heat required to melt the nugget
[latex] =4000-1000=3000 \mathrm{J}[/latex]
Volume of nugget
[latex] =\frac{3000}{20}=150 \mathrm{mm}^{3}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider an ordinary differential equation [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d} x}{\mathrm{d} t}=4t+4[/latex]. If [latex]x=x_{0}[/latex] at [latex]t=0[/latex]  the increment in x calculated using Runge-Kutta fourth order multi-step method with a step size of [latex]\Delta t=0.2[/latex] is
raw_source.solution:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{d x}{d t} &=4 t+4 \\ &=f\left(t_{0}, x_{0}\right) \\ \text { At } t=0, & x=x_{0} \end{aligned} [/latex]
Irrespective of values of [latex] x, f\left(t_{0}, x_{0}\right)[/latex] depends on t only.
[latex] \begin{aligned} k_{1} &=h f\left(t_{0}, x_{0}\right)=0.2 x \times 4=0.8 \\ \mathrm{k}_{2} &=h f\left(t_{0}+\frac{1}{2} h, x_{0}+\frac{k_{1}}{2}\right) \\ &=h f\left(0.1, x_{0}+0.4\right) \\ &=0.2(4 \times 0.1+4)=0.88 \\ k_{3} &=h f\left(t_{0}+\frac{1}{2} h, x_{0}+\frac{k_{2}}{2}\right) \\ &=0.2 f\left(0.1, x_{0}+0.44\right) \\ &=0.2(4 \times 0.1+4)=0.88 \\ k_{4} &=h f\left(t_{0}+h, x_{0}+k_{3}\right) \\ &=0.2 f\left(0.2, x_{0}+0.88\right) \\ &=0.2(4 \times 0.2+4)=0.96 \\ k &=\frac{1}{6}\left(k_{1}+2 k_{2}+2 k_{3}+k_{4}\right) \\ &=\frac{1}{6}(0.8+2 \times 0.88+2 \times 0.88+0.96) \\ &=0.88 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A shaft is subjected to pure torsional moment. The maximum shear stress developed in the shaft is 100 MPa. The yield and ultimate strengths of the shaft material in tension are 300 MPa and  450 MPa, respectively. The factor of safety using maximum distortion energy (von-Mises) theory  is  _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma_{1}&=100 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \sigma_{2}&=-100 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]
As per Von-Mises yield theory:


[latex] N^{2}\left[\left(\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{2}\right)^{2}+\left(\sigma_{2}-\sigma_{3}\right)^{2}+\left(\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{3}\right)^{2}\right] \leq 2 \sigma_{y}^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \text{In this case, } \sigma_{3}=0 [/latex]
[latex] 2 N^{2}\left[\sigma_{1}^{2}+\sigma_{2}^{2}-\sigma_{1} \sigma_{2}\right] \leq 2 \sigma_{y}^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow N^{2}\left[(100)^{2}+(100)^{2}+(100)^{2}\right] \leq(300)^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow N^{2}=\frac{9}{3} \Rightarrow N \leq \sqrt{3} [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad N=1.732[/latex]

raw_source.text: It is desired to avoid interference in a pair of spur gears having a 20[latex]^{\circ}[/latex] pressure angle. With increase in pinion to gear speed ratio, the minimum number of teeth on the pinion

raw_source.text: A uniform slender rod (8 m length and 3 kg mass) rotates in a vertical plane about a horizontal axis 1 m from its end as shown in the figure. The magnitude of the angular acceleration (in rad/[latex]s^{2}[/latex]) of the rod at the position shown is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex] \begin{aligned} A P &=1 \mathrm{m} \\ A C &=4 \mathrm{m} \\ P C &=3 \mathrm{m} \\ I_{C} &=\frac{m L^{2}}{12}=\frac{3 \times 8 \times 8}{12} \\ &=16 \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ I_{P} &=I_{C}+m(P C)^{2} \\ &=16+3 \times 3^{2}=43 \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ \text { Torque } &=m_{2} g \times \frac{P B}{2}-m_{1} g \frac{A P}{2} \\ T &=m_{2} \times 9.81 \times \frac{7}{2}-m_{1} \times 9.81 \times \frac{1}{2}\\ &=34.335 \mathrm{m}_{2}-4.905 \mathrm{m}_{1} \\ m_{1} &=\frac{3}{8} \mathrm{kg}, \mathrm{m}_{2}=\frac{3 \times 7}{8}=2.625 \\ T &=34.335 \times 2.625-4.905 \times 0.375 \\ &=88.29 \mathrm{N} \mathrm{m} \\ T &=I_{P} \alpha \\ \alpha &=\frac{T}{I_{p}}=\frac{88.29}{43}=2.053 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A bolt of major diameter 12 mm is required to clamp two steel plates. Cross sectional area of the threaded portion of the bolt is 84.3 [latex]mm^{2}[/latex]. The length of the threaded portion in grip is 30 mm, while the length of the unthreaded portion in grip is 8 mm. Young's modulus of material is 200 GPa. The effective stiffness (in MN/m) of the bolt in the clamped zone is _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]k_{t}=\frac{A_{4} E}{4} [/latex] (Stiffness in threaded portion)
[latex] \begin{aligned} k_{t} &=\frac{84.3 \times 200 \times 10^{3}}{30 \times 10^{-3}}=562 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m} \\ &=562 \mathrm{MN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned} [/latex]
[latex] k_{d}=\frac{A_{d} E}{L_{d}} [/latex] (Stiffness in unthreaded region)
[latex] A_{d}[/latex]( major diameter c/s area )
[latex] =\frac{\pi}{4} \mathrm{d}^{2}=0.785 \times 144 [/latex]
[latex] =113.04 \mathrm{mm}^{2} [/latex]
[latex] L_{d} [/latex] (length of unthreaded portion) = 8mm
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad & k_{d}=\frac{113.04 \times 200 \times 10^{3}}{8 \times 10^{-3}} \\ &=2826 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}=2826 \mathrm{MN} / \mathrm{m} \\ \frac{1}{k} &=\frac{1}{k_{t}}+\frac{1}{k_{d}} \Rightarrow k=\frac{k_{d} k_{t}}{k_{d}+k_{t}}=\frac{2826 \times 562}{2826+562} \\ &=468.77 \mathrm{MN} / \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A frame is subjected to a load P as shown in the figure. The frame has a constant flexural rigidity EI. The effect of axial load is neglected. The deflection at point A due to the applied load P is
raw_source.solution:
Bending moment in section AB
[latex] \begin{aligned} M &=-P x \\ \frac{\partial M}{\partial P} &=-x \end{aligned}[/latex]
Bending moment in section BC:
[latex] \begin{aligned} M&=-P L\\ \frac{\partial M}{\partial P}&=-L \\ \delta_{A}&=\frac{1}{E I}\left[\int_{0}^{L}(-P x)(-x) d x+\int_{0}^{L}(-P L)(-L) d x\right] \\ \delta_{A}&=\frac{P}{E I}\left[\int_{0}^{L} x^{2} d x+L^{2} \int_{0}^{L} d x\right] \\ &=\frac{P}{E I}\left(\frac{L^{3}}{3}+L^{3}\right)=\frac{4 P L^{3}}{3 E I} \end{aligned}[/latex]

as P is horizontal force and it will be over come

raw_source.text: Torque and angular speed data over one cycle for a shaft carrying a flywheel are shown in the figures. The moment of inertia (in kg.[latex]m^{2}[/latex]) of the flywheel is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} I &=? \\ E &=3000 \times\left[\pi-\frac{\pi}{2}\right]-1500 \times[2 \pi-\pi] \\ &=3000 \times \frac{\pi}{2}-1500 \pi=0 \\ T_{\text {mean }} \times & 2 \pi=E \\ T_{\text {mean }} &=\frac{E}{2 \pi}=0 \\ \omega_{\min } &=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \mathrm{at} 0=\pi / 2 \\ \omega_{\max } &=20 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \mathrm{at} 0=\pi \\ C_{s} &=\frac{\omega_{\max }-\omega_{\min }}{\frac{\omega_{\max }+\omega_{\min }}{2}} \\ &=\frac{2\left\{\omega_{\max }-\omega_{\min }\right\}}{\omega_{\max }+\omega_{\min }} \\ &=\frac{2 \times\{20-10\}}{20+10}=0.67 \\ \Delta E &=3000 \times \frac{\pi}{2}=1500 \pi \\ \Delta E &=I \omega^{2} C_{s}\\ 1500 \pi &=I \times \omega_{\text {mean }}^{2} \times 0.67 \\ 1500 \pi &=I \times\left\{\frac{20+10}{2}\right\}^{2} \times 0.67 \\ I &=\frac{1500 \pi}{15^{2} \times 0.67}=31.26 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A single degree of freedom system has a mass of 2 kg, stiffness 8 N/m and viscous damping  ratio 0.02. The dynamic magnification factor at an excitation frequency of 1.5 rad/s is  _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} M F&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left[1-\left(\frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}\right]^{2}+\left[2 \zeta \frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right]^{2}}}\\ \text{Given, } \omega&=1.5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ \omega_{n} &=\sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{8}{2}}=2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ \zeta &=0.02, \frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}=\frac{1.5}{2}=0.75 \\ \therefore \quad M F &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left[1-(0.75)^{2}\right]^{2}+(2 \times 0.02 \times 0.75)^{2}}} \\ \therefore \quad M F &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{(0.4375)^{2}+(0.03)^{2}}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{0.1923}} \\ \therefore \quad M F &=2.28 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A ladder AB of length 5 m and weight (W) 600 N is resting against a wall. Assuming frictionless contact at the floor (B) and the wall (A), the magnitude of the force P (in newton) required to maintain equilibrium of the ladder is _______
raw_source.solution:
For ladder to be in equilibrium
[latex] \Sigma F=0[/latex]
[latex] \Sigma M=0 [/latex] (about any point 'or' line)
FBD of lader

[latex] \begin{aligned} W &=N_{B}=600 \quad \ldots(i) \\ P &=N_{A} \quad \ldots(ii)\\ \Sigma M_{A} &=0 \\ W \times 2+P \times 3 &-N_{B} \times 4=0 \\ P &=\frac{600 \times 4-600 \times 2}{3} \\ &=\frac{600 \times 2}{3}=400 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] N_{A}[/latex] is also equal to 4 nn
raw_source.tag2: FBD, Equilirbium, Plane Trusses and Virtual work

raw_source.text: A closed system contains 10 kg of saturated liquid ammonia at 10[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C. Heat addition required to convert the entire liquid into saturated vapour at a constant pressure is 16.2 MJ. If the entropy of the saturated liquid is 0.88 kJ/kg.K, the entropy (in kJ/kg.K) of saturated vapour is _______
raw_source.solution:
For closed system, [latex]\delta Q=T d S [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \delta Q&=m T\left(s_{g}-s_{f}\right) \\ \therefore s_{g}&=\frac{\delta Q}{m T}+s_{f} \\ s_{g} &=\frac{16.2 \times 10^{3}}{10 \times(273+3)}+0.88 \\ &=5.724+0.88\\ &=6.604 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

raw_source.text: A plane wall has a thermal conductivity of 1.15 W/m.K.  If the inner surface is at 1100[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C and the outer surface is at 350[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]C, then the design thickness (in meter) of the wall to maintain a steady heat flux of 2500 W/[latex]m^{2}[/latex] should be _______
raw_source.solution: [latex] \begin{aligned} k&=1.15 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{mK} ;\; T_{1}=1100^{o};\;T_{2}=350^{o}C\\ q&=2500 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2}\\ \mathrm{T}_{1}&=1100^{\circ} \mathrm{C}_{i}, T_{2}=350^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ Q&=\frac{T_{1}-T_{2}}{R_{t}} \\ \frac{Q}{A}&=\frac{k\left(T_{1}-T_{2}\right)}{\delta} \\ q&=\frac{k\left(T_{1}-T_{2}\right)}{\delta} \\ 2500&=\frac{1.15(1100-350)}{\delta} \\ \text{or}\quad \delta&=0.345 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Consider the following statements regarding streamline(s):

raw_source.text: Consider a velocity field [latex]\vec{V}=K(y\hat{i}+x\hat{k})[/latex] where K is a constant. The vorticity, [latex]\Omega_{Z}[/latex], is
raw_source.solution:
Velocity vector
[latex] \begin{aligned} \vec{V} &=K(y \hat{i}+x \hat{k}) \\ &=K y \hat{i}+K x \hat{k} \end{aligned}[/latex]
where,
[latex] u=K y, v=0 \text { and } w=K x [/latex]
Vorticity about z-axis,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Omega_{z} &=\frac{\partial v}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial u}{\partial y} \\ \frac{\partial v}{\partial x} &=0, \quad \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}=K \\ \therefore \quad \Omega_{z} &=0-K=-K \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Water flows through a tube of diameter 25 mm at an average velocity of 1.0 m/s. The properties of water are [latex]\rho =1000 kg/m^{3}[/latex] , [latex]\mu =7.25\times 10^{-4} N.s/m^{2}[/latex] , [latex]k=0.625 W/m.K, P_{r}=4.85[/latex].  Using [latex]Nu=0.023 Re^{0.8} Pr^{0.4}[/latex],  the convective heat transfer coefficient (in [latex]W/m^{2}.K[/latex] )is______
raw_source.solution:
Reynolds number,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \operatorname{Re} &=\frac{\rho V d}{\mu}=\frac{1000 \times 1 \times 25 \times 10^{-3}}{7.25 \times 10^{-4}} \\ &=34482.75 \\ \operatorname{Pr} &=4.85 \\ \mathrm{Nu} &=0.023 \mathrm{Re}^{0.8} \mathrm{Pr} .^{0.4} \\ \mathrm{Nu} &=0.023 \times(34482.758)^{0.8}(4.85)^{0.4} \\ &=184.546 \\ \text { also, } \quad \mathrm{Nu} &=\frac{h d}{k} \\ \text { or } \quad h &=\frac{\mathrm{Nuk}}{d}=\frac{184.546 \times 0.625}{25 \times 10^{-3}}\\ &=4613.66 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Heat Transfer in Flow Over Plates and Pipes

raw_source.text: Two identical metal blocks L and M (specific heat = 0.4 kJ/kg.K), each having a mass of 5 kg, are initially at 313 K. A reversible refrigerator extracts heat from block L and rejects heat to block M until the temperature of block L reaches 293 K. The final temperature (in K) of block M is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
Specified heat,
[latex] \begin{aligned} c&=0.4 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \text{ each body}\\ \text{Mass:}m&=5 \mathrm{kg} \quad \text { each body } \end{aligned}[/latex]
Initial temperature,
[latex] T_{1}=313 \mathrm{K} \quad \text { each body }[/latex]
Final temprature of block L
[latex] T_{2}=293 \mathrm{K}[/latex]
Let [latex]\quad T_{f}=[/latex] Final temperature of block M,
Entropy change of block L
[latex] \Delta S_{L}=m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}[/latex]
Entropy change of block M
[latex] \Delta S_{M}=m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}[/latex]
Entropy change of universe,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta S_{\text {univ }} &=\Delta S_{L}+\Delta S_{M} \\ &=mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}+mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For a reversible refrigeration,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta S_{\text {univ }}&=0 \\ m c \log _{e} \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}&+m_{c} \log _{e} \frac{T_{f}}{T_{1}}=0\\ mc \log _{e} \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}}&=0\\ \text{or}\quad \log _{e} \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}}&=0\\ \text{or}\quad \frac{T_{2} T_{f}}{T_{1}^{2}} &=e^{0}=1 \\ T_{f} &=\frac{T_{1}^{2}}{T_{2}}=\frac{(313)^{2}}{293}=334.36 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Steam with specific enthalpy (h) 3214 kJ/kg enters an adiabatic turbine operating at steady state with a flow rate 10 kg/s. As it expands, at a point where h is 2920 kJ/kg, 1.5 kg/s is extracted for heating purposes. The remaining 8.5 kg/s further expands to the turbine exit, where h = 2374 kJ/kg. Neglecting changes in kinetic and potential energies, the net power output (in kW) of the turbine   is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} m_{1} &=10 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad m_{2}=1.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad m_{3}=8.5 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ h_{1} &=3214 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} ; \quad h_{2}=2920 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=2374 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ W_{T} &=m_{1}\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)+m_{3}\left(h_{2}-h_{3}\right) \\ &=10(3214-2920)+8.5(2920-2374) \\ &=7581 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Two infinite parallel plates are placed at a certain distance apart. An infinite radiation shield is inserted between the plates without touching any of them to reduce heat exchange between the plates. Assume that the emissivities of plates and radiation shield are equal. The ratio of the net heat exchange between the plates with and without the shield is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\epsilon_{1}=\epsilon_{s}=\epsilon_{2}=\epsilon[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \mathrm{R}(\text { with N shields})&=(N+1)\left(\frac{2}{\epsilon}-1\right) \\ \text { R(without shield) }&=\frac{2}{\epsilon}-1 \\ \left(\frac{Q}{A}\right)_{\text {with } N \text { shield }}&=\frac{1}{N+1}\left(\frac{Q}{A}\right)_{\text {without shild }} \\ \therefore \frac{Q_{\text {with shield }}}{Q_{\text {without shield }}}=\frac{1}{N+1}&=\frac{1}{2} \quad(\because N=1) \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a compression ignition engine, the inlet air pressure is 1 bar and the pressure at the end of isentropic compression is 32.42 bar. The expansion ratio is 8. Assuming ratio of specific heats ([latex]\gamma[/latex] ) as 1.4, the air standard efficiency (in percent) is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given, [latex]p_{1}=1[/latex] bar, [latex]p_{2}=32.42 [/latex] bar
[latex] \begin{aligned} \gamma &=\frac{C_{p}}{c_{v}}=1.4 \\ \frac{V_{4}}{V_{3}} &=\frac{V_{1}}{V_{3}}=8 \end{aligned}[/latex]
For process 1-2
[latex] \begin{aligned} p_{1} v_{1}^{\gamma}&=p_{2} v_{2}^{\gamma} \\ \therefore\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma}&=\frac{p_{2}}{p_{1}}=32.42 \\ \text { or } \quad \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}} &=(32.42)^{1 / 1.4}=11.999 \approx 12 \\ r_{c} &=\frac{V_{3}}{V_{2}}=\frac{V_{1}}{8} \times \frac{12}{V_{1}}=1.5 \\ \eta_{\text {Diesel }} &=1-\frac{1}{r^{\gamma-1}}\left[\frac{r_{C}^{\gamma}-1}{\gamma\left(r_{C}-1\right)}\right] \\ &=1-\frac{1}{12^{0.4}}\left[\frac{1.5^{1.4}-1}{1.4 \times 0.5}\right] \\ &=0.596=59.6 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: At a work station, 5 jobs arrive every minute. The mean time spent on each job in the work station is 1/8 minute. The mean steady state number of jobs in the system is _______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \lambda(\text { arrival rate })&=5 \text { jobs/minute } \\ \mu \text { (service rate) }&=8 \text { jobs/minute } \\ \qquad L_{S}&=\frac{\lambda}{\mu-\lambda}=\frac{5}{8-5}=\frac{5}{3}=1.67 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A cylindrical riser of 6 cm diameter and 6 cm height has to be designed for a sand casting mould for producing a steel rectangular plate casting of 7 cm x 10 cm x 2 cm dimensions having the total solidification time of 1.36 minute. The total solidification time (in minute) of the riser is  _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} V_{\text {casting }}&=7 \times 10 \times 2=140 \mathrm{cm}^{3} \\ A_{\text {casting }}&= 2(7 \times 10+7 \times 2+2 \times 10) \\ &=2 \times(70 \times 20 \times 14)\\&=2 \times 104=208 \mathrm{cm}^{2}\\ \qquad\left(\frac{V}{A}\right)_{\text {casting }}&=\frac{140}{208}=0.673 \mathrm{cm} \\ \qquad\left(\frac{V}{A}\right)_{\text {Top Riser }}&=\frac{\frac{\pi}{4} d^{3}}{\frac{\pi}{4} d^{2}+\pi d^{2}}=\frac{d}{5}\\ &=1.2\mathrm{cm}\qquad(\therefore d=h=6\mathrm{cm}) \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \left(\frac{V}{A}\right)_{\text {Bottom Riser }}&=\frac{\frac{\pi}{4} d^{3}}{\frac{\pi}{2} d^{2}+\pi d^{2}}=\frac{d}{6}=1 \mathrm{cm} \\ \frac{t_{R}}{t_{C}}&= \frac{(V / A)_{\text {Top Riser }}^{2}}{(V / A)_{\text {Casting }}^{2}}=\left(\frac{1.2}{0.673}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow t_{R}&=4.133 \text { minute } \text { (for top riser) }\\ \frac{t_{R}}{t_{C}} &=\frac{(V / A)_{\text {Bottom Riser }}^{2}}{(V / A)_{\text {Casting }}^{2}}=\left(\frac{1}{0.673}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow t_{R} &=3 \text { minute } \quad \text { (for bottom riser) } \end{aligned}[/latex]
Solidification time considering top and bottom riser comes under range given in the answer.

raw_source.text: A cast iron block of 200 mm length is being shaped in a shaping machine with a depth of cut of  4 mm, feed of 0.25 mm/stroke and the tool principal cutting edge angle of 30[latex]^{\circ}[/latex]. Number of cutting strokes per minute is 60. Using specific energy for cutting as 1.49 J/[latex]mm^{3}[/latex], the average power consumption (in watt) is _______
raw_source.solution:
The volume rate of material removal is:
[latex] \begin{aligned} Q&=f d L N \\ \text { where } f(\text { feed })&=0.25 \mathrm{mm} / \mathrm{stroke} \\ d(\text { depth of } \mathrm{cut})&=4 \mathrm{mm} \\ \quad L(\text { length of block })&=200 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
N(number of cutting stroke per minute) =60
[latex] \begin{aligned} Q&=\frac{0.25 \times 4 \times 200 \times 60}{60}\left(\frac{m m^{3}}{s}\right)\\ &=200 \mathrm{mm}^{3} / \mathrm{s} \\ U_{c} &=1.49 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{mm}^{2} \\ P_{\text {average }} &=U_{c} \times Q=1.49 \times 200 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{s}=298 \mathrm{W} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A butt weld joint is developed on steel plates having yield and ultimate tensile strength of 500 MPa and 700 MPa, respectively. raw_source.text: Among the four normal distributions with probability density functions as shown below, which one has the lowest variance?
raw_source.solution:
We know that probability density function of normal distribution is given by
[latex]F(x)=\frac{1}{\sigma \sqrt{2 \pi}}e^{-\frac{1}{2}\left ( \frac{x-\mu }{\sigma } \right )^2}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Simpson's [latex]1/3[/latex]  rule is used to integrate the function [latex]\frac{3}{5}x^{2}+\frac{9}{5}[/latex] between x = 0 and x = 1 using the least number of equal sub -intervals. The value of the integral is _____________

raw_source.text: Given two complex numbers [latex]z_{1}=5+(5\sqrt{3})i[/latex]  and [latex]z_{2}=2/\sqrt{3}+2i[/latex], the argument of [latex]z_{1}/z_{2}[/latex]  in degrees is

raw_source.text: Consider a spatial curve in three-dimensional space given in parametric form by [latex]x(t)=cos t[/latex], [latex]y(t)=sin t[/latex], [latex]z(t)=(2/\pi)t, 0\leq t\leq \pi/2[/latex]. The length of the curve is _______

raw_source.text: Consider an ant crawling along the curve [latex](x-2)^{2}+y^{2}=4[/latex] , where x and y are in meters. The ant starts at the point (4, 0) and moves counter-clockwise with a speed of 1.57 meters per second. The time taken by the ant to reach the point (2, 2) is  (in seconds) ____________
raw_source.solution:
[latex](x-2)^{2}+\left(y^{2}\right)=(2)^{2},[/latex] is a circle of radius 2m and
centre at (2,0)
Time to reach from (4,0) to (2,2) is

[latex] \text{Time } =\frac{\text { Distance }}{\text { Speed }} [/latex]
[latex] =\frac{\left(\frac{2 \pi r}{4}\right)}{1.57}=\frac{\left(\frac{2 \pi^{2}}{4}\right)}{1.57}=\frac{\pi}{1.57}=2 \mathrm{s}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Find the solution of [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}=y[/latex]  which passes through the origin and the point ([latex]\ln 2,3/4[/latex]).
raw_source.solution:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}} &=y \\ \Rightarrow D^{2} y &=y \\ \left(D^{2}-1\right) y &=0 \\ D^{2}-1 &=0 \\ D &=\pm 1 \\ y &=C_{1} e^{x}+C_{2} e^{-x} \qquad ...(i) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Given point passes through origin
[latex] \Rightarrow O=C_{1}+C_{2} [/latex]
[latex] C_{1}=-C_{2} [/latex]
Also, point passes through (In 2,3 / 4 )
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{3}{4}=C_{1} e^{\ln 2}+C_{2} e^{\ln 2} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{3}{4} =2 C_{1}+\frac{C_{2}}{2} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad C_{2}+4 C_{1} =1.5 \qquad ...(ii)[/latex]
From (i) [latex]]C_{1}=-C_{2}[/latex], putting in (ii), we get
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad-3 C_{2}=1.5 [/latex]
[latex] C_{2}=-0.5 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad C_{1}=0.5 [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow y=0.5\left(e^{x}-e^{-x}\right) [/latex]
[latex] y=\frac{e^{x}-e^{-x}}{2}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider fully developed flow in a circular pipe with negligible entrance length effects. Assuming the mass flow rate, density and friction factor to be constant, if the length of the pipe  is doubled and the diameter is halved, the head loss due to friction will increase by a factor of
raw_source.solution:
Head loss due to friction,
[latex] \begin{aligned} h_{f}&=\frac{f L V^{2}}{2 g d}\\ &\text{Mass flow rate,}\\ m&=\rho A V=\rho \times \frac{\pi}{4} d^{2} V\\ or\quad V&=\frac{4 m}{\rho \pi d^{2}} \\ \therefore \quad h_{f}&=\frac{f L}{2 g d} \times \frac{16 m^{2}}{\rho^{2} \pi^{2} d^{4}}\\ &=\frac{8 f m^{2}}{\rho^{2} \pi^{2}} \times \frac{L}{d^{5}} \\ &=C \times \frac{L}{d^{5}} \text { where } C=\frac{8 f m^{2}}{\rho^{2} \pi^{2}} \\ h_{f_{1}}&=C \times \frac{L}{d^{5}}\\ and\quad h_{2} &=C \times \frac{2 L}{(d / 2)^{5}}=\frac{C \times 2 L}{\frac{d^{5}}{2^{5}}} \\ &=\frac{C \times 2 \times 2^{5} L}{d^{5}}=\frac{C \times 64 L}{d^{5}} \\ h_{1 / 2} &=64 h_{11} \end{aligned}[/latex]
The head loss due to friction will increase by a factor of 64

raw_source.text: A Carnot engine (CE-1) works between two temperature reservoirs A and B, where [latex]T_{A}[/latex] = 900 K and [latex]T_{B}[/latex]  = 500 K. A second Carnot engine (CE-2) works between temperature reservoirs B and C, where [latex]T_{C}[/latex]  = 300 K. In each cycle of CE-1 and CE-2, all the heat rejected by CE-1 to reservoir B is used by CE-2. For one cycle of operation, if the net Q absorbed by CE-1 from reservoir A is 150 MJ, the net heat rejected to reservoir C by CE-2 (in MJ) is ______________
raw_source.solution:
For Carnot engine (CE-2)
[latex] \begin{aligned} \eta_{2}&=1-\frac{T_{C}}{T_{B}}\\ \text{also}\qquad \eta_{2} &=1-\frac{Q_{C}}{Q_{B}} \\ \therefore \quad 1-\frac{T_{C}}{T_{B}} &=1-\frac{Q_{C}}{Q_{B}}\\ \text{or}\qquad\frac{T_{C}}{T_{B}} &=\frac{Q_{C}}{Q_{B}} \\ \frac{300}{500} &=\frac{Q_{C}}{\frac{5 \times 150}{9}}\\ \text{or}\qquad Q_{c}&=50 \mathrm{MJ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For Carnot engine (CE-2)
[latex] \begin{aligned} \eta_{2}&=1-\frac{T_{C}}{T_{B}}\\ \text{also}\qquad \eta_{2} &=1-\frac{Q_{C}}{Q_{B}} \\ \therefore \quad 1-\frac{T_{C}}{T_{B}} &=1-\frac{Q_{C}}{Q_{B}}\\ \text{or}\qquad\frac{T_{C}}{T_{B}} &=\frac{Q_{C}}{Q_{B}} \\ \frac{300}{500} &=\frac{Q_{C}}{\frac{5 \times 150}{9}}\\ \text{or}\qquad Q_{c}&=50 \mathrm{MJ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

raw_source.text: Air enters a diesel engine with a density of 1.0 kg/[latex]m^{3}[/latex] . The compression ratio is 21. At steady state, the air intake is 30 x [latex]10^{-3}[/latex]  kg/s and the net work output is 15 kW. The mean effective pressure (in kPa) is ____________
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \rho &= 1kg/m^3\\ r&= \frac{V_1}{V_c}=21\\ m &=30 \times 10^{-3}kg/s \\ W&=15kW \\ V_1&=\frac{m}{\rho }=\frac{30 \times 10^{-3}}{1}m^3/s \\ &= 30 \times 10^{-3}m^3/s\\ V_c &=\frac{V_1}{r}=\frac{30 \times 10^{-3}}{21} \\ &= 1.428 \times 10^{-3}m^3/s\\ V_s&=V_1-V_c \\ &= 30 \times 10^{-3} -1.428 \times 10^{-3}\\ &= 28.572 \times 10^{-3}m^3/s \end{aligned}[/latex]
Mean effective pressure,
[latex]\rho _m=\frac{W}{V_s}=\frac{15}{28.572 \times 10^{-3}} [/latex]
[latex]\;\;\;=524.99kW\approx 525kW[/latex]

raw_source.text: A stream of moist air (mass flow rate = 10.1 kg/s) with humidity ratio of 0.01 [latex]\frac{kg}{kg \; dry \; air}[/latex]  mixes with a second stream of superheated water vapour flowing at 0.1 kg/s. Assuming proper and uniform mixing with no condensation, the humidity ratio of the final stream  (in [latex]\frac{kg}{kg \; dry \; air}[/latex] )  is  _____________
raw_source.solution:
Mass flow rate of moist air [latex]=10.1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
[latex] \text { Humidity ratio: } \omega=\frac{m_{v}}{m_{a}}=0.01 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}[/latex]
Mass of moist air = Mass of dry air + Mass of water vapour
[latex] \begin{aligned} 10.1 &=m_{a}+0.01 \times m_{a} \\ 10.1 m_{a} &=10.1 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Mass of dry air: [latex]m_{a}=\frac{10.1}{1.01}=10 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
Mass of water vapour,
[latex] \begin{aligned} m_{v_{1}} &=10.1-10=0.1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ m_{v_{2}} &=0.1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ \left(m_{\mathrm{v}}\right)_{\mathrm{total}} &=m_{v_{1}}+m_{v_{2}}=0.2 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Humidity ratio
[latex] \begin{aligned} \omega_{\mathrm{final}}=\frac{m_{v}}{m_{\mathrm{a}}} &=\frac{0.2}{10}\\ &=0.02 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kg} \text{ of dry air} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider a slider crank mechanism with nonzero masses and inertia. A constant torque [latex]\tau[/latex] is applied on the crank as shown in the figure. Which of the following plots best resembles variation of crank angle, [latex]\theta[/latex] versus time
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \tau(\text { torque }) &=I \ddot{\theta} \\ \tau &=\text { constant } \\ I &=\text { constant } \\ \tau &=I \frac{d^{2} \theta}{d t^{2}} \\ \frac{d^{2} \theta}{d t^{2}} &=\frac{\tau}{I} \\ \frac{d \theta}{d t} &=\frac{\tau}{I} t+C_{1} \\ \theta &=\frac{\tau}{I} \frac{t^{2}}{2}+C_{1} t+C_{2}\\ \theta=f(t)&= \text{ parabolic function}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Which one of the following is the most conservative fatigue failure criterion?
raw_source.solution:
When a component is subjected to fluctuating stresses there is mean stress [latex](\sigma _m)[/latex] as well as stress amplitude [latex](\sigma _a)[/latex]. It has been observed that the mean stress component has an effect on fatigue failure when it is present in combination with an alternating component.
When the component is subjected to both component of stress [latex](\sigma _m)[/latex] and [latex](\sigma _a)[/latex] the actual failure occurs at different scattered points as shown in figure. There exist a border which decides sole region from unsole region for various combinations of [latex](\sigma _m)[/latex] and [latex](\sigma _a)[/latex] and different criterion are proposed to constant the borderline dividing safe zone and failure zone, they include Gerber line, soderberg line, Goodman line, ASME elliptic.

Gerber Line:
A parabolic curve jointing [latex]\sigma _e[/latex] on the ordinate to [latex]\sigma _{ut}[/latex] on the abscissa is called Gerber line. It is written as
[latex]\left (\frac{\sigma _a}{\sigma _e} \right )+\left (\frac{\sigma _m}{\sigma _{ut}} \right )^2=1[/latex]

Soderberg Line:
A straight line joining [latex]\sigma _e[/latex] on the ordinate to [latex]\sigma _{yt}[/latex] on the abscissa is called soderberg line. It is written as
[latex]\left (\frac{\sigma _a}{\sigma _e} \right )+\left (\frac{\sigma _m}{\sigma _{yt}} \right )=1[/latex]

Goodman Line:
A straight line joining [latex]\sigma _e[/latex] on the ordinate to [latex]\sigma _{ut}[/latex] on the abscissa is called the Goodman line. It is written as
[latex]\left (\frac{\sigma _a}{\sigma _e} \right )+\left (\frac{\sigma _m}{\sigma _{ut}} \right )=1[/latex]

ASME Elliptic:
The ASME elliptic is written as
[latex]\left (\frac{\sigma _a}{\sigma _e} \right )^2+\left (\frac{\sigma _m}{\sigma _{yt}} \right )^2=1[/latex]

The soderberg line is a more conservative failure criterion and there is no need to consider even yielding in this case.

raw_source.text: In a linear arc welding process, the heat input per unit length is inversely proportional to
raw_source.solution:
In Linear arc welding process the heat input per unit length depends on many factors.

(A) Welding current:
As welding current increase as heat input increases because we know that heat input is [latex]I^2RT[/latex] so
[latex](\text{Heat input per unit length})\propto ( \text{current} )^2[/latex]

(B) Welding Voltage:
As welding voltage increase as heat input also increase because we know that heat input is [latex]\frac{V^2}{R}[/latex]
[latex](\text{Heat input per unit length})\propto ( \text{voltage} )^2[/latex]

(C) Welding Speed:
As welding speed increase as welding electrode spend less time to release heat so as speed increase as heat input per unit length decrease proportionaly
[latex](\text{Heat input per unit length})\propto \frac{1}{( \text{welding speed} )}[/latex]

(D) Duty cycle:
Duty cycle is defined as the % of time for which arc is on without overheating element of welding machine so
[latex](\text{Heat input per unit length})\propto ( \text{duty cycle} )[/latex]
options: duty cycle of the power source

raw_source.text: Find the solution of [latex]\frac{\mathrm{d}^{2}y}{\mathrm{d} x^{2}}=y[/latex]  which passes through the origin and the point ([latex]\ln 2,3/4[/latex]).
raw_source.solution:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{d^{2} y}{d x^{2}} &=y \\ \Rightarrow D^{2} y &=y \\ \left(D^{2}-1\right) y &=0 \\ D^{2}-1 &=0 \\ D &=\pm 1 \\ y &=C_{1} e^{x}+C_{2} e^{-x} \qquad ...(i) \end{aligned}[/latex]
Given point passes through origin
[latex] \Rightarrow O=C_{1}+C_{2} [/latex]
[latex] C_{1}=-C_{2} [/latex]
Also, point passes through (In 2,3 / 4 )
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad \frac{3}{4}=C_{1} e^{\ln 2}+C_{2} e^{\ln 2} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{3}{4} =2 C_{1}+\frac{C_{2}}{2} [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad C_{2}+4 C_{1} =1.5 \qquad ...(ii)[/latex]
From (i) [latex]]C_{1}=-C_{2}[/latex], putting in (ii), we get
[latex] \Rightarrow \quad-3 C_{2}=1.5 [/latex]
[latex] C_{2}=-0.5 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore \quad C_{1}=0.5 [/latex]
[latex] \Rightarrow y=0.5\left(e^{x}-e^{-x}\right) [/latex]
[latex] y=\frac{e^{x}-e^{-x}}{2}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The probability of obtaining at least two "SIX" in throwing a fair dice 4 times is
raw_source.solution:
Let P be the probability that six occurs on a fair dice,
[latex] \therefore P=\frac{1}{6}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore q=\frac{5}{6}[/latex]
Let X , be the number of times 'six' occurs,
Probability of obtaining at least two 'six' in throwing a fair dice 4 times is
=1-\{P(X=0)+P(X=1)\} [/latex]
[latex] =1-\left\{^{4} C_{0} p^{0} q^{4}+^{4} C_{1} p^{1} q^{3}\right\} [/latex]
[latex] =1-\left\{\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{4}+\left[4 \times \frac{1}{6} \times\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{3}\right]\right\} [/latex]
[latex] =1-\left\{\frac{125}{144}\right\}=\frac{19}{144} [/latex]

raw_source.text: A ball of mass 0.1 kg, initially at rest, is dropped from height of 1 m. Ball hits the ground and bounces off the ground. Upon impact with the ground, the velocity reduces by 20%. The height  (in m) to which the ball will rise is _______

Velocity with which ball hits the ground
[latex] \begin{aligned} V_{1} &=\sqrt{2 g h}=\sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times 1} \\ &=4.4294 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \text{and }\qquad V_{2} &=0.8 \times 4.4294=3.54 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A pinion with radius [latex]r_{1}[/latex] , and inertia [latex]I_{1}[/latex] is driving a gear with radius [latex]r_{2}[/latex] and inertia [latex]I_{2}[/latex] . Torque [latex]\tau _{1}[/latex] is applied on pinion. The following are free body diagrams of pinion and gear showing important forces (F1 and F2) of interaction. Which of the following relations hold true?
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\tau_{1}-F_{1} r_{1} =I_{1} \theta_{1}\qquad \ldots(i)[/latex]
[latex] F_{1} =F_{2}\qquad\ldots(ii)[/latex]
[Action and reaction are equal by Newton's 3rd law]
[latex] F_{2} r_{2}=\tau_{2}=I_{2} \ddot{\theta}_{2}\ldots(iii)[/latex]
From (ii) and (iii)
[latex] F_{2}=F_{1}=\frac{I_{2} \ddot{\theta}_{2}}{r_{2}}\qquad\ldots(iv)[/latex]
From (i) and (iv)
[latex] \tau_{1}-\left(\frac{I_{2} \ddot{\theta}_{2}}{r_{2}}\right) r_{1}=I_{1} \ddot{\theta}_{1}\qquad\ldots(v)[/latex]
We know,
[latex] r_{1} \omega_{1}=r_{2} \omega_{2} [/latex]
[latex] r_{1} \dot{\theta}_{1}=r_{2} \dot{\theta}_{2}[/latex]
Differentiating with respect to time
[latex] \begin{aligned} r_{1} \ddot{\theta}_{1} &=r_{2} \ddot{\theta}_{2} \\ \ddot{\theta}_{2} &=\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}} \ddot{\theta}_{1} \\ \tau_{1} &=I_{1} \ddot{\theta}_{1}+\frac{I_{2}}{r_{2}}\left[\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}} \ddot{\theta}_{1}\right] r_{1} \\ \tau_{1} &=\left[I_{1}+I_{2}\left[\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}}\right]^{2}\right] \ddot{\theta}_{1} \\ \tau_{2} &=I_{2} \ddot{\theta}_{2}=F_{2} r_{2} \\ F_{2} &=\frac{I_{2}}{r_{2}} \ddot{\theta}_{2}=\frac{I_{2}}{r_{2}}\left[\frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}} \ddot{\theta}_{1}\right] \\ F_{2} &=I_{2} \frac{r_{1}}{r_{2}^{2}} \ddot{\theta}_{1} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A machine element is subjected to the following bi-axial state of stress:  [latex]\sigma _{x}[/latex] = 80 MPa;  [latex]\sigma _{y}[/latex] = 20 MPa; [latex]\tau _{xy}[/latex]  = 40 MPa. If the shear strength of the material is 100 MPa, the factor of safety as per Tresca's maximum shear stress theory is

raw_source.text: A cantilever beam with flexural rigidity of 200 N.[latex]m^{2}[/latex] is loaded as shown in the figure. The deflection (in mm) at the tip of the beam is _______

raw_source.text: A precision instrument package (m = 1 kg) needs to be mounted on a surface vibrating at 60 Hz. It is desired that only 5% of the base surface vibration amplitude be transmitted to the instrument. [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Given, } \omega&=2 \pi f=2 \pi \times 60 \\ \omega &=120 \pi \\ m &=1 \mathrm{kg} \\ \frac{F_{\mathrm{TR}}}{F_{0}} &=\frac{\sqrt{1+(2 \xi r)^{2}}}{\sqrt{\left(1-r^{2}\right)^{2}+(2 \xi r)^{2}}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
No damping,

raw_source.text: For flow through a pipe of radius R, the velocity and temperature distribution are as follows  [latex]u(r,x)=C_{1} [/latex]  and [latex]T(r,x)=C_{2}[1-(\frac{r}{R})^{3}],[/latex] where [latex]C_{1}[/latex]   and [latex]C_{2}[/latex]   are constants.  The bulk mean temperature is given by [latex]T_{m}=\frac{2}{U_{m}R^{2}}\int_{0}^{R}u(r,x)T(r,x)rdr[/latex] , with [latex]U_{m}[/latex]  being the mean velocity of flow. The value of [latex]T_{m}[/latex] is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} u(r, x)&=C_{1} \\ T(r, x)&=C_{2}\left[1-\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^{3}\right] \\ T_{m}&=\frac{2}{U_{m} R^{2}} \int_{0}^{R} u(r, x) T(r, x) r d r \\ &=\frac{2}{U_{m} R^{2}} \int_{0}^{R} C_{1} \times C_{2}\left[1-\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^{3}\right] r d r \\ &=\frac{2 C_{1} C_{2}}{U_{m} R^{2}} \int_{0}^{R}\left[1-\left(\frac{r}{R}\right)^{3}\right] r d r \\ &=\frac{2 C_{1} C_{2}}{U_{m} R^{2}} \int_{0}^{R}\left(r-\frac{r^{4}}{R^{3}}\right) d r \\ &=\frac{2 C_{1} C_{2}}{U_{m} R^{2}}\left[\frac{r^{2}}{2}-\frac{r^{5}}{5 R^{3}}\right]_{0}^{R}\\ &=\frac{2 C_{1} C_{2}}{U_{m} R^{2}}\left[\frac{R^{2}}{2}-\frac{R^{5}}{5 R^{3}}\right] \\ &=\frac{2 C_{1} C_{2}}{U_{m} R^{2}}\left[\frac{R^{2}}{2}-\frac{R^{2}}{5}\right] \\ &=\frac{2 C_{1} C_{2}}{U_{m} R^{2}}\left[\frac{5 R^{2}-2 R^{2}}{10}\right] \\ &=\frac{2 C_{1} C_{2}}{U_{m} R^{2}} \times \frac{3}{10} R^{2}=\frac{0.6 C_{1} C_{2}}{U_{m}} \quad\ldots(i) \end{aligned}[/latex]
since [latex] u(r, x)=C_{1}[/latex], constant [latex]U_{m}=C_{1} [/latex]
Substituting [latex]U_{m}=C_{1} [/latex] in above Eq. (i), we get
[latex] T_{m}=\frac{0.6 C_{1} C_{2}}{C_{1}}=0.6 C_{2}[/latex]

Drag force = average shear stress x area
where [latex]\bar{\tau}=[/latex] average shear stress

raw_source.text: Water ([latex]\rho =1000 kg/m^{3}[/latex]) flows through a venturimeter with inlet diameter 80 mm and throat diameter 40 mm. The inlet and throat gauge pressures are measured to be 400 kPa and 130 kPa respectively. Assuming the venturimeter to be horizontal and neglecting friction, the inlet velocity (in m/s)  is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \rho &=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ d_{1} &=80 \mathrm{mm}=0.08 \mathrm{mm} \\ d_{2} &=40 \mathrm{mm}=0.04 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex] \begin{aligned} p_{1}&=400 \mathrm{kPa}=400 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{Pa} \\ p_{2}&=130 \mathrm{kPa}=130 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{Pa} \end{aligned} [/latex]
Applying Bernoullis equation between sections 1 and 2
[latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{p_{1}}{\rho g}+\frac{V_{1}^{2}}{2 g}&+z_{1}=\frac{p_{2}}{\rho g}+\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2 g}+z_{2} \\ \text{where }z_{1}&=z_{1} \text{ for horizontal pipe}\\ \therefore \quad \frac{p_{1}}{\rho g}+\frac{V_{1}^{2}}{2 g}&=\frac{p_{2}}{\rho g}+\frac{V_{2}^{2}}{2 g} \\ or \quad \frac{p_{1}-p_{2}}{\rho g}&=\frac{V_{2}^{2}-V_{1}^{2}}{2 g} \\ or \quad \frac{p_{1}-p_{2}}{\rho}&=\frac{V_{2}^{2}-V_{2}^{2}}{2} \quad\ldots(i)\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Applying continuity equation between sections and 2
[latex]\begin{aligned} A_{1} V_{1}&=A_{2} V_{2} \\ \frac{\pi}{4} d_{1}^{2} V_{1}&=\frac{\pi}{2} d_{2}^{2} V_{2}\\ \text{or }\quad d_{1}^{2} V_{1}&=d_{2}^{2} V_{2}\\ \text{or }\quad V_{2}&=\left(\frac{d_{1}}{d_{2}}\right)^{2} V_{1}=\left(\frac{0.08}{0.04}\right)^{2} V_{1} \\ V_{2}&=4 V_{1}\\ \text{Substituting } V_{2}&=4 V_{1} \text{ in Eq. }( i ),\text{ we get}\\ \frac{400 \times 10^{3}-130 \times 10^{3}}{1000}&=\frac{\left(4 V_{1}\right)^{2}-V_{1}^{2}}{2} \\ 540&=16 \mathrm{V}_{1}^{2}-V_{1}^{2} \\ 540&=15 \mathrm{V}_{1}^{2}\\ or \quad V_{1}^{2}&=36\\ or \quad V_{1}&=6 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A well insulated rigid container of volume 1[latex]m^{3}[/latex]  contains 1.0 kg of an ideal gas [[latex]C_{p}[/latex] = 1000 J/(kg.K) and [latex]C_{v}[/latex] = 800 J/(kg.K)] at a pressure of [latex]10^{5}[/latex] Pa. A stirrer is rotated at constant rpm in the container for 1000 rotations and the applied torque is 100 N-m.  The final temperature of the gas (in K) is
raw_source.solution:
Work done = Torque [latex]\times[/latex] angular displacement
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=100 \times 2 \pi \times 1000=-628.318 \mathrm{kJ} \\ p_{1} V_{1} &=m R T_{1} \\ T_{1}=\frac{p_{1} V_{1}}{m R} &=\frac{10^{2} \times 1}{0.2 \times 1}=500 \mathrm{K} \\ \therefore \quad R &=c_{p}-c_{v}=0.2 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \end{aligned}[/latex]
According to 1 st law of thermodynamic
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \quad Q-W=\Delta U \\ -(-628.318) \mathrm{kJ}=m c_{v}\left(T_{2}-T_{1}\right) \\ \text { or } \quad T_{2}=500+\frac{628.318}{1 \times 0.8}=1285.39 \mathrm{K} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Steam enters a well insulated turbine and expands isentropically throughout. At an intermediate pressure, 20 percent of the mass is extracted for process heating and the remaining steam expands isentropically to 9 kPa.
Inlet to turbine: P = 14 MPa, T =[latex]560^{\circ}C[/latex] , h = 3486 kJ/kg, s = 6.6 kJ/(kg.K)
Intermediate stage: h = 2776 kJ/kg
Exit of turbine: P = 9 kPa, [latex]h_{f}[/latex] = 174 kJ/kg, [latex]h_{g}[/latex] = 2574 kJ/kg, [latex]s_{f}[/latex] = 0.6 kJ/(kg.K), [latex]s_{g}[/latex] = 8.1 kJ/(kg.K)

If the flow rate of steam entering the turbine is 100 kg/s, then the work output (in MW) is _________
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
At turbine inlet:
[latex] \begin{aligned} h_{1} &=3486 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \mathrm{s}_{1} &=6.6 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{K} \\ m_{1} &=100 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]
At intermediate stage:
[latex] \begin{aligned} h_{2}&=2776 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ m_{2}&=0.2 \mathrm{m}_{1}=0.2 \times 100=20 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]
At turbine exit:
[latex] \begin{aligned} P_{3} &=9 \mathrm{kPa} \\ m_{3} &=0.8 \mathrm{m}_{1}=0.8 \times 100=80 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}\\ \mathrm{At} \quad P_{3}&=9 \mathrm{kPa} \\ h_{f} &=174 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{g} &=2574 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ s_{f} &=0.6 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ s_{g} &=8.1 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ s_{3} &=s_{1}=s_{f}+x_{3}\left(s_{g}-s_{f}\right) \\ 6.6 &=0.6+x_{3}(8.1-0.6) \\ 6 &=7.5 x_{3} \\ \text{or}\quad x_{3} &=0.8\\ h_{3}&=h_{f}+x_{3}\left(h_{g}-h_{f}\right)\\ &=174+0.8(2574-174) \\ &=2094 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Work output,
[latex] \begin{aligned} W &=m_{1}\left(h_{1}-h_{2}\right)+m_{3}\left(h_{2}-h_{3}\right) \\ &=100(3486-2776) \\ &\quad +80(2776-2094) \\ &=71000+54560 \\ &=125560 \mathrm{kW} \\ &=125.56 \mathrm{MW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: During the development of a product, an entirely new process plan is made based on design logic, examination of geometry and tolerance information. This type of process planning is known as
raw_source.solution:
A generative manufacturing process different from a traditional manufacturing process develops a product with the addition of material instead of removal of the excess material as in case of a traditional manufacturing process.
In the generative manufacturing process, plans are generated by means of decision logic, formulas, technology algorithm and geometry-based data to perform uniquely the many processing decision for converting a part from raw material to a finished state.
There are two major components of a generative process planning system.

A geometry-based coding scheme.
Process knowledge in the form of decision logic and data.

Geometry-based coding scheme:
The objective of a geometric based coding scheme is to define all geometric features for all process related surfaces together with feature dimensions, locations, tolerances and the surface finish desired on the features.

Advantage of Generative Manufacturing Process:
No tools and fixtures are required.
No restriction on geometry of the part shape exists.
Composite parts and assemblies can be produced in one go.
Small batch production of complex parts is economically viable.

raw_source.text: The head loss for a laminar incompressible flow through a horizontal circular pipe is [latex]h_{1}[/latex]. Pipe length and fluid remaining the same, if the average flow velocity doubles and the pipe diameter reduces to half its previous value, the head loss is[latex]h_{2}[/latex] . The ratio [latex]\frac{h_{2}}{h_{1}}[/latex]  is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text { Head loss: } & h_{f}=\frac{32 \mu \bar{u} L}{\rho g D^{2}} \\ & h_{1}=\frac{32 \mu \bar{u} L}{\rho g D^{2}}\\ \text{and }\quad h_{2}&=\frac{32 \mu \times 2 \bar{u} L}{\rho g(D / 2)^{2}} \\ &=\frac{32 \mu 2 \bar{u} L \times 4}{\rho g D^{2}}=\frac{8 \times 32 \mu \pi L}{\rho g D^{2}} \\ \frac{h_{2}}{h_{1}} &=\frac{8 \times 32 \mu \bar{u} L}{\rho g D^{2}} \times \frac{\rho g D^{2}}{32 \mu \bar{U} L}=8 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: For a fully developed laminar flow of water (dynamic viscosity 0.001 Pa-s) through a pipe of radius 5 cm, the axial pressure gradient is -10 Pa/m. The magnitude of axial velocity (in m/s) at a radial location of 0.2 cm is _______
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \mu &=0.001 \mathrm{Pa}-\mathrm{s} \\ R &=5 \mathrm{cm}=0.05 \mathrm{m} \\ \frac{\partial p}{\partial x} &=-10 \mathrm{Pa} / \mathrm{m} \\ r &=0.2 \mathrm{cm}=0.002 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

For incompressible laminar flow throughpipe Local velocity,
[latex] \begin{aligned} u &=-\frac{1}{4 \mu} \frac{\partial p}{\partial x}\left[R^{2}-r^{2}\right] \\ &=-\frac{1}{4 \times 0.001} \times(-10)\left[(0.05)^{2}-(0.002)^{2}\right] \\ &=6.24 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A balanced counterflow heat exchanger has a surface area of 20 [latex]m^{2}[/latex]  and overall heat transfer coefficient of 20 W/[latex]m^{2}[/latex] -K. Air ([latex]C_{p}[/latex] =1000 J/kg-K) entering at 0.4 kg/s and 280 K is to be preheated by the air leaving the system at 0.4 kg/s and 300 K. The outlet temperature (in K) of the preheated air is
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} A&=20 \mathrm{m}^{3} ; \quad U=20 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} ; \quad c_{p h}=1000 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kg} \mathrm{K} \\ m_{c}&=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad T_{c 1}=280 \mathrm{K} ; \quad m_{h}=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \\ T_{h 2}&=300 \mathrm{K} ; \quad T_{c 2}=? \end{aligned}[/latex]
By energy balance,
Heat lost by hot fluid = Heat gained by cold fluid
[latex] m_{h} c_{p h}\left(T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}\right)=m_{c} c_{p c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right) [/latex]
[latex] \text{or }\quad T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}=T_{c 2}-T_{c 1} \quad \because m_{h} c_{p h}=m_{c} c_{p c}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} T_{h 1}-T_{c 2} &=T_{h 2}-T_{c 1} \\ \theta_{1} &=\theta_{2} \\ \text { If } \theta_{1}&=\theta_{2} \text { , then } L M T D=\theta_{1}=\theta_{2} \\ Q &=A U L M T D \\ Q &=A U \times \theta_{1} \\ &=20 \times 20 \times\left(T_{h 2}-T_{c 1}\right) \\ &=400(300-280)=8000 \mathrm{kW} \\ \text{also }\quad Q&=m_{c} c_{p c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right) \\ \therefore \quad 8000 &=0.4 \times 1000\left(T_{c 2}-280\right) \\ 20&=T_{c 2}-280 \\ \text{or}\quad T_{c 2}&=300^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned} [/latex]
Alternatively:
Given data:
[latex] A=20 \mathrm{m}^{3} ; U=20 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} ; \quad [/latex]
[latex] c_{\mathrm{ph}}=1000 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} [/latex]
[latex] m_{c}=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} ; \quad T_{c 1}=280 \mathrm{K} ; \quad m_{h}=0.4 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
[latex] T_{h 2}=300 \mathrm{K} ; \quad T_{c 2}=?[/latex]

By energy balance,
Heat lost by hot fluid = Heat gained by cold fluid
[latex] m_{h} c_{p h}\left(T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}\right)=m_{c} c_{p c}\left(T_{c 2}-T_{c 1}\right) [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { or } T_{h 1}-T_{h 2} &=T_{c 2}-T_{c 1} \qquad \because m_{h} c_{p h}=m_{c} c_{p c} \\ T_{h 1}-300 &=T_{c 2}-280 \\ T_{h 1}-T_{c 2} &=300-280 \qquad \ldots(1) \\ T_{h 1}-T_{c 2} &=20 \\ \epsilon&=\frac{N T U}{N T U+1} \quad[ \text{For balancing heat exchanger}]\\ \frac{T_{h 1}-T_{h 2}}{T_{h 1}-T_{c 1}} &=\frac{1}{1+1} \\ \frac{T_{h 1}-300}{T_{h 1}-280} &=\frac{1}{2} \\ 2 T_{h 1}-600 &=T_{h 1}-280 \\ T_{h 1} &=600-280=320 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned} [/latex]
Substitute the value of [latex]T_{h 1}=320 \mathrm{K} [/latex] in Eq. (1), we get
[latex] 320-T_{c 2}=20 [/latex]
[latex] \text{or }\quad T_{c 2}=300 \mathrm{K}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A cylindrical uranium fuel rod of radius 5 mm in a nuclear reactor is generating heat at the rate of [latex]4\times 10^{7} Wm^{3}[/latex] . The rod is cooled by a liquid (convective heat transfer coefficient 1000 W/[latex]m^{2}[/latex]-K) at  [latex]25^{\circ}C[/latex]. At steady state, the surface temperature (in K) of the rod is
raw_source.solution:
Given data:
[latex] \begin{aligned} r&=5 \mathrm{mm}=0.005 \mathrm{m}\\ \therefore \quad &=2 r=2 \times 0.005=0.010 \mathrm{m} \\ q_{G} &=4 \times 10^{7} \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ h_{0} &=1000 \mathrm{W} / \mathrm{m}^{2} \mathrm{K} \\ T_{0} &=25^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For steady state heat transfer,
Rate of heat generation in the rod
= rate of convection heat transfer from rod surface to fluid
[latex] \begin{aligned} q_{G} \times \text { volume of } \operatorname{rod} &=h_{0} A\left(T_{s}-T_{0}\right) \\ q_{G} \times \frac{\pi}{4} d^{2} l^{\prime} &=h_{0} \times \pi d l\left(T_{s}-T_{0}\right) \\ \frac{d q_{G}}{4} &=h_{0}\left(T_{s}-T_{0}\right) \\ \frac{0.010 \times 4 \times 10^{7}}{4} &=1000\left(T_{s}-25\right) \\ \text{or }\quad T_{s}-25 &=100\\ \text{or }\quad T_{s}&=100+25=125^{\circ} \mathrm{C}\\ &=(125+273) \mathrm{K}=398 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Work is done on an adiabatic system due to which its velocity changes from 10 m/s to 20 m/s, elevation increases by 20 m and temperature increases by 1 K. The mass of the system is 10 kg,  [latex]C_{v}[/latex]  = 100 J/(kg.K) and gravitational acceleration is 10 m/[latex]s^{2}[/latex] . If there is no change in any other component of the energy of the system, the magnitude of total work done (in kJ) on the system is _______

raw_source.text: A cube and a sphere made of cast iron (each of volume 1000 [latex]cm^{3}[/latex]) were cast under identical conditions.  The time taken for solidifying the cube was 4 s. The solidification time (in s) for the sphere is __________
raw_source.solution:
Time of solidification(T)
[latex] \begin{array}{l} =k\left[\frac{\text { volume }}{\text { surface area }}\right]^{2} \\ {\left[\begin{array}{l} \left.\frac{T_{\text {sphere }}}{T_{\text {cube }}}\right]=\left[\frac{A_{\text {cube }}}{A_{\text {sphere }}}\right]^{2}=\left[\frac{6 a^{2}}{4 / 3 \pi r^{3}}\right]^{2}-(1) \end{array}\right.}\\ \because\left[V_{\text {sphere }}=V_{\text {cube }}\right] \\ V_{\text {cube }}=a^{3}=1000 \mathrm{cm}^{3} \\ \therefore \qquad a =10\mathrm{cm}\\ V_{\text {sphere }}=\frac{4}{3} \pi r^{3}=1000\\ \Rightarrow \qquad r=6.2035 \mathrm{cm} \\ \end{array}[/latex]
Putting in Eq.(1), we get
[latex] \frac{T_{\text {sphere }}}{T_{\text {cube }}}=\left[\frac{6 \times 10^{2}}{4 \pi \times(6.2035)^{2}}\right]^{2} [/latex]

raw_source.text:
The flow stress (in MPa) of a material is given by
[latex]\sigma=500\varepsilon^{0.1}[/latex] ;

where [latex]\varepsilon[/latex] is true strain. The Young's modulus of elasticity of the material is 200 GPa. A block of thickness 100 mm made of this material is compressed to 95 mm thickness and then the load is removed. The final dimension of the block (in mm) is _________
raw_source.solution:
Equating the stress to the equation up to elastic limit, we get
[latex] \begin{aligned} \sigma &=500 \varepsilon^{0.1}=200 \times 10^{3} \times \varepsilon \\ \Rightarrow \qquad\varepsilon^{0.9} &=\frac{500}{200 \times 10^{3}}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \varepsilon(\text { tuestain })&=1.28476 \times 10^{-3}\\ \Rightarrow \quad \varepsilon_{T}&=\ln (1+\varepsilon)\\ \varepsilon(\text { engg.strain })_{\text {upto elastic limit }}&=1.285586 \times 10^{-3}=\frac{\Delta L}{L} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad(\Delta L)_{\text {upto elastic limit }}&=0.128558 \mathrm{mm}\\ \Rightarrow \qquad & \text{Final dimension of block} \\ &=95+ \text{ elastic recover}\\ &=95.128558 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
