By Trapezoidal rule
[latex] \begin{aligned} \int_{0}^{1} f(x) d x &=\frac{h}{2}\left[\left(y_{0}+y_{2}\right)+2 y_{1}\right] \\ &=\frac{0.5}{2}[(3+5)+2(4)]=4 \end{aligned} [/latex]
By Simpson rule
[latex] \int_{0}^{1} f(x) d x=\frac{h}{3}\left[\left(y_{0}+y_{2}\right)+4 y_{1}\right] [/latex]
[latex] =\frac{0.5}{3}[(3+5)+4(4)]=4 [/latex]
The difference between the two results will be zero.

raw_source.text: The velocity profile inside the boundary layer for flow over a flat plate is given as [latex]\frac{u}{U_{\infty}}=\sin (\frac{\pi }{2} \frac{y}{\delta } )[/latex] , Where [latex]U_{\infty}[/latex] is the free stream velocity and  [latex]\delta[/latex]  is the local boundary layer thickness. If [latex]\delta ^{*}[/latex] is the local displacement thickness,is the local displacement thickness, the value of  [latex]\frac{\delta ^{*}}{\delta }[/latex]  is
raw_source.solution:
Given [latex]\quad \frac{u}{U_{\infty}}=\sin \left(\frac{\pi}{2} \frac{y}{\delta}\right) [/latex]
where [latex]\quad \delta= [/latex] Boundary layer thickness Local displacement thickness,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \delta^{*}&=\int_{0}^{\delta}\left(1-\frac{u}{U_{\infty}}\right) d y \\ &=\int_{0}^{\delta}\left[1-\sin \left(\frac{\pi y}{2 \delta}\right)\right] d y \\ &=\left[y+\frac{2 \delta}{\pi} \times \cos \left(\frac{\pi y}{2 \delta}\right)\right]_{0}^{\delta} \\ &=\left[\delta+0-0-\frac{2 \delta}{\pi}\right] \\ \delta^{*}&=\delta\left(1-\frac{2}{\pi}\right)\\ or,\quad \frac{\delta^{*}}{\delta}&=1-\frac{2}{\pi} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

raw_source.text: Consider steady flow of an incompressible fluid through two long and straight pipes of diameters [latex]d_{1}[/latex]  and [latex]d_{2}[/latex]  arranged in series. Both pipes are of equal length and the flow is turbulent in both pipes. The friction factor for turbulent flow though pipes is of the form. [latex]f=k(Re)^{-n}[/latex], where K and n are known positive constants and Re is the Reynolds number. Neglecting minor losses, the ratio of the frictional pressure drop in pipe 1 to that in pipe 2,[latex](\frac{\Delta P_{1}}{\Delta P_{2}})[/latex], is given by
raw_source.solution:
For series connection,
[latex] Q_{1}=Q_{2}=Q[/latex]
As given [latex]\quad l_{1}=l_{2}=l [/latex]
For horizontal pipe,
[latex] \begin{aligned} h_{f}&=\Delta p \\ h_{f_{1}}&=\frac{f_{1} L Q^{2}}{12.1 d_{1}^{5}} ; \quad h_{f_{2}}=\frac{f_{2} L Q^{2}}{12.1 d_{2}^{5}} \\ \frac{\Delta P_{1}}{\Delta P_{2}}&=\frac{f_{1}}{d_{1}^{5}} \times \frac{d_{2}^{5}}{f_{2}} \\ f&=\frac{k}{\operatorname{Re}^{n}}=\frac{k}{\left(\frac{V D}{v}\right)^{n}} \\ Q&=\frac{\pi}{4} D^{2} \times V \\ V &\propto \frac{1}{D^{2}} \\ f &\propto \frac{1}{\left(\frac{1}{D^{2}} D\right)^{n}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
By equation (i) [latex]f \propto D^{n} [/latex]
[latex] \frac{\Delta P_{1}}{\Delta P_{2}}=\frac{d_{1}^{n}}{d_{1}^{5}} \times \frac{d_{2}^{5}}{d_{2}^{n}}[/latex]
[latex] \frac{\Delta P_{1}}{\Delta P_{2}}=\frac{d_{2}^{5-n}}{d_{1}^{5-n}}[/latex]

raw_source.text: For a steady flow, the velocity field is [latex]\overrightarrow{\textrm{v}}=(-x^{2}+3y)\hat{i}+(2xy)\hat{j}[/latex] , The magnitude of the acceleration of a particle at (1, -1) is
raw_source.solution:
Given velocity field,
[latex] \vec{V}=\left(-x^{2}+3 y\right) \hat{i}+(2 x y) \hat{j}[/latex]
[latex] where \quad u=-x^{2}+3 y \text { and } v=2 x y[/latex]
The acceleration components along x and y -axis.
[latex] \begin{aligned} a_{x}&=u \frac{\partial u}{\partial x}+v \frac{\partial u}{\partial y}\\ \text{and}\quad a_{y} &=u \frac{\partial v}{\partial x}+v \frac{\partial v}{\partial y} \\ &=\left(-x^{2}+3 y\right) \times(-2 x)+2 x y \times 3 \\ &=2 x^{3}-6 x y+6 x y=2 x^{3}\\ \text{and}\quad a_{y} &=\left(-x^{2}+3 y\right) \times 2 y+2 x y \times 2 x \\ &=-2 y x^{2}+6 y^{2}+4 x^{2} y=2 y x^{2}+6 y^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
At point (1,-1)
[latex] \begin{aligned} a_{x}&=2\\ \text{and}\quad a_{y} &=2 \times(-1) \times 1+6 \times(-1)^{2} \\ &=-2+6=4 \\ \vec{a} &=a_{x} \hat{i}+a_{y} \hat{j}=2 i+4 \hat{j} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Resultant acceleration:
[latex] \begin{aligned} a &=\sqrt{4+16}=\sqrt{20} \\ &=\sqrt{4 \times 5}=2 \sqrt{5} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: One kg of an ideal gas (gas constant, R = 400 J/kg.K; specific heat at constant volume,[latex]c_{\textrm{v}}[/latex] =1000 J / kg .K) at 1 bar, and 300 K is contained in a sealed rigid cylinder. During an adiabatic process, 100kJ of work is done on the system by a stirrer. The increase in entropy of the system is _________ J/K.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]m=1 \mathrm{kg} ; \quad R=400 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{k}[/latex]


[latex] \begin{aligned} c_{v}&=1000 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K} \\ T_{i}&=300 \mathrm{K} ; P_{i}=100 \mathrm{kPa} \\ W&=100 \mathrm{kJ} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Applying first law:
[latex] \begin{aligned} Q&=\Delta U+W\\ \Rightarrow \quad 0&=m c_{v}\left(T_{f}-T_{i}\right)+(-100) \times 10^{3} J \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0&=1 \times 1000 \times\left(T_{f}-300\right)-100 \times 10^{3} \\ \Rightarrow \quad T_{f}&=400 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Entropy change for ideal gas
[latex] \begin{aligned} \Delta S &=m\left[C_{v} \ln \frac{T_{f}}{T_{i}}+R \ln \frac{V_{f}}{V_{i}}\right] \quad \because V_{i}=V_{f} \\ &=1 \times\left[1000 \ln \frac{400}{300}+0\right] \\ &=287.682 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

raw_source.text: The Pressure ratio across a gas turbine (for air, specific heat at constant pressure,[latex]c_{\textrm{p}}[/latex] 1040 J / kg .K and ratio of specific heats, [latex]\gamma =1.4[/latex]  ) is 10. If the inlet temperature to the turbine is 1200K and the isentropic efficiency is 0.9, the gas temperature at turbine exit is ______ K.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Given data:}\;\mathrm{c}_{p}&=1040 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kgK} ; \gamma=1.4 ; r_{p}=10; \\ T_{3}&=1200 \mathrm{K};\;\eta=0.9 \\ \frac{T_{7}}{T_{4 s}}&=\left(r_{p}\right) \frac{\gamma-1}{\gamma} \end{aligned}[/latex]


[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{1200}{T_{4 s}} &=(10)^{(1.4-1) / 1.4} \\ \text { or } \quad T_{4 s} &=621.53 \mathrm{K} \\ \eta_{T} &=\frac{T_{3}-T_{4}}{T_{3}-T_{4 s}} \\ 0.9 &=\frac{1200-T_{4}}{1200-621.53} \\ \text{or}\qquad T_{4} &=679.4 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Moist air is treated as an ideal gas mixture of water vapor and dry air (molecular weight of air = 28.84 and molecular weight of water = 18). At a location, the total pressure is 100 kPa, the temperature is [latex]30^{\circ}C[/latex]  and the relative humidity is 55%. Given that the saturation pressure of water at [latex]30^{\circ}C[/latex].is 4246 Pa, the mass of water vapor per kg of dry air is _____________ grams.
raw_source.solution:
Relative humidity:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \phi &=\frac{p_{v}}{p_{v s}} \\ 0.55 &=\frac{p_{v}}{4246}\\ \text { or } \quad p_{v}&=2335.3 \mathrm{Pa}=2.335 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \therefore \quad \omega &=\frac{(\mathrm{Mol} \cdot \mathrm{wt})_{\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{O}}}{(\mathrm{Mol} \cdot \mathrm{w} \mathrm{t})_{\mathrm{air}}} \times\left(\frac{p_{v}}{p-p_{v}}\right) \\ &=\frac{18}{28.84} \times\left(\frac{2.335}{100-2.335}\right) \\ &=0.01492 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kg} \text { of d.a } \\ \text { also } \quad \omega &=\frac{m_{v}}{m_{a}} \\ \therefore \quad 0.01492 &=\frac{m_{v}}{1}\\ \text{or }\quad m_{v}&=0.01492 \mathrm{kg}=14.92 \mathrm{gm} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Air contains 79% N2 and 21%  [latex]O_{2}[/latex] on a molar basis. Methane ([latex]CH_{4}[/latex]) is burned with 50% excess air than required stoichiometrically. Assuming complete combustion of methane, the molar percentage of [latex]N_{2}[/latex]  in the products is _______________
raw_source.solution:
Stoichiometrically balanced equation for combustion of [latex]{\mathrm{CH}}_4[/latex]
[latex]{\mathrm{CH}}_4+2{\mathrm O}_2\rightarrow{\mathrm{CO}}_2+2{\mathrm H}_2\mathrm O[/latex]
Actual moles of [latex]{\mathrm{O}}_2[/latex] used [latex]=2\times\left(\frac{150}{100}\right)=3[/latex] moles of [latex]{\mathrm{O}}_2[/latex]

Actual equation
[latex]{\mathrm{CH}}_4+3{\mathrm o}_2\rightarrow{\mathrm{Co}}_2+2{\mathrm H}_2\mathrm o+{\mathrm O}_2[/latex]

Consider Air instead of pure [latex]{\mathrm{O}}_2[/latex]
[latex]{\mathrm{CH}}_4+\left[3{\mathrm o}_2+3\left(\frac{79}{21}\right){\mathrm N}_2\right]\rightarrow{\mathrm{Co}}_2+2{\mathrm H}_2\mathrm O+{\mathrm O}_2+\frac{79}7\mathrm N2[/latex]

Total moles in product [latex]=1+2+1+\frac{79}7=15.285[/latex]
Molar percentage of [latex]{\mathrm N}_2=\frac{11.285}{15.285}\times100=73.830\%[/latex]

raw_source.text: Two black surfaces, AB and BC, of lengths 5m and 6m, respectively, are oriented as shown. Both surfaces extend infinitely into the third dimension. Given that view factor [latex]F_{12}=0.5[/latex],[latex]T_{1}=800K[/latex],[latex]T_{2}=600K[/latex] , [latex]T_{surrounding} =300K[/latex], and Stefan Boltzmann constant, [latex]\sigma =5.67\,\times\,10^{-8}W/(m^{2}K^{4})[/latex], the heat transfer rate from Surface 2 to the surrounding environment is ____________ kW.

[latex]F_{12} =0.5[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} T_{1} &=800 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{2} &=600 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{\text {surounding }} &=300 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Let (3) denote the surrounding environment
(Assume unit width perpendicular to plane of Fig.)
From summation rule:
[latex] \begin{aligned} F_{21}+F_{\beta 2}^{0}+F_{23} &=1 \\ A_{1} F_{12} &=A_{2} F_{21}=6 \times 1 \times 0.5 \\ &=(5 \times 1) \times F_{21} \\ F_{21} &=\frac{6 \times 0.5}{5}=0.6\\ \therefore \quad F_{23}&=1-F_{21}=0.4 \end{aligned}[/latex]
since surrounding environment being large,
No surface has a surface resistance.

Heat transfer rate from (2) and (3)[latex]=\frac{E_{b_{2}}-E_{b_{3}}}{\frac{1}{A_{2} F_{23}}} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} &=\frac{\sigma\left(T_{2}^{4}-T_{3}^{4}\right)}{1} \\ &=\frac{5.67 \times 10^{-8}\left(600^{4}-300^{4}\right)}{A_{2} F_{23}} \text { watt/metre }\\ &=13.778 \mathrm{kW} / \mathrm{metre} \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Assume that heat exchange is per unit width perpendicular to plane of figure

raw_source.text:
An initially stress-free massless elastic beam of length L and circular cross-section with diameter d [latex](d \lt \! \lt l)[/latex] is held fixed between two walls as shown. The beam material has Young's modulus E and coefficient of thermal expansion [latex]\alpha[/latex] .

Condition for buckling,

load

raw_source.text: A point mass of 100 kg is dropped onto a massless elastic bar (cross-sectional area=[latex]100\,mm^{2}[/latex] , length = 1m, Young's moduls = 100 GPa) from a height H of 10mm as shown (Figure is not to scale). If [latex]g=10\,m/s^{2}[/latex],, the maximum compression of the elastic bar is _______mm.
raw_source.solution:
Given loading is impact loading
[latex] \begin{aligned} \delta_{\text {impact }} &=\delta_{\text {static }} \times \text { Impact factor } \\ \delta_{\text {static }} &=\frac{W L}{A E}=\frac{100 \times 10 \times 1000}{100 \times 100 \times 10^{3}} \\ &=0.1 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Impact factor (I.F.)
[latex] =1+\sqrt{1+\frac{2 h}{\delta_{\text {static }}}}[/latex]
[latex] =1+\sqrt{1+\frac{2 \times 10}{0.1}}=15.178[/latex]
Hence maximum compression of bar
= Impact elongation
[latex] =0.1 \times 15.178=1.5178 \mathrm{m}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A mass m of a perfect gas at pressure [latex]P_{1}[/latex]  and volume [latex]V_{1}[/latex]  undergoes an isothermal process. raw_source.solution:
Work done on the system is considered as positive, so
[latex] \delta W=-P d V[/latex]

raw_source.text: The surface integral  [latex]\int \underset{s}{\int} F. n dS[/latex] over the surface S of the sphere [latex]x^{2}+y^{2}+z^{2}=9[/latex], where [latex]F=(x+y)i+(x+z)j+(y+z)k[/latex] and n is the unit outward surface normal, yields ______.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\quad F = ( x + y ) i + ( x + z ) j + ( y + z ) k [/latex]
[latex] \nabla \cdot F = \frac { \partial } { \partial x } ( x + y ) + \frac { \partial } { \partial y } ( x + z ) + \frac { \partial } { \partial z } ( y + z ) [/latex]
[latex] = 1 + 0 + 1 = 2 [/latex]
By Gauss divergence theorem
[latex] { l } \iint _ { s } F \cdot \hat { n } d S = \iint _ { V } \nabla \cdot \bar { F } d V = \iint _ { V } 2 d V [/latex]
[latex] = 2 V \text { where } V \text { is volume of } x ^ { 2 } + y ^ { 2 } + z ^ { 2 } [/latex]
[latex] = 2 \left( \frac { 4 } { 3 } \pi ( 3 ) ^ { 3 } \right) = 226.08[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider the differential equation [latex]3y{}''(x)+27y(x)=0[/latex]  with initial conditions [latex]y(0)=0[/latex] and [latex]y{}'(0)=2000[/latex]. The value of y at x=1 is ____.
raw_source.solution:
The direction is [latex]3 y^{\prime \prime}(x)+27 y(x)=0 [/latex]
The auxillary equation is
[latex] \begin{aligned} 3 m^{2}+27 &=0 \\ m^{2}+9 &=0 \\ m &=\pm 31 \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \text{Solution is} y=c_{1} \cos 3 x+c_{2} \sin 3 x [/latex]
[latex] \text{given that} y(0)=0 [/latex]
[latex] \therefore 0=c_{1} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} y^{\prime} &=-3 c_{1} \sin 3 x+3 c_{2} \cos 3 x \\ y^{\prime}(0) &=2000 \\ 2000 &=0+3 c_{2} \\ c_{2} &=\frac{2000}{3} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex]\therefore[/latex] Solution is
[latex] y=\frac{2000}{3} \sin 3 x[/latex]
[latex] \text{when }x=1 \quad y=\frac{2000}{3} \sin 3=94.08[/latex]

raw_source.text: Consider the matrix [latex]A=\begin{bmatrix} 50 & 70\\ 70 & 80 \end{bmatrix}[/latex]  whose eigenvectors  corresponding to eigenvalues [latex]\lambda _{1}[/latex] and [latex]\lambda _{2}[/latex] are [latex]X_{1}=\begin{bmatrix} 70\\ \lambda _{1}-50 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] and [latex]X_{2}=\begin{bmatrix} \lambda _{2}-80\\ 70 \end{bmatrix}[/latex] ,  respectively. The value of [latex]X_{1}^{T} X_{2}[/latex]  is _____.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]A=\left[\begin{array}{ll}50 & 70 \\70 & 80\end{array}\right][/latex]
Eigen values of A are [latex]\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2} &=130 \\ \lambda_{1} \lambda_{2} &=-900 \\ &\text { Given that } \\ X_{1} &=\left[\begin{array}{c}70 \\\lambda_{1}-50\end{array}\right] \\ X_{2}&=\left[\begin{array}{c}\lambda_{2}-80 \\70\end{array}\right] \\ X_{1}^{T} X_{2} &=\left[70 \quad \lambda_{1}-50\right]\left[\begin{array}{c}\lambda_{2}-80 \\70\end{array}\right] \\ &=70 \lambda_{2}-5600+70 \lambda_{1}-3500 \\ &=70\left(\lambda_{1}+\lambda_{2}\right)-9100 \\ &=70(130)-9100 \\ &=9100-9100=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: If [latex]f(z)=(x^{2}+ay^{2})+ibxy[/latex]  is a complex analytic function of [latex]z=x+iy[/latex] ,where [latex]i=\sqrt{-1}[/latex], then
raw_source.solution:
Given that the analytic function
[latex] \begin{aligned} f(2) &=\left(x^{2}+a y^{2}\right)+i b x y \\ u+i v &=\left(x^{2}+a y^{2}\right)+i(b x y) \\ u &=x^{2}+a y^{2} ; \quad v=b x y \\ u_{x} &=2 x ; \quad u_{y}=2 a y \\ v_{x} &=b y ; \quad v_{y}=b x \\ u_{x} &=v_{y} ; \quad u_{y}=-v_{x} \\ 2 x &=b x ; \quad 2 a y=-b y \\ b &=2 ; \quad 2 a=-b \quad \text { since } b=2 \\ 2 a &=-2 \\ a &=-1 \end{aligned}[/latex]

be there

raw_source.text: The radius of gyration of a compound pendulum about the point of suspension is 100mm. The distance between the point of suspension and the centre of mass is 250mm. Considering the acceleration due to gravity as [latex](9.81\, m/s^{2})[/latex], the natural frequency (in radian/s) of the compound pendulum is ______.
raw_source.solution:
If we displace this by an angle [latex]\theta[/latex] clockwise:

[latex]I \ddot{\theta}+m g \cdot a \sin \theta=0[/latex]
Taking [latex]\theta [/latex] very small:
[latex] \begin{array}{c} \sin \theta \approx \theta \qquad(k=100 \mathrm{mm}=0.1 \mathrm{m}) \\ \mathrm{r} \ddot{\theta}+\mathrm{mg} \cdot \mathrm{a} \cdot \theta=0 \\ \ddot{\theta}+\left(\frac{\mathrm{mg}}{\mathrm{I}} \mathrm{a}\right) \theta=0 \\ \mathrm{Here} \quad I=m \mathrm{k}^{2}=\mathrm{m}(0.1)^{2} \end{array}[/latex]
(I is the MI about the point of Hinge)
[latex] \begin{array}{l}\qquad\begin{aligned} I&=m(0.01) \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{m}^{2} \\ a&=250 \mathrm{mm}=0.250 \mathrm{m} \\ g&=9.81 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}\\ \ddot{\theta}+\left(\frac{m \times 9.81 \times 0.250}{(0.01) m}\right) \theta=0 \\ \ddot{\theta}+(245.25) \theta=0 \\ \qquad \omega_{n}=\sqrt{245.25}=15.660 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A gear train shown in the figure consists of gear P, Q, R and S. Gear Q and gear R are mounted on the same shaft. All the gears are mounted on parallel shafts and the number of teeth of P, Q, R and S are 24, 45, 30 and 80, respectively. Gear P is rotating at 400 rpm. The speed (in rpm) of the gear S is _____
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{ll} T_{P}=24 \\ T_{Q}=45 & N_{P}=400 \mathrm{rpm} \\ T_{R}=30 & N_{S}=? \\ T_{S}=80 \end{array}[/latex]
[latex] Here gear R is not meshing at all.
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \frac{N_{P}}{N_{Q}}=\frac{T_{O}}{T_{P}}=\frac{45}{24} \qquad \cdots(1)\\ \frac{N_{Q}}{N_{S}}=\frac{T_{S}}{T_{Q}}=\frac{80}{45}\qquad \cdots(2)\\ \text{By }(1) \times(2) \\ \frac{N_{P}}{N_{S}}=\frac{45}{24} \times \frac{80}{45} \\ N_{S}=N_{P} \times \frac{24}{80}=\frac{400 \times 24}{80} \\ N_{S}=120 \text { r.p.m } \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A helical compression spring made of wire of circular cross-section is subjected to a compressive load. The maximum shear stress induced in the cross-section of the wire is 24 MPA. For the same compressive load, if both the wire diameter and the mean coil diameter are doubled, the maximum shear stress (in MPa) induced in the cross-section of the wire is _______
raw_source.solution:
Max. shear stress induced in spring wire of a
helical compression spring is given by,
[latex] \begin{array}{c} \tau_{\max }=\frac{8 W D}{\pi d^{2}} k_{W} \quad \text { or } \quad \frac{8 W C}{\pi d^{2}} k_{W} \\ \tau_{\max } \propto \frac{1}{d^{2}} \\ {\left[\because W_{1}=W_{2}=W ; C_{1}=C_{2}\left(\text { i.e., } C=\frac{D}{d}\right)\right.} \\ \left.\left(k_{W}\right)_{1}=\left(k_{W}\right)_{2}=k_{W}\right] \\ \frac{\tau_{2}}{\tau_{1}}=\left(\frac{d_{1}}{d_{2}}\right)^{2} \\ \frac{\tau_{2}}{24}=\left(\frac{d}{2 d}\right)^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \tau_{2}=6 \mathrm{MPa} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Three masses are connected to a rotating shaft supported on bearings A and B as shown in the figure. The system is in a space where the gravitational effect is absent. Neglect the mass of shaft and rods connecting the masses.for [latex]m_{1}=10[/latex] kg,[latex]m_{2}=5[/latex] kg and [latex]m_{3}=2.5[/latex] kg and for a shaft angular speed of 1000 radian/s, the magnitude of the bearing reaction (in N) at location B is_____
raw_source.solution:
It means all three masses are in same plane
let us calculates the net force
[latex] \begin{array}{c} \Sigma F_{x}= \Sigma \mathrm{m} \mathrm{r} \omega^{2} \cos \theta \\ =\left(10 \times 0.1 \times \omega^{2}\right)-\left(5 \times 0.2 \times 6^{2} \cos 60^{\circ}\right) \\ -\left(2.5 \times 0.4 \times \omega^{2} \cos 60^{\circ}\right) \\ =\left[1-\left(5 \times 0.2 \times \frac{1}{2}\right)-\left(2.5 \times 0.4 \times \frac{1}{2}\right)\right] \omega^{2}=0 \\ \Sigma F_{y}= \Sigma \mathrm{mr} \omega^{2} \sin \theta \\ =\left(5 \times 0.2 \times \omega^{2} \sin 60^{\circ}\right) \\ -\left(2.5 \times 0.4 \times \omega^{2} \sin 60^{\circ}\right) \\ =\left[\left(1 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)-\left(1 \times \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right] \omega^{2} \\ =\left[\left(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)\right] \omega^{2}=0 \end{array}[/latex]
Net force,
[latex] =\sqrt{\Sigma F_{x}^{2}+\Sigma F_{y}^{2}}=0[/latex]
Therefore reaction at B is zero.
[latex] R_{B}=0[/latex]

raw_source.text: A steel plate, connected to a fixed channel using three identical bolts A, B and D, carries a load of 6kN as shown in the figure. Considering the effect of direct load of moment, the magnitude of resultant shear force (in kN) on bolt C is.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} P_{P}&=\frac{P}{n}=\frac{P}{3}=2 \mathrm{kN} \\ r_{A}&=r_{C}=50 ;\left(P_{S}\right)_{A}=\left(P_{S}\right)_{C} \\ r_{B}&=0 \Rightarrow\left(P_{S}\right)_{B}=0 \\ \frac{\left(P_{S}\right)_{C}}{r_{C}}\left[r_{C}^{2}+r_{B}^{2}+r_{A}^{2}\right]&=P \times e \end{aligned}[/latex]

[latex] \left(P_{S}\right)_{C} \times 2 \times r_{C}=P \times e [/latex]
[latex] \left(P_{S}\right)_{C}=\frac{6 \times 250}{2 \times 50}=15 \mathrm{kN} [/latex]
[latex] \theta_{A}=180^{\circ} ; \theta_{C}=0^{\circ} [/latex]
Resultant shear force [latex] \left(R_{C}\right)=P_{P}+\left(P_{S}\right)_{C} [/latex]
[latex][\therefore \theta_{C}=0^{0}] [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} R_{C}&=2+15=17 \mathrm{kN} \\ R_{A}&=\left(P_{S}\right) A-P_{P}=13 \mathrm{kN} \\ R_{B}&=P_{P}=2 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A single - plate clutch has a friction disc with inner and outer radii of 20 mm and 40 mm, respectively. The friction lining in the disc is made in such a way that the coefficient of friction [latex]\mu[/latex]  varies radially as [latex]\mu=0.01r[/latex], where r is in mm. The clutch needs to transmit a friction torque of 18.8 [latex]kN\! \! \cdot\! mm[/latex]. As per uniform pressure theory, the pressure (in MPa) on the disc is ________
raw_source.solution:
Normal load on elemental ring [latex](d M)=p 2 \pi r d r [/latex]
Frictional force on elemental ring [latex]\left(d F_{f}\right)=\mu d W [/latex]
Frictional torque transmitted by elemental ring,
[latex] d T_{f}=\left(d F_{f}\right) r[/latex]
Hence, [latex] \quad d T_{f}=\mu p 2 \pi r^{2} d r [/latex]
Total frictional torque transmitted by clutch plate
[latex] \begin{aligned} \left(T_{f}\right)&=\int_{R_{i}}^{R_{0}} d T_{f} \\ T_{f}&=\int_{R_{i}}^{P_{0}} \mu p 2 \pi r^{2} d r\\ \text{As per U.P.T.}\\ T_{f} &=2 \pi p \int_{R_{i}}^{R_{0}} \mu r^{2} d r \\ T_{f} &=2 \pi p \int_{R_{i}}^{R_{0}}(0.01 r) r^{2} d r \\ \left(T_{f}\right)_{U . P . T .} &=(2 \pi p)(0.01)\left[\frac{R_{0}^{4}-R_{i}^{4}}{4}\right] \\ 18.85 \times 10^{3} &=2 \pi p(0.01)\left[\frac{40^{4}-20^{4}}{4}\right] \\ p &=0.5 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The principal stresses at a point in a critical section of a machine component are [latex]\sigma _{1}=60[/latex] MPa, [latex]\sigma _{2}=5[/latex] MPa and [latex]\sigma _{2}=-40[/latex] MPa. For the material of the component, the tensile yield strength is [latex]\sigma _{y}=200[/latex] MPa. According to the maximum shear stress theory, the factor of safety is
raw_source.solution:
As per max. shear stress theory,
safe condition for design,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { Absolute } \tau_{\max }&=\frac{S_{Y S}}{N} \text { or } \frac{S_{Y_{t}}}{2 N}\\ \text{Absolute }\tau_{\max }&= \text{larger of}\\ &\begin{array}{l} {\left[\left|\frac{\sigma_{1}-\sigma_{2}}{2}\right|,\left|\frac{\sigma_{2}-\sigma_{3}}{2}\right|,\left|\frac{\sigma_{3}-\sigma_{1}}{2}\right|\right]} \\ =\left|\frac{\sigma_{3}-\sigma_{1}}{2}\right| \end{array}\\ &\left[\because \sigma_{1} \text { and } \sigma_{3} \text { are unlike in nature }\right] \\ &=\left|\frac{-40-60}{2}\right|=50 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \text{Hence,}\quad50&=\frac{200}{2(N)}\\ N&=2 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The rod PQ of length [latex]L=\sqrt{2}[/latex] m,and uniformly distributed mass of M=10 kg, is released from rest at the position shown in the figure. The ends slide along the frictionless faces OP and OQ. Assume acceleration due to gravity, [latex]g=10 \:m/s^{2}[/latex]. The mass moment of inertia of the rod about its centre of mass and an axis perpendicular to the plane of the figure is [latex](ML^{2}/12)[/latex]. At this instant, the magnitude of angular acceleration (in radian/[latex]s^{2}[/latex] ) of the rod is _____
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} L&=\sqrt{2} m \\ M&=10 \mathrm{kg}\\ g&=10 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Both the surfaces are smooth
[latex] \begin{aligned} \ddot{\theta} &=\alpha=\frac{3 g}{2 L} \sin \theta \\ \alpha &=\frac{3 \times 10}{2 \times \sqrt{2}} \sin 45^{\circ} \quad\left[\because \theta=45^{\circ}\right] \\ a &=\frac{3 \times 10}{2 \times \sqrt{2}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}=\frac{30}{4} \\ &=7.5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The arrangement shown in the figure measures the velocity V of a gas of density [latex]1\, kg/m^{3}[/latex] flowing through a pipe. The acceleration due to gravity is [latex]9.81\, m/s^{2}[/latex].If the manometric fluid is water (density 1000 kg/[latex]s^{2}[/latex]) and the velocity V is 20 m/s, the differential head h (in mm) between the two arms of the manometer is _____
raw_source.solution:
Method: (i)
Given data: [latex] p_{\text {gas }}=1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} ; \quad g=9.81 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} [/latex]
[latex] \rho_{m}=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}, \quad V=20 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} [/latex]
Dynamic pressure of gas [latex] =(\rho g h)_{\text {water }} [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{1}{2} \rho_{\mathrm{gas}} V^{2} &=\rho_{m} \times 9.81 \times h \\ \frac{1}{2} \times 1 \times(20)^{2} &=1000 \times 9.81 \times h\\ \text{or }h &=0.02038 \mathrm{m} \text { of water } \\ &=20.38 \mathrm{mm} \text { of water } \end{aligned}[/latex]
Method: (ii)
[latex] \begin{aligned} \rho_{m} &=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3}, \rho_{w}=1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ V &=20 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V &=\sqrt{2 g h\left(\frac{\rho_{m}}{\rho_{w}}-1\right)} \\ 20 &=\sqrt{2 \times 9.81 \times h\left(\frac{1000}{1}-1\right)} \\ h &=20.40 \mathrm{mm} \text { of water } \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A 60 mm-diameter water jet strikes a plate containing a hole of 40 mm diameter as shown in the figure. Part of the jet passes through the hole horizontally, and the remaining is deflected vertically. The density of water is 1000 kg/[latex]m^{3}[/latex]. If velocities are as indicated in the figure, the magnitude of horizontal force (in N) required to hold the plate is ______
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \rho&=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ \text{Force, F}&= \text{momentum }_{\text {inlet }}- \text{ momentum }_{\text {outlet }} \\ F &=(\dot{m} v)_{i n}-(\dot{m} v)_{o u t} \\ F &=\rho\left[\frac{\pi}{4}\left(D_{1}^{2}-D_{2}^{2}\right)\right] \times V^{2} \\ &=1000 \frac{\pi}{4} \times\left[0.06^{2}-0.04^{2}\right] \times 20^{2} \\ &=628.32 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: For the laminar flow of water over a sphere, the drag [latex]C_{F}[/latex]  is defined as [latex]C_{F}=F/(pU^{2}D^{2})[/latex], where F is drag force,[latex]\rho[/latex] is the fluid density, U is the fluid velocity  and D is the diameter of the sphere. The density of water is 1000 kg/[latex]m^{3}[/latex]. When the diameter of the sphere is 100mm and the fluid velocity is 2m/s, the drag coefficient is 0.5. If water now flows over another sphere of diameter 200mm under dynamically similar conditions, the drag force (in N) on this sphere is_____
raw_source.solution:
Drag coefficient:
[latex] C_{F}=\frac{F}{\rho U^{2} D^{2}}[/latex]
or Drag force:
[latex] F=C_{F} \rho U^{2} D^{2}[/latex]
Given data for sphere- -1
[latex] \begin{aligned} \rho_{1}&=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ D_{1}&=100 \mathrm{mm}=0.1 \mathrm{m} \\ U_{1}&=2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ C_{F}&=0.5 \end{aligned}[/latex]
For sphere- 2
[latex] \begin{aligned} \rho_{2}&=1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ D_{2}&=200 \mathrm{mm}=0.2 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]
For dynamically similar conditions,
[latex] \begin{aligned} (\mathrm{Re})_{1}&=(\mathrm{Re})_{2}\\ \frac{U_{1} D_{1}}{v_{1}}&=\frac{U_{2} D_{2}}{v_{2}}\\ \text{or }\qquad U_{1} D_{1} &=U_{2} D_{2} \quad \therefore v_{1}=v_{2} \\ 2 \times 0.1 &=U_{2} \times 0.2\\ \text{or }\qquad U_{2}&=1 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}\\ F_{2} &=C_{F} \rho U_{2}^{2} D_{2}^{2} \\ &=0.5 \times 1000 \times(1)^{2} \times(0.2)^{2} \\ &=20 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Viscous, Turbulent Flow and Boundary Layer Theory

raw_source.text: In the Rankine cycle for a steam power plant the turbine entry and exit enthalpies are 2803 kJ/kg and 1800 kJ/kg, respectively. The enthalpies of water at pump entry and exit are 121 kJ/kg and 124 kJ/kg, respectively. The specific steam consumption (in kg/k W.h) of the cycle is _______
raw_source.solution:
Given data [latex]h_{1}=2803\mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}[/latex]

[latex]\begin{aligned} h_{2} &=1800 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{3} &=121 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ h_{4} &=124 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ w_{T} &=h_{1}-h_{2} \\ &=2803-1800=1003 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ w_{P} &=h_{4}-h_{3} \\ &=124-121=3 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ w_{\text {net }} &=w_{T}-w_{P}=1003-3 \\ &=1000 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \mathrm{SSC} &=\frac{3600}{W_{\text {net }}}=\frac{3600}{1000}=3.6 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{kWh} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A calorically perfect gas (specific heat at constant pressure 1000 J/[latex]kg\cdot K[/latex] ) enters and leaves a gas turbine with the same velocity. The temperatures of the gas at turbine entry and exit are 1100 K and 400 K, respectively. The power produced is 4.6 MW and heat escapes at the rate of 300 kJ/s through the turbine casing. The mass flow rate of the gas (in kg/s) through the turbine is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} c_{p}&1\mathrm{kJ}/\mathrm{kg-K}\\ V_{i}&=V_{e}(\text { Inlet and exit velocity same }) \\ \dot{W}_{C . V} &=4.6 \mathrm{MW}=4.6 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{kW} \\ \dot{Q} &=300 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Applying SFEE,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \dot{m}(h_{i}+\frac{1}{2} V_{i}^{2}+g z_{i})+ \dot{Q} &=\dot{m}(h_{e}+\frac{1}{2} V_{e}^{2}+g z_{e})+\dot{W}_{C . V} \\ \dot{m}[c_{p}(T_{i}-T_{e})]+\dot{Q}&=\dot{W}_{C . V} \quad \text { (Let } z_{i}=z_{e}) \\ \dot{m}[1 \times(1100-400)]+(-300)&=4.6 \times 10^{3} \\ \Rightarrow \quad \dot{m}&=7 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: One kg of an ideal gas (gas constant R=287 J/kg.K) undergoes an irreversible process from state-1 (1 bar,300K) to state -2 (2 bar, 300 K). The change in specific entropy ([latex]s_{2}-s_{1}[/latex]) of the gas (in J/[latex]kg\cdot K[/latex]) in the process is ______
raw_source.solution:
Change in specific entropy of ideal gas
[latex] \begin{aligned} S_{f}-s_{i} &=c_{p} \ln \frac{T_{f}}{T_{i}}-R \ln \frac{P_{f}}{P_{i}} \\ &=1005 \ln \frac{300}{300}-287 \ln \frac{2}{1} \\ &=0-287 \ln 2=-198.93 \mathrm{J} / \mathrm{kg}^{-k} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a counter-flow heat exchanger, water is heated at the rate of 1.5kg/s from [latex]40\,^{\circ} C[/latex]  to [latex]80\,^{\circ} C[/latex] by an oil entering at [latex]120\,^{\circ} C[/latex] and leaving at [latex]60\,^{\circ} C[/latex].  The specific heat of water and oil are [latex]4.2\:kJ/kg \! \cdot\!K[/latex]  and [latex]2\:kJ/kg \! \cdot\!K[/latex], respectively. The overall heat transfer coefficient is [latex]400\, W/m^{2} \cdot K[/latex]  The required heat transfer surface area (in [latex]m^{2}[/latex] ) is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \Delta T_{i} &=120-80=40^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ \Delta T_{e} &=60-40=20^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ (L M T D) \text { Counterflow }&=\frac{\Delta T_{i}-\Delta T_{e}}{\ln \frac{\Delta T_{i}}{\Delta T_{e}}} =28.86^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ &=\frac{40-20}{\ln \frac{40}{20}} = 28.86^{o}\mathrm{C}\\ Q &=\dot{m}_{C} c_{p_{c}}\left(T_{c e}-T_{c i}\right) \\ &=1.5 \times 4.2 \times 10^{3}(80-40) \mathrm{watt} \\ Q &=252000 \mathrm{W} \\ Q &=U A \Delta T_{m} \\ A &=\frac{Q}{U \Delta T_{m}}=\frac{1.5 \times 4.2 \times 10^{3} \times 40}{400 \times 28.86} \\ &=21.83 \mathrm{m}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

since K being high and size of ball being small,

raw_source.text: A strip of 120 mm width and 8 mm thickness is rolled between two 300 mm-diameter rolls to get a strip of 120 mm width and 7.2 mm thickness. The speed of the strip at the exit is 30 m/min. There is no front or back tension. Assuming uniform roll pressure of 200 MPa in the roll bite and 100% mechanical efficiency, the minimum total power (in kW) required to drive the two roll is _______.
raw_source.solution:
Method-1:

Projected length,
[latex] \begin{aligned} L_{p} &=R \sin \alpha \approx \sqrt{R \Delta h} \\ &=\sqrt{150 \times(8-7.2)}=10.954 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Projected Area,
[latex] \begin{aligned} A_{p} &=L_{p} \times b=10.954 \times 120 \\ &=1314.48 \mathrm{mm}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Roll Separating Force,
[latex] \begin{aligned} F &=\sigma_{0} \times L_{p} \times b N \\ &=200 \times 1314.48 \mathrm{N}=262.9 \mathrm{kN}\\ &\left[\sigma_{o} \text { in } N / m m^{2} \text { i.e. } M P a\right] \\ \text{ Arm length (a in mm)}&=0.5 L_{p} \text{for hot rolling}\\ &=0.5 \times 10.954 \mathrm{mm}=5.477 \mathrm{mm}\\ &=0.45 L_{p} \;\text{for cold rolling }\\ \end{aligned}[/latex]
Torque per roller,
[latex] \begin{aligned} T &=F \times \frac{a}{1000} \mathrm{Nm} \\ &=262.9 \mathrm{kN} \times 5.477 \mathrm{mm} \\ &=1439.9 \mathrm{Nm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Total power for two roller,
[latex] P=2 T \omega \text { in } W=2 T \times \frac{2 \pi N}{60}[/latex]
For the calculation of N we need velocity of neutral plane
Continuity equation
[latex] \begin{aligned} h_{0} b_{0} v_{0} &=h_{f} b_{f} v_{f} \\ 8 \times 120 \times v_{0} &=7.2 \times 120 \times 30 \\ \text{or}\quad v_{0} &=27 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Assuming velocity of neutral plane
average velocity,
[latex] \begin{aligned} V &=\frac{V_{0}+V_{f}}{2}=\frac{27+30}{2} \\ &=28.5 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min}\\ \text{Now,}V&=\pi D N\\ \text{or}\quad 28.5&=\pi \times 0.300 \times N\\ \text{or}\quad N&=30.24 \mathrm{rpm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
[latex] \therefore [/latex] Total power for two roller,
[latex] \begin{aligned} P &=2 T \times \frac{2 \pi N}{60} \\ &=2 \times 1439.9 \times \frac{2 \times \pi \times 30.24}{60} \mathrm{W} \\ &=9.1195 \mathrm{kW} \approx 9.12 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Method-II :
Velocity at the neutral plane =?
[latex] \begin{aligned} H_{n} V_{n}&=H_{2} V_{2} \quad(\text { Applying continuity }) \\ H_{n}&=H_{2}+0.25 \Delta H\\ &\text{(Standard relation)}\\ &=7.2+0.25 \times 0.8=7.4 \mathrm{mm} \\ V_{n}&=\frac{\mathrm{H}_{2} \mathrm{V}_{2}}{\mathrm{H}_{n}}=29.19 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min} \\ N&=\frac{29.19 \times 1000}{\pi \times 300}=30.98 \mathrm{rpm}\\ \text{total power }&=2 T \omega \\ &=2 \times 1439.9 \times 2 \pi \frac{30.98}{60} \\ &=9.34 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: During the turning of a 20mm-diameter steel bar at a spindle speed of 400 rpm, a tool life of 20 minute is obtained. When the same bar is turned at 200 rpm, the tool life become 60 minute. Assume that Taylor's tool life equation is valid. When the bar is turned at 300 rpm, the tool lidfe (in minute) is approximately.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} V_{1}=\pi D \times 400 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min} ; & T_{1}=20 \mathrm{min} \\ V_{2}=\pi D \times 200 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min} ; & T_{2}=60 \mathrm{min} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Now using Taylor's equation
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \qquad V_{1} T_{1}^{n}=V_{2} T_{2}^{n} \\ \text { or } \pi D \times 400 \times(20)^{n}=\pi D \times 200 \times 60^{\text {n }} \\ \text { or } \quad n=0.6309\\ \text { and } \quad V_{3}=\pi D \times 300 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min} ; \quad T_{3}=?\\ \qquad V_{1} T_{1}^{n}=V_{2} T_{2}^{n}=V_{3} T_{3}^{n} \\ \pi D \times 400 \times(20)^{0.6309}=\pi D \times 300 \times T_{3}^{0.6309} \\ \therefore \quad T_{3}=31.55 \mathrm{min} \approx 32 \mathrm{min} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In an orthogonal machining with a tool of [latex]9^{\circ}[/latex] orthogonal rake angle, the uncut chip thickness is 0.2mm. The chip thickness fluctuates between 0.25 mm and 0.4 mm. The ratio of the maximum shear angel to the minimum shear angle during machining is _________
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \text{Given} \quad\alpha &=9^{\circ} \\ t &=0.2 \mathrm{mm} \\ t_{c \max } &=0.4 \mathrm{mm} \\ t_{c \min } &=0.25 \mathrm{mm} \\ \tan \phi_{\max } &=\frac{r_{\max } \cos \alpha}{1-r_{\max } \sin \alpha}=\frac{\frac{0.2}{0.25} \cos 9^{\circ}}{1-\frac{0.2}{0.25} \sin 9}\\ \text{or }\quad \phi_{\max } &=42.09^{\circ} \\ \tan \phi_{\min } &=\frac{r_{\min } \cos \alpha}{1-r_{\min } \sin \alpha}=\frac{\frac{0.2}{0.4} \cos 9^{\circ}}{1-\frac{0.2}{0.4} \sin 9^{\circ}}\\ \text{or}\quad \phi_{\mathrm{min}} &=28.18^{\circ} \\ \text { Ratio } &=\frac{\phi_{\max }}{\phi_{\min }}=\frac{42.09}{28.18}=1.494 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A six-faced fair dice is rolled five times. The probability (in %) of obtaining "ONE" at least four times is
raw_source.solution:
A dice is rolled 5 times
[latex] \begin{aligned} n&=5 \\ P&=(\text { Probability of getting } 1)=\frac{1}{6} \\ q&=1-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{5}{6} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Probability of getting 1 at least 4 times is
[latex] \begin{aligned} P(x \geq 4) &=P(x=4)+P(x=5) \\ &=^{n} C_{4} p^{4} q^{n-4}+^{n} C_{5} p^{5} q^{n-5} \\ &=^{5} C_{4} p^{4} q^{1}+^{5} C_{5} p^{5} q^{0} \\ &=5 \times\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{4}\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{1}+1 \times\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{5} \times\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{0}\\ &=\frac{25}{(6)^{5}}+\frac{1}{(6)^{5}}=\frac{26}{(6)^{5}}=0.0033 \end{aligned}[/latex]
% probability =0.33%

raw_source.text: Let [latex]X_{1}[/latex], [latex]X_{2}[/latex]  be two independent normal random variables with means [latex]\mu 1[/latex], [latex]\mu 2[/latex] and standard deviations, respectively. Consider  [latex]Y=X_{1}-X_{2}[/latex]; [latex]\mu _{1} = \mu _{2}[/latex]=1, [latex]\sigma _{1}=1, \sigma _{2}=2[/latex]. Then
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\mu_{1}=1, \mu_{2}=1, \sigma_{1}=1, \sigma_{2}=2 [/latex]
[latex] x_{1} \text{ and } x_{2}[/latex] are two independent random variables
[latex] \begin{aligned} Y &=X_{1}-X_{2} \\ \mu(Y) &=\mu\left(X_{1}-X_{2}\right) \\ &=\mu\left(X_{1}\right)-\mu\left(X_{2}\right)=\mu_{1}-\mu_{2}=1-1=0 \\ \text{Var}(Y) &=\text{Var}\left(X_{1}-X_{2}\right) \\ &=\text{Var}\left(X_{1}\right)+\text{Var}\left(X_{2}\right)-\text{Cov}\left(X_{1}, X_{2}\right) \end{aligned}[/latex]
since [latex] X_{1} \text{ and }X_{2}[/latex] are independent variables
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{Var}(Y) &=\operatorname{Var}\left(X_{1}\right)+\operatorname{Var}\left(X_{2}\right) \\ &=\sigma_{1}^{2}+\sigma_{2}^{2}=1+4 \\ \operatorname{Var}(Y) &=5 \end{aligned}[/latex]
options: Y is normally distributed with mean 0 and variance 1
Y is normally distributed with mean 0 and variance 5
Y has mean 0 and variance 5, but is NOT normally distributed
Y has mean 0 and variance 1, but is NOT normally distributed

raw_answer.option_text: Y is normally distributed with mean 0 and variance 5

raw_source.text:
The minimum value of [latex]3x+5y[/latex]
such that:
[latex]3x+5y\leq 15[/latex]
[latex]4x+9y\leq 8[/latex]
[latex]13x+2y\leq 2[/latex]
[latex]x\geq 0,y\geq 0[/latex]
is _______.
raw_source.solution:
[latex]Z=3 x+5 y[/latex]
Let us consider [latex]3 x+5 y \leq 15 \qquad \ldots(i)[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { If }\quad 3 x+5 y&=15 \\ x &=0 y=3 \\ x &=5 y=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Let us consider [latex]4 x+9 y \leq 8 \qquad \ldots(ii)[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { If } \quad 4 x+9 y &=8 \\ x &=0 y= \frac{8}{9} \\ x &=2 y =0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Let us consider [latex]13 x+2 y \leq 2 \qquad \ldots(iii)[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{If}\quad 3 x+2 y &=2 \\ x &=0 y=1 \\ x &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} y=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Comparing (ii) and (iii)
[latex] \begin{array}{r} 4 x+9 y=8 \qquad \ldots(ii)\\ 13 x+2 y=2 \qquad \ldots(iii)\end{array}[/latex]
From(ii) [latex]\qquad x=\frac{8-9 y}{4}[/latex]
Putting in (iii)
[latex] \frac{13(8-9 y)}{4}+2 y=2[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} 104-117 y+8 y &=8 \\ 109 y &=96\\ \therefore \quad y=0.88 \\ x=0.02 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Hence, Checking at corner points:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad Z\left(0, \frac{8}{9}\right) &=3(0)+5\left(\frac{8}{9}\right)=4.44 \\ Z(0.02,0.88) &=3(0.02)+5(0.88)=4.46 \\ Z\left(\frac{2}{13}, 0\right) &=3\left(\frac{2}{13}\right)+5(0)=0.46 \end{aligned}[/latex]
At (0, 0) Z=0 so minimum value will be 0

raw_source.text: A six-faced fair dice is rolled five times. The probability (in %) of obtaining "ONE" at least four times is

Probability of getting 1 at least 4 times is
[latex] \begin{aligned} P(x \geq 4) &=P(x=4)+P(x=5) \\ &=^{n} C_{4} p^{4} q^{n-4}+^{n} C_{5} p^{5} q^{n-5} \\ &=^{5} C_{4} p^{4} q^{1}+^{5} C_{5} p^{5} q^{0} \\ &=5 \times\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{4}\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{1}+1 \times\left(\frac{1}{6}\right)^{5} \times\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)^{0}\\ &=\frac{25}{(6)^{5}}+\frac{1}{(6)^{5}}=\frac{26}{(6)^{5}}=0.0033 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: An ideal gas undergoes a process from state  1 [latex](T_{1} = 300K, p_{1} = 100kPa)[/latex]  to state 2 [latex](T_{2} = 600K, p_{2} = 500kPa)[/latex]. The specific heats of the ideal gas are : [latex]C_{p} = 1kJ/kg-K[/latex] and [latex]C_{v} = 0.7kJ/kg-K[/latex] . The change in specific entropy of the ideal gas from state 1 to state 2 (in kJ/kg-K) is ________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
Ideal gas
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \text { State-1: } T_{1}=300 \mathrm{K}, P_{1}=100 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \text { State-2: } T_{2}=600 \mathrm{K}, P_{2}=500 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \begin{aligned} c_{p}=1 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K}, c_{p}-c_{v}&=R, c_{v}=0.7 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad c_{p}-c_{v}&= 1-0.7=R \\ R &=0.3 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K} \end{aligned} \end{array}[/latex]
Change in specific entropy
[latex] \begin{aligned} s_{2}-s_{1} &=c_{p} \ln \frac{T_{2}}{T_{1}}-R \ln \frac{P_{2}}{P_{1}} \\ &=1 \times \ln \frac{600}{300}-0.3 \ln \frac{500}{100}=0.21 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Let [latex]X_{1}[/latex], [latex]X_{2}[/latex]  be two independent normal random variables with means [latex]\mu 1[/latex], [latex]\mu 2[/latex] and standard deviations, respectively. raw_source.text:
The value of the integral

over the closed surface S bounding a volume V, where [latex]\overrightarrow{r} = x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}[/latex] is the position vector and [latex]\overrightarrow{n}[/latex] is the normal to the surface S, is
raw_source.solution:
By Gauss Divergence Theorem
[latex] \begin{aligned} \iint_{S} \vec{r} \cdot \hat{n} d s &=\iiint_{V} \bar{V} \cdot \vec{r} d V \\ &=\iiint_{V} 3 d V=3 \mathrm{V} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A point mass is shot vertically up from ground level with a velocity of 4 m/s at time, [latex]t_0[/latex]. It loses 20% of its impact velocity after each collision with the ground. Assuming that the acceleration due to gravity is [latex]10m/s^{2}[/latex]  and that air resistance is negligible, the mass stops bouncing and comes to complete rest on the ground after a total time (in seconds) of
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} (1) \rightarrow \qquad t&=? \\ v&=u+a t \\ 0&=4-10 t \\ t&=\frac{4}{10}=0.4 s \\ (2) \rightarrow \qquad t^{\prime}&=? \\ u^{\prime}&=0.8 \times u \\ &=0.8 \times 4=3.2 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ \mathrm{v}^{\prime}&=U^{\prime}+\mathrm{al}^{\prime} \\ 0&=3.2-10 t^{\prime} \\ t^{\prime}&=\frac{3.2}{10}=0.32 \mathrm{s} \\ (3) \rightarrow \qquad t^{\prime \prime}&=? \\ U^{\prime \prime} &=0.8 u^{\prime} \\ &=0.8 \times 3.2=2.56 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V^{\prime \prime} &=U^{\prime \prime}+a t^{\prime} \\ 0 &=2.56-10 t^{\prime \prime} \\ t^{\prime \prime} &=0.256 s \end{aligned}[/latex]
So, [latex]t, t^{\prime}, t^{\prime \prime}[/latex] are forming a GP series
[latex] \begin{array}{l} \text{So, total time }=2\left(t+t^{\prime}+t^{\prime \prime}+\ldots . .0\right)\\ =2[0.4+0.32+0.256+\ldots .0] \\ =2 \times \frac{0.4}{1-0.8}=2 \times 2=4 s \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The state of stress at a point, for a body in plane stress, is shown in the figure below. If the minimum principal stress is 10 kPa, then the normal stress [latex]\sigma_{y}[/latex] (in kPa) is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} \sigma_{x} &=100 \mathrm{kPa}, \tau_{x y}=50 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \text { Minimum principal stress } &=\frac{\sigma_{x}+\sigma_{y}}{2}-\sqrt{\left(\frac{\sigma_{x}-\sigma_{y}}{2}\right)^{2}+\tau_{x y}^{2}} \\ 10 &=\frac{100+\sigma_{y}}{2}-\sqrt{\left(\frac{100-\sigma_{y}}{2}\right)^{2}+50^{2}} \\ \therefore \quad \sqrt{\left(50-\frac{\sigma_{y}}{2}\right)^{2}+50^{2}} &=50+\frac{\sigma_{y}}{2}-10=40+\frac{\sigma_{y}}{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]
By squaring
[latex] 2500+\frac{\sigma_{y}^{2}}{4}-50 \sigma_{y}+2500=1600+\frac{\sigma_{y}^{2}}{4}+40 \sigma_{y}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad 90 \sigma_{y} &=3400 \\ \sigma_{y} &=37.78 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A self-aligning ball bearing has a basic dynamic load rating ( [latex]C_{10}[/latex]  for [latex]10^{6}[/latex] revolutions) of 35 kN. If the equivalent radial load on the bearing is 45 kN, the excepted life (in  revolutions) is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} C &=35 \mathrm{kN} \\ \mathrm{P}_{C} &=45 \mathrm{kN} \\ L_{90} &=\left(\frac{C}{P_{C}}\right)^{3}=\left(\frac{35}{45}\right)^{3}=0.4705 \mathrm{MR} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A tank open at the top with a water level of 1 m, as shown in the figure, has a hole at a height of 0.5 m. A free jet leaves horizontally from the smooth hole. The distance X (in m) where the jet strikes the floor is
raw_source.solution:
Let free jet velocity is x displacement
[latex] t=\frac{x}{v}[/latex]
As per Torricelli's formula, [latex]V=\sqrt{2 g h} [/latex]
[latex] t=\frac{x}{\sqrt{2 g h}} \qquad \ldots(i)[/latex]


By second law of motion equation
[latex] \begin{aligned} s&=u t+\frac{1}{2} g t^{2} \\ \text{For free fall}\quad u&=0, s=\frac{1}{2} g t^{2}\\ t&=\sqrt{\frac{2 S}{g}} \quad \ldots(ii) \\ \text{ is the time of free fall of object} \end{aligned}[/latex]
By equation (i) and (ii)
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{x}{\sqrt{2 g h}} &=\sqrt{\frac{2 s}{g}} \\ x &=\sqrt{4 h s}=\sqrt{4 \times 0.5 \times 0.5}=1 \mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a Lagrangian system, the position of a fluid particle in a flow is described as [latex]x=x_{o}e^{-kt}[/latex] and [latex]y=y_{o}e^{kt}[/latex] where t is the time while [latex]x_{o}[/latex]  ,[latex]x_{o}[/latex], and k are constants. The flow is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]x[/latex] direction scalar of velocity field,
[latex] \begin{array}{l} u=\frac{d x}{d t} \\ u=-k x_{0} e^{-k t} \end{array}[/latex]
[latex]y[/latex] direction scalar of velocity field
[latex] \begin{aligned} v&=\frac{d y}{d t}\\ v &=k y_{0} e^{k t} \end{aligned}[/latex]
u & v are non zero scalar [latex]t \geq 0[/latex]. So the fluid has its motion in both x and y direction indicating 2-dimensional flow.

Now if we carefully see [latex]'u'[/latex] and [latex]'v'[/latex] functions.
[latex]'u'[/latex] can be expressed as [latex]u=-kx[/latex] as [latex]x=x_{0} e^{-k t}[/latex]
[latex]'v'[/latex] can be expressed as [latex]v=ky[/latex] as [latex]y=y_{0} e^{k t}[/latex]
So both [latex]'u'[/latex] and [latex]'v'[/latex] are the function of positions only.
[latex]\begin{aligned} \vec{V} &=u \hat{i}+v \hat{j} \\ V &=-k x \hat{i}+k y \hat{j} \end{aligned}[/latex]

So, flow is steady.

raw_source.text: The maximum reduction in cross-sectional area per pass ( R ) of a cold wire drawing process is [latex]R=1-e^{-(n+1)}[/latex] where n represents the strain hardening coefficient. For the case of a perfectly plastic  material, R is
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\sigma_{d}=\sigma_{0} \ln \frac{A_{0}}{A_{f}}[/latex]
For maximum reduction
[latex] \begin{aligned} \sigma_{d} &=\sigma_{0} \\ \sigma_{0} &=\sigma_{0} \ln \frac{A_{0}}{A_{f, \min }} \\ \Rightarrow \qquad 1&=\ln \left(\frac{A_{0}}{A_{f, \min }}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \qquad \frac{A_{0}}{A_{f, \min }} &=e=2.71828 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Maximum reduction in Area
[latex] R=\frac{A_{0}-A_{f, \min }}{A_{0}}=\left(1-\frac{1}{e}\right)=\left(1-\frac{1}{2.71828}\right)=0.632[/latex]

raw_source.text: The percentage scrap in a sheet metal blanking operation of a continuous strip of sheet metal as shown in the figure is _______ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
This rectangle ABCD will be repeated again and again.
[latex] \begin{aligned} A_{t}&=\text { Total Area }=\frac{7}{5} D \times \frac{6}{5} D=\frac{42}{25} D^{2} \\ A_{u}&=\text { Area of blanking Disc }=\frac{\pi D^{2}}{4}\\ \% \text { of scrap } &=\frac{A_{t}-A_{v}}{A_{t}} \times 100 \% \\ &=\left[1-\frac{\left(\frac{\pi}{4}\right)}{\left(\frac{42}{25}\right)}\right] \times 100 \%=53.25 \% \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
An explicit forward Euler method is used to numerically integrate the differential equation
[latex]\frac{\mathrm{d} y}{\mathrm{d} x}=y[/latex]
using a time step of 0.1. With the initial condition y(0) = 1, the value of y(1) computed by this method is ___________ (correct to two decimal places).

F(s) is the Laplace transform of the function
[latex]f(t)=2t^{2}e^{-t}[/latex]
F(1) is ____________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} L\left(t^{2}\right)&=\frac{L^{2}}{S^{3}}\\ L\left(2 t^{2}\right)&=\frac{4}{S^{3}} \\ F(s)&=L\left[e^{-t} \cdot 2 t^{2}\right]=\frac{4}{(S+1)} \\ F(1)&=\frac{4}{(1+1)^{3}}=\frac{4}{8}=0.5 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A simply supported beam of width 100 mm, height 200 mm and length 4 m is carrying a uniformly distributed load of intensity 10 kN/m. The maximum bending stress (in MPa) in the beam is __________ (correct to one decimal place).
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\text { Maximum B.M.. } M=\frac{w L^{2}}{8}=\frac{10 \times 16}{8}=20 \mathrm{kNm} \quad (L=4)[/latex]
Maximum Bending Stress
[latex] \begin{aligned} \sigma_{\max } &=\frac{M}{I} y_{\max }=\frac{20 \times 10^{3}}{\left(\frac{0.1 \times 0.2^{3}}{12}\right)} \times 0.1 \\ &=30 \times 10^{6} \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m}^{2}=30 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A machine of mass m = 200 kg is supported on two mounts, each of stiffness k = 10 kN/m. The machine is subjected to an external force (in N) F(t)=50cos5t. Assuming only vertical translatory motion, the magnitude of the dynamic force (in N) transmitted from each mount to the ground is ______ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} m&=200 \mathrm{kg}, k=10 \mathrm{kN} / \mathrm{m}=10000 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m} \\ \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{eq}}&=K+K=10000+10000=20000 \mathrm{N} / \mathrm{m} \\ F_{t}&=50 \cos 5 t \\ F_{0}&=50 \mathrm{N} \\ \omega&=5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ \omega_{n}&=\sqrt{\frac{K_{e q}}{m}}=\sqrt{\frac{20000}{200}} \\ &=\sqrt{100}=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ \frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}&=\frac{5}{10}=\frac{1}{2} \\ \mathrm{Nodamping\Rightarrow} c=0 &\Rightarrow \xi=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
No damping [latex]\Rightarrow c=0 \Rightarrow \xi=0 [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{Transmissibility}\quad \epsilon&=\frac{\sqrt{1+\left(\frac{2 \xi \omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}}}{\sqrt{\left\{1-\left(\frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}\right\}^{2}+\left\{\frac{2 \xi \omega}{\omega_{n}}\right\}^{2}}} \qquad (\xi=0)\\ &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left\{1-\left(\frac{\omega}{\omega_{n}}\right)^{2}\right\}^{2}}} \\ &=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\left\{1-\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^{2}\right\}^{2}}}\\ &=\frac{1}{1-\frac{1}{4}}=\frac{1}{\frac{3}{4}}=\left(\frac{4}{3}\right) \\ \epsilon&=\frac{F_{t}}{F_{0}} \frac{3}{4}&=\frac{F_t}{50} \\ F_t&=\frac{200}{3}=66.666N\\ &\text{Force from each mount}\\ &=\frac{F_t}{2}=\frac{66.666}{2}=33.333N\end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A slider crank mechanism is shown in the figure. At some instant, the crank angle is [latex]45^{\circ}[/latex] and a force of 40 N is acting towards the left on the slider. The length of the crank is 30 mm and the connecting rod is 70 mm. Ignoring the effect of gravity, friction and inertial forces, the magnitude of the crankshaft torque (in Nm) needed to keep the mechanism in equilibrium is _________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} 30 \sin 45^{\circ} &=70 \sin \beta \\ \sin \beta &=\frac{30 \sin 45}{70}=0.303045 \\ \beta &=17.6406^{\circ} \\ F_{C} \cos \beta &=40 \\ F_{C} &=\frac{40}{\cos \beta}=41.9737 \mathrm{N} \\ F_{t} &=F_{C} \sin (\theta+\beta) \\ &=41.9737 \times \sin \left(17.6406^{\circ}+45^{\circ}\right) \\ F_{t} &=37.2785 \mathrm{N} \\ T &=F_{t} \times r=47.2785 \times 0.030 \\ &=1.1183 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m}=1.118 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m} \\ &=1.12 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A sprinkler shown in the figure rotates about its hinge point in a horizontal plane due to water flow discharged through its two exit nozzles.

The total flow rate Q through the sprinkler is 1 litre/sec and the cross-sectional area of each exit nozzle is [latex]1 cm^{2}[/latex]. Assuming equal flow rate through both arms and a frictionless hinge, the steady state angular speed of rotation (in rad/s) of the sprinkler is ______ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
Relative velocities of water with sprinkler
[latex] \begin{aligned} V_{A}&=\frac{Q / 2}{A}=\frac{1 \times 10^{-3}}{2 \times 10^{-4}}=5 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \\ V_{B}&=5 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Absolute velocity from B side
[latex] \begin{aligned} V_{\text {Abs }}^{\prime}-\left(+r_{B} \omega\right)&=V_{B}\\ V_{A b s}^{\prime} &=V_{B}+r_{B} \omega \\ &=5+0.1 \omega \end{aligned}[/latex]
Absolute velocity from A side
[latex] \begin{aligned} V_{\mathrm{Abs}}-\left(-r_{A} \omega\right)&=V_{A}\\ V_{\mathrm{Abs}}&=V_{A}-r_{A} \omega \\ V_{\mathrm{Abs}}&=5-0.2 \mathrm{c} \end{aligned}[/latex]
The external torque to the sprinkler is zero.
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{So,}\qquad \Sigma T&=0\\ \dot{m}_{A} V_{A b s} r_{A}-\dot{m}_{B} V_{A b s}^{\prime} r_{B}&=0 \\ \rho\left(\frac{Q}{2}\right)\{5-0.2 \omega\} 0.2-\rho \frac{Q}{2}\{5+0.1 \omega\} 0.1&=0 \\ 1-0.04 \omega-0.5-0.01 \omega&=0 \\ 0.05 \omega&=0.5 \\ \omega&=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A solid block of 2.0 kg mass slides steadily at a velocity V along a vertical wall as shown in the figure below. A thin oil film of thickness h = 0.15 mm provides lubrication between the block and the wall. The surface area of the face of the block in contact with the oil film is 0.04 m2. The velocity distribution within the oil film gap is linear as shown in the figure. Take dynamic viscosity of oil as [latex]7\times 10^{-3}[/latex] Pa-s and acceleration due to gravity as 10 [latex]m/s^{2}[/latex]. Neglect weight of the oil. The terminal velocity V (in m/s) of the block is _________ (correct to one decimal place).
raw_source.solution:
Terminal velocity is a constant velocity i.e. the net acceleration is zero.
[latex]\begin{aligned} \text{So,} \qquad \Sigma \mathrm{F}_{\mathrm{net}}&=m a \\ \mathrm{mg}-\tau \mathrm{A} &=0 \\ \tau \mathrm{A} &=\mathrm{mg} \\ \mu \frac{V}{h} A &=\mathrm{mg} \\ \mathrm{T} \times 10^{-3} \times \frac{V}{0.15 \times 10^{-3}} \times 0.04&=2 \times 10 =10.714 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
A tank of volume 0.05 [latex]m^{3}[/latex] contains a mixture of saturated water and saturated steam at [latex]200^{\circ}C[/latex] . The mass of the liquid present is 8 kg. The entropy (in kJ/kg K) of the mixture is ___________ (correct to two decimal places).

Property data for saturated steam and water are:
At [latex]200^{\circ}C[/latex] , [latex]p_{sat}[/latex] = 1.5538 MPa
[latex]v_{f}[/latex] = 0.001157 [latex]m^{3}[/latex] /kg, [latex]v_{g}[/latex] = 0.12736 [latex]m^{3}[/latex] /kg
[latex]s_{fg}[/latex] =4.1014 kJ/kg K, [latex]s_{f}[/latex]= 2.3309 kJ/kg K
raw_source.solution:
Total volume of tank (V) = 0.05 m3
Means of liquid ([latex]m_{2}[/latex]) = 8 kg

[latex]\begin{aligned} x &=\frac{m_{v}}{m_{v}+m_{L}}(\text { dryness fraction }) \\ V &=V_{L}+v_{v} \\ \text{where, } &V_{L}-\text{ liquid in tank} \\&V_{v} - \text{ vapour in tank}\\ V_{V} &=m_{v} v_{v} \\ v_{v} &=v_{g} @ 200^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ &=0.12736 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{kg} \\ V_{V} &=m_{L} v_{L} \\ v_{L} &=v_{f} @ 200^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \\ &=0.001157 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{kg} \\ V_{L} &=8 \times 0.001157=9.256 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ 0.05 &=9.256 \times 10^{-3}+\mathrm{V}_{V} \\ V_{V} &=0.0474 \mathrm{m}^{3}\\ \text{So,}\qquad 0.04074 &=m_{v} \times 0.12736 \\ m_{v} &=0.3198 \mathrm{kg} \\ x &=\frac{0.3198}{0.3198+8} \\ \Rightarrow \quad x &=0.0384 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Specific entropy of mixture(s)
[latex] \begin{aligned} s&=s_{f}+x s_{f g} \\ s&=2.3309+0.0384 \times 4.1014 \\ s&=2.4884 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}-\mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]
raw_source.tag2: Second Law, Carnot Cycle and Entropy

raw_source.text: Steam flows through a nozzle at a mass flow rate of [latex]\dot{m}=0.1[/latex] kg/s with a heat loss of 5 kW. The enthalpies at inlet and exit are2500kJ/kg and 2350 kJ/kg, respectively. Assuming negligible velocity at inlet ([latex]C_{1}\approx 0[/latex] ), the velocity ( [latex]C_{2}[/latex] ) of steam (in m/s) at the nozzle exit is __________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\dot{m}=0.1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{s}, \dot{Q}=5 \mathrm{kW} \text { (heat loss) }[/latex]
Applying SFEE
[latex] \begin{aligned} \dot{m}\left(h_{1}+\frac{1}{2} c_{1}^{2}+g z_{1}\right)+\dot{Q}&=\dot{m}\left(h_{2}+\frac{1}{2} c_{2}^{2}+g z_{2}\right)+\dot{w}_{c v}\\ c_{1}=0 \text{ and }\dot{w}_{c v}&=0 \\ z_{1} &=z_{2}(\text { assume }) \\ \Rightarrow \quad \dot{m} h_{1}+\dot{Q} &=\dot{m} h_{2}+\dot{m} \frac{1}{2} c_{2}^{2} \\ \Rightarrow \quad 0.1 \times \frac{1}{2} c_{2}^{2} \times 10^{-3} &=0.1(2500-2350)-5 \\ c_{2} &=447.213 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: An engine working on air standard Otto cycle is supplied with air at 0.1 MPa and [latex]35^{\circ}C[/latex]. The compression ratio is 8.  The heat supplied is 500 kJ/kg.   Property data for air: [latex]c_{p}[/latex] = 1.005 kJ/kg K, [latex]c_{v}[/latex] = 0.718 kJ/kg K, R = 0.287 kJ/kg K. The maximum temperature (in K) of the cycle is _________ (correct to one decimal place).
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{c} P_{1}=0.1 \mathrm{MPa}, T_{1}=35^{\circ} \mathrm{C}=308 \mathrm{K} \\ \frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}=n=8 \\ Q_{s}=500 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ c_{p}=1.005 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ c_{v}=0.718 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ R=0.287 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kgK} \\ \gamma=\frac{c_{p}}{c_{v}}=1.399 \simeq 1.40 \\ T_{3}=T_{\max }=? \end{array}[/latex]
For process 1-2
[latex]\begin{aligned} P_{1} V_{1}^{\gamma} &=P_{2} V_{2}^{\gamma} \\ P_{2} &=P_{1}\left(\frac{V_{1}}{V_{2}}\right)^{\gamma}=0.1 \times(8)^{1.4} \\ P_{2} &=1.8379 \mathrm{MPa}\\ \text{and}\qquad \frac{P_{1} V_{1}}{T_{1}} &=\frac{P_{2} V_{2}}{T_{2}} \Rightarrow T_{2} \frac{P_{2} V_{2}}{P_{1} V_{1}} T_{1} \\ T_{2} &=\frac{1.8379 \times 1}{0.1 \times 8} \times 308 \\ T_{2} &=707.6 \mathrm{K}\\ \text{For process } 2 \rightarrow 3 \\ Q_{s}&=C_{V}\left(T_{3}-T_{2}\right)=500 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}\\ 0.718\left(T_{3}-707.6\right) &=500 \\ T_{3} &=1403.97 \mathrm{K} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A plane slab of thickness L and thermal conductivity k is heated with a fluid on one side (P), and the other side (Q) is maintained at a constant temperature, [latex]T_{Q}[/latex] of [latex]25^{\circ}C[/latex] , as shown in the figure. The fluid is at [latex]45^{\circ}C[/latex] and the surface heat transfer coefficient, h, is [latex]10 W/m^{2}K[/latex] . The steady state temperature, [latex]T_{P}[/latex] , (in [latex]^{\circ}C[/latex] ) of the side which is exposed to the fluid is _______ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
Assuming steady state conditions
Thermal circuit

[latex]\begin{aligned} q &=\text { Rate of heat transfer }\\ &=\frac{45-T_{P}}{1 / h A}\\ &=\frac{T_{p}-25}{L / k A} \\ \Rightarrow\qquad \frac{45-T_{P}}{\left(\frac{1}{10}\right)} &=\frac{T_{P}-25}{\frac{0.2}{2.5}} \\ T_{p} &=33.889^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: The true stress ([latex]\sigma[/latex] ) - true strain ([latex]\varepsilon[/latex] ) diagram of a strain hardening material is shown in figure. First, there is loading up to point A, i.e., up to stress of 500 MPa and strain of 0.5. Then from point A, there is unloading up to point B, i.e., to stress of 100 MPa. Given that the Young's modulus E = 200 GPa, the natural strain at point B ( [latex]\varepsilon _{B}[/latex] ) is _________ (correct to three decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
We know that
Slope of AB line is E
[latex]\begin{aligned} E &=\frac{A C}{B C} \\ 200 \times 10^{3} \mathrm{MPa} &=\frac{(500-100) \mathrm{MPa}}{B C} \\ B C &=\frac{400}{200 \times 10^{3}}=0.002 \\ \therefore \qquad \epsilon_{E} &=0.5-0.002=0.498 \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: An orthogonal cutting operation is being carried out in which uncut thickness is 0.010 mm, cutting speed is 130 m/min, rake angle is [latex]15^{\circ}[/latex]  and width of cut is 6 mm. It is observed that the chip thickness is 0.015 mm, the cutting force is 60 N and the thrust force is 25 N. The ratio of friction energy to total energy is __________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} t &=0.010 \mathrm{mm} \\ v &=130 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min} \\ \alpha &=15^{\circ} \\ b &=6 \mathrm{mm} \\ t_{c} &=0.015 \mathrm{mm} \\ F_{c} &=60 \mathrm{N} \\ F_{t} &=25 \mathrm{N} \\ F &=F_{c} \sin \alpha+F_{t} \cos \alpha \\ &=60 \sin 15+25 \cos 15=39.6773 \mathrm{N} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Ratio of frictional energy to total energy
[latex] \begin{array}{l} =\frac{F}{F_{C}} \cdot \frac{V_{C}}{V}=\frac{F}{F_{C}}\left(\frac{t}{t_{C}}\right) \qquad \left[\therefore \; \frac{t}{t_{C}}=\frac{V_{C}}{V}=r \right] \\ =\frac{39.6773}{60} \times \frac{0.010}{0.015}=0.4408 \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
The minimum value of [latex]3x+5y[/latex]

[latex]13x+2y\leq 2[/latex]
[latex]x\geq 0,y\geq 0[/latex]

raw_source.solution:
[latex]Z=3 x+5 y[/latex]
Let us consider [latex]3 x+5 y \leq 15 \qquad \ldots(i)[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { If }\quad 3 x+5 y&=15 \\ x &=0 y=3 \\ x &=5 y=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Let us consider [latex]4 x+9 y \leq 8 \qquad \ldots(ii)[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text { If } \quad 4 x+9 y &=8 \\ x &=0 y= \frac{8}{9} \\ x &=2 y =0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Let us consider [latex]13 x+2 y \leq 2 \qquad \ldots(iii)[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} \text{If}\quad 3 x+2 y &=2 \\ x &=0 y=1 \\ x &=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}} y=0 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Comparing (ii) and (iii)
[latex] \begin{array}{r} 4 x+9 y=8 \qquad \ldots(ii)\\ 13 x+2 y=2 \qquad \ldots(iii)\end{array}[/latex]
From(ii) [latex]\qquad x=\frac{8-9 y}{4}[/latex]
Putting in (iii)
[latex] \frac{13(8-9 y)}{4}+2 y=2[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} 104-117 y+8 y &=8 \\ 109 y &=96\\ \therefore \quad y=0.88 \\ x=0.02 \end{aligned}[/latex]
Hence, Checking at corner points:
[latex] \begin{aligned} \therefore \quad Z\left(0, \frac{8}{9}\right) &=3(0)+5\left(\frac{8}{9}\right)=4.44 \\ Z(0.02,0.88) &=3(0.02)+5(0.88)=4.46 \\ Z\left(\frac{2}{13}, 0\right) &=3\left(\frac{2}{13}\right)+5(0)=0.46 \end{aligned}[/latex]
At (0, 0) Z=0 so minimum value will be 0

[latex] \begin{aligned} a_{R P} &=(R P) \omega^{2}=10 \\ \Rightarrow\quad 20 \omega^{2} &=10\\ \Rightarrow \quad \omega&=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \end{aligned}[/latex]
as [latex]\alpha[/latex] of whole body remains same so point R has only radial acceleration at that instant

and will be in the horizontal backward design, but our reference is only P R. So the angle of it from reference is [latex](180+\theta) [/latex]

raw_source.text: A rigid rod of length 1 m is resting at an angle [latex]\theta = 45^{\circ}[/latex] as shown in the figure. The end P is dragged with a velocity of U = 5 m/s to the right.At the instant shown, the magnitude of the velocity V (in m/s) of point Q as it moves along the wall without losing contact is
raw_source.solution:
Treating like the elliptical trammeds. Rod motion (P, Q) (By sitting on [latex]I_{13} [/latex])
[latex] \begin{array}{c} \frac{V_{P}}{I_{13} P}=\frac{V_{Q}}{I_{13} Q} \\ \frac{5}{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}=\frac{V_{Q}}{\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)} \\ V_{Q}=5 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s} \end{array}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A bar of circular cross section is clamped at ends P and Q as shown in the figure. A torsional moment T=150 Nm is applied at a distance of 100 mm from end P. The torsional reactions [latex]\left ( T_{P}, T_{Q} \right )[/latex] in Nm at the ends P and Q respectively are
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} T_{P}+T_{Q} &=T \ldots(i)\\ Q_{P R}+Q_{R Q} &=0 \\ \frac{T_{P} \cdot L}{G I_{P}}+\frac{\left(T_{P}-T\right) 2 L}{G I_{P}} &=0 \\ T_{P}+2 T_{P} &=2 T \\ T_{P} &=\frac{2 T}{3}=100 \mathrm{Nm}\\ \text{From equation (i)}\\ T_{Q}&=\frac{T}{3}=50 \mathrm{N}-\mathrm{m} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: In a cam-follower,the follower rises by h as the cam rotates by [latex]\delta [/latex] (radians)  at constant angular velocity [latex]\omega [/latex] ( radins/ s ). The follower is uniformly accelerating during the first half of the rise period and it is uniformly decelerating in the latter half of the rise period. Assuming that the magnitudes of the acceleration and deceleration are same, the maximum velocity of the follower is
raw_source.solution:
Here, outstroke angle
[latex] \begin{aligned} \theta_{0} &=\delta \\ \text { and stroke length } &=h \\ \text { angular velocity } &=\omega \end{aligned}[/latex]


[latex] \begin{aligned} V &=u+a t \\ \left(V_{0}\right)_{\max } &=0+a \times \frac{t_{0}}{2}=a \times \frac{\delta}{2 \omega} \quad \ldots(i)\\ \frac{h}{2} &=0+\frac{1}{2} a\left(\frac{t_{0}}{2}\right)^{2} \\ h &=\frac{a t_{0}^{2}}{4}=\frac{a \delta^{2}}{4 \omega_{2}} \\ a &=\frac{4 \omega^{2} \cdot h}{\delta^{2}} \quad\ldots(ii)\\ &\text{ By(i) and (ii),} \\ \left(V_{0}\right)_{\max } &=\frac{a \delta}{2 \omega}=\frac{4 \omega^{2} \cdot h}{\delta^{2}} \times \frac{\delta}{2 \omega}=\frac{2 \omega \cdot h}{\delta} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A bimetallic cylindrical bar of cross sectional area 1 [latex]m^{2}[/latex] is made by bonding Steel (Young's modulus = 210 GPa) and Aluminium (Young's modulus = 70 GPa) as shown in the figure. To maintain tensile axial strain of magnitude [latex]10^{-6}[/latex] in Steel bar and compressive axial strain of magnitude [latex]10^{-6}[/latex] in Aluminum bar, the magnitude of the required force P (in kN) along the indicated direction is
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} P_{s t}+P_{A l} &=P \\ \Delta_{\mathrm{st}}+\Delta_{\mathrm{A} 1} &=0 \quad\ldots(i)\\ \frac{P_{s t} \cdot \frac{L}{2}}{A E_{s t}}+\frac{\left(P_{s t}-P\right) \frac{L}{2}}{A E_{A L}} &=0 \\ \frac{P_{s t}}{210}+\frac{P_{s t}-P}{70} &=0 \\ \therefore \quad P_{s t} &=\frac{3 P}{4} \\ \text{Now,}\quad \Delta_{\mathrm{st}} &=\frac{P_{s t \cdot} \frac{L}{2}}{A E_{s t}}\\ \epsilon_{s t}&=\frac{P_{s t}}{A . E_{s t}}=\frac{3 P}{4 A E_{s t}}\\ \therefore\quad P&=\frac{E_{s t} \times 4 A \epsilon_{s t}}{3}\\ &=\frac{10^{-6} \times 4 \times 1 \times 2.10 \times 10^{9}}{3} \\ &=280 \mathrm{kN} \end{aligned}[/latex]

A thin-walled cylindrical can with rigid end caps has a mean radius R=100 mm and a wall thickness of t=5 mm . The can is pressurized and an additional tensile stress of 50 MPa is imposed along the axial direction as shown in the figure. Assume that the state of stress in the wall is uniform along its length. If the magnitudes of axial and circumferential components of stress in the can are equal, the pressure (in MPa) inside the can is ___________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
Circumferential stress, [latex]\sigma_{n}=\frac{P R}{t} [/latex]
[latex] \text { Axial stress, } \sigma_{L}=\frac{P R}{2 t}+50 \mathrm{MPa}[/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} {Now,}\quad \sigma_{n} &=\sigma_{L} \\ \frac{P R}{t} &=\frac{P R}{2 t}+50 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \therefore\quad \frac{P R}{2 t} &=50 \mathrm{MPa}\\ P&=\frac{50 \times 2 \times 5}{100}=5 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A bar is subjected to a combination of a steady load of 60 kN and a load fluctuating between -10 kN and 90 kN. The corrected endurance limit of the bar is 150 MPa, the yield strength of the material is 480 MPa and the ultimate strength of the material is 600 MPa. The bar cross-section is square with side a. If the factor of safety is 2, the value of a (in mm), according to the modified Goodman's criterion, is ________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{array}{l} P_{m}=\frac{P_{\max }+P_{\min }}{2} \\ P_{a}=\frac{P_{\max }-P_{\min }}{2} \\ P_{m}=100 \mathrm{kN} \\ \mathrm{Pa}=50 \mathrm{kN} \\ \sigma_{\mathrm{m}}=\frac{100 \times 10^{3}}{a^{2}} \mathrm{MPa} \\ \sigma_{a}=\frac{50 \times 10^{3}}{a^{2}} \mathrm{MPa} \end{array}[/latex]
Solution by Goodman Equation,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{\sigma_{m}}{S_{u t}}+\frac{\sigma_{a}}{\sigma_{e}} &=\frac{1}{N} \\ 100\left[\frac{100}{a^{2} \times 600}+\frac{50}{150 a^{2}}\right] &=\frac{1}{2} \\ a^{2} &=1000 \\ a &=31.62 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Solution by Langar equation,
[latex] \begin{aligned} \frac{\sigma_{m}}{S_{y t}}+\frac{\sigma_{a}}{S_{y t}}&=\frac{1}{N}\\ 100\left[\frac{100}{480 a^{2}}+\frac{50}{480 a^{2}}\right] &=\frac{1}{2} \\ a^{2} &=625 \\ a &=25 \mathrm{mm} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Hence final answer by modified Goodman's Griterion is 31.62 mm.

raw_source.text: A force of 100 N is applied to the centre of a circular disc, of mass 10 kg and radius 1 m, resting on a floor as shown in the figure. If the disc rolls without slipping on the floor, the linear acceleration (in m/[latex]s^{2}[/latex] ) of the centre of the disc is ________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \mathrm{m} &=10 \mathrm{kg}, R=1 \mathrm{m} \\ I &=\frac{m R^{2}}{2}=\frac{m \times 1^{2}}{2}=\frac{m}{2} \\ 100-f_{s} &=m_{a} \\ 100-f_{s} &=10 \mathrm{a} \quad\ldots(i)\\ f_{s} \times R &=I \alpha \\ f_{s} \times 1 &=\frac{m}{2} \times \alpha \\ f_{s} &=\frac{m}{2} \times a \quad\left [\begin{aligned}a=R\alpha=1\times\alpha \\a = \alpha\end{aligned} \right] \\ f_{s} &=\frac{m a}{2}\quad\ldots(ii)\\ \text{By (i) and (ii):}\quad 100-\frac{m a}{2}&=10 a\\ 100-\frac{10 \times a}{2} &=10 a \\ 100-5 a &=10 a \\ 15 a &=100 \\ a &=\frac{100}{15}=6.666 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2} \end{aligned}[/latex]

A 0.2 m thick infinite black plate having a thermal conductivity of 3.96 W/m-K is exposed to two infinite black surfaces at 300 K and 400 K as shown in the figure. At steady state, the surface temperature of the plate facing the cold side is 350 K. The value of Stefan- Boltzmann constant, [latex]\sigma[/latex] , is [latex]5.67 \times 10^{-8} \: W/m^{2}\: K^{4}[/latex] Assuming 1-D heat conduction, the magnitude of heat flux through the plate (in W/[latex]m^{2}[/latex]) is ________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
Under steady state condition, all rate of heat transfer i.e. from surface at 400 K to black plate (via radiation), inside black plate (via conduction) and from black plate to surface at 300 K (via radiation) are equal.
So, heat flux through wall= flux from wall to surface at 300 K
[latex]=\frac{\sigma\left(350^{4}-300^{4}\right)}{\frac{1}{1}+\frac{1}{1}-1}=391.612 \text { watt/m }^{2}[/latex]

raw_source.text: Air is held inside a non-insulated cylinder using a piston (mass M=25 kg and area A=100 [latex]cm^{2}[/latex] and stoppers (of negligible area), as shown in the figure. The initial pressure [latex]P_{i}[/latex] and temperature [latex]T_{i}[/latex] of air inside the cylinder are 200 kPa and [latex]400^{\circ}[/latex]C, respectively. The ambient pressure [latex]P_{\infty }[/latex] and temperature [latex]T_{\infty }[/latex] are 100 kPa and [latex]27^{\circ}C[/latex], respectively. The temperature of the air inside the cylinder [latex](^{\circ}C)[/latex] at which the piston will begin to move is _________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
[latex]\begin{aligned} P_{\infty} &=100 \mathrm{kPa} \\ P_{\text {piston }} &=\frac{M g}{A}=\frac{25 \times 9.81 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{kN}}{0.01 \mathrm{m}^{2}} \\ P_{\text {piston }} &=24.525 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \text { Total external pressure } &=P_{\infty}+P_{\text {piston }}=124.525 \mathrm{kPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]
Initial pressure of air, [latex]P_{i}=200 \mathrm{kPa}[/latex]
Piston will be about to come down if system pressure is equal to total pressure i.e. 124.525kPa
[latex] \Rightarrow [/latex] Final pressure of air at which is about to move is [latex]p_{f}=124.525 \mathrm{kPa}[/latex]
Applying mass conservation at two states [latex]i \xi f [/latex]
[latex] \begin{aligned} M_{i} &=M_{f} \\ \frac{P_{i} V_{i}}{R T_{i}} &=\frac{P_{f} V_{f}}{R T_{f}}=V_{i}=V_{f} \\ \frac{200 \mathrm{kPa}}{673 \mathrm{K}} &=\frac{124.525 \mathrm{kPa}}{T_{f}} \\ T_{f} &=419.026 \mathrm{K} \\ T_{f} &=146.026^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A standard vapor compression refrigeration cycle operating with a condensing temperature of [latex]35^{\circ}C[/latex] and an evaporating temperature of [latex]-10^{\circ}C[/latex] develops 15 kW of cooling. The p-h diagram shows the enthalpies at various states. If the isentropic efficiency of the compressor is 0.75, the magnitude of compressor power (in kW) is _________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} R C &=15 \mathrm{kW} \\ R C &=\dot{m} \times\left(h_{1}-h_{4}\right) \\ 15 &=\dot{m} \times(400-250) \\ \dot{m} &=0.1 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{sec} \\ \omega_{\text {isentropic }} &=\left(h_{2}-h_{1}\right)=(475-400)=75 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg}\\ \eta_{C} &=\frac{\omega_{\text {isentropic }}}{\omega_{\text {actual }}} \\ \omega_{\text {actual }} &=\frac{75}{0.75}=100 \mathrm{kJ} / \mathrm{kg} \\ \omega_{\text {actual }} &=\dot{m} \times \omega_{\text {actual }}=0.1 \times 100 \\ P_{\dot{m}} &=10 \mathrm{kW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

Ambient air is at a pressure of 100 kPa, dry bulb temperature of  [latex]30^{\circ}C[/latex]  and and 60% relative
humidity. The saturation pressure of water at [latex]30^{\circ}C[/latex]  is 4.24 kPa. The specific humidity of
air (in g/kg of dry air) is ________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} P_{\mathrm{atm}} &=100 \mathrm{kPa} \\ D B T &=t=30^{\circ} \mathrm{C} \rightarrow P_{v s}=4.24 \mathrm{kPa} \\ \phi &=60 \%\\ \phi &=\frac{P_{V}}{P_{V S}} \Rightarrow 0.6=\frac{P_{V}}{4.24} \\ P_{V} &=2.544 \mathrm{kPa} \\ W &=0.622 \times \frac{P_{V}}{P_{\mathrm{atm}}-P_{V}} \\ W &=0.622 \times \frac{2.544}{100-2.544} \\ W&=16.24 \text{gram/kg of dry Air} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text: A test is conducted on a one-fifth scale model of a Francis turbine under a head of 2 m and volumetric flow rate of 1 [latex]m^{3}/s[/latex] at 450 rpm. Take the water density and the acceleration due to gravity as  [latex]10^{3}[/latex] kg/[latex]m^{3}[/latex] and 10 m/[latex]s^{2}[/latex], respectively. Assume no losses both in model and prototype turbines. The power (in MW) of a full sized turbine while working under a head of 30 m is _______ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} \frac{D_{m}}{D_{p}}&=\frac{1}{5} \\ &\text { Model }  &\text{Prototype}\\ H&=2 \mathrm{m} &H=30 \mathrm{m} \\ Q&=1 \mathrm{m}^{3} / \mathrm{s} &P=? \\ N&= 450 \mathrm{rpm} \\ \rho&= 1000 \mathrm{kg} / \mathrm{m}^{3} \\ g&=10 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}^{2}\\ \text{For model}\quad \rho_{m}&=\rho_{g} Q H\\ &=1000 \times 10 \times 1 \times 2=20 \mathrm{kW} \\ \left.\frac{H}{D^{2} N^{2}}\right|_{P}&=\left.\frac{H}{D^{2} N^{2}}\right|_{M}\\ N_{P} &=\sqrt{\frac{H_{P}}{H_{M}}} \times \frac{D_{M}}{D_{P}} \times N_{M} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{30}{2}} \times \frac{1}{5} \times 450=348.56 \mathrm{rpm} \\ \left.\frac{P}{D^{5} N^{3}}\right|_{P} &=\left.\frac{P}{D^{5} N^{3}}\right|_{M}\\ P_{P}&=P_{M} \times \frac{D_{P}^{5}}{D_{M}^{5}} \times \frac{N_{P}^{3}}{N_{M}^{3}} \\ P_{P}&=20 \times 5^{5} \times \frac{348.56^{3}}{450^{3}} \\ P_{P}&=29.05 \mathrm{MW} \end{aligned}[/latex]

A steel wire is drawn from an initial diameter([latex]d_{i}[/latex]) of 10 mm to a final diameter ([latex]d_{f}[/latex]) of 7.5 mm. The half cone angle ([latex]\alpha[/latex]) of the die is [latex]5^{\circ}[/latex] and the coefficient of friction ([latex]\mu[/latex]) between the die and the wire is 0.1. The average of the initial and final yield stress [latex][(\sigma_{Y}) _{avg}][/latex] is 350 MPa. The equation for drawing stress [latex]\sigma_{f}[/latex], (in MPa) is given as :
[latex]\sigma _{f}=(\sigma _{Y})_{avg}\left \{ 1+\frac{1}{\mu cot \alpha } \right \}\left [ 1-{\left (\frac{d_{f}}{d_{i}}\right )}^{2\mu cot\alpha } \right ][/latex]
The drawing stress (in MPa) required to carry out this operation is _________ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution: [latex]\begin{aligned} d_{i} &=10 \mathrm{mm} \\ d_{f} &=7.5 \mathrm{mm} \\ \alpha &=5^{\circ} \\ \mu &=0.1 \\ (\sigma y)_{\mathrm{avg}} &=350 \mathrm{MPa} \\ \sigma_{f} &=\left(\sigma_{y}\right)_{\mathrm{avg}} \times\left\{1+\frac{1}{\mu \cot \alpha}\right\}\left[1-\left(\frac{d_{f}}{d_{i}}\right)^{2 \mu \cot \alpha}\right] \\ &=350 \times\left[1+\frac{1}{0.1 \mathrm{cot} 5}\right]\left[1-\left(\frac{7.5}{10}\right)^{2 \times 0.1 \times \cot 5}\right] \\ &=316.2472 \mathrm{MPa} \approx 316.25 \mathrm{MPa} \end{aligned}[/latex]

raw_source.text:
Taylor's tool life equation is used to estimate the life of a batch of identical HSS twist drills
by drilling through holes at constant feed in 20 mm thick mild steel plates. In test 1, a drill
lasted 300 holes at 150 rpm while in test 2, another drill lasted 200 holes at 300 rpm. The
maximum number of holes that can be made by another drill from the above batch at 200
rpm is ______ (correct to two decimal places).
raw_source.solution:
Time required for drilling a hole
[latex] t=\frac{L}{f N}[/latex]
Here 'L' const. 'f const, N is variable.
[latex] \begin{array}{l} V_{1}=\pi D \times 150 \mathrm{m} / \mathrm{min} \\ T_{1}=300 \times \frac{L}{f \times 150} \mathrm{min}\\ V_{2}=\pi D \times 300 \mathrm{min} \\ T_{2}=200 \times \frac{L}{f \times 300} \mathrm{min} \\ V_{3}=\pi D \times 200 \mathrm{min} \\ T_{3}=x \times \frac{L}{f \times 200} \mathrm{min}\qquad \text{[No. of hole is 'x'] }\\ V_{1} T_{1}^{n}=V_{2} T_{2}^{n} \end{array}[/latex]
[latex]\begin{aligned} \pi D \times 150 \times\left(300 \times \frac{L}{f \times 150}\right)^{n} &=\pi D \times 300 \times\left(200 \times \frac{L}{f \times 300}\right)^{n} \\ \text{Or,}\quad2^{n} &=2\left(\frac{2}{3}\right)^{n} \\ \text{Or,}\quad 3^{n}&=2 \\ n &=0.63093 \\ V_{1} T_{1}^{n} &=V_{3} T_{3}^{n} \\ \pi D \times 150 \times\left(300 \times \frac{L}{f \times 150}\right)^{0.63093} &=\pi D \times 200 \times\left(x \times \frac{L}{f \times 200}\right)^{0.63093} \\ 3 \times 2^{0.63093} &=4 \times\left(\frac{x}{200}\right)^{0.63093} \\ \Rightarrow & x=253.53 \end{aligned}[/latex]
